distractors.whyFailsId: kata kunci “In 2010” maku kalimatnya ke masa lalu, jadi “will” nggak sejalan.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk masa depan yang berpijak masa kini dipakai di bingkai cerita lampau.

distractors.misconception: collapsing future-in-the-past into simple past
distractors.whyFails: Simple past would state the transformation as an established past fact, losing the 'seen from an earlier viewpoint' meaning the sentence needs.
distractors.whyFailsId: past simple nyatain perubahannya sebagai fakta lampau biasa, jadi sudut pandangnya ilang.
distractors.misconceptionId: masa depan dari sudut masa lalu diciutin jadi past simple.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Would' + base verb expresses an event that was still in the future relative to 2010, narrated from a later viewpoint.
explanation.rule: Future-in-the-past: would/was going to + verb, used to describe what was going to happen after a past reference point.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Past continuous marks an ongoing action at that moment; a bare future modal breaks the past time frame; simple past removes the 'later than 2010' perspective.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: is this describing something that, from that past moment, was still ahead in time?
explanation.memoryCue: Past moment + 'would' = a future that has now already happened.
explanation.ruleId: Masa depan yang dilihat dari masa lalu pakai would atau was going to + kata kerja. Buat nggambarin apa yang nyusul sesudah satu titik lampau.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Would” + kata kerja dasar nyatain kejadian yang saat itu masih di depan kalau diukur dari 2010. Diceritain dari sudut yang lebih belakangan.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Past continuous nandain tindakan yang masih jalan saat itu. “Will” yang berpijak di masa kini ngerusak bingkai lampaunya, dan past simple ngilangin sudut pandang “sesudah 2010”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya: dari titik lampau itu, kejadiannya masih bakal datang?
explanation.memoryCueId: Titik lampau ditambah “would” berarti masa depan yang sekarang udah kejadian.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu bedain “would” buat masa depan yang dilihat dari titik masa lalu. “Was going to” nyatain niat yang udah diucapin sebelumnya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngira “would” dari sudut masa lalu selalu berarti kebiasaan berulang. Padahal ini satu kejadian yang nyusul.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali bingkai cerita lampaunya → pilih bentuk masa depan dari masa lalu buat satu kejadian yang nyusul

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use past perfect continuous to show a duration-based cause behind a past state/result, distinct from past perfect simple's completed-fact focus
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner treats past perfect simple and past perfect continuous as interchangeable whenever two past events are sequenced
templates.reasoningOperation: detect duration-as-cause meaning -> select past perfect continuous over past perfect simple
templates.stem: His eyes were red because he ___ all night for the exam. (the long hours of studying are the cause)

distractors.misconception: treating past perfect simple as sufficient for any earlier past event
distractors.whyFails: This is correct English and does mark the earlier time, but it stresses that the studying was finished rather than how long it accumulated.
distractors.whyFailsId: bahasanya bener dan waktunya lebih awal, tapi nekanin belajarnya udah tuntas, bukan lamanya.
distractors.misconceptionId: past perfect simple dianggap cukup buat semua kejadian lampau yang lebih awal.

distractors.misconception: using simple past for a state that must be shown as prior to another past moment
distractors.whyFails: This is correct English — 'because' already marks the cause — but it reports the fact plainly instead of foregrounding how long the studying went on.
distractors.whyFailsId: bahasanya bener, tapi cuma nglaporin faktanya, nggak nonjolin lamanya belajar.
distractors.misconceptionId: past simple dipakai buat keadaan yang harus ditunjukin lebih dulu dari titik lampau lain.

distractors.misconception: confusing past continuous with past perfect continuous
distractors.whyFails: Past continuous places the action at the same time as another past event, not clearly before it as the cause of a later result.
distractors.whyFailsId: past continuous naruh tindakannya bareng kejadian lampau lain, bukan jelas mendahuluinya.
distractors.misconceptionId: past continuous ketuker sama past perfect continuous.

explanation.whyCorrect: Past perfect continuous highlights the duration of studying as the direct cause of the later past result (red eyes).
explanation.rule: Past perfect continuous = had been + verb-ing, used for a duration before another past point, especially when that duration explains a visible result.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Past perfect simple stresses completion, not duration-as-cause; simple past and past continuous fail to sequence the studying clearly before the result.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: is the length of the earlier action the reason for what happened next?
explanation.memoryCue: Red eyes need a reason with duration: 'had been -ing'.
explanation.ruleId: Past perfect continuous bentuknya had been + kata kerja -ing. Dipakai buat durasi sebelum satu titik lampau, terutama kalau durasi itu nerangin akibat yang kelihatan.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Past perfect continuous nonjolin lamanya belajar sebagai sebab langsung dari mata yang memerah.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Past perfect simple nekanin tuntasnya, bukan durasi sebagai sebab. Past simple dan past continuous nggak naruh belajarnya jelas sebelum akibatnya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya gini dulu, ya: lamanya tindakan yang lebih awal itu yang jadi alasan kejadian berikutnya?
explanation.memoryCueId: Mata memerah butuh sebab berdurasi: “had been -ing”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pakai past perfect continuous buat nunjukin sebab berdurasi di balik satu keadaan lampau. Bentuk itu beda dari past perfect simple yang nekanin tuntasnya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngira past perfect simple dan past perfect continuous bisa tuker-tukeran tiap ada dua kejadian lampau berurutan.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali makna durasi sebagai sebabnya → pilih past perfect continuous, bukan past perfect simple

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Select 'had better' over 'should' when the context implies an urgent consequence if the advice is ignored
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses 'should' for all advice regardless of urgency, missing that 'had better' signals a specific negative consequence is imminent
templates.reasoningOperation: detect urgency/consequence marker -> select modal of urgent advice
templates.stem: You ___ leave now — if you miss this train, there isn't another one until tomorrow. (strong warning)

distractors.misconception: treating general advice modal as equally strong as urgent-consequence modal
distractors.whyFails: 'Should' gives general advice but doesn't carry the specific-consequence-if-ignored force the 'if you miss...' clause signals.
distractors.whyFailsId: nasihat umum, tanpa desakan akibat yang ditandai anak kalimat “if”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu nasihat umum dianggap sekuat nasihat yang berakibat mendesak.

distractors.misconception: using a possibility modal where obligation/urgency is meant
distractors.whyFails: 'Could' only suggests an option, not the strong urgency implied by the stated consequence.
distractors.whyFailsId: cuma nawarin pilihan, bukan desakan kuat dari akibat yang disebut.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu kemungkinan dipakai padahal yang dimaksud desakan.

distractors.misconception: using a modal of weak possibility for a directive
distractors.whyFails: 'Might' expresses uncertainty about a future event, not advice with an urgent consequence.
distractors.whyFailsId: bilang nggak pasti soal kejadian nanti, bukan nasihat mendesak.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu kemungkinan lemah dipakai buat sebuah arahan.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Had better' is used for urgent advice with a clearly stated bad consequence for not following it.
explanation.rule: Had better + base verb = strong, situation-specific advice implying a negative result if ignored.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Should' is general advice without urgency; 'could' and 'might' express possibility, not directive urgency.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: does the sentence name a specific bad thing that happens if the advice isn't followed right now?
explanation.memoryCue: Missed train tomorrow = 'had better' today.
explanation.ruleId: “Had better” plus kata kerja dasar berarti nasihat kuat buat keadaan tertentu. Bentuk ini bawa akibat buruk kalau diabaikan.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Had better” dipakai buat nasihat mendesak yang akibat buruknya disebut jelas.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Should” cuma nasihat umum tanpa desakan. “Could” dan “might” bilang kemungkinan, bukan arahan yang mendesak.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dulu: kalimatnya nyebut satu akibat buruk kalau nasihatnya diabaikan sekarang?
explanation.memoryCueId: Kereta terakhir sampai besok, berarti “had better” hari ini.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pilih “had better” di atas “should” kalau konteksnya bawa akibat buruk yang mendesak.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai “should” buat semua nasihat tanpa lihat mendesaknya. “Had better” nandain akibat buruk yang udah di depan mata.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cari tanda mendesak atau akibat buruknya → pilih kata bantu nasihat yang paling kuat

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Choose a modal expressing uncertain present speculation rather than confident prediction
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses 'will' for any guess about the present, not distinguishing confident claims from tentative speculation
templates.reasoningOperation: detect epistemic uncertainty marker -> select speculative modal over confident future modal
templates.stem: I'm not sure where Sam is — he ___ still be stuck in traffic.

distractors.misconception: using the confident future/prediction modal for uncertain present speculation
distractors.whyFails: 'Will' asserts confident certainty, which conflicts with the stated 'I'm not sure'.
distractors.whyFailsId: negesin keyakinan, padahal “I’m not sure” bilang sebaliknya.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu ramalan yang yakin dipakai buat dugaan soal sekarang.

distractors.misconception: using the strong-deduction modal where only weak possibility is intended
distractors.whyFails: 'Must' signals a confident logical conclusion from evidence, stronger than the tentative guess the sentence expresses.
distractors.whyFailsId: bilang kesimpulan yakin dari bukti, jauh lebih kuat dari tebakan.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu kesimpulan kuat dipakai padahal maksudnya kemungkinan lemah.

distractors.misconception: using 'can' for a specific present possibility about one situation
distractors.whyFails: 'Can' expresses general possibility/ability, not a specific tentative guess about what's happening right now.
distractors.whyFailsId: bilang kemungkinan umum, bukan tebakan soal keadaan sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: “can” dipakai buat kemungkinan satu keadaan tertentu sekarang.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Might' expresses a tentative, uncertain guess about a present situation, matching 'I'm not sure'.
explanation.rule: May/might/could + base verb = weak epistemic possibility about the present; must = strong deduction; will = confident prediction.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Will' and 'must' both express more confidence than the context supports; 'can' isn't used for one-off specific speculation.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: does the speaker sound sure, or just guessing?
explanation.memoryCue: 'Not sure' pairs with 'might', not 'will'.
explanation.ruleId: “May”, “might”, dan “could” plus kata kerja dasar bilang kemungkinan lemah soal sekarang. “Must” bilang kesimpulan kuat, “will” bilang ramalan yang yakin.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Might” bilang tebakan yang masih ragu soal keadaan sekarang, dan itu cocok sama “I’m not sure”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Will” dan “must” kedengeran lebih yakin daripada yang didukung konteksnya. “Can” nggak dipakai buat dugaan satu keadaan tertentu.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dulu: pembicaranya kedengeran yakin, atau cuma nebak?
explanation.memoryCueId: “Not sure” pasangannya “might”, bukan “will”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pilih kata bantu yang bilang dugaan ragu soal keadaan sekarang, bukan ramalan yang yakin.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai “will” buat semua tebakan soal sekarang. Pernyataan yang yakin dan dugaan yang ragu jadi ketuker.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temuin tanda ketidakpastiannya → pilih kata bantu dugaan, bukan yang yakin

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Correctly negate a past-regret modal to criticize an action that WAS done but shouldn't have been
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner confuses 'shouldn't have' (criticizing something that happened) with 'should have' (criticizing something that didn't happen)
templates.reasoningOperation: identify whether the criticized action occurred or was omitted -> select correctly polarized past modal
templates.stem: He's exhausted today — he ___ up so late watching movies last night.

distractors.misconception: missing the negation needed for criticizing a completed unwise action
distractors.whyFails: This wrongly implies he DIDN'T stay up late, when the context shows he did and that was the mistake.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk ini malah bilang dia nggak begadang, padahal konteksnya bilang sebaliknya.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata negatif yang dibutuhin buat negur tindakan keliru justru ilang.

distractors.misconception: using present-form advice modal instead of past-regret structure
distractors.whyFails: The event (staying up) is already finished and being judged in hindsight, which requires 'should have + past participle', not present 'should'.
distractors.whyFailsId: begadangnya udah kelar dan lagi dinilai dari belakang, jadi “should” bentuk present nggak pas.
distractors.misconceptionId: modal nasihat bentuk present dipakai ganti susunan penyesalan lampau.

distractors.misconception: confusing third conditional result clause with a past-regret judgement
distractors.whyFails: 'Wouldn't have' belongs to hypothetical conditional results, not a direct criticism of a real past action.
distractors.whyFailsId: “wouldn’t have” punya hasil pengandaian, bukan teguran langsung atas tindakan nyata.
distractors.misconceptionId: anak kalimat hasil third conditional ketuker sama teguran atas kejadian nyata.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Shouldn't have stayed' criticizes an action that did happen (staying up late) and caused today's tiredness.
explanation.rule: Should have + past participle = regret over a missed good action; shouldn't have + past participle = criticism of a real action that was a mistake.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Should have stayed' reverses the meaning; 'should stay' isn't past-oriented; 'wouldn't have stayed' belongs to conditional, not direct criticism.
explanation.howToAvoid: First decide: did the action happen or not? Then pick should have (didn't happen, wish it did) or shouldn't have (happened, wish it didn't).
explanation.memoryCue: Tired today = did stay up = 'shouldn't have'.
explanation.ruleId: “Should have” + bentuk ke-3 nyesalin kebaikan yang nggak jadi dilakuin. “Shouldn’t have” + bentuk ke-3 negur tindakan nyata yang ternyata keliru.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Shouldn’t have stayed” negur tindakan yang memang kejadian, yaitu begadang, dan itu penyebab kelelahannya hari ini.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Should have stayed” mbalik maknanya. “Should stay” nggak nengok ke masa lalu, dan “wouldn’t have stayed” punya kalimat pengandaian.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Putusin dulu: tindakannya kejadian atau nggak? Baru pilih kutub modalnya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Kelelahan hari ini berarti tadi malam memang begadang, jadi “shouldn’t have”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu negatifin modal (kata kayak should) buat negur tindakan yang MEMANG dilakuin padahal seharusnya nggak.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nuker “shouldn’t have” yang negur tindakan yang kejadian. “Should have” nyesalin sesuatu yang nggak dilakuin.
templates.reasoningOperationId: tentuin tindakan yang ditegur itu kejadian atau nggak → pilih modal lampau dengan kutub yang tepat

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Recognize formal inverted conditional structure (Had + subject + past participle) as equivalent to 'If I had known'
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner doesn't recognize subject-auxiliary inversion as a valid formal alternative to 'if', and expects 'if' to always be present
templates.reasoningOperation: detect inverted auxiliary-subject order without 'if' -> recognize as formal third conditional equivalent
templates.stem: ___ known about the delay, I would have booked a later flight.

distractors.misconception: mixing formal inversion with the conjunction 'if' at the same time
distractors.whyFails: Formal inversion replaces 'if' entirely — combining both 'if' and inverted word order is redundant and ungrammatical.
distractors.whyFailsId: pembalikan formal udah gantiin “if”, jadi majang keduanya sekaligus bikin susunannya nggak sah.
distractors.misconceptionId: pembalikan formal dan kata sambung “if” dipakai bersamaan.

distractors.misconception: using normal subject-verb order, missing the inversion signal
distractors.whyFails: Without 'if', normal word order 'I had known' cannot function as a conditional clause on its own.
distractors.whyFailsId: tanpa “if”, urutan biasa “I had known” nggak bisa berdiri sendiri sebagai anak kalimat pengandaian.
distractors.misconceptionId: urutan subjek dan kata kerja tetap biasa jadi tanda pembalikannya hilang.

distractors.misconception: using the result-clause auxiliary structure at the start of the if-clause
distractors.whyFails: 'Would' belongs in the result clause ('I would have booked'), not the condition clause, which needs 'had'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “would” itu milik anak kalimat hasil, bukan milik anak kalimat syarat yang minta “had”.
distractors.misconceptionId: susunan kata bantu milik anak kalimat hasil ditaruh di awal anak kalimat syarat.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Had I known' is the formal inverted version of 'If I had known', used in third conditionals in formal or literary style.
explanation.rule: Formal conditional inversion: Had + subject + past participle (no 'if') = 'If + subject + had + past participle'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Combining 'if' with inversion duplicates the conditional marker; plain 'I had' lacks any conditional signal; 'would' is reserved for the main clause.
explanation.howToAvoid: When you see a sentence starting with 'Had + subject' and no 'if', read it as an 'if I had...' clause.
explanation.memoryCue: Drop 'if', flip the order: 'Had I known' = 'If I had known'.
explanation.ruleId: Pembalikan pengandaian formal: Had + subjek + past participle tanpa “if” sama artinya dengan If + subjek + had + past participle.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Had I known” itu bentuk formal terbalik dari “If I had known”, biasa dipakai di third conditional ragam formal.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Gabungin “if” sama pembalikan berarti nandain pengandaiannya dua kali. “I had” polos nggak bawa tanda pengandaian, dan “would” itu milik induk kalimat.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau kalimat dibuka “Had + subjek” tanpa “if”, baca aja sebagai anak kalimat “if I had ...”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Buang “if”, balik urutannya: “Had I known” sama dengan “If I had known”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu ngenalin susunan pengandaian formal Had + subjek + past participle sebagai padanan “If I had known”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu belum ngenalin pembalikan kata bantu dan subjek sebagai bentuk formal yang sah, dan ngira “if” wajib selalu ada.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali urutan kata bantu mendahului subjek tanpa “if” → baca sebagai padanan third conditional yang formal

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Interpret 'otherwise' as an implied conditional connector meaning 'if that were/had not been the case'
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner treats 'otherwise' as a simple contrast word like 'but', missing its hidden conditional logic
templates.reasoningOperation: identify implied unreal condition behind 'otherwise' -> select verb form consistent with that hidden condition
templates.stem: The bridge was closed for repairs; otherwise, the trip ___ much shorter.

distractors.misconception: reading 'otherwise' as a simple future contrast marker
distractors.whyFails: The sentence describes a hypothetical past outcome (a trip that didn't happen shorter), not a real future event.
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimatnya ngomongin hasil lampau yang cuma dibayangin, bukan kejadian nyata di masa depan.
distractors.misconceptionId: “otherwise” dibaca cuma tanda pertentangan soal masa depan.

distractors.misconception: treating the implied condition as a real past fact rather than a hypothetical one
distractors.whyFails: Simple past would claim the trip actually was shorter, contradicting the fact that the bridge was closed.
distractors.whyFailsId: past simple bakal ngeklaim perjalanannya memang lebih singkat, padahal jembatannya ditutup.
distractors.misconceptionId: syarat yang tersirat diperlakukan sebagai fakta lampau yang nyata.

distractors.misconception: ignoring the past time frame set by 'was closed'
distractors.whyFails: Present tense doesn't match the past hypothetical scenario the sentence is describing.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk present nggak cocok sama keadaan lampau yang cuma dibayangin di kalimat ini.
distractors.misconceptionId: waktu lampau yang dipasang “was closed” diabaikan.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Otherwise' here hides the meaning 'if the bridge hadn't been closed', so the result needs third-conditional form: would have been.
explanation.rule: 'Otherwise' can imply an unreal condition; the following clause takes the conditional result form matching that hidden condition's time frame.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Future and present forms don't match the past hypothetical situation being implied by the closed bridge.
explanation.howToAvoid: Mentally rewrite 'otherwise' as 'if that hadn't happened' and check which conditional tense fits.
explanation.memoryCue: 'Otherwise' = a hidden 'if not', so it often needs 'would have + past participle'.
explanation.ruleId: “Otherwise” bisa nyimpen syarat yang nggak nyata. Anak kalimat sesudahnya pakai bentuk hasil pengandaian sesuai waktu syarat tersembunyi itu.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Otherwise” di sini nyimpen makna “kalau jembatannya nggak ditutup”. Jadi hasilnya minta bentuk third conditional.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Bentuk masa depan dan masa kini nggak cocok sama keadaan lampau yang cuma dibayangin di balik jembatan yang ditutup.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tulis ulang “otherwise” dalam hati jadi “kalau itu nggak terjadi”, terus cek bentuk pengandaian mana yang cocok.
explanation.memoryCueId: “Otherwise” itu “if not” yang tersembunyi, jadi sering minta “would have + past participle”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu baca “otherwise” sebagai penghubung yang nyimpen syarat tersirat, yaitu “kalau hal itu nggak terjadi”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngira “otherwise” cuma kata pertentangan kayak “but”, jadi logika pengandaian yang kesimpen di dalamnya kelewat.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temukan syarat nggak nyata yang tersirat di balik “otherwise” → pilih bentuk kata kerja yang sejalan sama syarat itu

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Form impersonal passive reporting structures used to attribute a claim without naming the source
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner tries to keep an active reporting verb structure ('they say that') when the context calls for the impersonal passive pattern
templates.reasoningOperation: detect unnamed/general source of a claim -> select impersonal passive reporting form
templates.stem: ___ that the ancient city was destroyed by an earthquake, though no written records survive.

distractors.misconception: using active voice with a vague 'they' plus an incorrect continuous form for a general belief
distractors.whyFails: 'Believe' isn't normally used in continuous form for a general, ongoing belief, and 'they' isn't specified anywhere in context.
distractors.whyFailsId: “believe” biasanya nggak dipakai bentuk continuous buat anggapan umum.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk aktif dengan “they” yang samar dipakai bareng bentuk continuous yang keliru.

distractors.misconception: treating 'it' as an active subject capable of believing
distractors.whyFails: 'It' is a dummy subject here; it cannot actively 'believe' something, only serve as the subject of the passive construction.
distractors.whyFailsId: “it” di sini cuma subjek semu dan nggak bisa yakin sama sesuatu.
distractors.misconceptionId: “it” diperlakuin sebagai subjek pelaku yang bisa meyakini sesuatu.

distractors.misconception: dropping the required dummy subject 'it' from the impersonal passive pattern
distractors.whyFails: The impersonal passive pattern requires 'It is believed that...'; without 'it', the sentence has no grammatical subject.
distractors.whyFailsId: tanpa “it” di depan, kalimatnya kehilangan subjeknya.
distractors.misconceptionId: subjek semu “it” yang diwajibin pola ini dihilangin.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'It is believed that...' is the standard impersonal passive used to report a widely-held but unattributed belief.
explanation.rule: Impersonal passive reporting: It + is/was + past participle + that-clause (It is said/believed/thought/reported that…). The dummy subject "it" is always singular.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Active 'they are believing' misuses tense and an unspecified subject; 'it believes' misassigns agency to a dummy subject; omitting 'it' leaves the sentence without a subject.
explanation.howToAvoid: When a claim has no clear speaker and needs to sound objective, reach for 'It is said/believed/thought/reported that...'.
explanation.memoryCue: No named source + formal claim = 'It is believed that...'.
explanation.ruleId: Pelaporan pasif tanpa pelaku: It + is atau was + past participle + anak kalimat that. Subjek semu “it” selalu tunggal.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “It is believed that ...” itu bentuk baku pasif pelaporan tanpa pelaku. Dipakai buat anggapan yang luas dianut tapi nggak jelas sumbernya.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “They are believing” salah bentuk waktu dan pakai subjek yang nggak pernah disebut. “It believes” ngasih peran pelaku ke subjek semu, dan tanpa “it” kalimatnya nggak punya subjek.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau sebuah anggapan nggak punya penutur yang jelas dan perlu kedengeran objektif, pakai “It is said/believed that ...”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Tanpa sumber yang disebut dan bernada resmi: “It is believed that ...”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu nyusun passive (fokus ke yang kena tindakan) buat pelaporan tanpa pelaku, biar anggapan kesampaian tanpa nyebut sumbernya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu maksa nahan susunan aktif kayak “they say that”, padahal konteksnya minta pola pasif pelaporan tanpa pelaku.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali sumber anggapannya umum atau nggak diketahui → pilih bentuk pasif pelaporan tanpa pelaku

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use the passive infinitive (to be + past participle) after expectation verbs/modals where the subject receives the action
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner keeps an active infinitive after 'expected to' even when the subject is the receiver, not the doer, of the action
templates.reasoningOperation: identify subject as recipient of the action -> select passive infinitive form
templates.stem: The new policy is expected ___ next month, though the exact date hasn't been confirmed.

distractors.misconception: using active infinitive when the subject (the policy) cannot perform the announcing itself
distractors.whyFails: 'To announce' makes the policy the announcer, even though the policy is the thing receiving the announcement.
distractors.whyFailsId: “to announce” bikin kebijakan itu jadi pihak yang ngumumin.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk to aktif dipakai padahal subjeknya nggak mungkin ngumumin sendiri.

distractors.misconception: using a gerund where an infinitive pattern after 'expected' is required
distractors.whyFails: 'Expected' takes a to-infinitive complement, not a gerund, regardless of voice.
distractors.whyFailsId: “expected” diikuti pelengkap bentuk to, bukan bentuk -ing.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dipakai padahal sesudah “expected” yang diminta pola bentuk to.

distractors.misconception: adding continuous aspect to the passive infinitive unnecessarily
distractors.whyFails: 'To be announcing' stretches a one-off announcement into an ongoing process that the sentence never describes.
distractors.whyFailsId: “to be announcing” bikin pengumuman sekali jadi kedengeran kayak proses panjang.
distractors.misconceptionId: makna berkelanjutan ditambahin ke bentuk to pasif tanpa perlu.

explanation.whyCorrect: Since the policy receives the action of announcing, the passive infinitive 'to be announced' is required after 'is expected'.
explanation.rule: Passive infinitive = to be + past participle, used when the infinitive's subject is the receiver of the action, often after expect/believe/report + to.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Active infinitive wrongly makes the policy the doer; a gerund doesn't fit the 'expected to' pattern; continuous passive infinitive adds unneeded ongoing aspect.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: can the subject actually perform this verb, or does it just receive the action? A policy can't announce — it gets announced.
explanation.memoryCue: The policy is announced, not announcing: 'to be announced'.
explanation.ruleId: Bentuk to pasif itu to be + past participle. Dipakai kalau subjek dari bentuk to itu nerima tindakannya, sering sesudah expect, believe, atau report.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Kebijakan itulah yang kena tindakan ngumumin, jadi bentuk to pasif “to be announced” diwajibin sesudah “is expected”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Bentuk to aktif keliru bikin kebijakannya jadi pelaku. Bentuk -ing nggak cocok sama pola “expected to”. Bentuk to pasif berkelanjutan nambah makna berjalan yang nggak perlu.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya: subjeknya bisa beneran ngelakuin kata kerja ini, atau cuma nerima? Kebijakan nggak bisa ngumumin, dia diumumin.
explanation.memoryCueId: Kebijakannya diumumin, bukan ngumumin: “to be announced”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pakai infinitive (to + kata kerja) bentuk pasif, yaitu to be + past participle, sesudah kata kerja harapan. Itu kepakai kalau subjeknya yang kena tindakan.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nahan bentuk to aktif sesudah “expected to”, padahal subjeknya penerima tindakan, bukan pelakunya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali subjeknya sebagai penerima tindakan → pilih bentuk to yang pasif

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Shift time and place deictic expressions (today, here) correctly when converting direct speech to reported speech at a later time/different place
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner backshifts the verb tense correctly but forgets that time/place words like 'today' and 'here' must also change to match the new reporting context
templates.reasoningOperation: detect deictic time/place word inside quoted speech -> convert to context-appropriate reported equivalent
templates.stem: On Monday, Maria said, 'I'll finish the report today.' A week later you report: Maria said she would finish it ___.

distractors.misconception: leaving the original deictic time word unchanged despite the shift in reporting time
distractors.whyFails: 'Today' only made sense on the actual Monday she spoke; a week later, 'today' would wrongly refer to the current day of reporting.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata itu cuma masuk akal di hari Senin waktu Maria ngomong.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata waktu aslinya dibiarin utuh padahal waktu pelaporannya udah beda.

distractors.misconception: misreading the original 'today' as if it referred to the day after speaking
distractors.whyFails: Maria said 'today', meaning the same day she was speaking (Monday), not the following day.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata aslinya “today”, artinya hari yang sama, bukan besoknya.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata “today” dibaca kayak nunjuk hari setelah dia ngomong.

distractors.misconception: producing an incomplete deictic shift missing the demonstrative
distractors.whyFails: 'The day' alone isn't a grammatical time reference here; the correct shifted form needs 'that day' to point back to the specific Monday.
distractors.whyFailsId: “the day” doang belum utuh, kata penunjuknya kelupaan.
distractors.misconceptionId: gesernya belum lengkap karena kata penunjuknya ilang.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'That day' correctly points back to the specific day (Monday) Maria was originally speaking about, from the later reporting viewpoint.
explanation.rule: In reported speech, deictic time/place words shift: today -> that day, here -> there, tomorrow -> the next day, yesterday -> the day before.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Today' and 'tomorrow' are anchored to the moment of the original speech and become inaccurate once time has passed; 'the day' is grammatically incomplete.
explanation.howToAvoid: Whenever you backshift a reported verb, also check every time/place word in the sentence for a matching shift.
explanation.memoryCue: Verb shifts back, and so does 'today' -> 'that day'.
explanation.ruleId: Di kalimat pelaporan, kata waktu dan tempat ikut geser: “today” jadi “that day”, “here” jadi “there”, “tomorrow” jadi “the next day”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “That day” nunjuk balik ke hari yang dimaksud Maria, yaitu Senin, dari sudut pandang sekarang.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Today” dan “tomorrow” keiket ke saat ucapan aslinya, jadi keliru begitu waktunya lewat. “The day” susunannya belum lengkap.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tiap kali mundurin kata kerja pelaporan, cek juga semua kata waktu dan tempatnya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Kata kerjanya mundur, “today” pun ikut geser jadi “that day”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Geser keterangan waktu dan tempat waktu ucapan langsung dilaporin di waktu atau tempat yang beda.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu udah bener mundurin kata kerjanya, tapi lupa kata kayak “today” dan “here” juga ikut geser.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temuin kata waktu atau tempat di dalam ucapan yang dikutip → ubah jadi padanan yang cocok

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Correctly report a first conditional sentence, applying backshift to both clauses consistently
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner either backshifts nothing in reported conditionals, or over-backshifts both clauses into third-conditional forms
templates.reasoningOperation: identify original conditional type -> apply correct backshift pattern for reported conditional speech
templates.stem: He said, 'If it rains, I'll cancel the picnic.' The picnic day has passed. He said that if it ___, he ___ the picnic.

distractors.misconception: leaving the first conditional entirely unbackshifted in reported speech
distractors.whyFails: 'Rains / will cancel' repeats the direct quote unchanged, ignoring that the reporting frame has moved the moment of speaking into the past.
distractors.whyFailsId: kutipan langsungnya diulang apa adanya, padahal momen bicaranya udah pindah ke masa lampau.
distractors.misconceptionId: first conditional dibiarin tanpa geseran sama sekali di kalimat pelaporan.

distractors.misconception: over-backshifting a first conditional into third-conditional (hypothetical past) forms
distractors.whyFails: The original was a real first conditional about the future, not a hypothetical past situation, so it shouldn't become 'had rained / would have cancelled'.
distractors.whyFailsId: aslinya syarat nyata soal masa depan, bukan pengandaian lampau yang mustahil.
distractors.misconceptionId: first conditional digeser berlebihan sampai jadi bentuk third conditional.

distractors.misconception: backshifting only the if-clause and leaving the result clause unshifted
distractors.whyFails: Both clauses of a reported first conditional typically backshift together; shifting only one creates an inconsistent tense pattern.
distractors.whyFailsId: kedua anak kalimatnya biasanya mundur bareng, jadi mundur separuh bikin tense-nya nggak selaras.
distractors.misconceptionId: cuma anak kalimat syaratnya yang digeser, anak kalimat hasilnya dibiarin.

explanation.whyCorrect: A reported first conditional shifts 'rains' to 'rained' and 'will cancel' to 'would cancel', preserving the same real-future-condition meaning one step back in time.
explanation.rule: Reported first conditional: if + present + will -> if + past simple + would, keeping the same logical relationship, just backshifted.
explanation.whyOthersFail: No backshift ignores standard reported-speech rules; full third-conditional backshift misrepresents a real condition as an impossible hypothetical; partial backshift breaks tense agreement between clauses.
explanation.howToAvoid: Backshift first conditionals one 'notch' in both clauses together: present->past, will->would.
explanation.memoryCue: First conditional reported = both clauses take one step back together.
explanation.ruleId: First conditional yang dilaporin: if + present + will jadi if + past simple + would. Hubungan maknanya sama, cuma mundur satu langkah.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Kata pelapornya “He said” udah lampau, jadi “rains” mundur jadi “rained” dan “will cancel” jadi “would cancel”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Tanpa geseran, aturan pelaporannya diabaikan. Geseran penuh sampai third conditional bikin syarat nyata jadi pengandaian mustahil, dan geseran separuh bikin tense-nya nggak selaras.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Geser first conditional satu tingkat di kedua anak kalimatnya sekaligus: present jadi past, will jadi would.
explanation.memoryCueId: First conditional yang dilaporin: kedua anak kalimatnya mundur bareng.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu ngelaporin kalimat first conditional dengan nggeser mundur tense di kedua anak kalimatnya sekaligus.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nggak nggeser apa pun di pengandaian yang dilaporin, atau malah nggeser dua-duanya sampai jadi third conditional.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali jenis pengandaian aslinya → terapkan pola geser mundur yang tepat buat pengandaian yang dilaporin

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'the' before superlatives and uniquely identifiable nouns, distinguishing them from ordinary first-mention nouns needing 'a/an'
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner applies 'a/an' to superlative or uniquely-identifiable nouns as if they were any ordinary first mention
templates.reasoningOperation: detect superlative form or unique-referent noun -> select definite article
templates.stem: Mount Everest is ___ tallest mountain in the world.

distractors.misconception: treating a superlative noun phrase as an ordinary indefinite first mention
distractors.whyFails: 'A' introduces one unspecified item among several, but the superlative 'tallest' singles out the only member of its category, which cannot be presented as merely one of many.
distractors.whyFailsId: “a” ngenalin gunungnya sebagai salah satu di antara banyak, jadi bentrok sama makna “tallest”.
distractors.misconceptionId: frasa bentuk “paling” diperlakukan kayak penyebutan pertama biasa.

distractors.misconception: same indefinite-article error as 'a', plus a vowel-sound trigger confusion
distractors.whyFails: 'An' goes wrong twice: it is an indefinite article, so it cannot single out the one member of a category, and it is chosen only by the following vowel sound rather than by what the phrase means.
distractors.whyFailsId: sama salahnya kayak “a”, ditambah salah timbang bunyi vokal.
distractors.misconceptionId: salah yang sama kayak “a”, plus bingung soal bunyi vokal.

distractors.misconception: assuming proper-noun-adjacent phrases never take an article
distractors.whyFails: Dropping the article treats 'tallest mountain' like a proper name, but it is an ordinary noun phrase whose uniqueness has to be marked; leaving it bare leaves that uniqueness unexpressed.
distractors.whyFailsId: ngosongin artikelnya bikin “tallest mountain” kebaca kayak nama diri, padahal dia frasa benda biasa.
distractors.misconceptionId: frasa di sebelah nama diri dikira nggak pernah pakai kata di depannya.

explanation.whyCorrect: Superlative adjectives point to one unique item in a category, so English marks them with 'the'.
explanation.rule: Use 'the' before superlative adjectives (the tallest, the best, the most famous) and other uniquely identifiable nouns.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'A/an' introduce one of several possible items, which contradicts the 'only one exists' meaning of a superlative; omitting the article isn't standard for superlative noun phrases.
explanation.howToAvoid: Whenever you see -est or 'most', expect 'the' right before it.
explanation.memoryCue: Superlative = there's only one, so it gets 'the'.
explanation.ruleId: Pakai “the” di depan bentuk “paling” (superlative) kayak the tallest atau the best. Benda yang cuma satu-satunya juga pakai “the”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Bentuk “paling” (superlative) nunjuk satu hal yang unik di kelompoknya. Bahasa Inggris nandain keunikan itu pakai “the”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “A” dan “an” nyodorin satu dari banyak kemungkinan. Ngosongin tempat itu juga bukan bentuk baku.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tiap lihat akhiran -est atau kata “most”, siapin “the” di depannya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Bentuk “paling” berarti cuma ada satu, jadi pakai “the”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “the” di depan bentuk “paling” (superlative). Pakai “the” juga buat benda yang cuma satu-satunya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai a atau an buat benda satu-satunya, kayak penyebutan pertama biasa.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali bentuk “paling” atau benda satu-satunya → pilih a, an, atau the

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Match demonstrative determiners to number (singular/plural) and physical/temporal distance (near/far)
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner matches demonstratives to distance but ignores number agreement, or vice versa
templates.reasoningOperation: identify noun number and distance cue -> select matching demonstrative
templates.stem: Can you pass me ___ books on the shelf over there?

distractors.misconception: using a singular near demonstrative with a plural, distant noun
distractors.whyFails: 'Books' is plural and 'over there' signals distance, but 'this' is singular and near.
distractors.whyFailsId: cuma buat satu benda yang letaknya dekat.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata penunjuk tunggal dekat dipakai buat benda banyak yang jauh.

distractors.misconception: correctly matching distance but ignoring plural agreement
distractors.whyFails: 'That' correctly signals distance but is singular, while 'books' requires a plural determiner.
distractors.whyFailsId: jaraknya udah pas, tapi cuma buat satu benda.
distractors.misconceptionId: jaraknya udah cocok tapi jumlahnya kelupaan.

distractors.misconception: correctly matching plural but ignoring the distance cue
distractors.whyFails: 'These' correctly matches the plural noun but wrongly signals nearness, contradicting 'over there'.
distractors.whyFailsId: jumlahnya udah pas, tapi nunjuk benda yang dekat.
distractors.misconceptionId: jumlahnya udah cocok tapi petunjuk jaraknya kelupaan.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Those' is plural and far, matching both the plural noun 'books' and the distance cue 'over there'.
explanation.rule: Demonstratives combine number and distance: this (singular/near), that (singular/far), these (plural/near), those (plural/far).
explanation.whyOthersFail: Each distractor matches only one of the two features (number or distance) correctly, not both.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check two things separately: is the noun singular or plural, and is it near or far?
explanation.memoryCue: Plural + far = 'those'.
explanation.ruleId: this buat satu benda dekat. that buat satu benda jauh. these buat banyak benda dekat. those buat banyak benda jauh.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Books” jumlahnya banyak. “Over there” bilang bendanya jauh. “Those” pas buat dua-duanya.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Pilihan lain cuma bener di satu hal: jumlahnya atau jaraknya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek dua hal: bendanya satu atau banyak? Dekat atau jauh?
explanation.memoryCueId: Banyak dan jauh: “those books over there”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Milih kata penunjuk sesuai jumlah bendanya dan jaraknya, dekat atau jauh
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu sering cuma cocokin jaraknya, jumlahnya kelupaan. Atau kebalikannya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek jumlah kata bendanya dan petunjuk jaraknya → pilih kata penunjuk yang pas

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Select the correct particle for a phrasal verb whose meaning changes entirely with a different particle
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner assumes any particle after a phrasal verb base is roughly interchangeable, ignoring that particle choice changes meaning completely
templates.reasoningOperation: match intended meaning (postpone) to the specific particle that produces that meaning with this verb
templates.stem: The meeting has been put ___ until next Thursday because two directors are traveling.

distractors.misconception: confusing 'put down' (to set something down / write something / criticize) with 'put off' (postpone)
distractors.whyFails: 'Put down' means to physically set something down, write it, or criticize someone — none of which fits 'until next Thursday'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “put down” berarti naruh, nulis, atau ngerendahin orang.
distractors.misconceptionId: “put down” dikira bisa dipakai buat nunda rapat.

distractors.misconception: confusing 'put up' (to erect / accommodate / tolerate) with 'put off' (postpone)
distractors.whyFails: 'Put up' means to build/display something or tolerate a situation, not to delay a meeting to a later date.
distractors.whyFailsId: “put up” berarti mendirikan, masang, atau nahan keadaan.
distractors.misconceptionId: “put up” dikira bisa dipakai buat nunda rapat.

distractors.misconception: confusing 'put away' (to store something) with 'put off' (postpone)
distractors.whyFails: 'Put away' means to store or tidy something, which doesn't match rescheduling a meeting to a future date.
distractors.whyFailsId: “put away” berarti nyimpen atau ngerapiin sesuatu.
distractors.misconceptionId: “put away” dikira bisa dipakai buat nunda rapat.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Put off' specifically means to postpone or delay something to a later time, matching 'until next Thursday'.
explanation.rule: Phrasal verb particles aren't interchangeable — the same base verb with a different particle can produce an unrelated meaning.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Each alternative particle creates a real phrasal verb, but with a completely different meaning that doesn't fit a rescheduled meeting.
explanation.howToAvoid: Learn phrasal verbs as whole units (put off = postpone), not as base verb + any particle.
explanation.memoryCue: 'Put off' a meeting = push it further off in time.
explanation.ruleId: Partikel di kata kerja gabungan (phrasal verb) nggak bisa gantian. Kata kerja yang sama plus partikel beda bisa bikin makna yang jauh.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Put off” khusus berarti nunda sesuatu ke waktu yang lebih belakangan, cocok sama “until next Thursday”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Tiap partikel lainnya memang bikin kata kerja gabungan yang sah. Tapi maknanya beda jauh dan nggak cocok buat rapat yang dijadwal ulang.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Hafalin kata kerja gabungan sebagai satu paket utuh, bukan kata kerja plus partikel apa saja.
explanation.memoryCueId: “Put off” sebuah rapat berarti ndorong jadwalnya lebih jauh ke depan.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pilih kata kecil di belakang kata kerja (partikel) yang bikin maknanya pas.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngira partikel di belakang kata kerja bisa gantian bebas. Padahal ganti partikel bisa ngubah maknanya total.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cocokin makna yang dimaksud, yaitu nunda → pilih partikel yang bikin makna itu

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Match a movement preposition to the shape of the path described (a tight enclosed opening vs. an open flat surface vs. a linear route)
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner treats all movement prepositions (through/across/along) as generally meaning 'in the direction of' without attending to the shape of the space being moved through
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the spatial shape implied by the noun (narrow gap/enclosed opening) -> select the movement preposition matching that shape
templates.stem: We squeezed ___ the narrow gap in the fence.

distractors.misconception: using the flat-open-surface preposition for an enclosed three-dimensional space
distractors.whyFails: 'Across' moves over an open flat expanse such as a road or a field; a narrow gap has no surface to cross.
distractors.whyFailsId: “across” nyeberangi bidang datar, celah nggak punya bidang.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata depan buat bidang datar dipakai di ruang tertutup.

distractors.misconception: using the linear-edge preposition (following a line such as a river or street) for movement inside an enclosed space
distractors.whyFails: 'Along' follows the length of something like a path or a river; squeezing 'along a gap' would mean travelling lengthwise inside it, not passing to the other side.
distractors.whyFailsId: “along” nyusuri panjangnya, bukan nembus ke sisi lain.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata depan buat nyusuri garis panjang dipakai di ruang tertutup.

distractors.misconception: using the above-and-across preposition for movement inside a space, not above it
distractors.whyFails: 'Over' would mean climbing above the fence, but the sentence describes using the gap in it.
distractors.whyFailsId: “over” lewat bagian atas pagar, bukan celahnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata depan buat lewat di atas dipakai buat gerak di dalam ruang.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Through' marks movement into one side of a tight enclosed opening and out the other, which is exactly what squeezing past a gap in a fence involves.
explanation.rule: Through = inside an enclosed space; across = a flat open surface; along = following the length of something; over = above and across.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Each alternative fits a different path shape (flat surface, linear edge, or overhead arc), not a tight enclosed opening like a gap in a fence.
explanation.howToAvoid: Picture the shape of the space: enclosed and three-dimensional signals 'through'.
explanation.memoryCue: A gap or opening has an inside — you squeeze 'through' it.
explanation.ruleId: “Through” nembus ruang tertutup. “Across” nyeberangi bidang datar terbuka. “Along” nyusuri panjangnya sesuatu. “Over” lewat di atasnya.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Celah pagar itu sempit dan tertutup, dimasuki dari satu sisi. “Through” nandain gerak masuk lalu keluar di sisi lain.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Pilihan lain cocok buat jalur lain: bidang datar, tepi panjang, atau bagian atas.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Bayangin bentuk ruangnya: tertutup dan ada bagian dalamnya berarti “through”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Celah punya bagian dalam, jadi ditembus pakai “through”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pasangin kata depan gerak sama bentuk jalurnya: ruang tertutup, bidang datar, atau jalur panjang.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngira through, across, dan along sama-sama berarti “ke arah”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: bayangin bentuk ruang dari kata bendanya → pilih kata depan geraknya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Distinguish 'try + gerund' (experiment with a method) from 'try + infinitive' (make an effort to do something difficult)
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner assumes 'try' always takes the same pattern regardless of whether the meaning is 'attempt something difficult' or 'experiment with an option'
templates.reasoningOperation: identify whether context implies difficulty-of-achievement or experimentation-with-a-method -> select matching verb pattern
templates.stem: If the file won't open, try ___ the computer — that usually fixes it.

distractors.misconception: using 'try to' (make a difficult effort) where 'try -ing' (experiment with a solution) is meant
distractors.whyFails: 'Try to restart' would suggest restarting itself is a difficult challenge, but the sentence is suggesting an easy solution to experiment with.
distractors.whyFailsId: “try to restart” nyiratin mulai ulang itu tantangan yang susah.
distractors.misconceptionId: “try to” yang berarti usaha keras dipakai padahal maksudnya nyoba satu cara.

distractors.misconception: using the bare infinitive after 'try', which isn't a valid pattern
distractors.whyFails: 'Try' requires either a gerund or a to-infinitive complement, never a bare base form.
distractors.whyFailsId: “try” minta pelengkap bentuk -ing atau bentuk to, nggak pernah bentuk dasar.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar dipakai sesudah “try” padahal itu bukan pola yang sah.

distractors.misconception: using a perfect gerund, implying the action is already completed
distractors.whyFails: The sentence is suggesting an action to try now, not referring back to something already done.
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimatnya nyaranin tindakan yang dicoba sekarang, bukan yang udah terlanjur.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing perfect dipakai jadi tindakannya seolah udah kelar.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Try restarting' means 'experiment with restarting as a possible solution', which matches the suggestion to fix the file problem.
explanation.rule: Try + gerund = experiment with an action as a possible solution; try + infinitive = make an effort at something difficult or challenging.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Try to restart' implies restarting is hard to accomplish; the bare form is ungrammatical after 'try'; the perfect gerund wrongly implies the action is already finished.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: is this framed as a possible fix to experiment with, or as a difficult task to accomplish?
explanation.memoryCue: Troubleshooting tip = 'try -ing'.
explanation.ruleId: “Try” + bentuk -ing berarti nyoba satu tindakan sebagai kemungkinan jalan keluar. “Try” + to berarti usaha ngelakuin sesuatu yang susah.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Try restarting” berarti nyoba mulai ulang sebagai kemungkinan jalan keluar. Itu pas sama saran buat berkas yang nggak mau kebuka.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Try to restart” nyiratin mulai ulangnya sendiri susah. Bentuk dasar nggak sah sesudah “try”, dan bentuk -ing perfect bilang tindakannya udah kelar.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya: ini disodorin sebagai jalan keluar yang dicoba, atau tugas susah yang harus diperjuangin?
explanation.memoryCueId: Saran ngatasi masalah pakai “try” + -ing.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu bedain “try” + gerund (bentuk -ing) yang berarti nyoba satu cara, dari “try” + to yang berarti usaha keras.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngira “try” selalu diikuti pola yang sama. Kamu nggak lihat maksudnya usaha keras atau nyoba satu cara.
templates.reasoningOperationId: tentuin konteksnya nyiratin kesulitan atau percobaan satu cara → pilih pola kata kerjanya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Complete a too/enough + adjective structure with the correct infinitive form and word order
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses a gerund after too/enough + adjective, or places 'enough' incorrectly relative to the adjective
templates.reasoningOperation: recognize too/enough + adjective structure -> complete with to-infinitive in correct word order
templates.stem: The coffee was too hot ___ right away, so she waited a few minutes.

distractors.misconception: using a gerund where the too/enough + adjective structure requires a to-infinitive
distractors.whyFails: 'Too + adjective' is completed by a to-infinitive, not a gerund, to express the result of the excessive degree.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk -ing nggak muat di pola tetap ini.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dipakai padahal polanya minta bentuk “to”.

distractors.misconception: inserting an unnecessary preposition before the verb form
distractors.whyFails: The too + adjective + to-infinitive pattern doesn't take 'for' before the verb; 'for' is only used before a noun/pronoun subject of the infinitive, not before the verb itself.
distractors.whyFailsId: “for” nggak boleh nempel langsung di depan kata kerjanya.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata depan disisipin tanpa perlu di depan bentuk kata kerjanya.

distractors.misconception: using the bare infinitive instead of the required to-infinitive
distractors.whyFails: The too/enough structure specifically requires 'to' before the base verb, not a bare infinitive.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk dasar telanjang belum lengkap buat pola tetap ini.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar telanjang dipakai di pola yang minta lebih dari itu.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Too hot to drink' uses the standard too + adjective + to-infinitive pattern to show a degree preventing an action.
explanation.rule: Too + adjective + (for someone) + to-infinitive expresses that something is excessively [adjective] to allow an action.
explanation.whyOthersFail: A gerund doesn't fit this fixed pattern; 'for drinking' misplaces a preposition meant only before a noun subject; the bare infinitive drops the required 'to'.
explanation.howToAvoid: Memorize the fixed frame: too + adjective + to + verb.
explanation.memoryCue: Too hot to drink — 'to' always follows 'too + adjective'.
explanation.ruleId: Pola “too” + kata sifat + bentuk “to” bilang kadarnya kelewatan. Akibatnya satu tindakan nggak bisa dilakukan. Kalau pelakunya perlu disebut, sisipin “for” + orangnya sebelum bentuk “to”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Too hot to drink” pakai pola baku “too” + kata sifat + bentuk “to”. Kadar panasnya bikin minum langsung nggak mungkin.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Bentuk -ing nggak muat di pola tetap ini. “For” cuma boleh berdiri di depan orangnya. Bentuk dasar telanjang kehilangan “to” yang diminta.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Hafalin kerangkanya apa adanya, ya: “too” + kata sifat + “to” + kata kerja.
explanation.memoryCueId: Habis “too” + kata sifat, selalu nyusul “to”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Lengkapi pola “too” atau “enough” + kata sifat pakai bentuk “to” dan urutan yang bener.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai bentuk -ing setelah “too” atau “enough” + kata sifat. Atau kamu salah naruh “enough”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali pola “too” atau “enough” + kata sifat → lengkapi pakai bentuk “to” dengan urutan yang bener

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Recognize the formal register pattern of fronting a preposition before 'whom/which' versus the informal pattern of stranding it at the clause end
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner assumes 'who' can follow a fronted preposition just like 'whom', not distinguishing subject/object relative pronoun forms in formal register
templates.reasoningOperation: detect formal register cue -> select the object relative pronoun compatible with a fronted preposition
templates.stem: This is the colleague ___ I was speaking earlier — a very formal way to phrase it.

distractors.misconception: using subject-form 'who' after a fronted preposition, which requires the object form
distractors.whyFails: A preposition placed immediately before the relative pronoun must be followed by the object form 'whom', not the subject form 'who'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “with who” masang bentuk pelaku “who” tepat di belakang kata depannya — kombinasi yang justru dilarang di gaya formal.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk subjek “who” dipakai sesudah kata depan yang dimajuin, padahal yang diminta bentuk objek.

distractors.misconception: reverses the preposition-pronoun order, putting 'with' directly after 'who' mid-clause
distractors.whyFails: 'Who with' flips the order, dropping the preposition directly after 'who' in mid-clause — 'the colleague who with I was speaking' — an order that is ungrammatical in any register, formal or informal.
distractors.whyFailsId: urutannya kebalik, “with” jatuh persis sesudah “who” di tengah kalimat, dan itu nggak sah.
distractors.misconceptionId: urutan kata depan dan kata gantinya kebalik jadi “with” jatuh persis sesudah “who” di tengah kalimat.

distractors.misconception: using the non-personal relative pronoun for a person
distractors.whyFails: 'Which' refers to things, not people; 'colleague' is a person and needs a personal relative pronoun.
distractors.whyFailsId: “which” nunjuk benda, sedangkan “colleague” itu orang yang minta kata penghubung buat orang.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata penghubung buat bukan orang dipakai buat orang.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'With whom' is the correct formal structure: preposition + object relative pronoun 'whom', used for people in formal register.
explanation.rule: In formal English, a fronted preposition must be followed by 'whom' (object form) for people, not 'who' (subject form); informal English instead strands the preposition at the clause end with 'who'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'With who' incorrectly pairs the fronted preposition with the subject-form pronoun; 'who with' reverses the preposition-pronoun order and is ungrammatical in any register; 'which' is for non-persons.
explanation.howToAvoid: Whenever a preposition comes directly before the relative pronoun, switch to 'whom' for people.
explanation.memoryCue: Preposition up front needs 'whom', not 'who'.
explanation.ruleId: Di Bahasa Inggris formal, kata depan yang dimajuin wajib diikuti “whom” buat orang, bukan “who”. Ragam santai malah naruh kata depannya di akhir bareng “who”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “With whom” itu susunan formal yang bener: kata depan diikuti bentuk objek “whom” buat orang.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “With who” masangin kata depan yang dimajuin sama bentuk subjek. “Who with” ngebalik urutannya jadi nggak sah di ragam mana pun, dan “which” buat bukan orang.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tiap kali kata depan berdiri persis di depan kata penghubung, ganti jadi “whom” buat orang.
explanation.memoryCueId: Kata depan di depan minta “whom”, bukan “who”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu ngenalin pola formal yang majuin kata depan di depan whom atau which. Pola santai malah naruh kata depannya di akhir anak kalimat.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngira “who” bisa nyusul kata depan yang dimajuin sama kayak “whom”, tanpa misahin bentuk subjek dan bentuk objek.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali tanda ragam formalnya → pilih kata penghubung bentuk objek yang cocok sama kata depan yang dimajuin

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Select 'fewer' for countable plural nouns and reserve 'less' for uncountable nouns
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses 'less' for all quantity comparisons regardless of whether the noun is countable or uncountable
templates.reasoningOperation: classify noun as countable or uncountable -> select matching quantity comparative
templates.stem: This recipe uses ___ eggs than the one my grandmother used to make.

distractors.misconception: applying the uncountable-noun comparative to a countable plural noun
distractors.whyFails: 'Eggs' is a countable plural noun, and standard usage reserves 'less' for uncountable nouns like 'less sugar' or 'less time'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “less” disediain buat benda yang nggak bisa dihitung satu-satu.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk perbandingan buat benda yang nggak bisa dihitung dipakai pada benda jamak.

distractors.misconception: using the base uncountable quantifier instead of its comparative form
distractors.whyFails: 'Little' isn't a comparative form at all here; it would need to be 'less' (still wrong for countables) or 'fewer' for a comparison with countables.
distractors.whyFailsId: “little” bukan bentuk perbandingan sama sekali.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata jumlah bentuk dasar dipakai menggantikan bentuk perbandingannya.

distractors.misconception: intensifying the wrong (uncountable) comparative rather than switching to the countable form
distractors.whyFails: Adding 'much' doesn't fix the underlying countability mismatch — 'eggs' still needs 'fewer', not any form of 'less'.
distractors.whyFailsId: nambah “much” nggak nyentuh salah pasang keterhitungannya.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk buat benda yang nggak bisa dihitung dikuatin, bukan diganti.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Fewer' is the correct comparative quantifier for countable plural nouns like 'eggs'.
explanation.rule: Fewer + countable plural nouns; less + uncountable nouns (though 'less' is increasingly common informally, standard/formal usage keeps the distinction).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Less', 'little', and 'much less' are all uncountable-noun forms, mismatched with the countable noun 'eggs'.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: can I count these one by one (one egg, two eggs)? If yes, use 'fewer'.
explanation.memoryCue: Countable eggs need 'fewer', not 'less'.
explanation.ruleId: “Fewer” buat benda jamak yang bisa dihitung satu-satu. “Less” buat benda yang nggak bisa dihitung satu-satu. Di percakapan santai “less” makin sering kedengeran, tapi pemakaian baku tetap bedain keduanya.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Eggs” itu benda jamak yang bisa dihitung satu-satu. Bentuk perbandingan jumlahnya “fewer”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Less”, “little”, dan “much less” semuanya bentuk buat benda yang nggak bisa dihitung satu-satu. Semuanya bentrok sama “eggs”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dulu: bendanya bisa dihitung satu-satu, satu telur terus dua telur?
explanation.memoryCueId: Telur bisa dihitung satu-satu, jadi pakai “fewer”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pilih “fewer” buat benda jamak yang bisa dihitung satu-satu. Sisain “less” buat yang nggak bisa dihitung satu-satu.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai “less” buat semua perbandingan jumlah. Kamu nggak cek bendanya bisa dihitung satu-satu atau nggak.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kelompokin bendanya bisa dihitung satu-satu atau nggak → pilih bentuk perbandingan jumlah yang cocok

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Recognize and avoid non-standard double negation in favor of a single negation with an indefinite pronoun
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner combines a negative verb with a negative pronoun ('didn't...nothing'), producing a non-standard double negative instead of standard single negation
templates.reasoningOperation: detect existing verb negation -> select the non-negative indefinite pronoun to avoid double negation
templates.stem: I looked everywhere, but I didn't find ___ in the drawer.

distractors.misconception: combining a negated verb ('didn't') with a negative pronoun, creating a non-standard double negative
distractors.whyFails: Standard English negates a clause only once; 'didn't find nothing' doubles the negation, which is non-standard.
distractors.whyFailsId: “nothing” nempelin negasi kedua ke kalimat yang kata kerjanya udah disangkal, jadi sangkalannya dobel.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja negatif digabung kata ganti negatif, jadi dobel.

distractors.misconception: using a positive indefinite pronoun that contradicts the negative context
distractors.whyFails: 'Something' implies a specific unnamed item exists and was found, which contradicts 'didn't find'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “something” bilang ada benda yang ketemu, padahal kalimatnya nyangkal.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti positif dipakai padahal konteksnya negatif.

distractors.misconception: incorrectly splitting the compound negative pronoun into two words
distractors.whyFails: 'Nothing' is one word functioning as a negative pronoun; splitting it into 'no thing' isn't standard and still creates double negation with 'didn't'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “nothing” itu satu kata, dipenggal jadi nggak baku.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti negatif yang satu kata dipenggal jadi dua.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Anything' is the non-negative indefinite pronoun that pairs correctly with an already-negated verb ('didn't').
explanation.rule: Standard English uses only one negation per clause: a negative verb pairs with 'any-' words (anything, anyone, anywhere), not 'no-' words.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Nothing' and 'no thing' both duplicate the negation already present in 'didn't'; 'something' wrongly implies a positive outcome.
explanation.howToAvoid: If the verb is already negative, switch any 'no-' word to its 'any-' equivalent.
explanation.memoryCue: One negative per clause: 'didn't...anything', never 'didn't...nothing'.
explanation.ruleId: Inggris baku cuma pakai satu kata negatif per kalimat. Kata kerja negatif dipasangin kata berawalan any, bukan berawalan no.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Anything” nggak bawa arti negatif sendiri. Jadi dia cocok dipasangin “didn’t” yang udah negatif.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Nothing” dan “no thing” bikin negatifnya dobel bareng “didn’t”. “Something” malah bilang ada yang ketemu.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau kata kerjanya udah negatif, ganti kata berawalan no jadi berawalan any.
explanation.memoryCueId: Satu kata negatif per kalimat: “didn’t ... anything”, bukan “didn’t ... nothing”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai cuma satu kata negatif dalam satu kalimat Inggris baku.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu gabung “didn’t” sama “nothing”, jadi negatifnya dobel.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek kata kerjanya udah negatif → pilih kata ganti yang nggak bawa negatif

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Select the correct short-agreement structure ('Neither do I') to agree with a negative statement
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses the positive agreement pattern 'So do I' to agree with a negative statement, instead of the negative pattern 'Neither/Nor do I'
templates.reasoningOperation: detect polarity of the statement being agreed with -> select matching agreement structure (so/neither)
templates.stem: A: 'I don't really enjoy horror movies.' B: '___ I. They give me nightmares.'

distractors.misconception: using the positive agreement structure to agree with a negative statement
distractors.whyFails: 'So do I' is used to agree with a positive statement; A's statement is negative ('don't enjoy'), so it needs the negative agreement form.
distractors.whyFailsId: “so do I” buat nyetujuin pernyataan positif.
distractors.misconceptionId: susunan persetujuan positif dipakai buat pernyataan negatif.

distractors.misconception: combining the wrong polarity structure with the wrong subject-verb agreement form
distractors.whyFails: Besides being the wrong polarity for a negative statement, 'does' doesn't agree with the subject 'I'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “does” nggak cocok sama subjek “I”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kutub susunannya keliru sekaligus kata bantunya nggak cocok sama subjeknya.

distractors.misconception: confusing 'either' (used with 'not...either' at the end of a clause) with the fronted 'neither' agreement structure
distractors.whyFails: 'Either' is used in patterns like 'I don't either', not in the fronted inverted structure that requires 'neither' at the start.
distractors.whyFailsId: “either” dipakai di pola “I don’t either”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “either” yang dipakai di akhir kalimat ketuker sama susunan yang dimajukan.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Neither do I' is the correct fronted structure to agree with a negative statement, matching A's 'don't enjoy'.
explanation.rule: So + auxiliary + subject agrees with a positive statement; Neither/Nor + auxiliary + subject agrees with a negative statement.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'So do' and 'So does' are positive-agreement forms mismatched with a negative statement; 'either' isn't used in this fronted inverted pattern.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check the polarity of the first speaker's verb: negative statement pairs with 'Neither/Nor', positive with 'So'.
explanation.memoryCue: Negative + negative agreement: 'don't' meets 'Neither do'.
explanation.ruleId: “So” + kata bantu + subjek nyetujuin pernyataan positif. “Neither” atau “Nor” + kata bantu + subjek nyetujuin pernyataan negatif.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Ucapan “A” negatif lewat “don’t enjoy”. Jadi persetujuannya juga harus bentuk negatif, yaitu “Neither do I”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “So do” dan “So does” itu bentuk persetujuan positif. “Does” juga nggak cocok sama subjek “I”. “Either” nggak dipakai di susunan yang dimajukan kayak gini.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek dulu, ya, kata kerja penutur pertama negatif atau positif.
explanation.memoryCueId: Ada “don’t”, berarti persetujuannya juga negatif.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pilih bentuk persetujuan singkat yang cocok buat nyetujuin pernyataan negatif.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai pola persetujuan positif “So do I” buat nyetujuin pernyataan negatif.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek pernyataannya positif atau negatif → pilih bentuk persetujuan yang sekutub

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Identify and correct a comma splice by joining two independent clauses with a coordinating conjunction
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner believes a comma alone is sufficient to join two complete independent clauses
templates.reasoningOperation: detect two independent clauses joined only by a comma -> select correction with proper conjunction/punctuation
templates.stem: Find and correct the error: "The rain didn't stop, we decided to cancel the picnic."
options: The rain didn't stop, so we decided to cancel the picnic.
The rain didn't stop, so we decide to cancel the picnic.
The rain didn't stop therefore, we decided to cancel the picnic.
The rain didn't stop, we therefore decided to cancel the picnic.

distractors.option: The rain didn't stop, so we decide to cancel the picnic.
distractors.misconception: tense inconsistency after a past event
distractors.whyFails: Decide is present tense, but the sentence describes a completed past decision, so decided is required.
distractors.whyFailsId: “decide” masih bentuk present buat keputusan yang udah lewat.
distractors.misconceptionId: tense jadi nggak selaras sesudah kejadian yang udah lampau.

distractors.option: The rain didn't stop therefore, we decided to cancel the picnic.
distractors.misconception: misplacing therefore between independent clauses
distractors.whyFails: Therefore cannot be inserted in this position with only a comma to join the two independent clauses.
distractors.whyFailsId: “therefore” di posisi itu nggak sah tanda bacanya.
distractors.misconceptionId: “therefore” ditaruh di antara dua kalimat utuh dengan cara yang keliru.

distractors.option: The rain didn't stop, we therefore decided to cancel the picnic.
distractors.misconception: keeping the comma splice while adding an adverb
distractors.whyFails: Therefore does not repair the comma splice; the two independent clauses are still joined by a comma alone.
distractors.whyFailsId: nambah kata keterangan nggak nyembuhin sambungan komanya.
distractors.misconceptionId: sambungan komanya dibiarin dan cuma ditambahin kata keterangan.

explanation.whyCorrect: Adding the coordinating conjunction 'so' after the comma properly joins the two independent clauses and expresses the cause-effect relationship.
explanation.rule: Two independent clauses cannot be joined by a comma alone (a comma splice); use a coordinating conjunction after the comma, a semicolon, or split into two sentences.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Decide' slips into the present tense although the decision already happened; putting 'therefore' after 'stop' with only a comma is not valid punctuation; and adding 'therefore' inside the second clause still leaves the two full sentences joined by a comma alone.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check each side of a comma: if both sides could stand alone as a full sentence, you need more than just a comma to join them.
explanation.memoryCue: Comma alone can't join two full sentences — add 'so/and/but' or use a semicolon.
explanation.ruleId: Dua kalimat utuh nggak boleh disambung cuma pakai koma. Tambahin kata sambung setara sesudah komanya. Bisa juga pakai titik koma atau pisahin jadi dua kalimat.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Kata sambung setara “so” sesudah koma nyambungin dua kalimat utuh itu dengan bener. Hubungan sebab akibatnya jadi kebaca.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Decide” masih bentuk present, padahal keputusannya udah lewat. “Therefore” di posisi itu nggak sah tanda bacanya. Nambah kata keterangan juga nggak nyembuhin sambungan komanya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek dua sisi komanya: masing-masing bisa berdiri sendiri sebagai kalimat utuh?
explanation.memoryCueId: Koma sendirian nggak bisa nyambung dua kalimat utuh.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kenali dua kalimat utuh yang cuma disambung koma. Betulin pakai kata sambung setara.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngira koma sendirian udah cukup buat nyambung dua kalimat yang sama-sama utuh.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temukan dua kalimat utuh yang cuma disambung koma → pilih perbaikan pakai kata sambung atau tanda baca yang pas

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Distinguish 'affect' (verb, to influence) from 'effect' (noun, a result) in context
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner treats 'affect' and 'effect' as interchangeable spellings of the same word rather than distinct parts of speech
templates.reasoningOperation: identify grammatical role needed (verb vs noun) -> select the word matching that role
templates.stem: Find and correct the error: "The new policy will effect thousands of employees across the company."
options: The new policy will affect thousands of employees across the company.
The new policy will affects thousands of employees across the company.
The new policy will be effect thousands of employees across the company.
The new policy will affection thousands of employees across the company.

distractors.option: The new policy will affects thousands of employees across the company.
distractors.misconception: correctly swapping to 'affect' but adding an unneeded third-person -s after a modal verb
distractors.whyFails: After the modal 'will', verbs stay in their base form; 'affects' incorrectly adds the third-person singular ending.
distractors.whyFailsId: modal “will” nuntut kata kerja bentuk dasar tanpa akhiran -s.
distractors.misconceptionId: akhiran orang ketiga ditambahin padahal posisinya sesudah modal.

distractors.option: The new policy will be effect thousands of employees across the company.
distractors.misconception: keeping the noun 'effect' but inserting 'be' as if that fixes the part-of-speech mismatch
distractors.whyFails: Inserting 'be' doesn't turn the noun 'effect' into a working verb in this slot; the sentence still needs the verb 'affect'.
distractors.whyFailsId: nyisipin “be” nggak ngubah kata benda jadi kata kerja.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata benda dipertahanin dan disisipin “be” seolah itu nyelesaiin salah jenis katanya.

distractors.option: The new policy will affection thousands of employees across the company.
distractors.misconception: substituting an unrelated noun ('affection') that only superficially resembles the needed verb
distractors.whyFails: 'Affection' means fondness/love and is a noun, not a verb meaning 'to influence', so it doesn't fit the sentence's grammatical or semantic slot.
