distractors.misconception: applies a singular indefinite article to a plural noun
distractors.whyFails: 'A' can only introduce a singular countable noun, so it cannot stand before the plural 'animals' at all.
distractors.whyFailsId: “a” cuma buat kata benda tunggal, nggak bisa di depan “animals”.
distractors.misconceptionId: artikel tunggal dipasang di depan kata benda jamak.

distractors.misconception: applies a singular indefinite article to a plural noun and ignores that the noun is already specific
distractors.whyFails: 'An' is also a singular article, so it cannot precede the plural noun 'animals', identified or not.
distractors.whyFailsId: “an” juga artikel tunggal, nggak mungkin di depan kata jamak “animals”.
distractors.misconceptionId: artikel tunggal dipakai buat kata jamak yang malah udah jelas kelompoknya.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'The animals we saw there' refers to one specific, identifiable set of animals — the ones on that farm — so the plural noun needs the definite article.
explanation.rule: 'The' + plural noun = a specific group the listener can identify (often pinned down by a relative clause or shared context); zero article + plural noun = the category in general.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Zero article would turn the sentence into a claim about animals in general, clashing with 'we saw there'; 'a' and 'an' are singular articles that cannot precede a plural noun.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: can the reader point at exactly which ones I mean? If yes (a clause like 'we saw there' identifies them), use 'the'.
explanation.memoryCue: Identified set -> 'the'; whole category -> no article.
explanation.ruleId: “The” + kata benda jamak nunjuk kelompok tertentu yang bisa dikenali, sering dijelasin anak kalimat kayak “we saw there”. Kata jamak tanpa artikel bicara soal kategorinya secara umum.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “The animals we saw there” nunjuk satu kelompok hewan tertentu, yaitu yang ada di peternakan itu. Jadi kata jamaknya wajib pakai “the”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Tanpa artikel, kalimatnya jadi soal hewan secara umum, padahal ada “we saw there”. “A” dan “an” itu artikel tunggal yang nggak bisa berdiri di depan kata jamak.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dulu: pembaca bisa nunjuk persis yang mana yang kumaksud? Kalau bisa, pakai “the”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Kelompok yang udah jelas pakai “the”; kategori umum tanpa artikel.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pilih “the” di depan kata benda jamak yang udah jelas kelompoknya dari konteks kalimat.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu buang artikel di depan semua kata jamak, padahal kata jamak yang kelompoknya udah dikenali tetap butuh “the”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek konteksnya udah nunjuk kelompok yang mana atau belum → kalau udah jelas pakai “the”, kalau umum tanpa artikel

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use the gerund (-ing form) for a verb that follows a preposition in an adjective + preposition pattern
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner puts a to-infinitive or a bare verb directly after a preposition instead of switching to the gerund the preposition requires
templates.reasoningOperation: spot the preposition before the blank -> select the -ing form of the verb
templates.stem: My sister is really good at ___ with difficult customers without losing her temper.

distractors.misconception: inserts a to-infinitive right after the preposition 'at', treating every verb complement as needing 'to'
distractors.whyFails: After a preposition like 'at', a verb must take the -ing form; 'good at to deal' is never grammatical in English.
distractors.whyFailsId: “to deal” nyelipin bentuk tujuan pakai “to”, padahal “at” di depannya nggak bisa disusul “to” lagi.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk “to” ditaruh persis sesudah kata depan, seolah semua kata kerja butuh “to”.

distractors.misconception: leaves the verb in its bare form after a preposition
distractors.whyFails: A bare verb cannot follow a preposition; 'at' needs a noun-like form, and for verbs that noun-like form is the gerund 'dealing'.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata kerja telanjang nggak bisa nempel di belakang kata depan.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar dibiarin polos sesudah kata depan.

distractors.misconception: mixes 'to' with the gerund, assuming the -ing form still needs a 'to' in front of it
distractors.whyFails: In 'good at + verb', the preposition is 'at', not 'to' — adding 'to' before 'dealing' stacks two prepositions and breaks the fixed pattern.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata depannya udah “at”, nambah “to” malah numpuk dua kata depan.
distractors.misconceptionId: “to” ditempel di depan bentuk -ing padahal kata depannya udah ada.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Good at' ends in the preposition 'at', and any verb that follows a preposition must appear in the gerund: 'good at dealing with difficult customers'.
explanation.rule: Adjective + preposition (good at, interested in, tired of) + verb-ing; a verb after a preposition always takes the -ing form.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'To deal' puts an infinitive where a gerund is required; bare 'deal' cannot follow a preposition; 'to dealing' stacks an extra 'to' onto a pattern whose preposition is 'at'.
explanation.howToAvoid: Look at the word right before the blank: if it's a preposition (at, in, of, about), the verb must end in -ing.
explanation.memoryCue: Preposition + verb = verb-ing: good at dealing.
explanation.ruleId: Kata sifat + kata depan, kayak “good at”, “interested in”, atau “tired of”, disusul kata kerja bentuk -ing. Kata kerja sesudah kata depan selalu pakai -ing.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Good at” berakhir di kata depan “at”. Kata kerja sesudah kata depan wajib bentuk -ing, jadi “good at dealing” yang pas.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “To deal” naruh bentuk “to” di tempat yang minta -ing. “Deal” telanjang nggak bisa nempel di kata depan. “To dealing” numpuk “to” padahal kata depannya udah “at”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Lihat kata persis sebelum titik-titiknya. Kalau itu kata depan kayak “at”, “in”, “of”, atau “about”, kata kerjanya harus -ing.
explanation.memoryCueId: Kata depan ketemu kata kerja, hasilnya -ing: good at dealing.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai bentuk -ing buat kata kerja yang nyusul kata depan di pola kata sifat + kata depan.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu naruh bentuk “to” atau kata kerja telanjang persis sesudah kata depan, padahal kata depan minta bentuk -ing.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temuin kata depan sebelum titik-titiknya → pilih kata kerja bentuk -ing

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Recognize that among the advice modals only 'ought' combines with 'to' before the base verb
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner treats should, ought to, and had better as fully interchangeable in form, not noticing that only 'ought' is followed by 'to'
templates.reasoningOperation: spot the 'to' already in the sentence -> select the one advice modal whose pattern includes 'to'
templates.stem: That cough sounds bad — you ___ to see a doctor before it gets worse.

distractors.misconception: attaching 'to' to 'should' because 'ought to' has one, blending the two advice modals' patterns
distractors.whyFails: 'Should' is followed directly by the base verb — 'you should see', never 'you should to see' — so it cannot fill a slot that already has 'to' after it.
distractors.whyFailsId: “should” langsung disusul kata kerja dasar, nggak pernah pakai “to”.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola “ought to” dicampur ke “should”, jadi muncul “should to” yang nggak ada.

distractors.misconception: assuming 'had better' takes 'to' like 'ought to' does
distractors.whyFails: 'Had better' is followed by the bare verb ('you had better see'), so 'had better to see' breaks its fixed pattern.
distractors.whyFailsId: “had better” disusul kata kerja telanjang, tanpa “to”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “had better” dikira ikut bawa “to” kayak “ought to”.

distractors.misconception: using a bare-verb obligation modal in a slot built for the to-pattern
distractors.whyFails: 'Must' takes the bare verb ('you must see'), so it cannot precede 'to'; it also expresses obligation, stronger than friendly advice.
distractors.whyFailsId: “must” juga minta kata kerja telanjang, jadi nggak bisa ketemu “to”.
distractors.misconceptionId: modal kewajiban berpola kata kerja telanjang dipaksa masuk pola yang ada “to”-nya.

explanation.whyCorrect: The sentence already contains 'to see', and among the advice modals only 'ought' is built with 'to': 'you ought to see a doctor'.
explanation.rule: Ought + to + base verb; should / had better / must + bare base verb. Same advice meaning, different fixed patterns.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Should', 'had better', and 'must' are all followed directly by the bare verb, so each of them would produce an ungrammatical double marker before 'to see'.
explanation.howToAvoid: Before choosing the modal, check the words after the blank: if 'to' is already there, only 'ought' fits; if the verb is bare, use should/had better/must.
explanation.memoryCue: Ought never travels without 'to'.
explanation.ruleId: “Ought” + “to” + kata kerja dasar. “Should”, “had better”, dan “must” langsung disusul kata kerja telanjang. Makna sarannya mirip, tapi pola bakunya beda.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Kalimatnya udah punya “to see”. Dari semua modal saran, cuma “ought” yang polanya bawa “to”: “you ought to see a doctor”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Should”, “had better”, dan “must” semuanya langsung ketemu kata kerja telanjang. Kalau dipasang di sini, semuanya nabrak “to” yang udah ada.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Sebelum milih modal, lihat kata sesudah titik-titiknya. Ada “to”? Berarti cuma “ought” yang muat. Kata kerjanya telanjang? Pakai “should”, “had better”, atau “must”.
explanation.memoryCueId: “Ought” nggak pernah jalan tanpa “to”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kenali kalau di antara modal saran, cuma “ought” yang gandeng “to” sebelum kata kerja dasar.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nganggep “should”, “ought to”, dan “had better” bisa saling tukar bentuk, padahal cuma “ought” yang disusul “to”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat “to” yang udah ada di kalimat → pilih modal saran yang polanya memang bawa “to”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Choose 'will' for a confident prediction backed by explicit certainty markers instead of a speculation modal
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner hedges every future statement with may/might/could, even when the context states firm evidence and full certainty
templates.reasoningOperation: detect certainty markers in the context -> select the confident prediction modal over speculative ones
templates.stem: I've checked the timetable twice, so I'm completely sure: the last train ___ leave at 11:40.

distractors.misconception: hedging with a weak-possibility modal despite the speaker's stated full certainty
distractors.whyFails: 'Might' signals an unsure guess, which contradicts 'I've checked... twice' and 'I'm completely sure'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “might” bilang tebakan ragu, padahal penuturnya bilang yakin banget.
distractors.misconceptionId: modal kemungkinan lemah dipakai walau buktinya udah pasti.

distractors.misconception: presenting a verified scheduled fact as just one tentative possibility
distractors.whyFails: 'Could' offers the departure time as merely possible, but a double-checked timetable makes it a confident prediction, not a maybe.
distractors.whyFailsId: “could” nawarin jam itu sebagai kemungkinan doang, padahal jadwalnya udah dicek dua kali.
distractors.misconceptionId: fakta jadwal yang udah diverifikasi disajiin kayak kemungkinan belaka.

distractors.misconception: defaulting to a polite weak-possibility modal for any statement about the future
distractors.whyFails: 'May' expresses roughly 50/50 uncertainty, clashing with the explicit certainty markers in the sentence.
distractors.whyFailsId: “may” bilang setengah yakin setengah nggak, bentrok sama “completely sure”.
distractors.misconceptionId: semua kalimat masa depan otomatis dikasih modal kemungkinan lemah.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'I've checked... twice' and 'I'm completely sure' are strong certainty markers, so the confident prediction modal 'will' matches the speaker's stance.
explanation.rule: Will = confident prediction; may/might/could = weaker degrees of speculation. Match the modal to how sure the evidence makes the speaker.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Might', 'could', and 'may' all inject doubt that the sentence explicitly rules out with its double-checked evidence.
explanation.howToAvoid: Scan for certainty language ('I'm sure', 'definitely', verified facts): if it's there, don't hedge — use 'will'.
explanation.memoryCue: 'Completely sure' pairs with 'will', not with 'might'.
explanation.ruleId: “Will” buat ramalan yang yakin. “May”, “might”, dan “could” buat tingkat dugaan yang lebih lemah. Cocokin modalnya sama seyakin apa buktinya.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “I've checked ... twice” dan “I'm completely sure” itu tanda keyakinan yang kuat. Jadi modal ramalan yakin “will” yang pas.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Might”, “could”, dan “may” semuanya nyelipin keraguan. Padahal kalimatnya udah nutup keraguan itu lewat jadwal yang dicek dua kali.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cari kata-kata keyakinan kayak “I'm sure” atau fakta yang udah dicek. Kalau ada, jangan ragu-ragu — pakai “will”.
explanation.memoryCueId: “Completely sure” pasangannya “will”, bukan “might”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pilih “will” buat ramalan yakin yang didukung tanda kepastian, bukan modal dugaan.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngasih “may”, “might”, atau “could” ke semua kalimat masa depan, padahal konteksnya udah nyebut bukti pasti dan keyakinan penuh.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temuin tanda kepastian di konteksnya → pilih modal ramalan yang yakin, bukan yang menduga-duga

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Select the particle that gives 'turn' the intended meaning of reducing volume, distinguishing it from opposite or absolute particles
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner picks a familiar particle for 'turn' without checking that each particle produces a different meaning (increase, switch off, flip)
templates.reasoningOperation: match the intended meaning (lower the volume slightly) to the particle that produces exactly that meaning with 'turn'
templates.stem: The music is too loud for the baby — could you turn it ___ a little?

distractors.misconception: confusing 'turn up' (increase the volume) with 'turn down' (decrease it)
distractors.whyFails: 'Turn up' would make the music louder, the opposite of what a too-loud situation calls for.
distractors.whyFailsId: “turn up” malah ngegedein suaranya, kebalikan dari yang diminta.
distractors.misconceptionId: partikel penambah volume ketuker sama partikel pengurangnya.

distractors.misconception: confusing 'turn off' (switch off completely) with 'turn down' (reduce by a degree)
distractors.whyFails: 'Turn off' is absolute — the music stops entirely — which clashes with 'a little', a request for a small reduction.
distractors.whyFailsId: “turn off” matiin total, nggak cocok sama permintaan “a little”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “turn off” yang total dikira bisa dipakai buat ngecilin dikit.

distractors.misconception: confusing 'turn over' (flip something / change TV channel) with volume control
distractors.whyFails: 'Turn over' means to flip something to its other side or switch channels; it has nothing to do with loudness.
distractors.whyFailsId: “turn over” berarti ngebalik sesuatu atau ganti saluran.
distractors.misconceptionId: “turn over” dikira nyambung ke urusan keras-pelannya suara.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Turn down' means to reduce the volume or intensity by a degree, matching both 'too loud' and the gentle request 'a little'.
explanation.rule: With 'turn', each particle makes a different verb: turn down = reduce, turn up = increase, turn off = stop completely, turn over = flip.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Up' reverses the intended direction, 'off' is an all-or-nothing action that can't be done 'a little', and 'over' belongs to flipping, not volume.
explanation.howToAvoid: Learn each 'turn + particle' as its own vocabulary item, and check gradable clues like 'a little' — they rule out absolute particles like 'off'.
explanation.memoryCue: Too loud? Turn it down; 'a little' means not 'off'.
explanation.ruleId: Sama kata “turn”, tiap partikel bikin kata kerja yang beda: “turn down” ngecilin, “turn up” ngegedein, “turn off” matiin total, “turn over” ngebalik.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Turn down” berarti ngurangin volume sebagian. Itu cocok sama “too loud” sekaligus permintaan halus “a little”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Up” muter arah yang dimaksud. “Off” itu aksi total yang nggak bisa “a little”. “Over” urusannya ngebalik, bukan volume.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Hafalin tiap “turn + partikel” sebagai kosakata sendiri. Cek juga petunjuk bertingkat kayak “a little” — itu nyingkirin partikel total kayak “off”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Kegedean suaranya? “Turn it down”. Ada “a little”, berarti bukan “off”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pilih partikel yang bikin “turn” berarti ngecilin volume, dan bedain dari partikel yang maknanya kebalik atau total.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu asal pilih partikel yang akrab buat “turn” tanpa ngecek kalau tiap partikel bikin makna beda: ngegedein, matiin, atau ngebalik.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cocokin makna yang dimaksud, yaitu ngecilin suara dikit → pilih partikel yang bikin makna persis itu

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Place 'enough' after the adjective in the adjective + enough + to-infinitive pattern
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner puts 'enough' before the adjective (like 'too') or swaps in 'too', not seeing that 'enough' follows the adjective and means sufficiency, not excess
templates.reasoningOperation: identify sufficiency meaning -> place 'enough' after the adjective, before the to-infinitive
templates.stem: My little brother isn't ___ to watch that horror movie yet.

distractors.misconception: placing 'enough' before the adjective on the model of 'too + adjective'
distractors.whyFails: With adjectives, 'enough' comes after the word it modifies: 'old enough', never 'enough old'.
distractors.whyFailsId: sama kata sifat, “enough” selalu di belakang: “old enough”.
distractors.misconceptionId: posisi “enough” disamain kayak “too”, ditaruh di depan kata sifatnya.

distractors.misconception: confusing 'too' (excess above the limit) with 'enough' (reaching the required level)
distractors.whyFails: 'Too old' says he is above the age limit, but 'isn't ... yet' shows he is still below the required age — a sufficiency meaning that needs 'enough'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “too old” bilang umurnya kelewat, padahal “yet” nunjukin dia belum nyampe.
distractors.misconceptionId: makna kelebihan “too” ketuker sama makna kecukupan “enough”.

distractors.misconception: scrambling the word order and attaching 'too' after the adjective as if it worked like 'enough'
distractors.whyFails: 'Too' must come before the adjective it intensifies ('too old'); placed after it, the pattern collapses and no to-infinitive can follow.
distractors.whyFailsId: “too” wajib di depan kata sifatnya; ditaruh di belakang, polanya rusak.
distractors.misconceptionId: urutan katanya diacak — “too” ditempel di belakang kayak aturan “enough”.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Isn't old enough to watch' uses the adjective + enough + to-infinitive pattern: he hasn't yet reached the age the action requires.
explanation.rule: Adjective + enough + to-infinitive = sufficiency ('old enough to watch'); too + adjective + to-infinitive = excess. 'Enough' follows the adjective; 'too' precedes it.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Enough old' reverses the required order; 'too old' states excess when the sentence means insufficiency; 'old too' puts 'too' in a position it can never occupy.
explanation.howToAvoid: Remember the mirror rule: 'too' walks in front of the adjective, 'enough' walks behind it — then add 'to + verb'.
explanation.memoryCue: Old ENOUGH, but TOO young — 'enough' after, 'too' before.
explanation.ruleId: Kata sifat + “enough” + bentuk “to” berarti kecukupan: “old enough to watch”. “Too” + kata sifat + bentuk “to” berarti kelebihan. “Enough” di belakang kata sifat, “too” di depannya.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Isn't old enough to watch” pakai pola kata sifat + “enough” + bentuk “to”. Umurnya belum nyampe syarat buat nonton film itu.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Enough old” muter urutan yang baku. “Too old” bilang kelebihan padahal maksudnya belum cukup. “Old too” naruh “too” di posisi yang nggak pernah ada.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Ingat aturan cerminnya: “too” jalan di depan kata sifat, “enough” jalan di belakangnya. Habis itu baru “to” + kata kerja.
explanation.memoryCueId: “Old enough”, tapi “too young” — “enough” di belakang, “too” di depan.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Taruh “enough” di belakang kata sifat pada pola kata sifat + “enough” + bentuk “to”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu naruh “enough” di depan kata sifat kayak “too”, atau malah pakai “too” padahal maksudnya kecukupan, bukan kelebihan.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali makna kecukupannya → taruh “enough” di belakang kata sifat, sebelum bentuk “to”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Select 'less' for uncountable nouns and resist hypercorrecting to 'fewer' where the noun cannot be counted
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner overapplies the drilled 'fewer' rule to uncountable nouns, hypercorrecting 'less coffee' into 'fewer coffee'
templates.reasoningOperation: classify the noun as uncountable -> select 'less', not the countable comparative 'fewer'
templates.stem: The doctor told him to drink ___ coffee and get more sleep.

distractors.misconception: hypercorrecting: applying the countable comparative to an uncountable substance noun
distractors.whyFails: 'Coffee' as a substance is uncountable, and 'fewer' only pairs with countable plurals ('fewer cups of coffee'), so 'fewer coffee' is ungrammatical.
distractors.whyFailsId: “coffee” di sini zat yang nggak bisa dihitung satu-satu, jadi bukan pasangan “fewer”.
distractors.misconceptionId: aturan “fewer” yang dihafal malah dipaksain ke benda yang nggak bisa dihitung.

distractors.misconception: using the base countable quantifier instead of a comparative, and with the wrong noun type
distractors.whyFails: 'Few' is not a comparative form and only works with countable plurals; it fails on both counts before 'coffee'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “few” bukan bentuk perbandingan dan cuma buat benda jamak yang bisa dihitung.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata jumlah dasar buat benda terhitung dipakai menggantikan bentuk perbandingannya.

distractors.misconception: confusing 'lesser' (lower in importance or rank) with 'less' (smaller quantity)
distractors.whyFails: 'Lesser' compares importance or degree ('a lesser problem'), not the amount of a substance you drink.
distractors.whyFailsId: “lesser” buat mutu atau tingkat, kayak “a lesser problem”, bukan jumlah minuman.
distractors.misconceptionId: “lesser” yang soal tingkat kepentingan ketuker sama “less” yang soal jumlah.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Coffee' here is an uncountable substance, and the comparative quantifier for uncountable nouns is 'less': drink less coffee.
explanation.rule: Less + uncountable noun (less coffee, less time); fewer + countable plural (fewer cups, fewer eggs). Don't swap them in either direction.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Fewer' demands a countable plural; 'few' is neither comparative nor compatible with uncountables; 'lesser' compares rank or importance, not quantity of a substance.
explanation.howToAvoid: Test the noun: can you say 'one coffee, two coffees' in this meaning? Drinking the substance, you can't — so use 'less'.
explanation.memoryCue: Substance you pour = 'less'; things you count = 'fewer'.
explanation.ruleId: “Less” + benda yang nggak bisa dihitung satu-satu, kayak “less coffee” atau “less time”. “Fewer” + benda jamak terhitung, kayak “fewer cups”. Jangan ketuker dua arah.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Coffee” di sini zat yang nggak dihitung satu-satu. Bentuk perbandingan jumlah buat benda begitu ya “less”: drink less coffee.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Fewer” nuntut benda jamak terhitung. “Few” bukan bentuk perbandingan dan nggak cocok sama benda tak terhitung. “Lesser” bandingin tingkat, bukan jumlah zat.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Uji bendanya: bisa nggak bilang “satu kopi, dua kopi” dalam makna ini? Buat zat yang diminum, nggak bisa — jadi pakai “less”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Zat yang dituang pakai “less”; barang yang dihitung pakai “fewer”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pilih “less” buat benda yang nggak bisa dihitung satu-satu, dan jangan kebablasan pakai “fewer” di sana.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu kebablasan nerapin aturan “fewer” yang udah dihafal ke benda tak terhitung, jadi “less coffee” malah ditulis “fewer coffee”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: pastiin bendanya nggak bisa dihitung satu-satu → pilih “less”, bukan “fewer”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Echo the correct auxiliary ('So have I') when agreeing with a positive present-perfect statement
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner memorizes 'So do I' as a fixed chunk and uses 'do' for every agreement, instead of echoing the auxiliary actually used in the statement
templates.reasoningOperation: detect polarity and the auxiliary of the statement -> front 'so' + the same auxiliary + subject
templates.stem: A: 'I've already seen that film twice.' B: '___ I — it's brilliant.'

distractors.misconception: treating 'So do I' as a frozen chunk instead of matching the auxiliary of the original statement
distractors.whyFails: A's statement uses the present perfect ('I've seen'), so the agreement must reuse 'have', not the default 'do'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “So do” ngambil kata bantu “do”, padahal nggak ada “do” di ucapan “A” yang bisa diikutin.
distractors.misconceptionId: “So do I” dihafal mati, kata bantunya nggak dicocokin sama kalimat aslinya.

distractors.misconception: picking the right auxiliary but the wrong polarity for a positive statement
distractors.whyFails: 'Neither' agrees with negative statements; A's statement is positive ('I've already seen'), so it needs 'so', not 'neither'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “neither” buat nyetujuin kalimat negatif, padahal kalimat “A” positif.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantunya udah bener, tapi kutub persetujuannya kebalik.

distractors.misconception: echoing a form of 'be' although the original statement contains no 'be' at all
distractors.whyFails: The agreement must copy the auxiliary from the statement, and A used 'have', not 'am/is/are'.
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimat “A” nggak ada bentuk “be”-nya sama sekali, adanya “have”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu “be” dipakai padahal kalimat aslinya pakai “have”.

explanation.whyCorrect: A's statement is positive and uses the auxiliary 'have' ('I've seen'), so the agreement fronts the same auxiliary: 'So have I'.
explanation.rule: So/Neither + auxiliary + subject: the polarity follows the statement (so = positive, neither = negative) and the auxiliary must echo the one in the statement (have/do/be/modal).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'So do' echoes the wrong auxiliary; 'Neither have' flips the polarity of a positive statement; 'So am' borrows a 'be' form that never appeared.
explanation.howToAvoid: Underline the auxiliary in the first speaker's sentence and copy exactly that one after 'so' or 'neither'.
explanation.memoryCue: 'I've seen' echoes as 'So HAVE I' — copy the helper, don't default to 'do'.
explanation.ruleId: “So” atau “Neither” + kata bantu + subjek: kutubnya ngikutin kalimat asli (“so” positif, “neither” negatif), dan kata bantunya harus niru yang dipakai kalimat itu, entah “have”, “do”, “be”, atau modal.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Kalimat “A” positif dan pakai kata bantu “have” di “I've seen”. Jadi persetujuannya majuin kata bantu yang sama: “So have I”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “So do” niru kata bantu yang salah. “Neither have” muter kutub kalimat yang positif. “So am” minjem bentuk “be” yang nggak pernah muncul.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Garisbawahi kata bantu di kalimat penutur pertama, terus salin persis kata bantu itu di belakang “so” atau “neither”.
explanation.memoryCueId: “I've seen” dibalas “So HAVE I” — salin kata bantunya, jangan otomatis “do”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Balas kalimat positif berbentuk present perfect pakai kata bantu yang sama: “So have I”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngafalin “So do I” sebagai satu paket mati dan pakai “do” buat semua persetujuan, padahal kata bantunya harus niru kalimat aslinya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek kutub dan kata bantu kalimat aslinya → majuin “so” + kata bantu yang sama + subjek

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Select 'effect' (noun, a result) for a noun slot after a determiner and adjective, distinguishing it from the verb 'affect'
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner writes 'affect' in noun positions, not recognizing that a slot after 'the + adjective' demands the noun 'effect'
templates.reasoningOperation: identify that the slot after 'the long-term' needs a noun -> select the noun 'effect', not the verb 'affect'
templates.stem: Find and correct the error: "Scientists are still studying the long-term affects of the new medicine."
options: Scientists are still studying the long-term effects of the new medicine.
Scientists are still studying the long-term affect of the new medicine.
Scientists are still studying the long-term effections of the new medicine.
Scientists are still studying the long-term affecting of the new medicine.

distractors.option: Scientists are still studying the long-term affect of the new medicine.
distractors.misconception: removing only the plural -s while keeping the verb 'affect' in a slot that needs a noun
distractors.whyFails: Dropping the -s doesn't fix the real error: after 'the long-term', the sentence needs the noun 'effect(s)', and 'affect' remains a verb.
distractors.whyFailsId: ngilangin -s nggak nyembuhin salahnya; posisi itu tetap minta kata benda “effect”.
distractors.misconceptionId: yang dibenerin cuma akhiran jamaknya, salah jenis katanya dibiarin.

distractors.option: Scientists are still studying the long-term effections of the new medicine.
distractors.misconception: inventing a fake noun by gluing a noun suffix onto 'effect'
distractors.whyFails: 'Effections' is not an English word; 'effect' is already the noun and simply takes a plural -s: 'effects'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “effections” bukan kata Bahasa Inggris; “effect” udah kata benda.
distractors.misconceptionId: akhiran pembentuk kata benda ditempel padahal katanya udah kata benda.

distractors.option: Scientists are still studying the long-term affecting of the new medicine.
distractors.misconception: using the -ing form as if it turned the verb 'affect' into the noun the slot requires
distractors.whyFails: 'The long-term affecting of...' is not idiomatic English; the established noun for a result is 'effect', so the slot takes 'effects'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “the long-term affecting of” nggak lazim; kata benda bakunya “effect”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dikira otomatis nyulap kata kerja jadi kata benda yang dibutuhin.

explanation.whyCorrect: The slot after 'the long-term' is a noun slot, and the noun meaning 'result' is 'effect' — plural 'effects' fits 'of the new medicine'.
explanation.rule: Effect (noun) = a result or outcome; affect (verb) = to influence. After a determiner + adjective ('the long-term ___'), only a noun can stand.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Affect' stays a verb whether or not it has -s; 'effections' is an invented word; 'affecting' is a verb form that doesn't become the required noun.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check the words before the gap: 'the' + adjective announces a noun, so pick 'effect(s)'; if the slot needs an action after a subject or modal, that's where 'affect' lives.
explanation.memoryCue: 'The ___' wants a noun — and the noun is Effect, with E.
explanation.ruleId: “Effect” itu kata benda yang berarti akibat. “Affect” itu kata kerja yang berarti memengaruhi. Sesudah “the” + kata sifat, cuma kata benda yang bisa berdiri.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Posisi sesudah “the long-term” itu posisi kata benda. Kata benda yang berarti akibat ya “effect”, dan bentuk jamaknya “effects” cocok sama “of the new medicine”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Affect” tetap kata kerja, ada -s atau nggak. “Effections” kata karangan yang nggak ada. “Affecting” bentuk kata kerja yang nggak berubah jadi kata benda yang diminta.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Lihat kata sebelum posisinya: “the” + kata sifat nandain kata benda, jadi pilih “effect(s)”. Kalau posisinya butuh tindakan sesudah subjek atau modal, di situ tempatnya “affect”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Habis “the” butuh kata benda — kata bendanya “effect”, pakai E.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pilih “effect” sebagai kata benda yang berarti akibat di posisi sesudah “the” + kata sifat, dan bedain dari kata kerja “affect”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nulis “affect” di posisi kata benda. Posisi sesudah “the long-term” cuma bisa diisi kata benda “effect”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: sadari posisi sesudah “the long-term” minta kata benda → pilih “effect”, bukan kata kerja “affect”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner chooses 'May I' over 'Can I' when making the most formal spoken permission request to a stranger.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners believe 'Can I' sounds just as formal as 'May I' when asking a stranger for permission.
templates.reasoningOperation: gauge the formality demanded by the listener and setting -> pick the permission modal that matches that register
templates.stem: You ask a stranger at the bank, in the most formal way: '___ I borrow your pen, please?'

distractors.misconception: treats 'can' as matching 'may' in formality when asking a stranger's permission
distractors.whyFails: 'Can I' is grammatically correct but conversational; the prompt explicitly asks for the most formal request to a stranger.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Can I” nggak salah, tapi kesannya santai, padahal yang diminta bentuk paling resmi ke orang asing.
distractors.misconceptionId: “can” dikira sama resminya dengan “may” waktu minta izin ke orang asing.

distractors.misconception: obligation read as formal permission
distractors.whyFails: 'Must I borrow your pen?' asks whether the speaker is obliged to borrow it, which is a question about duty, not a request for permission.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Must I” nanyain kewajiban, bukan minta izin.
distractors.misconceptionId: kewajiban ketuker sama izin yang resmi.

distractors.misconception: uses conditional 'would' with 'I' as if it formed a permission request
distractors.whyFails: Polite requests with 'would' need 'Would you...?'; 'Would I borrow...?' questions the speaker's own hypothetical behaviour instead of asking permission.
distractors.whyFailsId: Permintaan sopan pakai “Would you”, bukan “Would I”. “Would I” malah nanya perilaku diri sendiri.
distractors.misconceptionId: “would” + “I” dikira otomatis jadi kalimat minta izin.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'May I...?' is the conventional most formal way to request permission from a stranger, matching the polite tone of 'please' in the sentence.
explanation.rule: For permission requests, 'may' carries the highest formality; 'can' is neutral or conversational; 'could' sits in between. In formal settings with strangers, choose 'May I'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Can I' is conversational, not the most formal choice the prompt demands; 'Must I' asks about obligation; 'Would I' does not form a permission request at all.
explanation.howToAvoid: Picture the listener: a stranger or an official setting pushes you to 'May I'; a friend allows 'Can I'.
explanation.memoryCue: Stranger + please = May I.
explanation.ruleId: Buat minta izin, “may” itu bentuk paling resmi. “Can” lebih santai buat teman. Kalau situasinya resmi atau lawan bicaranya orang asing, pilih “May I”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “May I...?” itu cara paling resmi buat minta izin ke orang asing, cocok sama nada sopan “please” di kalimatnya.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Can I” terlalu santai buat permintaan paling resmi. “Must I” nanyain kewajiban. “Would I” malah bukan kalimat minta izin.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Bayangin lawan bicaranya dulu: orang asing atau situasi resmi berarti “May I”, teman dekat boleh “Can I”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Ketemu orang asing plus “please”? Pakai “May I”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pilih “May I”, bukan “Can I”, waktu minta izin paling resmi ke orang asing.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngira “Can I” sama resminya dengan “May I” waktu minta izin ke orang asing.
templates.reasoningOperationId: rasain seberapa resmi situasinya dan siapa lawan bicaranya → pilih kata bantu izin yang pas sama tingkat resminya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner places 'will' in the main clause when the sentence opens with a future time clause introduced by 'when'.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners extend the no-'will' rule of the time clause to the whole sentence and strip future marking from the main clause too.
templates.reasoningOperation: find the time clause -> keep it in present simple -> mark the future with 'will' in the main clause
templates.stem: When the meeting ends, I ___ you my notes straight away.

distractors.misconception: present simple used for a one-off future act
distractors.whyFails: The sending is a single future action in the main clause, so it needs 'will'; present simple belongs only inside the time clause after 'when'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “send” polos ninggalin janji kirimnya tanpa penanda nanti, padahal slot ini induk kalimat, bukan bagian “when”-nya.
distractors.misconceptionId: present simple dipakai buat satu kejadian nanti di induk kalimat.

distractors.misconception: uses past simple in the main clause for an event that is still in the future
distractors.whyFails: The meeting has not ended yet, so the sending cannot already be in the past; past simple clashes with the future timeline.
distractors.whyFailsId: Rapatnya aja belum selesai, jadi ngirimnya nggak mungkin udah lampau.
distractors.misconceptionId: kejadian yang masih nanti ditulis pakai bentuk lampau.

distractors.misconception: treats a real future sequence as hypothetical or future-in-the-past
distractors.whyFails: Nothing in the sentence sets up an unreal condition or a past reporting frame, so 'would' has no anchor here.
distractors.whyFailsId: Nggak ada pengandaian atau bingkai lampau di kalimat ini, jadi “would” nggak punya pijakan.
distractors.misconceptionId: rangkaian nanti yang nyata diperlakuin kayak pengandaian.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'When the meeting ends' is the future time clause (present simple), so the future marking 'will send' must sit in the main clause that follows.
explanation.rule: With future time clauses, the division of labour is fixed: present simple inside the when/as soon as clause, will + verb in the main clause.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Send' strips future marking from the sentence entirely; 'sent' pushes a future act into the past; 'would send' invents a hypothetical the sentence never sets up.
explanation.howToAvoid: Underline the two clauses: the one after 'when' stays present simple, and the other one carries 'will'.
explanation.memoryCue: Present after 'when', will in the main clause.
explanation.ruleId: Pembagian tugasnya tetap: anak kalimat setelah “when” atau “as soon as” pakai present simple, induk kalimatnya yang bawa “will”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “When the meeting ends” itu anak kalimat waktunya, udah present simple. Jadi tanda nanti “will send” harus ada di induk kalimatnya.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Send” bikin kalimatnya kehilangan tanda nanti sama sekali. “Sent” ngedorong kejadian nanti ke masa lampau. “Would send” bikin pengandaian yang nggak ada di kalimat.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Garisbawahi dua bagiannya: yang setelah “when” tetap present simple, bagian satunya yang bawa “will”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Setelah “when” present, “will”-nya di induk kalimat.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Taruh “will” di induk kalimat waktu kalimatnya dibuka anak kalimat waktu dengan “when”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngira larangan “will” di anak kalimat waktu berlaku buat seluruh kalimat, jadi induk kalimatnya ikut kehilangan “will”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temukan anak kalimat waktunya → biarin dia present simple → taruh “will” di induk kalimatnya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner builds the double genitive with a proper noun: indefinite article + noun + of + name's ('a cousin of Maria's').
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners drop the possessive 's after 'of' when the possessor is a name, or stack the article and the possessive in the wrong order.
templates.reasoningOperation: spot the introducing indefinite article -> keep 'of' -> put the name in possessive 's form
templates.stem: We ran into ____ at the market this morning, and she says hello.

distractors.misconception: drops the possessive 's after 'of' in the double genitive with a name
distractors.whyFails: In the double genitive the name after 'of' keeps its possessive form: 'a cousin of Maria's', parallel to 'a friend of mine', not the bare name.
distractors.whyFailsId: Di pola milik ganda, nama setelah “of” tetap pakai bentuk milik: “a cousin of Maria's”, sejajar sama “a friend of mine”, bukan nama polos.
distractors.misconceptionId: tanda milik 's setelah “of” dibuang, padahal polanya butuh itu.

distractors.misconception: stacks the indefinite article directly onto a name's possessive, marking the noun twice
distractors.whyFails: 'A' and 'Maria's' compete for the same determiner slot before 'cousin'; English allows only one of them, so they cannot be stacked.
distractors.whyFailsId: “A” dan “Maria's” rebutan satu tempat sebelum “cousin”. Bahasa Inggris cuma bolehin satu, jadi nggak bisa ditumpuk.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata sandang “a” ditumpuk langsung di depan nama bertanda milik.

distractors.misconception: drops the indefinite article that the double genitive pattern requires
distractors.whyFails: The double genitive needs a determiner in front of the noun; without 'a', the phrase 'cousin of Maria's' is left incomplete in this sentence.
distractors.whyFailsId: Pola milik ganda butuh kata sandang di depan kata bendanya. Tanpa “a”, frasa “cousin of Maria's” jadi nggak lengkap.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata sandang “a” yang dibutuhin polanya malah dibuang.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'A cousin of Maria's' follows the double genitive pattern exactly: indefinite article + noun + of + possessor in possessive form, introducing one of Maria's several cousins.
explanation.rule: Double genitive: a/an + noun + of + possessive form. With pronouns use mine/yours/hers; with names use the name + 's (a friend of Tom's).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'A cousin of Maria' loses the required 's; 'a Maria's cousin' stacks two determiners in one slot; 'cousin of Maria's' has no article at all.
explanation.howToAvoid: Test the phrase against the model 'a friend of mine': whatever follows 'of' must be a possessive form, and the phrase must start with a or an.
explanation.memoryCue: Of + name needs 's: a friend of Tom's.
explanation.ruleId: Pola milik ganda: a/an + kata benda + of + bentuk milik. Kalau ganti orangnya pakai kata ganti, bentuknya mine/yours/hers. Kalau pakai nama, namanya ditambah 's, contohnya “a friend of Tom's”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “A cousin of Maria's” persis ngikutin polanya: a + kata benda + of + nama bertanda milik. Artinya salah satu sepupunya Maria.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “A cousin of Maria” kehilangan 's yang wajib. “A Maria's cousin” numpuk dua penentu di satu tempat. “Cousin of Maria's” malah nggak punya kata sandang.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cocokkan sama model “a friend of mine”: yang setelah “of” harus bentuk milik, dan frasanya harus dibuka “a” atau “an”.
explanation.memoryCueId: “Of” + nama butuh 's: a friend of Tom's.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Bentuk milik ganda pakai nama orang: a + kata benda + of + nama dengan 's, contohnya “a cousin of Maria's”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu buang 's setelah “of” waktu pemiliknya nama orang, atau numpuk “a” langsung di depan nama bertanda milik.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat kata sandang “a” pembukanya → pertahanin “of” → ubah namanya jadi bentuk milik dengan 's

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner pairs an emotion adjective with 'about' when the cause is a situation or fact rather than a person or achievement.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners recycle 'with' from 'pleased with' after every emotion adjective, even ones that take 'about' before a situation.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify what follows the adjective: a situation or fact pairs with 'about', a person or achievement pairs with 'with'
templates.stem: He's been really worried ____ his final exam results all week.

distractors.misconception: transfers 'with' from 'pleased with' to an emotion adjective that needs 'about'
distractors.whyFails: 'Worried' points at a situation on the speaker's mind and collocates with 'about'; 'with' belongs to evaluating adjectives like 'pleased with' or 'satisfied with'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Worried” nunjuk situasi yang dipikirin dan pasangannya “about”. “With” itu punya kata sifat penilaian kayak “pleased with”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “with” dari “pleased with” dibawa ke kata sifat yang butuh “about”.

distractors.misconception: borrows 'at' from surprise adjectives such as 'surprised at'
distractors.whyFails: 'At' pairs with reaction adjectives like 'surprised at' or 'amazed at'; 'worried at' is not an English collocation.
distractors.whyFailsId: “At” pasangannya kata sifat kaget kayak “surprised at”. “Worried at” bukan pasangan yang ada di bahasa Inggris.
distractors.misconceptionId: “at” dari kata sifat kaget kayak “surprised at” dipinjam sembarangan.

distractors.misconception: uses 'for', the pattern for concern on someone's behalf, before a situation
distractors.whyFails: 'Worried for' introduces a person you feel concern on behalf of ('worried for his sister'), not a situation like exam results.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Worried for” buat orang yang kamu khawatirkan nasibnya, misalnya “worried for his sister”, bukan buat situasi kayak hasil ujian.
distractors.misconceptionId: “for” yang buat mengkhawatirkan orang dipakai buat situasi.

explanation.whyCorrect: Exam results are a situation occupying his mind, and 'worried' takes 'about' before situations and facts: worried about the results.
explanation.rule: Emotion adjectives choose their preposition by what follows: situations and facts take 'about' (worried/excited/happy about), while evaluated people, things, and results after adjectives like 'pleased' take 'with'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'With' belongs to evaluating adjectives like 'pleased with'; 'at' belongs to reaction adjectives like 'surprised at'; 'for' introduces a person you worry on behalf of, not a situation.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask what sits after the adjective: a situation in your head goes with 'about'; something you judge or measure goes with 'with'.
explanation.memoryCue: Worry about the situation, be pleased with the result.
explanation.ruleId: Kata depan setelah kata sifat emosi ngikut yang ada di belakangnya: situasi atau fakta pakai “about” (worried/excited/happy about), sedangkan hasil atau hal yang dinilai setelah kata kayak “pleased” pakai “with”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Hasil ujian itu situasi yang lagi dipikirin, dan “worried” pasangannya “about” kalau ngomongin situasi: worried about the results.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “With” punya kata sifat penilaian kayak “pleased with”. “At” punya kata sifat kaget kayak “surprised at”. “For” buat orang yang kamu khawatirkan, bukan situasi.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek yang duduk setelah kata sifatnya: situasi yang kepikiran pakai “about”, hal yang kamu nilai pakai “with”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Khawatir soal situasi pakai “about”, puas sama hasil pakai “with”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pasangkan kata sifat emosi sama “about” waktu penyebabnya situasi atau fakta, bukan orang atau hasil yang dinilai.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu bawa “with” dari “pleased with” ke semua kata sifat emosi, padahal sebagian butuh “about” sebelum situasi.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat yang ngikut setelah kata sifatnya: situasi atau fakta → “about”, orang atau hasil yang dinilai → “with”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner keeps the bare infinitive after causative 'make' in the active voice ('made the team run').
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners insert 'to' after 'make' by analogy with 'force someone to do something'.
templates.reasoningOperation: recognize active causative 'make' -> attach the bare infinitive with no 'to'
templates.stem: The coach made the whole team ____ an extra lap after training.

distractors.misconception: applies the to-infinitive pattern of 'force' to the causative 'make'
distractors.whyFails: 'Force' and 'order' take a to-infinitive, but active 'make' takes the bare infinitive: made the team run, not made the team to run.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Force” dan “order” memang pakai to-infinitive, tapi “make” aktif pakai bentuk dasar: made the team run, bukan made the team to run.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola “to” dari “force” dipindahin ke “make”, padahal “make” nggak pakai “to”.

distractors.misconception: Uses a gerund complement where a bare infinitive is required.
distractors.whyFails: After 'make + object' the second verb stays in the bare infinitive; the gerund 'running' does not fit this causative pattern.
distractors.whyFailsId: Setelah “make + objek”, kata kerja keduanya tetap bentuk dasar. Bentuk -ing nggak masuk pola ini.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dipakai, padahal polanya minta bentuk dasar.

distractors.misconception: makes the second verb carry past tense instead of staying in the bare infinitive
distractors.whyFails: Tense is already carried by 'made'; the verb after the object must stay in the bare infinitive, not repeat the past tense.
distractors.whyFailsId: Tanda lampaunya udah dibawa “made”. Kata kerja setelah objek harus tetap bentuk dasar, bukan ikut-ikutan lampau.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja keduanya ikut ditandai lampau, padahal cukup “made” yang bawa.

explanation.whyCorrect: Active causative 'make' takes object + bare infinitive, so 'made the whole team run' is the only well-formed choice.
explanation.rule: Make and let in the active voice take a bare infinitive: make/let + object + verb (no 'to', no -ing). Verbs like force, order, and allow take object + to-infinitive instead.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'To run' copies the pattern of 'force'; 'running' swaps in a gerund the pattern rejects; 'ran' doubles the past marking that 'made' already carries.
explanation.howToAvoid: When you see make or let, cover the first verb and check the second: it should look exactly like the dictionary form.
explanation.memoryCue: Make and let drop the 'to'.
explanation.ruleId: “Make” dan “let” di kalimat aktif pakai bentuk dasar: make/let + objek + kata kerja tanpa “to” dan tanpa -ing. Kata kayak force, order, dan allow yang pakai objek + to-infinitive.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Make” aktif polanya objek + bentuk dasar, jadi “made the whole team run” satu-satunya yang bentuknya benar.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “To run” niru pola “force”. “Running” masukin bentuk -ing yang ditolak polanya. “Ran” ngedobelin tanda lampau yang udah dibawa “made”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Ketemu “make” atau “let”? Tutup kata kerja pertamanya, terus cek yang kedua: harus persis bentuk kamusnya.
explanation.memoryCueId: “Make” dan “let” buang “to”-nya.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pertahanin bentuk dasar setelah “make” aktif: made the team run, tanpa “to”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nambahin “to” setelah “make” karena niru pola “force someone to do”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali “make” aktif sebagai kata kerja penyebab → sambungin bentuk dasar tanpa “to”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner selects past simple, not 'used to' or 'would', for a single dated past event.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners attach 'used to' or 'would' to one-off past events because the events feel distant, although both forms need a repeated habit.
templates.reasoningOperation: check the time marker -> one specific occasion means past simple, a repeated old habit allows used to or would
templates.stem: We ____ our grandmother in the hospital last Saturday afternoon.

distractors.misconception: treats the sentence as a habitual routine
distractors.whyFails: 'Last Saturday afternoon' pins the visit to one specific occasion, but 'used to' can only describe a repeated habit or long-lasting past state.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Last Saturday afternoon” ngunci kunjungannya ke satu kejadian, padahal “used to” cuma buat kebiasaan berulang atau keadaan lama.
distractors.misconceptionId: satu kejadian bertanggal dibaca kayak kebiasaan lama.

distractors.misconception: uses habitual 'would' for a single dated past event
distractors.whyFails: Habitual 'would' needs a series of repeated past actions; a visit fixed to one dated afternoon is a single event, so past simple is required.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Would” kebiasaan butuh rangkaian aksi yang berulang. Kunjungan yang kejadiannya cuma sekali di satu sore harus pakai past simple.
distractors.misconceptionId: “would” kebiasaan dipakai buat kejadian yang cuma sekali.

distractors.misconception: drops the -d of 'used to', copying the question and negative form into an affirmative sentence
distractors.whyFails: The bare 'use to' only appears after did/didn't; in an affirmative sentence the form would be 'used to', and even that meaning fails here.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Use to” polos cuma muncul setelah did/didn't. Di kalimat positif bentuknya “used to”, dan itu pun maknanya tetap salah di sini.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk “use to” dari kalimat tanya atau negatif dipindah ke kalimat positif.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Last Saturday afternoon' names one specific occasion, and single dated past events take past simple: we visited.
explanation.rule: Past simple reports single or dated past events. 'Used to' needs a repeated habit or long past state, and habitual 'would' needs repeated past actions; neither fits a one-off occasion.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Used to visit' and 'would visit' both claim repetition the date rules out, and 'use to visit' is a form that only exists after did or didn't.
explanation.howToAvoid: Look for a date or 'once/last...' marker: if the event happened one time, refuse 'used to' and 'would' automatically.
explanation.memoryCue: A date on it = plain past simple.
explanation.ruleId: Past simple buat kejadian lampau yang sekali atau bertanggal. “Used to” butuh kebiasaan berulang atau keadaan lama, dan “would” kebiasaan butuh aksi yang berulang. Dua-duanya nggak cocok buat kejadian sekali.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Last Saturday afternoon” nyebut satu kejadian tertentu, dan kejadian lampau bertanggal pakai past simple: we visited.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Used to visit” dan “would visit” sama-sama ngaku ada pengulangan, padahal tanggalnya nolak itu. “Use to visit” cuma ada setelah did atau didn't.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cari tanggal atau penanda kayak “once” dan “last...”: kalau kejadiannya sekali, langsung coret “used to” dan “would”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Ada tanggalnya, berarti past simple polos.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pilih past simple, bukan “used to” atau “would”, buat satu kejadian lampau yang bertanggal.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nempelin “used to” atau “would” ke kejadian sekali karena kejadiannya terasa lama, padahal dua bentuk itu butuh kebiasaan berulang.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek penanda waktunya → satu kejadian tertentu berarti past simple, kebiasaan lama yang berulang baru boleh used to atau would

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner uses the fixed phrase 'on foot' for walking, resisting the 'by + vehicle' pattern.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners extend 'by' from vehicles (by bus, by car) to walking and produce 'by foot' instead of the fixed phrase 'on foot'.
templates.reasoningOperation: check the transport noun: a vehicle pairs with 'by', but walking uses the fixed phrase 'on foot'
templates.stem: The lift was broken, so we climbed six floors ____ foot.

distractors.misconception: extends the 'by + vehicle' rule to the fixed phrase 'on foot'
distractors.whyFails: 'By' combines with vehicles (by bus, by taxi, by plane); walking is the one means of travel with its own fixed phrase, 'on foot'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “By” pasangannya kendaraan: by bus, by taxi, by plane. Jalan kaki satu-satunya yang punya frasa tetap sendiri, “on foot”.
distractors.misconceptionId: aturan “by + kendaraan” diseret ke frasa tetap “on foot”.

distractors.misconception: Treats modes of transport as tools/instruments requiring 'with'.
distractors.whyFails: 'With' introduces hand-held tools and instruments ('with a knife'); a means of travel like walking never takes 'with'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “With” buat alat yang dipegang, kayak “with a knife”. Cara bepergian kayak jalan kaki nggak pernah pakai “with”.
distractors.misconceptionId: cara bepergian diperlakuin kayak alat yang dipegang pakai “with”.

distractors.misconception: treats 'foot' as an enclosed space that takes 'in'
distractors.whyFails: 'In' marks being inside an enclosed space (in a taxi, in a box); 'foot' is not a space you can be inside, so 'in foot' is impossible.
distractors.whyFailsId: “In” nandain berada di dalam ruang tertutup, kayak “in a taxi”. “Foot” bukan ruang yang bisa dimasukin, jadi “in foot” mustahil.
distractors.misconceptionId: “foot” dianggap ruang tertutup yang bisa dipasangin “in”.

explanation.whyCorrect: Walking is expressed with the fixed collocation 'on foot', so 'we climbed all six floors on foot' is the only standard wording.
explanation.rule: Means of transport take 'by' + bare vehicle noun (by bus, by train), but walking uses the fixed phrase 'on foot'; 'with' is reserved for hand-held instruments.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'By foot' bends the vehicle pattern onto a phrase that is already fixed as 'on foot'; 'with' marks instruments; 'in' marks enclosed spaces.
explanation.howToAvoid: Memorize 'on foot' as a single vocabulary chunk instead of building it from the 'by' rule.
explanation.memoryCue: Feet go on the ground: on foot.
explanation.ruleId: Alat transportasi pakai “by” + nama kendaraannya: by bus, by train. Tapi jalan kaki pakai frasa tetap “on foot”. “With” khusus alat yang dipegang tangan.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Jalan kaki diungkapin pakai frasa tetap “on foot”, jadi “we climbed all six floors on foot” satu-satunya susunan yang baku.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “By foot” maksa pola kendaraan ke frasa yang udah tetap bentuknya. “With” buat alat pegangan. “In” buat ruang tertutup.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Hafalin “on foot” sebagai satu potongan kosakata utuh, jangan dirakit dari aturan “by”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Kaki napak di atas tanah: on foot.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai frasa tetap “on foot” buat jalan kaki, jangan kebawa pola “by + kendaraan”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu narik “by” dari kendaraan (by bus, by car) ke jalan kaki, jadinya “by foot”, padahal frasa tetapnya “on foot”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek kata transportasinya: kendaraan pasangannya “by”, jalan kaki pakai frasa tetap “on foot”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner selects 'in order to' + bare infinitive when the purpose shares the main clause subject.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners put 'so that' or 'for' directly before a bare infinitive, though that slot belongs to 'in order to' or 'so as to'.
templates.reasoningOperation: check whether the purpose has its own subject: no subject -> in order to + infinitive, own subject -> so that + full clause
templates.stem: He left home early ____ catch the first train to the airport.

distractors.misconception: uses the clause-purpose connector 'so that' before a bare infinitive with no subject of its own
distractors.whyFails: 'So that' must introduce a full clause with its own subject and verb ('so that he could catch...'); it cannot sit directly before the bare verb 'catch'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “So that” harus buka klausa utuh yang punya subjek dan kata kerja sendiri, misalnya “so that he could catch...”. Dia nggak bisa nempel langsung ke “catch”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “so that” yang butuh klausa utuh ditaruh langsung di depan kata kerja polos.

distractors.misconception: puts 'for' directly before a bare verb to express purpose, transferring Indonesian 'untuk'
distractors.whyFails: English does not allow 'for + bare verb' for purpose; 'for' takes a noun or gerund, and the infinitive slot here belongs to 'in order to' or plain 'to'.
distractors.whyFailsId: Bahasa Inggris nggak kenal “for + kata kerja polos” buat tujuan. “For” pasangannya kata benda atau bentuk -ing, dan tempat ini punya “in order to” atau “to”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “for” ditaruh di depan kata kerja polos, kebawa pola “untuk” dari bahasa Indonesia.

distractors.misconception: chooses 'in order that', which must introduce a full clause, before a bare verb
distractors.whyFails: 'In order that' is the formal clause version and needs a subject plus verb after it ('in order that he could...'); before the bare 'catch' it collapses.
distractors.whyFailsId: “In order that” itu versi klausanya dan butuh subjek plus kata kerja setelahnya, misalnya “in order that he could...”. Di depan “catch” polos dia rontok.
distractors.misconceptionId: “in order that” yang minta klausa utuh dipasang ke kata kerja polos.

explanation.whyCorrect: The purpose 'catch the first train' has no subject of its own — the catcher is the same 'he' — so the infinitive connector 'in order to' is the fit.
explanation.rule: Same subject in the purpose: use in order to / so as to / to + bare infinitive. Different or repeated subject: use so that / in order that + full clause, usually with a modal.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'So that' and 'in order that' both demand a full clause with its own subject, and 'for' can only be followed by a noun or gerund, never a bare verb.
explanation.howToAvoid: Look right after the gap: a bare verb calls for 'in order to' or 'to'; a new subject calls for 'so that'.
explanation.memoryCue: No new subject? In order to. New subject? So that.
explanation.ruleId: Kalau tujuannya sama subjeknya: pakai in order to / so as to / to + kata kerja dasar. Kalau tujuannya punya subjek sendiri: pakai so that atau in order that + klausa utuh, biasanya ditemenin kata bantu.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Tujuan “catch the first train” nggak punya subjek sendiri, yang ngejar tetap “he”. Jadi penghubung infinitif “in order to” yang pas.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “So that” dan “in order that” sama-sama nuntut klausa utuh bersubjek. “For” cuma bisa diikutin kata benda atau bentuk -ing, nggak pernah kata kerja polos.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Lirik yang persis setelah titik-titiknya: kata kerja polos manggil “in order to” atau “to”, subjek baru manggil “so that”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Nggak ada subjek baru? In order to. Ada subjek baru? So that.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pilih “in order to” + kata kerja dasar waktu tujuannya masih milik subjek yang sama.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu naruh “so that” atau “for” langsung di depan kata kerja polos, padahal tempat itu punya “in order to” atau “so as to”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek tujuannya punya subjek sendiri atau nggak: nggak ada → in order to + infinitif, ada → so that + klausa utuh

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner selects 'stop + gerund' to express quitting an activity for good.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners pick 'stop + to-infinitive' for quitting a habit, though that pattern means pausing in order to do something else.
templates.reasoningOperation: decide the intended meaning -> quitting the activity takes the gerund, pausing for a new purpose takes the to-infinitive
templates.stem: After the doctor's warning, he stopped ____ completely — he hasn't touched a cigarette since.

distractors.misconception: reads 'stop + to-infinitive' (pause in order to do something) into a quitting context
distractors.whyFails: 'Stopped to smoke' means he paused another activity in order to smoke, which directly contradicts 'he hasn't touched a cigarette since'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Stopped to smoke” artinya dia berhenti sebentar justru buat merokok. Itu bertabrakan langsung sama “he hasn't touched a cigarette since”.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola “stop + to” yang artinya jeda buat ngelakuin sesuatu dipakai buat konteks berhenti total.

distractors.misconception: uses a bare verb after 'stop', which takes a gerund or a to-infinitive, never the bare form
distractors.whyFails: 'Stop' never combines with a bare verb; its two patterns are stop + -ing (quit) and stop + to-infinitive (pause for a purpose).
distractors.whyFailsId: “Stop” nggak pernah ketemu kata kerja polos. Dua polanya cuma stop + -ing (berhenti total) dan stop + to (jeda buat tujuan).
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja polos ditempel ke “stop”, padahal pola itu nggak ada.

distractors.misconception: blends gerund and infinitive into 'to + -ing', a pattern 'stop' never takes
distractors.whyFails: 'To smoking' fuses the two real patterns into a hybrid that 'stop' does not allow; the quitting meaning needs the plain gerund 'smoking'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “To smoking” ngegabungin dua pola asli jadi bentuk campuran yang nggak dikenal “stop”. Makna berhenti total cukup pakai “smoking”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dan “to” dicampur jadi satu pola yang nggak pernah ada.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'He hasn't touched a cigarette since' shows the activity ended for good, and quitting an activity is expressed by stop + gerund: stopped smoking.
explanation.rule: Stop + gerund = the activity itself ends (quit). Stop + to-infinitive = you pause one activity in order to do another. The follow-up sentence decides which meaning is live.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'To smoke' flips the sentence into a smoking break; 'smoke' uses a bare form 'stop' never takes; 'to smoking' is a hybrid of the two patterns that exists in neither.
explanation.howToAvoid: Read past the verb: if the context says the habit is gone, lock in the gerund; if a new purpose appears, take the to-infinitive.
explanation.memoryCue: Quit the -ing, pause to do.
explanation.ruleId: Stop + bentuk -ing artinya kegiatannya sendiri yang disetop (berhenti total). Stop + to artinya jeda dari satu kegiatan buat ngelakuin yang lain. Kalimat lanjutannya yang nentuin makna mana yang hidup.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “He hasn't touched a cigarette since” nunjukin kegiatannya beneran tamat. Berhenti total dari kegiatan pakai stop + -ing: stopped smoking.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “To smoke” malah ngubah kalimatnya jadi jeda buat merokok. “Smoke” bentuk polos yang nggak pernah nempel ke “stop”. “To smoking” campuran dua pola yang nggak ada.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Baca sampai lewat kata kerjanya: kalau konteksnya bilang kebiasaannya hilang, kunci bentuk -ing. Kalau muncul tujuan baru, ambil “to”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Berhenti total pakai -ing, jeda pakai “to”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pilih stop + bentuk -ing buat bilang kegiatannya disetop total.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pilih “stop + to” buat berhenti dari kebiasaan, padahal pola itu artinya jeda buat ngelakuin hal lain.
templates.reasoningOperationId: tentuin dulu maknanya → berhenti total pakai bentuk -ing, jeda buat tujuan baru pakai “to”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner chooses 'which', never 'that', to open a comma-marked non-defining relative clause about a thing.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners put 'that' after a comma to add extra information, though 'that' can only open defining clauses.
templates.reasoningOperation: spot the commas signalling extra information -> select 'which' for a non-human antecedent
templates.stem: The Eiffel Tower, ____ was completed in 1889, still attracts millions of visitors every year.

distractors.misconception: using 'that' to add extra detail after a comma, though it only opens essential clauses
distractors.whyFails: 'That' is barred from non-defining clauses; between commas, extra information about a thing must be introduced by 'which'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “That” dilarang masuk klausa tambahan. Di antara koma, info ekstra tentang benda harus dibuka “which”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “that” dipakai setelah koma buat info tambahan, padahal dia cuma buat klausa inti.

distractors.misconception: using 'what' as a relative pronoun, though it cannot point back to an antecedent
distractors.whyFails: 'What' means 'the thing that' and never refers back to a stated noun like 'the Eiffel Tower', so it cannot open this clause.
distractors.whyFailsId: “What” artinya “hal yang” dan nggak pernah nunjuk balik ke kata benda yang udah disebut kayak “the Eiffel Tower”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “what” dipakai kayak kata penghubung, padahal dia nggak bisa nunjuk balik ke kata sebelumnya.

distractors.misconception: Uses a personal relative pronoun for a non-human antecedent.
distractors.whyFails: 'Who' refers only to people; the Eiffel Tower is a structure, so the non-defining clause needs 'which'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Who” cuma buat orang. Menara Eiffel itu bangunan, jadi klausa tambahannya butuh “which”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata penghubung buat orang dipakai buat benda.

explanation.whyCorrect: The commas mark the clause as extra, non-defining information about a thing, and that combination allows only 'which': The Eiffel Tower, which was completed in 1889, ...
explanation.rule: Non-defining relative clauses sit between commas and take which (things) or who (people); 'that' is restricted to defining clauses without commas.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'That' cannot follow the comma into a non-defining clause; 'what' never points back to a named noun; 'who' is reserved for human antecedents.
explanation.howToAvoid: Treat the comma as a gate: once a comma opens the clause, 'that' is locked out and things take 'which'.
explanation.memoryCue: Comma closes the door on 'that'.
explanation.ruleId: Klausa tambahan duduk di antara koma dan pakai which buat benda atau who buat orang. “That” cuma boleh di klausa inti yang tanpa koma.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Komanya nandain klausa itu info ekstra tentang benda, dan kombinasi itu cuma ngizinin “which”: The Eiffel Tower, which was completed in 1889, ...
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “That” nggak boleh ngikut koma masuk klausa tambahan. “What” nggak pernah nunjuk balik ke kata benda yang udah disebut. “Who” khusus orang.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Anggap komanya gerbang: begitu koma buka klausanya, “that” terkunci di luar dan benda pakai “which”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Ada koma, pintu buat “that” ketutup.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pilih “which”, jangan pernah “that”, buat buka klausa tambahan berkoma tentang benda.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu naruh “that” setelah koma buat nambahin info, padahal “that” cuma boleh buka klausa inti.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat koma penanda info tambahannya → pilih “which” karena yang dirujuk benda, bukan orang

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Select present perfect continuous when visible side effects and a duration phrase spotlight the unfinished activity itself, rather than present perfect simple for a completed tally
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner jumps to present perfect simple whenever a verb of producing something appears, even though the context shows the activity is unfinished and its side effects are still visible
templates.reasoningOperation: scan for side-effect evidence and a duration-up-to-now phrase -> choose continuous for an unfinished activity, simple for a finished tally
templates.stem: Her hands are covered in flour — she ___ bread all afternoon, and the first batch still isn't in the oven.

distractors.misconception: confusing in-progress with completed result
distractors.whyFails: 'Has baked' announces finished bread as the news, but the flour on her hands and the batch that still isn't in the oven show the baking itself is unfinished.
distractors.whyFailsId: “has baked” ngumumin roti yang udah jadi, padahal adonan pertamanya aja belum masuk oven.
distractors.misconceptionId: proses yang masih jalan ketuker sama hasil yang udah kelar.

distractors.misconception: choosing the present progressive for right now, though the span from 2019 needs a past-to-present link
distractors.whyFails: 'Is baking' only captures this very moment, while 'all afternoon' stretches from earlier today up to now and needs a perfect form to carry that link.
distractors.whyFailsId: “is baking” cuma motret detik ini, padahal “all afternoon” narik dari siang tadi sampai sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk lagi-berlangsung dipilih, padahal rentang waktunya nyambung dari tadi ke sekarang.

distractors.misconception: shifts to a fixed past narrative tense
distractors.whyFails: 'Baked' locks the activity inside a closed past frame, but her floury hands and the unfinished batch tie the sentence firmly to the present moment.
distractors.whyFailsId: “baked” ngunci kegiatannya di masa lalu yang udah tutup, padahal jejaknya masih keliatan sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: cerita pindah ke bentuk lampau yang waktunya udah dipatok.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'All afternoon' plus the visible side effects — floury hands, no batch in the oven yet — put the spotlight on the unfinished activity itself, which is exactly what present perfect continuous expresses.
explanation.rule: Present perfect continuous (has/have been + verb-ing) highlights the duration or side effects of an activity still in progress; present perfect simple highlights a finished result or tally.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Has baked' claims a finished product; 'is baking' cannot carry a span reaching back through the afternoon; 'baked' cuts the link to the present entirely.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check what the sentence points at: messy evidence of an activity still running takes the continuous; a counted, finished outcome takes the simple.
explanation.memoryCue: Flour on the hands, nothing finished yet = has been + -ing.
explanation.ruleId: Present perfect continuous pakai has atau have been + kata kerja -ing buat nyorot lamanya atau jejak kegiatan yang masih jalan. Present perfect simple buat hasil yang udah kelar.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “All afternoon” plus tepung di tangan dan roti yang belum masuk oven nunjukin kegiatannya sendiri yang disorot, bukan hasilnya. Jadi “has been baking” yang pas.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Has baked” ngaku rotinya udah jadi. “Is baking” nggak bisa bawa rentang dari siang tadi, dan “baked” mutusin hubungan sama saat ini.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Lihat kalimatnya nunjuk apa: jejak kegiatan yang masih jalan pakai continuous, hasil yang udah kehitung pakai simple.
explanation.memoryCueId: Tangan belepotan tepung dan belum ada yang jadi: pakai has been + -ing.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pilih present perfect continuous pas jejak kegiatan dan lamanya yang disorot. Bukan hitungan hasil yang udah kelar.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu buru-buru pakai present perfect simple tiap ada kata kerja bikin sesuatu. Padahal konteksnya bilang kegiatannya belum kelar dan jejaknya masih keliatan.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cari jejak kegiatan dan rentang waktu sampai sekarang → pilih continuous buat yang belum kelar, simple buat hasil yang kehitung

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use future perfect for an action that must already be complete at a 'by the time' reference point, instead of future continuous or a plain future form
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner reads 'by the time' as just another future time marker and picks a plain or continuous future form, losing the finished-before-that-point meaning
templates.reasoningOperation: find the 'by the time' anchor -> ask whether the action must already be complete at that anchor -> choose will have + past participle
templates.stem: By the time your plane lands, we ___ the final report, so you can read it on the drive from the airport.

distractors.misconception: picking the future continuous for an event the timeline treats as already delivered
distractors.whyFails: 'Will be finishing' leaves the report still in progress at landing time, which clashes with the promise that it can be read on the drive from the airport.
distractors.whyFailsId: “will be finishing” bikin laporannya masih setengah jalan pas pesawatnya mendarat, padahal janjinya udah bisa dibaca.
distractors.misconceptionId: future continuous dipilih buat kejadian yang di garis waktunya udah harus kelar.

distractors.misconception: Treats the sentence as a plain future prediction, ignoring the 'by the time' anchor.
distractors.whyFails: 'Will finish' only predicts a future action without marking it as complete before the landing, which is exactly what 'by the time' demands here.
distractors.whyFailsId: “will finish” cuma nebak kejadian nanti, nggak nandain kelarnya sebelum pesawat mendarat.
distractors.misconceptionId: kalimatnya dibaca kayak ramalan masa depan biasa, patokan “by the time”-nya kelewat.

distractors.misconception: drops the future marker entirely, defaulting to present simple
distractors.whyFails: 'Finish' is a bare present form; the main clause of this sentence needs a future form measured against the landing time.
distractors.whyFailsId: “finish” bentuk sekarang polos, padahal induk kalimatnya butuh bentuk masa depan.
distractors.misconceptionId: tanda masa depannya ilang sama sekali dan jatuh ke present simple.

explanation.whyCorrect: The landing is the future reference point, and the report must already be complete before it so it can be read straight away — that finished-before-then meaning is future perfect 'will have finished'.
explanation.rule: Future perfect (will have + past participle) marks an action as complete before a stated future point, often signalled by 'by the time' or 'by + time'; future continuous (will be + verb-ing) would leave it in progress at that point.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Will be finishing' keeps the work unfinished at landing; 'will finish' ignores the completion deadline set by 'by the time'; 'finish' has no future marking at all.
explanation.howToAvoid: When you see 'by the time' plus a future event, ask: must the action be done before that event? If yes, use will have + past participle.
explanation.memoryCue: 'By the time X happens' = will have + past participle.
explanation.ruleId: Future perfect “will have” + past participle (bentuk ke-3 kata kerja) nandain tindakan yang udah kelar sebelum satu titik nanti, biasanya ada “by the time” atau “by + waktu”. Future continuous “will be” + -ing malah bikin tindakannya masih jalan di titik itu.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Mendaratnya pesawat itu titik acuannya, dan laporannya harus udah kelar sebelum itu biar langsung bisa dibaca. Makna kelar-sebelum-titik itu punya “will have finished”.
