explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Will be finishing” bikin kerjaannya masih jalan pas mendarat. “Will finish” ngabaikan tenggat dari “by the time”, dan “finish” nggak punya tanda masa depan sama sekali.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Lihat “by the time” plus kejadian nanti, terus tanya: tindakannya harus kelar sebelum itu? Kalau iya, pakai will have + bentuk ke-3.
explanation.memoryCueId: Ada “by the time”, berarti will have + bentuk ke-3.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pakai future perfect buat tindakan yang harus udah kelar di titik “by the time”. Bukan future continuous atau bentuk masa depan polos.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu baca “by the time” kayak keterangan waktu nanti biasa. Makna udah-kelar-sebelum-titik-itu jadi ilang.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temuin patokan “by the time” → tanya tindakannya harus udah kelar di titik itu atau belum → pilih will have + bentuk ke-3

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Choose 'can't have' when the evidence confidently rules a past event out, resisting the pull of 'must have', 'needn't have', or a hedged 'might have'
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner reaches for 'must have' or a softer modal even though the eyewitness evidence clearly shows the past event did not happen
templates.reasoningOperation: check whether the evidence confirms or rules out the past event -> pick can't have for a confident negative conclusion
templates.stem: Anna ___ taken the 7:40 train — I stood on that platform the whole time and never saw her.

distractors.misconception: reverses the polarity of the evidence
distractors.whyFails: 'Must have' concludes that she DID take the train, but the witness who watched the platform the whole time proves the exact opposite.
distractors.whyFailsId: “must have” nyimpulin dia MEMANG naik kereta itu, padahal saksinya mbuktiin kebalikannya.
distractors.misconceptionId: arah buktinya kebalik pas ditarik jadi kesimpulan.

distractors.misconception: negative obligation confused with negative deduction
distractors.whyFails: 'Needn't have taken' says an action she really performed was unnecessary; it cannot deny that the event happened at all.
distractors.whyFailsId: “needn't have” bilang tindakan yang beneran dia lakuin itu nggak perlu, bukan nyangkal kejadiannya.
distractors.misconceptionId: kewajiban yang nggak perlu ketuker sama kesimpulan bahwa sesuatu nggak kejadian.

distractors.misconception: weakens certainty when the evidence actually supports a confident conclusion
distractors.whyFails: 'Might have' keeps the possibility open, but an eyewitness who watched the platform the whole time removes that doubt completely.
distractors.whyFailsId: “might have” masih buka kemungkinan, padahal saksi mata yang nungguin peron dari awal sampai akhir udah nutup keraguan itu.
distractors.misconceptionId: tingkat keyakinannya diturunin padahal buktinya tegas.

explanation.whyCorrect: Someone stood on the platform the whole time and never saw Anna, so the evidence confidently denies the past event — that is 'can't have + past participle'.
explanation.rule: 'Can't have + past participle' = confident conclusion that a past event did NOT happen; 'must have' = confident conclusion that it did; 'might have' = mere possibility; 'needn't have' = a real past action that turned out to be unnecessary.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Must have' flips the conclusion against the evidence; 'needn't have' talks about an unnecessary action that actually happened; 'might have' hedges where the eyewitness leaves no room for doubt.
explanation.howToAvoid: First decide what the evidence proves: confidently yes takes 'must have', confidently no takes 'can't have', and only genuine uncertainty takes 'might have'.
explanation.memoryCue: Evidence says impossible = can't have.
explanation.ruleId: “Can't have” + bentuk ke-3 berarti yakin sesuatu NGGAK kejadian. “Must have” berarti yakin kejadian, “might have” cuma kemungkinan, dan “needn't have” buat tindakan nyata yang ternyata nggak perlu.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Ada orang yang berdiri di peron dari awal sampai akhir dan nggak pernah lihat Anna. Buktinya nyangkal kejadiannya dengan yakin, jadi “can't have” yang pas.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Must have” mbalik kesimpulan lawan buktinya. “Needn't have” ngomongin tindakan nyata yang nggak perlu, dan “might have” masih ragu padahal saksinya nggak nyisain keraguan.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tentuin dulu buktinya mbuktiin apa: yakin iya pakai “must have”, yakin nggak pakai “can't have”, ragu beneran baru “might have”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Bukti bilang mustahil: pakai “can't have”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pilih “can't have” pas buktinya dengan yakin nyangkal kejadian lampau. Jangan kegoda “must have”, “needn't have”, atau “might have” yang ragu.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngambil “must have” atau modal yang lebih lembek, padahal saksi matanya jelas nunjukin kejadiannya nggak pernah terjadi.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek buktinya ngonfirmasi atau nyangkal kejadiannya → pilih “can't have” buat kesimpulan nggak yang yakin

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Form the get-passive correctly in a habitual present context, keeping the finite verb and its third-person agreement with 'everyone'
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner knows the get-passive exists but breaks it in a routine context, dropping the -s agreement, losing the finite verb, or sliding into past tense
templates.reasoningOperation: spot the routine time phrase -> keep the get-passive in present simple -> match the verb form to the singular subject
templates.stem: At this company everyone ___ paid on the last Friday of the month, so plan your budget around that date.

distractors.misconception: leaving the bare verb with no third-person marking after a singular subject
distractors.whyFails: 'Everyone' counts as third-person singular, so the routine present get-passive needs 'gets', not the bare form 'get'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “everyone” itu orang ketiga tunggal, jadi butuh “gets”, bukan “get” polos.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerjanya dibiarin polos tanpa akhiran -s padahal subjeknya tunggal.

distractors.misconception: Uses a bare gerund with no finite verb to carry the sentence's tense.
distractors.whyFails: 'Everyone being paid' leaves the sentence without a finite verb, so nothing carries the present-routine meaning of the statement.
distractors.whyFailsId: “everyone being paid” bikin kalimatnya nggak punya kata kerja utama yang bawa waktunya.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dibiarin sendirian tanpa kata kerja utama yang megang waktu kalimat.

distractors.misconception: shifts to a fixed past narrative tense
distractors.whyFails: 'Was paid' pushes the payday routine into a closed past, clashing with the present advice to plan a budget around that date.
distractors.whyFailsId: “was paid” ndorong rutinitas gajiannya ke masa lalu, padahal sarannya berlaku sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: kebiasaan yang masih jalan digeser ke bentuk lampau yang udah tutup.

explanation.whyCorrect: The routine phrase 'on the last Friday of the month' plus the present-day advice make this a current habit, and the singular subject 'everyone' takes the finite get-passive 'gets paid'.
explanation.rule: The get-passive is get + past participle; in routine present statements 'get' must be a finite present form that agrees with the subject: everyone/he/she gets paid, they get paid.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Get' misses the third-person -s after 'everyone'; 'being' leaves no finite verb at all; 'was' moves a living routine into the past.
explanation.howToAvoid: In a get-passive, check two things in order: is 'get' finite and in the right tense, and does it agree with the subject?
explanation.memoryCue: Routine + everyone = everyone gets + past participle.
explanation.ruleId: Pasif “get” itu get + past participle (bentuk ke-3 kata kerja). Di pernyataan rutin masa kini, “get”-nya harus bentuk present yang nyesuaiin subjek: everyone gets paid, they get paid.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “On the last Friday of the month” plus saran yang berlaku sekarang nandain ini kebiasaan yang masih jalan. Subjek “everyone” itu tunggal, jadi “gets paid” yang pas.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Get” kelupaan akhiran -s buat “everyone”. “Being” ninggalin kalimatnya tanpa kata kerja utama, dan “was” mindahin rutinitas yang masih hidup ke masa lalu.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Di pasif “get”, cek dua hal berurutan: “get”-nya udah bentuk dan waktu yang bener, dan udah cocok sama subjeknya?
explanation.memoryCueId: Rutinitas plus “everyone”: everyone gets + bentuk ke-3.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu bentuk pasif “get” dengan bener di kebiasaan masa kini. Kata kerjanya tetap ada dan cocok sama subjek tunggal “everyone”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu tahu pasif “get”, tapi bentuknya rusak di kalimat rutinitas: akhiran -s ilang, kata kerja utamanya ilang, atau kepleset ke bentuk lampau.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temuin keterangan rutinitasnya → tahan pasif “get” di present simple → cocokin bentuk kata kerjanya sama subjek tunggal

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Report a direct instruction with 'tell + object + to-infinitive', resisting patterns that borrow 'suggest' or an -ing form for a command
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner avoids the tell + object + to-infinitive frame when reporting a command, either forcing 'suggest' onto an instruction or attaching an -ing form after 'told'
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the speech act as a direct instruction -> pick 'told' -> apply the object + to-infinitive pattern
templates.stem: "Hand in the report by Friday," the manager said. -> The manager ___ in the report by Friday.

distractors.misconception: copies the object pattern of 'tell/ask' (verb + object) onto 'suggest', which doesn't take a direct personal object this way
distractors.whyFails: 'Suggest' never takes 'us + to-infinitive'; that object pattern belongs to 'tell' and 'ask', and the original words were a firm instruction anyway.
distractors.whyFailsId: “suggest” nggak pernah nerima “us” + bentuk to; pola objek itu punya “tell” dan “ask”.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola objek punya tell dan ask ditempelin ke “suggest”.

distractors.misconception: using the -ing form on its own, which describes an activity instead of telling someone to act
distractors.whyFails: 'Told us handing' is not a valid pattern; after 'tell + object', English needs a to-infinitive to pass the instruction on.
distractors.whyFailsId: “told us handing” bukan pola yang sah; habis “tell” + orang, harus bentuk to.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dipakai sendirian, jadi cuma nggambarin kegiatan, bukan nyuruh orang bertindak.

distractors.misconception: Uses an infinitive complement after 'admit', a verb that takes a gerund, not an infinitive.
distractors.whyFails: Like 'admit', the verb 'suggest' takes a gerund or a that-clause and never a to-infinitive — and 'suggested' would also soften a firm deadline into a mere idea.
distractors.whyFailsId: sama kayak “admit”, kata “suggest” minta bentuk -ing atau anak kalimat that, bukan bentuk to; lagian ucapan aslinya perintah, bukan usulan.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk to dipasang di belakang kata kerja yang maunya bentuk -ing.

explanation.whyCorrect: The original words are a direct instruction with a deadline, so the reporting verb is 'told', and 'tell' requires object + to-infinitive: told us to hand in.
explanation.rule: 'Tell/ask/order + object + to-infinitive' reports instructions and requests; 'suggest + -ing / that-clause' reports ideas, and it never takes 'someone + to-infinitive' or a bare to-infinitive.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Suggested us to hand' forces the tell/ask object pattern onto 'suggest'; 'told us handing' swaps the required to-infinitive for -ing; 'suggested to hand' pairs 'suggest' with a to-infinitive it never takes and downgrades a command to an idea.
explanation.howToAvoid: First label the speech act — command or idea? Then lock in that verb's own pattern: told + person + to + verb, but suggested + -ing.
explanation.memoryCue: A reported command = told + person + to + verb.
explanation.ruleId: “Tell”, “ask”, dan “order” + orang + bentuk to buat nglaporin perintah atau permintaan. “Suggest” + bentuk -ing atau anak kalimat that buat nglaporin usulan, dan nggak pernah “suggest orang + to”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Ucapan aslinya perintah langsung dengan tenggat, jadi kata pelapornya “told”. Habis “tell” wajib ada orangnya terus bentuk to: told us to hand in.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Suggested us to hand” maksa pola objek punya tell ke “suggest”. “Told us handing” nuker bentuk to yang wajib sama -ing, dan “suggested to hand” masangin “suggest” sama bentuk to yang nggak pernah dia terima.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kasih label dulu ucapannya: perintah atau usulan? Baru kunci pola kata kerjanya sendiri: told + orang + to + kata kerja, tapi suggested + bentuk -ing.
explanation.memoryCueId: Perintah yang dilaporin: told + orang + to + kata kerja.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu nglaporin perintah langsung pakai “tell” + orang + bentuk to. Jangan minjem “suggest” atau bentuk -ing buat perintah.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngehindarin pola tell + orang + bentuk to pas nglaporin perintah. Kamu malah maksa “suggest” buat perintah atau nempelin bentuk -ing habis “told”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali ucapannya sebagai perintah langsung → pilih “told” → pasang pola orang + bentuk to

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'was going to' for a stated past intention that was interrupted before it could be carried out, keeping the sentence anchored in past time
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner reports an interrupted past intention with plain 'would' or a present-anchored future form instead of 'was going to'
templates.reasoningOperation: spot the past intention plus the interruption -> choose was/were going to + verb
templates.stem: I ___ call you last night, but my phone died.

distractors.misconception: inserting 'would' for the speaker's own situation, as if the sentence were a result clause
distractors.whyFails: Plain 'would call' reads like the result clause of a conditional that never appears; a real plan from last night that got interrupted needs 'was going to call'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “would call” kebaca kayak anak kalimat pengandaian yang syaratnya nggak ada; niat nyata semalam butuh “was going to”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “would” diselipin seolah kalimatnya hasil pengandaian, padahal ini niat nyata.

distractors.misconception: using present-tense future modal inside a past narrative frame
distractors.whyFails: 'Will' points forward from the present moment, but 'last night' and the dead phone lock this story entirely in the past.
distractors.whyFailsId: “will” nunjuk ke depan dari saat ini, padahal “last night” ngunci ceritanya di masa lalu.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk masa depan yang berpijak masa kini dipakai di bingkai cerita lampau.

distractors.misconception: uses present-tense modal for a clearly past narrative
distractors.whyFails: 'Am going to' announces an intention held right now, which cannot combine with a plan that already failed last night.
distractors.whyFailsId: “am going to” ngumumin niat yang dipegang sekarang, nggak nyambung sama rencana yang udah gagal semalam.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk niat masa kini dipakai buat cerita yang jelas-jelas lampau.

explanation.whyCorrect: The speaker had a concrete intention last night that a dead phone interrupted, and a stated-then-blocked past plan is exactly what 'was going to + verb' reports.
explanation.rule: 'Was/were going to + verb' reports a past intention, typically one that was interrupted or abandoned before it happened; plain 'would' in this slot belongs to conditionals or repeated past habits, not a one-off blocked plan.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Would' turns the plan into a floating conditional result; 'will' and 'am going to' both anchor the intention in the present, breaking the 'last night' frame.
explanation.howToAvoid: When a past plan meets a 'but' that blocked it, reach for 'was going to', not 'would' or a present future form.
explanation.memoryCue: Failed plan in the past = was going to ... but ...
explanation.ruleId: “Was” atau “were going to” + kata kerja nglaporin niat di masa lalu, biasanya yang keburu batal atau kepotong. “Would” polos di posisi ini punya kalimat pengandaian atau kebiasaan lampau, bukan rencana sekali yang gagal.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Semalam penuturnya punya niat nyata yang kepotong gara-gara ponselnya mati. Rencana lampau yang keburu batal itu persis kerjaannya “was going to” + kata kerja.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Would” ngubah rencananya jadi hasil pengandaian yang ngambang. “Will” dan “am going to” sama-sama majak niatnya ke masa kini dan ngerusak bingkai “last night”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau ada rencana lampau yang ketemu “but” penghalangnya, ambil “was going to”, bukan “would” atau bentuk masa depan masa kini.
explanation.memoryCueId: Rencana gagal di masa lalu: was going to ... but ...

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pakai “was going to” buat niat lampau yang keburu kepotong sebelum sempat jalan. Kalimatnya tetap napak di masa lalu.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nglaporin niat lampau yang kepotong pakai “would” polos atau bentuk masa depan yang berpijak masa kini. Padahal slotnya punya “was going to”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temuin niat lampaunya plus penghalangnya → pilih was atau were going to + kata kerja

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use affirmative 'should have + past participle' to regret a helpful action that was never taken
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner picks the wrong polarity or wrong modal for a regret about an omission, negating 'should have' or drifting into deduction when the sentence mourns something left undone
templates.reasoningOperation: decide whether the criticized action was done or skipped -> for a skipped action pick affirmative should have + past participle
templates.stem: The client is angry — we ___ them about the delay, but we kept quiet.

distractors.misconception: Confuses missed opportunity with retrospective advice/criticism.
distractors.whyFails: 'Shouldn't have warned' criticizes an action that was actually performed, but 'we kept quiet' shows the warning never happened — the regret targets the omission.
distractors.whyFailsId: “shouldn't have warned” negur tindakan yang dilakuin, padahal “we kept quiet” nunjukin peringatannya nggak pernah ada.
distractors.misconceptionId: kesempatan yang kelewat ketuker sama teguran atas tindakan yang kejadian.

distractors.misconception: using present-form advice modal instead of past-regret structure
distractors.whyFails: 'Should warn' gives advice for now or the future, while this sentence judges, in hindsight, something the team failed to do back then.
distractors.whyFailsId: “should warn” ngasih saran buat sekarang atau nanti, padahal kalimatnya lagi nilai kegagalan yang udah lewat.
distractors.misconceptionId: modal nasihat bentuk present dipakai ganti susunan penyesalan lampau.

distractors.misconception: Confuses past deduction ('must have') with retrospective criticism.
distractors.whyFails: 'Must have warned' draws a confident conclusion that the warning did happen, which collides head-on with 'we kept quiet' — the sentence needs a judgement, not a deduction.
distractors.whyFailsId: “must have warned” nyimpulin peringatannya beneran kejadian, padahal “we kept quiet” bilang sebaliknya.
distractors.misconceptionId: kesimpulan dari bukti ketuker sama penyesalan atas yang seharusnya dilakuin.

explanation.whyCorrect: The team never warned the client ('we kept quiet'), and the sentence regrets that missed action, so it needs affirmative 'should have warned'.
explanation.rule: 'Should have + past participle' regrets a good action that was NOT done; 'shouldn't have + past participle' criticizes a bad action that WAS done; 'must have' belongs to deduction, not regret.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Shouldn't have warned' blames an action nobody performed; 'should warn' loses the hindsight; 'must have warned' turns a self-criticism into a deduction the context contradicts.
explanation.howToAvoid: First ask: did the action happen? If it was skipped and the speaker wishes it had happened, use plain 'should have + past participle'.
explanation.memoryCue: We kept quiet = the warning never happened = should have warned.
explanation.ruleId: “Should have” + bentuk ke-3 nyesalin kebaikan yang NGGAK jadi dilakuin. “Shouldn't have” + bentuk ke-3 negur tindakan keliru yang kejadian, dan “must have” buat nyimpulin, bukan nyesal.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Timnya nggak pernah ngasih peringatan, kan “we kept quiet”. Kalimatnya nyesalin tindakan yang kelewat itu, jadi butuh “should have warned” tanpa negatif.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Shouldn't have warned” nyalahin tindakan yang nggak pernah ada. “Should warn” kehilangan kacamata masa lalunya, dan “must have warned” ngubah penyesalan jadi kesimpulan yang bentrok sama konteksnya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dulu: tindakannya kejadian atau nggak? Kalau kelewat dan pengin banget udah dilakuin, pakai “should have” + bentuk ke-3 tanpa negatif.
explanation.memoryCueId: “We kept quiet” berarti peringatannya nggak pernah ada, jadi “should have warned”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pakai “should have” + bentuk ke-3 tanpa negatif buat nyesalin tindakan baik yang nggak jadi dilakuin.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu salah kutub atau salah modal buat nyesalin yang kelewat: “should have”-nya dinegatifin atau malah kepleset ke kesimpulan, padahal kalimatnya nyesalin yang nggak dilakuin.
templates.reasoningOperationId: tentuin tindakan yang disorot itu dilakuin atau kelewat → buat yang kelewat pilih “should have” + bentuk ke-3 tanpa negatif

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Keep past simple for equal forward-moving steps in a narrative chain instead of promoting one step to past perfect
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner sprinkles past perfect over ordinary sequential events, treating it as a fancy past tense rather than a flashback marker for earlier events
templates.reasoningOperation: check whether the event steps forward on the main storyline or jumps back before it -> keep past simple for forward steps
templates.stem: She unlocked the office at seven, ___ the windows, and then switched on the coffee machine.

distractors.misconception: tense-timeline mismatch
distractors.whyFails: 'Had opened' would yank the window-opening back to before the unlocking, but the sentence lists three equal steps moving forward in order.
distractors.whyFailsId: “had opened” narik buka-jendelanya ke sebelum pintu dibuka, padahal ini tiga langkah maju berurutan.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk waktunya nggak cocok sama garis waktu ceritanya.

distractors.misconception: Uses past continuous to describe a series of completed actions.
distractors.whyFails: 'Was opening' freezes the second step mid-action, while the chain 'unlocked ... and then switched on' presents every step as complete.
distractors.whyFailsId: “was opening” ngegantungin langkah keduanya di tengah jalan, padahal rangkaiannya nyeritain langkah-langkah yang tuntas.
distractors.misconceptionId: past continuous dipakai buat rangkaian tindakan yang udah tuntas.

distractors.misconception: Uses present perfect, mixing a present-relevance tense into a past narrative.
distractors.whyFails: 'Has opened' drags a present-linked tense into a story pinned to seven o'clock in the past by 'unlocked' and 'switched on'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “has opened” nyeret bentuk yang nempel ke masa kini ke cerita yang udah dipaku di jam tujuh pagi yang lampau.
distractors.misconceptionId: present perfect yang berorientasi masa kini nyelonong ke cerita lampau.

explanation.whyCorrect: Opening the windows is simply the second of three equal steps on the main storyline, and forward-moving narrative steps stay in past simple: unlocked, opened, switched on.
explanation.rule: In a narrative chain, past simple carries each forward step in order; past perfect is reserved for an event that happened before the storyline's current point.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Had opened' fakes a flashback that isn't there; 'was opening' leaves a finished step hanging mid-action; 'has opened' breaks the past frame with a present-linked tense.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask of each event: does it move the story forward, or did it happen before the story reached this point? Only the jump-back gets past perfect.
explanation.memoryCue: Steps in order = past simple; jump back = past perfect.
explanation.ruleId: Di rangkaian cerita, past simple bawa tiap langkah maju sesuai urutan. Past perfect disimpen buat kejadian yang lebih dulu dari titik cerita saat itu.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Buka jendela itu cuma langkah kedua dari tiga langkah setara di alur utama. Langkah maju di cerita tetap pakai past simple: unlocked, opened, switched on.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Had opened” malsuin kilas balik yang nggak ada. “Was opening” ngegantungin langkah yang udah tuntas, dan “has opened” ngerusak bingkai lampau pakai bentuk masa kini.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanyain tiap kejadian: dia majuin cerita, atau kejadian sebelum cerita nyampe titik ini? Cuma yang lompat mundur yang dapet past perfect.
explanation.memoryCueId: Langkah urut pakai past simple; lompatan mundur pakai past perfect.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu tahan past simple buat langkah-langkah setara yang maju berurutan di cerita. Jangan ada satu langkah yang dinaikin jadi past perfect.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu naburin past perfect ke kejadian berurutan biasa, dianggap bentuk lampau yang lebih keren. Padahal dia penanda kilas balik buat kejadian yang lebih dulu.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek kejadiannya maju di alur utama atau lompat ke sebelumnya → langkah maju tetap past simple

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Complete the get-causative frame by putting a past participle in the slot after the object
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner builds 'get + object' correctly but fills the final slot with an -ing, base, or finite past form instead of the required past participle
templates.reasoningOperation: recognize the arranged-service meaning -> lock the frame get + object + past participle -> fill the final slot with the participle
templates.stem: She got her passport photo ___ at the little studio near the station yesterday.

distractors.misconception: uses the -ing form instead of the past participle after 'get'
distractors.whyFails: 'Got her passport photo taking' breaks the causative frame; the -ing form would present the photo as the one doing the action instead of receiving it.
distractors.whyFailsId: “taking” bikin fotonya seolah yang motret, bukan yang dipotret.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dipakai di belakang “get” padahal slotnya minta bentuk ke-3.

distractors.misconception: uses the base form instead of the past participle in the causative structure
distractors.whyFails: The causative frame is get + object + past participle, so the bare form 'take' cannot fill the final slot of this arranged-service sentence.
distractors.whyFailsId: kerangka nyuruhnya get + benda + bentuk ke-3, jadi “take” polos nggak bisa ngisi slot terakhirnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar dipakai di susunan nyuruh yang minta bentuk ke-3.

distractors.misconception: past-tense confusion
distractors.whyFails: 'Took' is a finite past form; the slot after 'got her passport photo' is non-finite and only accepts the past participle 'taken'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “took” itu bentuk lampau berdiri sendiri, padahal slot habis “got her passport photo” cuma nerima bentuk ke-3 “taken”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk lampau biasa ketuker sama bentuk ke-3 yang diminta slotnya.

explanation.whyCorrect: She arranged for the studio to take the photo, so the causative frame get + object + past participle applies, and the final slot takes 'taken'.
explanation.rule: Causative with get: subject + get + object + past participle = arrange for someone else to perform a service; the verb after the object always stays a past participle, whatever the tense of 'get'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Taking' flips the photo into the doer; 'take' leaves the slot in the bare form; 'took' plants a second finite past verb where only a participle fits.
explanation.howToAvoid: Once you spot get/have + object as an arranged service, freeze the next verb as a past participle and let 'get' alone carry the tense.
explanation.memoryCue: Got + thing + V3: got her photo taken, got his hair cut.
explanation.ruleId: Pola nyuruh pakai get: subjek + get + benda + past participle (bentuk ke-3 kata kerja), artinya ngatur biar jasanya dikerjain orang lain. Kata kerja habis bendanya selalu bentuk ke-3, apa pun waktunya “get”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Dia yang ngatur biar studionya motret, jadi kerangka nyuruh get + benda + bentuk ke-3 berlaku. Slot terakhirnya diisi “taken”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Taking” mbalik fotonya jadi pelaku. “Take” ninggalin slotnya di bentuk dasar, dan “took” nanem kata kerja lampau kedua di tempat yang cuma muat bentuk ke-3.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Begitu ketemu get atau have + benda sebagai jasa yang diatur, bekuin kata kerja berikutnya jadi bentuk ke-3. Biar “get” aja yang bawa waktunya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Got + bendanya + bentuk ke-3: got her photo taken, got his hair cut.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu ngelengkapin kerangka nyuruh pakai “get” dengan naruh bentuk ke-3 di slot habis bendanya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu udah bener nyusun “get” + benda, tapi slot terakhirnya diisi bentuk -ing, bentuk dasar, atau bentuk lampau biasa. Padahal slot itu cuma nerima bentuk ke-3.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali makna jasa yang diatur → kunci kerangka get + benda + bentuk ke-3 → isi slot terakhirnya dengan bentuk ke-3

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Match a gerund subject with a singular third-person verb, even when plural nouns sit inside the subject phrase
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner lets a plural noun inside the gerund phrase, or the -ing form itself, derail the main verb instead of treating the whole gerund subject as one singular unit
templates.reasoningOperation: find the true head of the subject (the -ing form) -> treat the whole phrase as singular -> mark the verb with third-person -s
templates.stem: Taking short breaks between study sessions ___ your focus, according to the latest research.

distractors.misconception: missing subject-verb agreement / bare form
distractors.whyFails: The head of the subject is the singular gerund 'taking', not the plural nouns 'breaks' or 'sessions', so the verb needs third-person singular 'improves'.
distractors.whyFailsId: kepala subjeknya itu “taking” yang tunggal, bukan “breaks” atau “sessions” yang jamak, jadi kata kerjanya wajib “improves”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata benda jamak di dalam frasa subjek ngecoh kesesuaian kata kerjanya.

distractors.misconception: reduces the sentence to a fragment: an -ing form with no finite verb to carry the tense
distractors.whyFails: With 'improving' the sentence stacks two -ing forms and never gets a finite verb, so nothing carries the tense of the statement.
distractors.whyFailsId: pakai “improving”, kalimatnya numpuk dua bentuk -ing tanpa kata kerja utama yang megang waktunya.
distractors.misconceptionId: kalimatnya nyusut jadi potongan: bentuk -ing doang tanpa kata kerja utama.

distractors.misconception: Blends the infinitive marker 'to' with a gerund ending, producing an invalid hybrid.
distractors.whyFails: 'To improving' welds the infinitive marker onto an -ing ending — an invalid hybrid — and still leaves the sentence without a main verb.
distractors.whyFailsId: “to improving” ngelas penanda “to” ke akhiran -ing, bentuk campuran yang nggak sah, dan kalimatnya tetap tanpa kata kerja utama.
distractors.misconceptionId: penanda “to” dicampur akhiran -ing jadi bentuk gado-gado yang nggak sah.

explanation.whyCorrect: The whole gerund phrase 'Taking short breaks between study sessions' works as one singular subject, so the verb takes third-person singular 'improves'.
explanation.rule: A gerund phrase as subject is grammatically singular and takes a third-person singular verb, whatever plural nouns appear inside it; a formal infinitive subject ('To take short breaks...') behaves exactly the same way.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Improve' agrees with the nearby plural nouns instead of the gerund head; 'improving' and 'to improving' both leave the sentence without any finite verb.
explanation.howToAvoid: Strip the subject down to its head: if it starts with an -ing form, treat everything after it as decoration and give the verb its -s.
explanation.memoryCue: An -ing subject counts as one thing: Taking breaks improves.
explanation.ruleId: Frasa gerund (bentuk -ing) sebagai subjek dihitung tunggal dan minta kata kerja orang ketiga tunggal, berapa pun kata benda jamak di dalamnya. Subjek bentuk to yang formal (“To take short breaks...”) kelakuannya persis sama.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Seluruh frasa “Taking short breaks between study sessions” jalan sebagai satu subjek tunggal. Jadi kata kerjanya “improves” dengan akhiran -s.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Improve” malah nyesuaiin diri sama kata benda jamak di dekatnya, bukan sama kepala subjeknya. “Improving” dan “to improving” sama-sama ninggalin kalimat tanpa kata kerja utama.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kupas subjeknya sampai kepalanya: kalau mulainya bentuk -ing, anggap sisanya hiasan dan kasih kata kerjanya akhiran -s.
explanation.memoryCueId: Subjek bentuk -ing dihitung satu: Taking breaks improves.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu masangin subjek gerund (bentuk -ing) sama kata kerja tunggal orang ketiga. Kata benda jamak di dalam frasanya jangan sampai ngecoh.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu kegoda kata benda jamak di dalam frasa subjek, atau bingung sama bentuk -ing-nya sendiri. Padahal seluruh subjek gerund dihitung satu kesatuan tunggal.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temuin kepala subjeknya, yaitu bentuk -ing → hitung seluruh frasanya sebagai tunggal → kasih kata kerjanya akhiran -s

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner selects 'could have' for a neutral unused past possibility, resisting the pull of 'should have' when the context explicitly signals that no criticism is intended.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners default to 'should have' for any unrealized past action, adding blame even when the context marks the alternative as perfectly acceptable.
templates.reasoningOperation: Check the evaluative tone — 'either way was fine' signals no judgment -> mark the unused option neutrally with could have + past participle.
templates.stem: We took the bus to the airport, but we ____ a taxi — either way was fine.

distractors.misconception: Adds blame to a past alternative that the context explicitly marks as acceptable and neutral.
distractors.whyFails: 'Should have taken' criticizes the choice of the bus as a mistake, but 'either way was fine' states that nobody regrets or blames that choice.
distractors.whyFailsId: “should have taken” negur pilihan naik bus sebagai kesalahan, padahal “either way was fine” bilang nggak ada yang disesalin.
distractors.misconceptionId: teguran ditambahin ke pilihan lampau yang konteksnya jelas-jelas bilang sama-sama oke.

distractors.misconception: Confuses past deduction ('must have') with naming an unused past possibility.
distractors.whyFails: 'Must have taken' would deduce that they probably did take a taxi, which directly contradicts 'we took the bus'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “must have taken” nyimpulin mereka kemungkinan besar naik taksi, padahal kalimatnya bilang mereka naik bus.
distractors.misconceptionId: kesimpulan soal masa lalu ketuker sama nyebut peluang yang nggak kepakai.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'would have' as if this were a hypothetical conditional result rather than a plain unused possibility.
distractors.whyFails: 'Would have taken' needs a conditional partner such as an if-clause; this sentence names a real past option that simply was not used, not a hypothesis.
distractors.whyFailsId: “would have taken” butuh pasangan anak kalimat if; kalimat ini cuma nyebut pilihan nyata yang nggak kepakai.
distractors.misconceptionId: “would have” dipakai seolah ini hasil pengandaian, padahal cuma peluang yang nggak kepakai.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Could have taken' names the taxi as a real but unused past possibility, matching 'either way was fine', which rules out any blame.
explanation.rule: Could have + past participle = a past possibility that was not used, with no judgment; should have + past participle adds criticism or regret.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Should have' imports blame the context rejects, 'must have' expresses deduction that contradicts the facts, and 'would have' needs a conditional pairing.
explanation.howToAvoid: Before choosing, scan for blame: if the sentence says the outcome was fine, use could have, never should have.
explanation.memoryCue: No blame in the sentence? Reach for could have, not should have.
explanation.ruleId: Could have + bentuk ke-3 nyebut peluang masa lalu yang nggak kepakai, tanpa menghakimi. Should have + bentuk ke-3 nambahin teguran atau penyesalan.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Could have taken” nyebut taksi sebagai peluang nyata yang nggak kepakai. Itu cocok sama “either way was fine” yang nutup pintu buat nyalahin.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Should have” masukin teguran yang ditolak konteksnya, “must have” nyatain kesimpulan yang bentrok sama faktanya, dan “would have” minta pasangan pengandaian.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Sebelum milih, cek ada nada nyalahin atau nggak. Kalau kalimatnya bilang hasilnya baik-baik aja, pakai could have, jangan should have.
explanation.memoryCueId: Nggak ada yang disalahin? Berarti could have, bukan should have.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu milih “could have” buat peluang masa lalu yang nggak kepakai dan netral, walau godaannya milih “should have”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu otomatis pakai “should have” buat semua tindakan lampau yang nggak kejadian, padahal konteksnya bilang pilihannya sama-sama oke.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek nada penilaiannya — “either way was fine” berarti nggak ada yang disalahin → tandain peluang yang nggak kepakai itu dengan could have + bentuk ke-3

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner selects 'unless' (negative exception, 'except if') where the sentence states the single escape from a bad outcome, instead of the positive-condition connectors provided that / as long as.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners swap 'unless' with 'provided that' or 'as long as' without checking that 'unless' carries negative, 'except if' logic.
templates.reasoningOperation: Test the logic — the bad result happens in every case except if the condition holds -> choose unless, the negative-exception connector.
templates.stem: Hurry up! You'll miss the last train ____ you leave right now.

distractors.misconception: Uses a positive required-condition connector where a negative exception is meant.
distractors.whyFails: 'Provided that you leave right now' would absurdly make leaving immediately the condition FOR missing the train; the warning needs 'except if' logic instead.
distractors.whyFailsId: “provided that” malah bikin berangkat sekarang jadi syarat buat ketinggalan kereta — kebalikan dari maksud peringatannya.
distractors.misconceptionId: penghubung syarat positif dipakai padahal yang dimaksud kekecualian negatif.

distractors.misconception: Treats 'as long as' as interchangeable with 'unless', ignoring their opposite polarity.
distractors.whyFails: 'As long as' states a positive condition for the result to hold, so it would claim that leaving now guarantees missing the train — the reverse of the warning.
distractors.whyFailsId: “as long as” nyatain syarat positif, jadi kalimatnya malah bilang berangkat sekarang bikin ketinggalan kereta.
distractors.misconceptionId: “as long as” dianggap bisa gantiin “unless” tanpa ngecek arah positif-negatifnya.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'in case' (precaution for a possible future event) instead of the negative exception that blocks the outcome.
distractors.whyFails: 'In case' introduces a precaution taken beforehand against something that might happen, not the single exception that prevents missing the train.
distractors.whyFailsId: “in case” nyatain persiapan buat kemungkinan, bukan satu-satunya jalan keluar biar nggak ketinggalan kereta.
distractors.misconceptionId: “in case” yang nyatain kesiapsiagaan dipakai gantiin kekecualian negatif yang nyegah hasil buruknya.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Unless you leave right now' means 'except if you leave right now' — leaving immediately is the only escape from missing the train, which fits the urgent warning.
explanation.rule: Unless = negative exception ('except if'); provided that / as long as = positive required condition. They point in opposite logical directions.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Provided that' and 'as long as' reverse the logic into 'leaving now causes you to miss the train', and 'in case' expresses precaution, not an exception.
explanation.howToAvoid: Paraphrase the connector: if 'except if' keeps the sentence sensible, the answer is unless; if 'only if' fits, use provided that or as long as.
explanation.memoryCue: Unless = 'except if' — the one exit door from a bad result.
explanation.ruleId: Unless berarti kecuali kalau, alias kekecualian negatif. Provided that dan as long as nyatain syarat positif yang wajib dipenuhi. Arah logikanya berlawanan.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Unless you leave right now” berarti kecuali kalau kamu berangkat sekarang. Berangkat sekarang itu satu-satunya jalan biar nggak ketinggalan kereta, pas sama peringatannya.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Provided that” dan “as long as” mbalik logikanya jadi berangkat sekarang malah bikin ketinggalan. “In case” nyatain kesiapsiagaan, bukan kekecualian.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Coba parafrase: kalau “kecuali kalau” bikin kalimatnya masuk akal, jawabannya unless. Kalau “cuma kalau” yang pas, pakai provided that atau as long as.
explanation.memoryCueId: Unless = kecuali kalau — satu-satunya pintu keluar dari hasil buruk.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu milih “unless” sebagai kekecualian negatif yang jadi satu-satunya jalan keluar dari hasil buruk, bukan penghubung syarat positif.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nuker “unless” sama “provided that” atau “as long as” tanpa ngecek bahwa “unless” berarti kecuali kalau.
templates.reasoningOperationId: uji logikanya — hasil buruknya kejadian di semua kasus kecuali kalau syaratnya dipenuhi → pilih unless, penghubung kekecualian negatif

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner forms the passive of a ditransitive verb with the direct object (the thing given) as subject, restoring the preposition 'to' before the recipient.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners drop the required 'to' before the recipient when the thing given, not the receiver, becomes the passive subject.
templates.reasoningOperation: Identify which object is now the subject — the thing given -> keep be + past participle and reinsert to before the recipient.
templates.stem: The committee gave the young scientist an award. → An award ____ the young scientist.

distractors.misconception: Drops the preposition 'to' that must reintroduce the recipient when the direct object is the passive subject.
distractors.whyFails: With 'an award' as the subject, the recipient can no longer follow the verb bare; standard modern English requires 'was given to the young scientist'.
distractors.whyFailsId: begitu “an award” jadi subjek, penerimanya nggak boleh nempel langsung; wajib disambung pakai “to”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata depan “to” yang wajib ngenalin penerimanya dibuang waktu benda yang dikasih jadi subjek pasif.

distractors.misconception: Fails subject-verb agreement, treating the singular subject 'an award' as plural.
distractors.whyFails: 'An award' is singular, so the passive auxiliary must be the singular 'was', not the plural 'were'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “an award” bentuknya tunggal, jadi kata bantunya harus “was”, bukan “were”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kesesuaian subjeknya gagal karena subjek tunggal diperlakuin sebagai jamak.

distractors.misconception: Keeps the active verb form instead of building be + past participle for the passive.
distractors.whyFails: 'An award gave to the scientist' would make the award the giver; the passive requires the auxiliary 'was' before the past participle 'given'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “an award gave” bikin penghargaannya seolah jadi pemberi; pasif wajib pakai “was” sebelum “given”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk aktifnya dipertahanin, padahal pasif butuh kata bantu be + bentuk ke-3.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Was given to' correctly passivizes the direct object 'an award' as subject and reintroduces the recipient with 'to', the pattern required when the thing given leads the sentence.
explanation.rule: With ditransitive verbs, if the direct object (the thing) becomes the passive subject, the recipient must be reattached with to: A bonus was sent to the staff.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Dropping 'to' leaves the recipient unconnected, 'were' breaks agreement with the singular subject, and 'gave to' is still active voice.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask which object leads the passive sentence: recipient first needs no 'to'; thing first needs 'to' before the receiver.
explanation.memoryCue: Thing as subject? Add 'to': An award was given TO the scientist.
explanation.ruleId: Di kata kerja berobjek dua, kalau objek langsungnya alias bendanya yang jadi subjek pasif, penerimanya wajib disambung lagi pakai to. Contoh: A bonus was sent to the staff.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Was given to” bikin “an award” jadi subjek pasif dan nyambungin penerimanya pakai “to”. Itu pola wajib waktu bendanya yang mimpin kalimat.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Ngebuang “to” bikin penerimanya ngambang, “were” ngerusak kesesuaian sama subjek tunggal, dan “gave to” masih bentuk aktif.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dulu objek mana yang mimpin kalimat pasifnya. Penerima di depan nggak butuh “to”; benda di depan butuh “to” sebelum penerimanya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Bendanya jadi subjek? Tambahin “to”: An award was given TO the scientist.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu nyusun kalimat pasif dari kata kerja berobjek dua dengan bendanya sebagai subjek, terus masang lagi “to” sebelum penerimanya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngebuang “to” yang wajib ada sebelum penerima waktu benda yang dikasih, bukan penerimanya, yang jadi subjek pasif.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali objek mana yang sekarang jadi subjek — kalau bendanya → pertahanin be + bentuk ke-3 dan pasang lagi to sebelum penerimanya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner selects the bare gerund after 'deny', which takes the -ing form directly with no preposition, unlike apologize for + gerund.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners either attach an infinitive to 'deny' or copy the preposition from 'apologize for', instead of using deny + gerund directly.
templates.reasoningOperation: Recall the fixed pattern of the reporting verb — deny + gerund, no preposition -> attach the -ing form straight after the verb.
templates.stem: The suspect denied ____ the missing money from the office safe.

distractors.misconception: Uses an infinitive complement after 'deny', a verb that takes a gerund, not an infinitive.
distractors.whyFails: 'Deny to take' is not a standard English pattern; 'deny' must be followed directly by the -ing form of the reported action.
distractors.whyFailsId: “deny to take” bukan susunan yang dikenal; bentuk to-nya bikin bantahannya kedengeran kayak rencana.
distractors.misconceptionId: pelengkap bentuk to dipakai sesudah “deny” yang justru minta bentuk -ing.

distractors.misconception: Copies the preposition from 'apologize for' onto 'deny', which takes its gerund directly.
distractors.whyFails: 'For' belongs to patterns like 'apologize for'; 'deny' links straight to the gerund with no preposition in between.
distractors.whyFailsId: nyelipin “for” di sini niru pola minta maaf kayak “apologize for”, padahal bantahan nggak pakai kata depan apa pun.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata depan dari “apologize for” dipindahin ke “deny” yang nggak butuh kata depan.

distractors.misconception: Uses the bare base form where the gerund complement is required.
distractors.whyFails: 'Denied take' has no valid grammatical structure; a reporting verb like 'deny' cannot be followed by a bare verb.
distractors.whyFailsId: “denied take” nggak punya susunan yang sah; “deny” nggak pernah diikuti kata kerja dasar.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja bentuk dasar dipakai padahal pelengkap bentuk -ing yang diwajibin.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Denied taking' uses the fixed pattern deny + gerund: the denied action attaches directly as an -ing form, with no preposition and no 'to'.
explanation.rule: Deny + gerund (direct, no preposition); apologize for + gerund (preposition first); admit + gerund (direct). Each reporting verb fixes its own pattern.
explanation.whyOthersFail: An infinitive after 'deny' is unidiomatic, 'for' belongs to apologize's pattern, and a bare verb has no grammatical link to the reporting verb.
explanation.howToAvoid: Memorize each reporting verb with its pattern as one chunk: deny doing, admit doing, apologize FOR doing.
explanation.memoryCue: Deny + -ing straight away — no 'to', no 'for'.
explanation.ruleId: Deny + bentuk -ing langsung tanpa kata depan; apologize for + bentuk -ing pakai kata depan dulu; admit + bentuk -ing langsung. Tiap kata kerja pelapor ngunci polanya sendiri.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Denied taking” pakai pola tetap deny + bentuk -ing: tindakan yang dibantah langsung nempel sebagai bentuk -ing, tanpa kata depan dan tanpa “to”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Bentuk to sesudah “deny” nggak lazim, “for” itu miliknya pola apologize, dan kata kerja dasar nggak punya sambungan yang sah ke kata kerja pelapornya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Hafalin tiap kata kerja pelapor bareng polanya sebagai satu paket: deny doing, admit doing, apologize FOR doing.
explanation.memoryCueId: Deny + bentuk -ing langsung — tanpa “to”, tanpa “for”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu milih bentuk -ing langsung sesudah “deny” tanpa kata depan, beda dari “apologize” yang butuh “for” dulu.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu masang bentuk to di belakang “deny”, atau niru kata depan dari “apologize for”, padahal “deny” langsung diikuti bentuk -ing.
templates.reasoningOperationId: inget pola tetap kata kerja pelapornya — deny + bentuk -ing tanpa kata depan → tempel bentuk -ing langsung sesudah kata kerjanya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner chooses the informal relative clause that strands the preposition at the clause end (with the relative pronoun omitted), matching a casual spoken register.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners carry the formal fronted-preposition pattern (to whom) into casual speech, or garble the stranded pattern by leaving 'whom' after the stranded preposition.
templates.reasoningOperation: Read the register cue — relaxed chat -> strand the preposition at the clause end and drop the relative pronoun.
templates.stem: Relaxed chat with a friend: That's the neighbour ____ at the bus stop yesterday.

distractors.misconception: Imports the formal fronted-preposition pattern into a context that explicitly asks for the casual register.
distractors.whyFails: 'To whom I was chatting' is correct in formal writing, but the question explicitly asks for the version that fits a relaxed chat, where English strands the preposition at the end instead.
distractors.whyFailsId: “to whom I was chatting” bener buat tulisan formal, tapi soalnya jelas minta versi obrolan santai yang naruh kata depannya di akhir.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola formal yang majuin kata depan dibawa ke obrolan santai, padahal soalnya jelas minta ragam santai.

distractors.misconception: using subject-form 'who' after a fronted preposition, which requires the object form
distractors.whyFails: A preposition fronted before the relative pronoun demands the object form 'whom'; 'to who' is ungrammatical in any register, formal or casual.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata depan yang dimajuin minta bentuk objek “whom”; “to who” nggak sah di ragam mana pun.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk subjek “who” dipakai sesudah kata depan yang dimajuin, padahal yang diminta bentuk objek.

distractors.misconception: Strands the preposition but leaves 'whom' dangling after it at the clause end.
distractors.whyFails: 'The neighbour I was chatting to whom' doubles the object slot; once the preposition is stranded, the relative pronoun is dropped or moved to the front as 'who/that', never left after 'to'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “whom” nyantol di belakang “to” jadi slot objeknya dobel; kalau kata depannya di akhir, kata penghubungnya dibuang atau pindah ke depan.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata depannya udah ditaruh di akhir, tapi “whom” malah ditinggal ngegantung di belakangnya.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'I was chatting to' strands the preposition at the clause end and omits the relative pronoun — exactly the pattern natural English uses in relaxed conversation, which the stem explicitly requests.
explanation.rule: Informal register strands the preposition at the clause end and can drop the object relative pronoun (the neighbour I was chatting to); formal register fronts it before whom (the neighbour to whom I was chatting).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'To whom' is formal and clashes with the requested register, 'to who' pairs a fronted preposition with the subject form, and leaving 'whom' after the stranded 'to' doubles the object slot.
explanation.howToAvoid: Match the pattern to the register first: casual speech ends with the preposition; formal writing fronts preposition + whom.
explanation.memoryCue: Chat casually, end with the preposition: '…the neighbour I was chatting to.'
explanation.ruleId: Ragam santai naruh kata depannya di akhir anak kalimat dan boleh ngebuang kata penghubung objeknya: the neighbour I was chatting to. Ragam formal majuin kata depannya sebelum whom: the neighbour to whom I was chatting.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “I was chatting to” naruh kata depan di akhir dan ngebuang kata penghubungnya. Itu persis pola obrolan santai yang diminta soalnya.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “To whom” itu formal dan bentrok sama ragam yang diminta, “to who” masangin kata depan yang dimajuin sama bentuk subjek, dan ninggalin “whom” di belakang “to” bikin slot objeknya dobel.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cocokkan polanya sama ragamnya dulu: obrolan santai berakhir di kata depan; tulisan formal majuin kata depan + whom.
explanation.memoryCueId: Lagi ngobrol santai? Akhiri di kata depannya: “…the neighbour I was chatting to.”

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu milih anak kalimat penjelas ragam santai yang naruh kata depannya di akhir dan ngebuang kata penghubungnya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu bawa pola formal “to whom” ke obrolan santai, atau ninggalin “whom” ngegantung di belakang kata depan yang udah ditaruh di akhir.
templates.reasoningOperationId: baca petunjuk ragamnya — obrolan santai → taruh kata depannya di akhir anak kalimat dan buang kata penghubungnya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner builds the passive as 'to be + past participle' when the governing verb (expect, hope, want) demands a to-infinitive slot, rejecting 'being + past participle' there.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners insert the passive gerund into the slot of verbs whose fixed pattern demands a to-infinitive, such as expect, hope, and want.
templates.reasoningOperation: Lock the pattern demanded by the governing verb — expect wants a to-infinitive -> wrap the passive meaning inside to be + past participle.
templates.stem: She fully expects ____ for the senior manager position next month.

distractors.misconception: Applies the passive gerund pattern to a verb ('expect') that specifically requires an infinitive complement.
distractors.whyFails: 'Expect' is followed by a to-infinitive, not a gerund; the passive form must therefore be 'to be considered', not 'being considered'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “expect” diikuti bentuk to, bukan bentuk -ing, jadi pola pasifnya ikut salah.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola bentuk -ing pasif dipakai di “expect” yang khusus minta pelengkap bentuk to.

distractors.misconception: Keeps the active continuous form, making the subject the one doing the considering instead of the one considered.
distractors.whyFails: 'To be considering' is active: she would be the one weighing candidates, but the sentence means the company considers her, which demands the passive participle 'considered'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “to be considering” bentuknya aktif: dia yang jadi penimbang, padahal maksudnya dia yang dipertimbangkan.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk aktif -ing dipertahanin jadi subjeknya seolah yang nimbang, bukan yang ditimbang.

distractors.misconception: Blends the infinitive marker with the past participle, dropping the required 'be'.
distractors.whyFails: 'To considered' skips the auxiliary 'be' that carries the passive meaning; the passive infinitive is always to + be + past participle.
distractors.whyFailsId: “to considered” ngelewatin “be” yang bawa makna pasifnya; bentuk to pasif selalu to + be + bentuk ke-3.
distractors.misconceptionId: penanda “to” langsung ditempel ke bentuk ke-3, padahal “be” yang diwajibin malah dibuang.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'To be considered' is the passive infinitive, correctly complementing 'expect', a verb that takes a to-infinitive, while keeping her as the one being considered.
explanation.rule: Passive infinitive (to be + past participle) follows verbs that take infinitive complements, like expect, hope, want; passive gerund (being + past participle) follows gerund-taking verbs like resent, avoid.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Being considered' uses the gerund pattern 'expect' rejects, 'to be considering' flips the voice to active, and 'to considered' drops the required 'be'.
explanation.howToAvoid: First fix the complement type from the verb (expect -> to-infinitive), then build the passive inside that shape: to be + past participle.
explanation.memoryCue: Expect / hope / want + to be + past participle (never 'being').
explanation.ruleId: Bentuk to pasif to be + bentuk ke-3 nyusul kata kerja yang minta pelengkap bentuk to, kayak expect, hope, dan want. Bentuk -ing pasif being + bentuk ke-3 nyusul kata kerja kayak resent dan avoid.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “To be considered” itu bentuk to pasif yang pas jadi pelengkap “expect”, dan tetap bikin dia yang dipertimbangkan, bukan yang mempertimbangkan.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Being considered” pakai pola -ing yang ditolak “expect”, “to be considering” mbalik jadi aktif, dan “to considered” ngebuang “be” yang diwajibin.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kunci dulu jenis pelengkap dari kata kerjanya (expect → bentuk to), baru bangun pasifnya di dalam pola itu: to be + bentuk ke-3.
explanation.memoryCueId: Expect, hope, dan want diikuti to be + bentuk ke-3, nggak pernah “being”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu milih bentuk pasif to be + bentuk ke-3 sesudah kata kerja kayak “expect” yang minta pelengkap bentuk to.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai bentuk -ing pasif sesudah kata kerja yang justru minta pelengkap bentuk to.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali dulu jenis pelengkap yang dituntut kata kerjanya — expect minta bentuk to → pasang pasifnya sebagai to be + bentuk ke-3

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner distinguishes 'go on + to-infinitive' (move on to a new, later stage) from 'go on + gerund' (continue the same activity).
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners treat 'go on doing' and 'go on to do' as interchangeable, missing that the gerund continues the same activity while the infinitive starts a new one.
templates.reasoningOperation: Ask whether the verb after 'go on' continues the same activity or begins a new stage -> a new stage takes the to-infinitive.
templates.stem: After finishing her law degree, she went on ____ one of the country's youngest judges.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'go on + gerund' (continue the same activity) where the sentence marks a new, later achievement.
distractors.whyFails: 'Went on becoming' would mean she was already in the middle of becoming a judge and simply continued, but 'after finishing her law degree' introduces a brand-new next stage.
distractors.whyFailsId: “went on becoming” berarti dia lagi di tengah proses itu terus lanjut, padahal kalimatnya mbuka babak baru sesudah lulus.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola go on + bentuk -ing yang nerusin kegiatan yang sama dipakai padahal kalimatnya nandain babak baru.

distractors.misconception: Drops the infinitive marker 'to' entirely.
distractors.whyFails: 'Go on' needs 'to' before the base verb to signal the move to a new stage; 'went on become' is not a grammatical sequence in English.
distractors.whyFailsId: “went on become” bukan rangkaian yang sah; “go on” butuh “to” sebelum kata kerja dasarnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: penanda bentuk to dibuang sama sekali dari pola go on + to.

distractors.misconception: Blends the infinitive marker 'to' with a gerund ending, producing an invalid hybrid.
distractors.whyFails: After 'go on', 'to' here is the infinitive marker and must be followed by the base form; attaching -ing to it produces a broken hybrid, not a valid pattern.
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “go on”, “to” di sini penanda bentuk to yang wajib diikuti kata kerja dasar, bukan bentuk -ing.
distractors.misconceptionId: penanda bentuk to digabung sama akhiran -ing jadi bentuk campuran yang nggak sah.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Went on to become' marks becoming a judge as the next, new stage after finishing her degree — exactly what go on + to-infinitive encodes.
explanation.rule: Go on + to-infinitive = finish one thing, then move on to a NEW action; go on + gerund = continue the SAME activity without stopping.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Becoming' claims she continued an activity already underway, 'become' loses the required 'to', and 'to becoming' fuses the infinitive marker with an -ing form.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check whether the action after 'go on' is the same one continuing (gerund) or a fresh, later step (to-infinitive).
explanation.memoryCue: Go on TO do = next chapter; go on DOING = same chapter continues.
explanation.ruleId: Go on + bentuk to berarti selesai satu hal, lanjut ke tindakan BARU. Go on + bentuk -ing berarti nerusin kegiatan yang SAMA tanpa berhenti. “Regret” dan “mean” ikut keluarga pola yang sama, tapi kartu ini nguji “go on”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Went on to become” nandain jadi hakim sebagai babak baru sesudah lulus kuliah hukum. Itu persis makna go on + bentuk to.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Becoming” ngeklaim dia nerusin kegiatan yang udah jalan, “become” kehilangan “to” yang wajib, dan “to becoming” ngegabung penanda bentuk to sama bentuk -ing.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek tindakan sesudah “go on”: kegiatan yang sama yang diterusin (bentuk -ing) atau langkah baru sesudahnya (bentuk to)?
explanation.memoryCueId: Go on TO do = bab baru; go on DOING = bab yang sama masih lanjut.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu bedain “go on” + bentuk to yang pindah ke babak baru, dari “go on” + bentuk -ing yang nerusin kegiatan yang sama.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nganggep “go on doing” dan “go on to do” sama aja, padahal maknanya beda: nerusin yang sama atau mulai yang baru.
templates.reasoningOperationId: tanya dulu: kata kerja sesudah “go on” nerusin kegiatan yang sama atau mulai babak baru → babak baru pakai bentuk to

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner selects the simple gerund when the gerund's action is simultaneous with the main verb, reserving the perfect gerund for actions explicitly earlier in time.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners overuse the perfect gerund ('having + past participle') even when the two actions happen at the same time.
templates.reasoningOperation: Compare the timing of the two actions — simultaneous with the main verb -> simple gerund; explicitly earlier -> perfect gerund.
templates.stem: She enjoys ____ to podcasts while she cooks dinner. (both actions happen at the same time)

distractors.misconception: using a perfect gerund, implying the action is already completed
distractors.whyFails: 'Having listened' marks the listening as finished before the enjoying, but 'while she cooks dinner' shows the two actions happen together in the same moment.
distractors.whyFailsId: “having listened” nandain dengernya udah selesai sebelum senengnya muncul, padahal “while she cooks dinner” nunjukin dua-duanya barengan.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing perfect dipakai jadi tindakannya seolah udah kelar duluan.

distractors.misconception: Uses an infinitive complement after 'enjoy', a verb that takes a gerund, not an infinitive.
distractors.whyFails: 'Enjoy to listen' is not a standard English pattern; 'enjoy' must be followed by the -ing form of its complement.
distractors.whyFailsId: “enjoy to listen” bukan pola yang baku; “enjoy” wajib diikuti bentuk -ing.
distractors.misconceptionId: pelengkap bentuk to dipakai sesudah “enjoy” yang justru minta bentuk -ing.

distractors.misconception: Uses the bare base form with no verb marking at all.
distractors.whyFails: 'Enjoys listen' has no valid grammatical function; 'enjoy' requires a gerund complement, never a bare verb.
distractors.whyFailsId: “enjoys listen” nggak punya fungsi tata bahasa yang sah; “enjoy” nggak pernah diikuti kata kerja dasar.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar telanjang dipakai tanpa tanda apa pun.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Listening' is the simple gerund, correct because 'while she cooks dinner' shows the listening happens at the same time as the enjoying, so no anteriority marking is needed.
explanation.rule: Simple gerund = the action is simultaneous with (or general relative to) the main verb; perfect gerund (having + past participle) explicitly marks the action as earlier.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Having listened' wrongly pushes a simultaneous action into the past, while 'to listen' and 'listen' are invalid complements of 'enjoy'.
explanation.howToAvoid: Only reach for having + past participle when the sentence needs to stress that one action came first; for same-time actions, keep the simple gerund.
explanation.memoryCue: Same time = simple -ing; earlier time = having + past participle.
explanation.ruleId: Bentuk -ing sederhana dipakai kalau tindakannya barengan sama kata kerja utama. Bentuk -ing perfect having + bentuk ke-3 khusus negesin tindakannya terjadi lebih dulu.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Listening” itu bentuk -ing sederhana yang pas, karena “while she cooks dinner” nunjukin dengernya barengan sama masaknya. Nggak perlu nandain mana yang duluan.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Having listened” keliru ndorong tindakan yang barengan ke masa sebelumnya. “To listen” dan “listen” bukan pelengkap yang sah buat “enjoy”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Pakai having + bentuk ke-3 cuma kalau kalimatnya perlu negesin satu tindakan duluan. Kalau barengan, cukup bentuk -ing sederhana.
explanation.memoryCueId: Barengan = bentuk -ing sederhana; duluan = having + bentuk ke-3.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pakai bentuk -ing sederhana waktu tindakannya barengan sama kata kerja utama, dan nyimpen having + bentuk ke-3 buat tindakan yang jelas duluan.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu kebanyakan pakai bentuk -ing perfect having + bentuk ke-3, padahal dua tindakannya kejadian barengan.
templates.reasoningOperationId: bandingin waktu dua tindakannya — barengan sama kata kerja utama → bentuk -ing sederhana; jelas duluan → bentuk -ing perfect

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner selects 'which' (not 'whom') inside the quantifier + of + relative pronoun pattern when the group referred back to consists of things, not people.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners pick 'whom' inside the quantifier + of pattern regardless of whether the antecedent is a person or a thing.
templates.reasoningOperation: Check the antecedent of the quantifier pattern — things take some of which; people take some of whom.
templates.stem: The gallery bought dozens of old paintings, ____ turned out to be extremely valuable.

distractors.misconception: Uses the personal relative pronoun 'whom' inside the quantifier pattern for a non-human antecedent.
distractors.whyFails: 'Whom' refers to people, but this clause points back to 'paintings', which are things and therefore require 'which' after the quantifier.
distractors.whyFailsId: “some of whom” salah sasaran: “whom” khusus buat manusia, sedangkan yang diomongin di sini lukisan-lukisan.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata penghubung buat orang dipakai di pola kata jumlah padahal yang ditunjuk benda.

distractors.misconception: Uses a personal pronoun 'them' instead of a relative pronoun, which cannot join two clauses.
distractors.whyFails: 'Them' is not a relative pronoun, so it cannot grammatically link the second clause to the first inside one sentence; the result is a comma splice.
distractors.whyFailsId: “them” bukan kata penghubung, jadi dua anak kalimatnya cuma nempel koma tanpa sambungan yang sah.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti biasa “them” dipakai gantiin kata penghubung, padahal nggak bisa nyambung dua anak kalimat.

distractors.misconception: Scrambles the fixed order of the quantifier + of + which pattern.
distractors.whyFails: The pattern is fixed as quantifier + of + which ('some of which'); putting 'which' first breaks the required sequence and is ungrammatical.
distractors.whyFailsId: urutannya wajib kata jumlah dulu, terus “of”, baru “which”; naruh “which” di depan bikin polanya rusak.
distractors.misconceptionId: urutan pola tetap kata jumlah + of + which diacak jadi “which” nongol duluan.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Some of which' correctly combines the quantifier with the non-personal relative pronoun 'which' to refer back to 'paintings', a group of things, in a non-defining clause.
explanation.rule: In the quantifier + of + relative pronoun pattern, the pronoun must match the antecedent: which for things (some of which), whom for people (many of whom).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Whom' is reserved for people, 'them' is a personal pronoun that cannot link clauses, and reordering the words breaks the fixed pattern.
explanation.howToAvoid: First identify what the clause points back to: things take which, people take whom — then keep the order quantifier + of + pronoun.
explanation.memoryCue: Paintings, books, ideas — some of WHICH; volunteers, students — many of WHOM.
explanation.ruleId: Di pola kata jumlah + of + kata penghubung, kata penghubungnya harus cocok sama yang ditunjuk: which buat benda (some of which), whom buat orang (many of whom).
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Some of which” madukan kata jumlah sama kata penghubung buat benda, “which”, buat nunjuk balik ke “paintings” di anak kalimat penjelas tambahan.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Whom” khusus buat orang, “them” itu kata ganti biasa yang nggak bisa nyambung antar anak kalimat, dan ngacak urutan katanya ngerusak pola tetapnya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek dulu anak kalimatnya nunjuk balik ke apa: benda pakai which, orang pakai whom. Terus jaga urutannya: kata jumlah + of + kata penghubung.
explanation.memoryCueId: Lukisan, buku, ide — “some of WHICH”; relawan, murid — “many of WHOM”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu milih “which”, bukan “whom”, di pola kata jumlah + of + kata penghubung waktu kelompok yang ditunjuk itu benda, bukan orang.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu asal pakai “whom” di pola kata jumlah + of tanpa ngecek yang ditunjuk itu orang atau benda.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek dulu pola kata jumlahnya nunjuk balik ke apa — benda pakai some of which, orang pakai some of whom

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Build two-item comparatives with '-er' for short adjectives and 'more' for long ones, without doubling the markers
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner translates 'lebih murah' word by word, producing 'more cheap' or the doubled 'more cheaper' instead of 'cheaper'
templates.reasoningOperation: count the syllables of 'cheap' and spot 'than' -> attach '-er' to the short adjective without adding 'more'
templates.stem: The bus to Bandung is ___ (cheap) than the train.

distractors.misconception: applies the periphrastic 'more + adjective' pattern to a short one-syllable adjective that takes '-er'
distractors.whyFails: 'More cheap' uses the 'more + adjective' pattern that belongs to long adjectives; one-syllable 'cheap' must take '-er': 'cheaper'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “More cheap” memakai pola untuk kata sifat panjang; “cheap” kata pendek satu suku, jadi bandingannya “cheaper”.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola “more + kata sifat” dipasang ke kata sifat pendek yang harusnya pakai “-er”.

distractors.misconception: doubles the comparative marking by putting 'more' before an adjective already ending in '-er'
distractors.whyFails: 'More cheaper' marks the comparison twice — 'more' and '-er' do the same job, so English only allows one of them: 'cheaper'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “More cheaper” nandain perbandingan dua kali — “more” dan “-er” kerjaannya sama, jadi cukup “cheaper” aja.
distractors.misconceptionId: komparatifnya ditandain dobel: “more” ditumpuk di depan kata yang udah ber-“-er”.

distractors.misconception: superlative used for a two-item comparison
distractors.whyFails: 'Cheapest' ranks three or more things; this sentence compares only the bus and the train, and the following 'than' also blocks a superlative.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Cheapest” itu buat tiga benda ke atas; di sini yang dibandingin cuma bus sama kereta, dan ada “than” yang nolak superlatif.
distractors.misconceptionId: superlatif dipakai buat bandingin dua benda doang.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Cheap' is a short one-syllable adjective, so the comparison of two things is built with '-er' plus 'than': 'cheaper than the train'.
explanation.rule: Short adjectives form the comparative with '-er' + 'than'; long adjectives like 'expensive' use 'more' + adjective + 'than'. Never combine 'more' with '-er'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'More cheap' applies the long-adjective pattern to one-syllable 'cheap'; 'more cheaper' marks the comparison twice; 'cheapest' is a superlative, but only two things — the bus and the train — are compared.
explanation.howToAvoid: Count the syllables first: one syllable takes '-er', and once the '-er' is there, 'more' must stay away.
explanation.memoryCue: One short word, one small tail: cheap -> cheaper, never 'more cheaper'.
explanation.ruleId: Kata sifat pendek bikin komparatif pakai “-er” + “than”; kata sifat panjang kayak “expensive” pakai “more” + kata sifat + “than”. “More” dan “-er” nggak boleh barengan.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Cheap” cuma satu suku kata, jadi bandingin dua benda cukup “-er” plus “than”: “cheaper than the train”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “More cheap” pakai pola kata panjang buat “cheap” yang pendek. “More cheaper” nandain banding dua kali. “Cheapest” bentuk paling, padahal cuma dua yang dibandingin.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Hitung suku katanya dulu: satu suku kata ambil “-er”, dan kalau “-er” udah nempel, “more” nggak boleh ikut.
explanation.memoryCueId: Kata pendek, ekor pendek: “cheap” → “cheaper”, jangan “more cheaper”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Bikin komparatif dua benda yang bener: “-er” buat kata sifat pendek, “more” buat yang panjang, tanpa penanda dobel.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nerjemahin “lebih murah” kata per kata, jadi keluarnya “more cheap” atau malah dobel “more cheaper”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: hitung suku kata “cheap” dan lihat “than” → tempelin “-er” ke kata sifat pendeknya tanpa nambah “more”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Describe how an action is done with a manner adverb in '-ly' instead of a bare adjective
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner describes the action with a bare adjective or 'with + adjective' because Indonesian uses one form like 'hati-hati' for both jobs
templates.reasoningOperation: see the action verb 'carry' being described -> choose the '-ly' manner adverb, not the adjective
templates.stem: Please carry the glasses ___ — they break easily.

distractors.misconception: uses the bare adjective after an action verb where a manner adverb in '-ly' is required
distractors.whyFails: 'Carry the glasses careful' leaves the adjective describing an action; the verb 'carry' needs the adverb 'carefully'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Carry the glasses careful” ninggalin kata sifat buat jelasin aksi; kata kerja “carry” butuhnya adverbia “carefully”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata sifat polos ditaruh sesudah kata kerja aksi.

distractors.misconception: builds the manner phrase as 'with' plus a bare adjective, copying Indonesian 'dengan hati-hati'
distractors.whyFails: 'With careful' puts a bare adjective after 'with'; English needs the adverb 'carefully' in this slot, because 'with' can only take a noun after it.
distractors.whyFailsId: “With careful” naruh kata sifat polos sesudah “with”; slot ini butuhnya adverbia “carefully”, soalnya “with” cuma bisa diikuti nomina.
distractors.misconceptionId: frasa cara dibangun “with” + kata sifat, niru pola “dengan hati-hati”.

distractors.misconception: switches to a comparative adjective although nothing is being compared and the slot needs an adverb
distractors.whyFails: 'More careful' is a comparative adjective, but the sentence compares nothing and the slot after 'carry' needs a manner adverb.
distractors.whyFailsId: “More careful” itu kata sifat komparatif; kalimatnya nggak bandingin apa-apa, dan sesudah “carry” yang dibutuhin adverbia cara.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk komparatif dipasang padahal nggak ada yang dibandingin dan slotnya butuh adverbia.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Carry' is an action verb, and the word describing how the action is done must be the manner adverb 'carefully'.
explanation.rule: To say how an action happens, add '-ly' to the adjective: careful -> carefully. The bare adjective stays with linking verbs like 'be' ('be careful').
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Careful' is an adjective and cannot describe the verb 'carry'; 'with careful' copies Indonesian 'dengan hati-hati' but strands an adjective after 'with'; 'more careful' is still an adjective, and nothing is being compared.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask what the word describes: a thing takes the adjective, an action takes the '-ly' adverb.
explanation.memoryCue: Action verb + '-ly': carry carefully, speak quietly, drive slowly.
explanation.ruleId: Buat bilang gimana caranya, tambahin “-ly” ke kata sifat: “careful” → “carefully”. Sesudah “be” kata sifatnya tetap polos: “be careful”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Carry” itu kata kerja aksi, jadi kata yang jelasin caranya harus adverbia “carefully”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Careful” kata sifat, nggak bisa jelasin “carry”. “With careful” salah bentuk. “More careful” bentuk banding, padahal nggak ada yang dibandingin.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dulu kata itu jelasin apa: benda dapet kata sifat, aksi dapet adverbia “-ly”.
