explanation.memoryCueId: Kata kerja aksi + “-ly”: “carry carefully”, “speak quietly”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Jelasin cara sebuah aksi dilakukan pakai adverbia “-ly”, bukan kata sifat polos.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu jelasin aksinya pakai kata sifat polos atau “with” + kata sifat, soalnya bahasa Indonesia cuma punya satu bentuk kayak “hati-hati” buat dua fungsi.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat kata kerja aksi “carry” yang lagi dijelasin caranya → pilih adverbia “-ly”, bukan kata sifatnya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Choose 'How much' for uncountable nouns and 'How many' for plural countable nouns in quantity questions
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner asks quantity with 'How many' for any noun because Indonesian 'berapa' never marks countability
templates.reasoningOperation: check that 'water' is uncountable and singular -> ask the quantity with 'How much'
templates.stem: ___ water do you drink every day?

distractors.misconception: asks about an uncountable noun with 'how many'
distractors.whyFails: 'How many water' pairs the countable question word with uncountable 'water'; 'how many' needs a plural noun like 'bottles'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “How many water” masangin kata tanya tercacah ke “water” yang tak tercacah; “how many” butuhnya nomina jamak kayak “bottles”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “how many” dipasang ke nomina tak tercacah.

distractors.misconception: asks quantity with bare 'how' and drops the quantity word entirely
distractors.whyFails: 'How water do you drink' has no quantity word at all; bare 'how' asks about manner, so the question stops making sense.
distractors.whyFailsId: “How water do you drink” nggak punya kata jumlah sama sekali; “how” doang nanyain cara, jadi pertanyaannya nggak jalan.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata jumlahnya dibuang, tinggal “how” doang.

distractors.misconception: adds a partitive 'of' straight after 'how much' before a bare noun
distractors.whyFails: 'How much of water' puts 'of' before a bare noun; 'of' only works with a determiner after it, as in 'how much of the water', so the plain question here is 'How much water'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “How much of water” naruh “of” sebelum nomina polos; “of” cuma jalan kalau ada penentu sesudahnya kayak “how much of the water”, jadi di sini cukup “How much water”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “of” diselipin langsung sebelum nomina polos sesudah “how much”.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Water' is uncountable and has no plural form here, so the quantity question is built with 'How much'.
explanation.rule: 'How much' asks about uncountable nouns; 'How many' asks about plural countable nouns: 'How much water', 'How many bottles'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'How many' needs a plural countable noun like 'bottles', not 'water'; bare 'How' asks about manner, not quantity; 'How much of' needs a determiner after 'of', never a bare noun.
explanation.howToAvoid: Look at the noun first: if you cannot count it one by one, ask with 'How much'.
explanation.memoryCue: 'How much water, how many bottles' — the noun decides the question word.
explanation.ruleId: “How much” buat nomina tak tercacah; “How many” buat nomina jamak tercacah: “How much water”, “How many bottles”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Water” nggak bisa dihitung satu-satu dan nggak ada bentuk jamaknya di sini, jadi nanyanya pakai “How much”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “How many” buat benda yang bisa dihitung, bukan “water”. “How” doang nanya cara. “How much of” butuh “the/this” sesudah “of”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Lihat nominanya dulu: kalau nggak bisa dihitung satu-satu, tanyanya pakai “How much”.
explanation.memoryCueId: “How much water, how many bottles” — nominanya yang nentuin kata tanyanya.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Nanya jumlah pakai “How much” buat nomina tak tercacah dan “How many” buat nomina jamak tercacah.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nanya jumlah pakai “How many” buat nomina apa aja, soalnya “berapa” di bahasa Indonesia nggak pernah bedain tercacah atau nggak.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek dulu “water” itu tak tercacah dan tunggal → nanya jumlahnya pakai “How much”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Pick the indefinite compound (something, anything or nothing) that matches the polarity of the clause
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner follows the meaning 'nggak ada apa-apa' without checking the verb, so 'anything' or 'something' lands in a positive clause
templates.reasoningOperation: notice the positive verb 'was' plus the empty-fridge meaning -> pick the negative compound 'nothing'
templates.stem: The fridge was empty — there was ___ inside at all.

distractors.misconception: uses 'anything' in a positive clause that has no negative word to license it
distractors.whyFails: 'There was anything inside' has no negative anywhere: 'anything' only works after a negative verb ('wasn't anything') or in a question.
distractors.whyFailsId: “There was anything inside” nggak punya kata negatif di mana pun; “anything” cuma jalan sesudah kata kerja negatif (“wasn't anything”) atau di kalimat tanya.
distractors.misconceptionId: “anything” dipasang di kalimat positif tanpa kata negatif sama sekali.

distractors.misconception: using a positive indefinite pronoun that contradicts the negative context
distractors.whyFails: 'Something' says an item really was in the fridge, but 'empty' and 'at all' rule that out in this sentence.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Something” bilang beneran ada barang di kulkas, padahal “empty” dan “at all” udah nutup kemungkinan itu.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti positif dipasang padahal konteksnya negatif.

distractors.misconception: leaves bare 'any' without a noun in a positive clause
distractors.whyFails: 'There was any inside' has a positive verb, and bare 'any' cannot make the clause negative by itself; only 'nothing' carries the negative meaning here.
distractors.whyFailsId: “There was any inside” kata kerjanya positif, dan “any” polos nggak bisa bikin kalimatnya negatif sendirian; yang bawa makna negatif di sini cuma “nothing”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “any” polos ditaruh tanpa nomina di kalimat positif.

explanation.whyCorrect: The verb 'was' is positive, so the negative meaning must come from the pronoun itself: 'nothing' means 'not anything'.
explanation.rule: 'Nothing' carries its own negative and goes with a positive verb; 'anything' needs a negative verb or a question; 'something' belongs in positive statements about things that exist.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Anything' has no negative word to support it because 'was' is positive; 'something' claims the fridge held an item, which 'empty' and 'at all' rule out; bare 'any' cannot stand alone in a positive clause.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check the verb first: if it is positive but the meaning is negative, choose the no- compound.
explanation.memoryCue: One negative per clause: 'wasn't anything' or 'was nothing', never half and half.
explanation.ruleId: “Nothing” udah bawa negatif sendiri dan jalan sama kata kerja positif; “anything” butuh kata kerja negatif atau kalimat tanya; “something” buat pernyataan positif.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Kata kerja “was” positif, jadi makna negatifnya harus dateng dari kata gantinya sendiri: “nothing” artinya “not anything”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Anything” butuh kata negatif, padahal “was” positif. “Something” bilang kulkasnya ada isinya, padahal “empty”. “Any” polos nggak bisa berdiri sendiri.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek kata kerjanya dulu: kalau positif tapi maknanya negatif, ambil kata yang berawalan “no-”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Satu negatif per kalimat: “wasn't anything” atau “was nothing”, jangan setengah-setengah.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pilih kata majemuk “something”, “anything”, atau “nothing” yang cocok: kalimatnya positif atau negatif.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nurutin arti “nggak ada apa-apa” tanpa ngecek kata kerjanya, jadi “anything” atau “something” kepasang di kalimat positif.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat kata kerja “was” yang positif plus makna kulkas kosong → pilih kata negatif “nothing”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Link a result back to its cause with 'because' and a cause forward to its result with 'so'
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner swaps 'because' and 'so', opening the reason clause with the result connector under the order-free 'karena ... maka' pattern
templates.reasoningOperation: decide that 'she was very tired' explains the early night -> introduce that reason clause with 'because'
templates.stem: Dewi went to bed early last night ___ she was very tired after work.

distractors.misconception: introduces the reason clause with the result connector 'so'
distractors.whyFails: 'So' introduces a result, but 'she was very tired after work' is the reason for the early night, not its outcome — going to bed at night cannot cause tiredness earlier that day.
distractors.whyFailsId: “So” ngenalin akibat, padahal “she was very tired after work” itu alasan dia tidur cepat, bukan akibatnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: klausa alasan dibuka pakai “so” yang jatahnya buat akibat.

distractors.misconception: puts 'because of' before a full clause although it only takes a noun phrase
distractors.whyFails: 'Because of' must be followed by a noun phrase like 'because of the rain'; here a full clause with a subject and verb follows, so 'because of' cannot attach to it.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Because of” harus diikuti frasa nomina kayak “because of the rain”; di sini yang ngikut klausa utuh bersubjek dan berkata kerja, jadi “because of” nggak nyambung.
distractors.misconceptionId: “because of” ditaruh di depan klausa utuh, padahal jatahnya cuma frasa nomina.

distractors.misconception: uses the purpose connector 'so that' where a plain reason connector is needed
distractors.whyFails: 'So that' announces a goal Dewi was trying to reach, but being very tired was never her goal — it is the reason, so the clause needs 'because'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “So that” ngumumin tujuan yang mau dicapai Dewi, padahal capek banget itu bukan tujuannya — itu alasannya, jadi klausanya butuh “because”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “so that” yang buat tujuan dipasang ke klausa alasan.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'She was very tired after work' explains why Dewi went to bed early, and a reason clause is introduced by 'because'.
explanation.rule: 'Because' introduces the reason; 'so' introduces the result: reason + 'so' + result, or result + 'because' + reason. Use only one of them per sentence.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'So' would present the tiredness as the outcome of going to bed, reversing the logic; 'because of' can only be followed by a noun phrase, not a full clause; 'so that' marks a purpose, and being tired was never the goal.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask which clause answers 'why?' — that clause starts with 'because'; the outcome clause is the one that takes 'so'.
explanation.memoryCue: Reason takes 'because', result takes 'so' — pick one, never both.
explanation.ruleId: “Because” buat alasan; “so” buat akibat: alasan + “so” + akibat, atau akibat + “because” + alasan. Pakai salah satunya aja per kalimat.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “She was very tired after work” jelasin kenapa Dewi tidur cepet, dan klausa alasan dibukanya pakai “because”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “So” bikin capeknya jadi akibat, logikanya kebalik. “Because of” cuma buat frasa benda, bukan klausa. “So that” nandain tujuan, padahal capek bukan tujuan.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya klausa mana yang jawab “kenapa?” — klausa itu mulainya pakai “because”; klausa hasilnya yang dapet “so”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Alasan dapet “because”, akibat dapet “so” — pilih satu, jangan dua-duanya.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Sambungin akibat balik ke sebabnya pakai “because” dan sebab maju ke akibatnya pakai “so”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nuker “because” sama “so”, klausa alasan malah dibuka pakai konektor akibat, kebawa pola “karena ... maka” yang urutannya bebas.
templates.reasoningOperationId: tentuin “she was very tired” itu penjelasan tidur cepetnya → buka klausa alasan itu pakai “because”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Place 'just', 'already' and 'yet' in the right position and polarity with the present perfect
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner drops 'already' or 'still' into the end slot of a negative perfect clause where English wants 'yet'
templates.reasoningOperation: spot the negative 'hasn't' with an empty slot at the end of the clause -> close the clause with 'yet'
templates.stem: It's almost midnight, but Dina hasn't finished her homework ___.

distractors.misconception: puts 'already' at the end of a negative statement where 'yet' belongs
distractors.whyFails: 'Hasn't finished her homework already' clashes: 'already' says the action is done, while 'hasn't' says it is not — a plain negative statement closes with 'yet'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Hasn't finished her homework already” tabrakan: “already” bilang udah selesai, “hasn't” bilang belum — kalimat negatif biasa nutupnya pakai “yet”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “already” ditaruh di ujung kalimat negatif yang harusnya ditutup “yet”.

distractors.misconception: drags 'just' to the end of the clause instead of mid-position between the auxiliary and the participle
distractors.whyFails: 'Just' needs mid-position — 'has just finished' — so parked at the very end of this negative clause it cannot modify the verb.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Just” butuh posisi tengah — “has just finished” — jadi kalau diparkir di ujung klausa negatif ini dia nggak bisa nempel ke kata kerjanya.
distractors.misconceptionId: “just” diseret ke ujung klausa, padahal tempatnya di tengah antara kata bantu dan participle.

distractors.misconception: parks 'still' at the end of a negative clause instead of before the auxiliary
distractors.whyFails: 'Still' must stand before the negative auxiliary — 'still hasn't finished'; at the end of the clause English switches to 'yet'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Still” harus berdiri sebelum kata bantu negatif — “still hasn't finished”; kalau slotnya di ujung klausa, bahasa Inggris gantinya “yet”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “still” diparkir di ujung kalimat negatif, padahal tempatnya sebelum kata bantu.

explanation.whyCorrect: The clause is negative ('hasn't finished') and the adverb sits at the very end, and that end slot in a negative present perfect belongs to 'yet'.
explanation.rule: 'Yet' closes negative statements and questions in the present perfect; 'just' and 'already' sit between 'have' and the participle in positive sentences; 'still' stands before the auxiliary to stress that a situation continues.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Already' expects a positive perfect ('has already finished') and contradicts 'hasn't' at the end of this statement; 'just' belongs in mid-position, not at the end; 'still' only works earlier in the clause, before 'hasn't'.
explanation.howToAvoid: See a negative present perfect with a gap at the very end? Reach for 'yet' before anything else.
explanation.memoryCue: 'Not ... yet' hugs the end; 'already' and 'just' live in the middle; 'still' pushes to the front of the negative.
explanation.ruleId: “Yet” nutup kalimat negatif dan pertanyaan present perfect; “just” dan “already” duduk di antara “have” dan participle di kalimat positif; “still” berdiri sebelum kata bantu buat nekanin situasinya masih lanjut.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Klausanya negatif (“hasn't finished”) dan adverbianya di paling ujung, dan slot ujung di present perfect negatif itu jatahnya “yet”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Already” maunya kalimat positif (“has already finished”) dan tabrakan sama “hasn't” di ujung kalimat ini; “just” tempatnya di tengah, bukan di ujung; “still” cuma jalan kalau pindah ke depan “hasn't”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Ketemu present perfect negatif dengan slot kosong di paling ujung? Ambil “yet” duluan.
explanation.memoryCueId: “Not ... yet” nempel di ujung; “already” dan “just” tinggal di tengah; “still” maju ke depan negatif.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Naruh “just”, “already”, dan “yet” di posisi yang pas, sesuai kalimatnya positif atau negatif, di kalimat present perfect.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu naruh “already” atau “still” di slot ujung kalimat perfect negatif, padahal slot itu punyanya “yet”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat “hasn't” yang negatif dengan slot kosong di ujung klausa → tutup klausanya pakai “yet”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use a reflexive pronoun that matches the subject when subject and object are the same person
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner reaches for a plain object pronoun, 'each other', or the wrong-person reflexive because Indonesian 'diri' phrases never change form
templates.reasoningOperation: match the object back to the subject 'I' -> choose the first-person reflexive 'myself'
templates.stem: Nobody helped me — I taught ___ to swim by watching videos.

distractors.misconception: uses the plain object pronoun although subject and object are the same person
distractors.whyFails: 'I taught me' points the plain pronoun back at its own subject; when subject and object are the same person, English forces the reflexive 'myself'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “I taught me” nunjukin kata ganti biasa balik ke subjeknya sendiri; kalau subjek dan objek orangnya sama, bahasa Inggris wajib pakai “myself”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti objek biasa dipakai padahal subjek dan objeknya orang yang sama.

distractors.misconception: uses the reciprocal 'each other' with a singular subject
distractors.whyFails: 'Each other' describes two or more people doing something to one another; the subject here is only 'I', one person teaching that same person.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Each other” buat dua orang atau lebih yang saling; subjek di sini cuma “I”, satu orang yang ngajarin dirinya sendiri.
distractors.misconceptionId: “each other” yang artinya saling dipasang ke subjek tunggal.

distractors.misconception: picks a reflexive that does not match the person of the subject
distractors.whyFails: 'Himself' is the reflexive of 'he'; after the subject 'I' the reflexive must be first person: 'myself'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Himself” itu refleksifnya “he”; sesudah subjek “I”, refleksifnya harus orang pertama: “myself”.
distractors.misconceptionId: refleksifnya nggak ngikutin orang si subjek.

explanation.whyCorrect: The subject 'I' and the object are the same person, so the object must be the matching reflexive 'myself'.
explanation.rule: When subject and object refer to the same person, use the reflexive that agrees with the subject: I -> myself, he -> himself, we -> ourselves. 'Each other' needs two or more people acting on one another.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Me' is the plain object pronoun and cannot point back at its own subject; 'each other' needs a plural subject, but 'I' is one person; 'himself' is the reflexive for 'he', so it does not agree with 'I'.
explanation.howToAvoid: First match the object to the subject: the same person means a '-self' form, and the '-self' form must copy the subject's person.
explanation.memoryCue: 'I' looks in the mirror and sees 'myself' — never 'me', never someone else's '-self'.
explanation.ruleId: Kalau subjek dan objek orangnya sama, pakai refleksif yang seiring sama subjeknya: “I” → “myself”, “he” → “himself”, “we” → “ourselves”. “Each other” butuh dua orang atau lebih yang saling.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Subjek “I” dan objeknya orang yang sama, jadi objeknya harus refleksif yang cocok: “myself”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Me” itu kata ganti objek biasa, nggak bisa nunjuk balik ke subjeknya sendiri; “each other” butuh subjek jamak, padahal “I” cuma satu orang; “himself” refleksifnya “he”, nggak nyambung sama “I”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cocokin dulu objek ke subjek: orangnya sama berarti bentuk “-self”, dan bentuk “-self”-nya harus ngikutin orang si subjek.
explanation.memoryCueId: “I” ngaca dan lihat “myself” — bukan “me”, bukan “-self” punya orang lain.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai kata ganti refleksif yang cocok sama subjeknya waktu subjek dan objek orangnya sama.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ambil kata ganti objek biasa, “each other”, atau refleksif orang lain, soalnya frasa “diri” di bahasa Indonesia nggak pernah berubah bentuk.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cocokin objeknya balik ke subjek “I” → pilih refleksif orang pertama “myself”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Replace a repeated countable noun with 'one' or 'ones' instead of repeating it or using 'it'
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner repeats the noun or uses definite 'it' instead of the indefinite substitute 'one', because Indonesian simply drops the repeated noun
templates.reasoningOperation: find the repeated countable noun after 'a new' -> substitute the singular indefinite 'one'
templates.stem: My old camera broke, so yesterday I bought a new ___.

distractors.misconception: uses definite 'it' after 'a new' where the indefinite substitute 'one' is needed
distractors.whyFails: 'A new it' is impossible: 'it' names the exact old camera, while 'a new' introduces a different, not-yet-identified camera — that slot takes 'one'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “A new it” nggak jalan: “it” nunjuk persis kamera lama, sementara “a new” ngenalin kamera lain yang belum jelas — slot itu jatahnya “one”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “it” yang definit dipasang sesudah “a new”, padahal slotnya minta pengganti tak tentu “one”.

distractors.misconception: picks plural 'ones' to replace a single noun
distractors.whyFails: 'A new ones' mixes the singular article 'a' with the plural substitute 'ones'; only one camera is bought, so it must be 'one'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “A new ones” nyampur artikel tunggal “a” sama pengganti jamak “ones”; yang dibeli cuma satu kamera, jadi harus “one”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “ones” jamak dipakai buat gantiin satu benda doang.

distractors.misconception: repeats the replaced noun and stacks the substitute 'one' after it
distractors.whyFails: 'A new camera one' says the noun twice — once as 'camera' and again as its substitute 'one'; English keeps either the noun or 'one', never both.
distractors.whyFailsId: “A new camera one” nyebut bendanya dua kali — sekali “camera”, sekali pengganti “one”; bahasa Inggris cuma pakai salah satu, nomina atau “one”.
distractors.misconceptionId: nominanya diulang terus masih ditumpuk lagi sama pengganti “one”.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'A new ___' introduces a new, not-yet-identified camera, and the singular substitute for a countable noun in that slot is 'one'.
explanation.rule: Use 'one' to replace a singular countable noun and 'ones' for a plural one; 'it' points to one specific, already-identified thing and never follows 'a new'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'It' points back at the broken camera itself and cannot follow the indefinite 'a new'; 'ones' is plural, but only one camera was bought; 'camera one' repeats the noun and stacks the substitute on top of it.
explanation.howToAvoid: After 'a/an + adjective', reach for 'one'; keep 'it' for the exact thing you already named.
explanation.memoryCue: 'A new one' opens the box; 'it' is the old thing you already know.
explanation.ruleId: Pakai “one” buat gantiin nomina tercacah tunggal dan “ones” buat yang jamak; “it” nunjuk satu benda spesifik yang udah jelas dan nggak pernah nempel sesudah “a new”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “A new ___” ngenalin kamera baru yang belum jelas yang mana, dan pengganti tunggal buat nomina tercacah di slot itu ya “one”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “It” nunjuk balik ke kamera lama yang rusak dan nggak bisa nempel sesudah “a new”; “ones” itu jamak, padahal yang dibeli cuma satu; “camera one” ngulang nominanya terus numpuk pengganti di atasnya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Sesudah “a/an + kata sifat”, ambil “one”; simpan “it” buat benda persis yang udah kamu sebut.
explanation.memoryCueId: “A new one” buka kotak baru; “it” barang lama yang udah kamu kenal.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Ganti nomina tercacah yang keulang pakai “one” atau “ones”, bukan ngulang nominanya atau pakai “it”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngulang nominanya atau naruh “it”, soalnya bahasa Indonesia biasa ngilangin nomina yang keulang begitu aja.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temuin nomina tercacah yang keulang sesudah “a new” → ganti pakai “one” tunggal tak tentu

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Complain about someone else's repeated annoying behaviour with 'wish + would'
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner freezes 'wish' with a past simple or plain present form, turning a demand that another person change their repeated behaviour into a wished-for state
templates.reasoningOperation: spot the annoyance cues 'keeps borrowing' + 'drives me crazy' about another person -> choose 'wish + would + base' for a demanded change of willed behaviour
templates.stem: My flatmate keeps borrowing my charger, and it drives me crazy. I wish he ___ doing that.

distractors.misconception: treats a complaint about repeated behaviour as a wished-for state with wish + past simple
distractors.whyFails: 'Wish + past simple' pictures a present state the speaker would like to be different, as in 'I wish I lived closer'; pressing another person to change a repeated, willed action needs 'wish + would stop'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Wish + past simple” gambarin keadaan sekarang yang diharap beda, kayak “I wish I lived closer”; nuntut orang berhenti ngelakuin sesuatu yang diulang-ulang butuh “wish + would stop”.
distractors.misconceptionId: keluhan soal kebiasaan orang lain dibungkus “wish + past simple”.

distractors.misconception: keeping the present tense after 'wish', reading the situation as a real current fact
distractors.whyFails: 'I wish he stops' keeps a plain present after 'wish', but 'wish' never takes the real present; the complaint about willed behaviour requires 'would' plus the base form.
distractors.whyFailsId: “I wish he stops” nahan bentuk kini polos sesudah “wish”, padahal “wish” nggak pernah nerima present nyata; keluhan perilaku butuh “would” plus kata dasar.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk sekarang dipertahanin sesudah “wish”.

distractors.misconception: puts future 'will' after 'wish', calquing Indonesian 'akan'
distractors.whyFails: 'Wish' does not combine with 'will': English uses 'hope + will' for realistic expectations and 'wish + would' for complaints, so 'wish he will stop' is not a valid frame.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Wish” nggak jalan bareng “will”: harapan realistis pakai “hope + will”, keluhan pakai “wish + would”, jadi “wish he will stop” bukan bingkai yang sah.
distractors.misconceptionId: “will” dipasang sesudah “wish” karena kebawa makna “akan”.

explanation.whyCorrect: The speaker is annoyed by a repeated, willed action of another person, and 'wish + subject + would + base' is exactly the frame English uses to press for that change: 'I wish he would stop.'
explanation.rule: Use 'wish + would' to complain about someone else's repeated behaviour you want changed; 'wish + past simple' is for states, and '*I wish I would' is impossible because you control your own actions.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Stopped' turns the complaint into a wished-for state, which suits 'I wish I lived closer' but not a demand that someone change; 'stops' leaves a real present that 'wish' never accepts; 'will stop' belongs after 'hope', not 'wish'.
explanation.howToAvoid: When the irritation is about what somebody keeps doing, reach for 'wish + would'; save 'wish + past simple' for situations, not behaviour.
explanation.memoryCue: Annoying habit? 'I wish they would stop' — 'would' for the willed.
explanation.ruleId: Pakai “wish + would” buat ngeluh soal kebiasaan orang lain yang kamu pengin berubah; “wish + past simple” buat keadaan, dan “I wish I would” nggak ada karena tindakanmu sendiri kamu yang pegang kendalinya.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Yang bikin kesal itu kelakuan berulang orang lain yang bisa dia ubah sendiri, dan bingkainya memang “wish + subjek + would + kata dasar”: “I wish he would stop”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Stopped” ngubah keluhan jadi keadaan yang diharap beda, cocoknya buat “I wish I lived closer”, bukan nuntut orang berubah; “stops” ninggalin bentuk kini nyata yang nggak pernah diterima “wish”; “will stop” jodohnya “hope”, bukan “wish”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau yang bikin sebal itu kelakuan yang diulang-ulang orang lain, ambil “wish + would”; simpan “wish + past simple” buat situasi, bukan perilaku.
explanation.memoryCueId: Kebiasaan nyebelin? “I wish they would stop” — “would” buat yang disengaja.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Ngeluh soal kebiasaan nyebelin orang lain pakai “wish + would”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngunci “wish” ke past simple atau bentuk kini biasa, jadi tuntutan supaya orang lain ngubah kebiasaannya malah kedengaran kayak keadaan yang diharap beda.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali sinyal kesal “keeps borrowing” + “drives me crazy” soal orang lain → pilih “wish + would + kata dasar” buat perubahan perilaku yang dituntut

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Distinguish 'be/get used to + -ing' for current familiarity from 'used to + base' for finished past habits
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner reads the 'to' in 'be used to' as an infinitive marker and slots a base or finite verb after it, copying the past-habit pattern 'used to ride'
templates.reasoningOperation: spot the present-state cue 'After two years ... is finally used to' -> treat this 'to' as a preposition and choose the -ing form
templates.stem: After two years in Medan, Laras is finally used to ___ her motorbike through the rush-hour traffic.

distractors.misconception: reads the 'to' in 'be used to' as an infinitive marker, copying the past-habit pattern
distractors.whyFails: 'Is used to ride' treats 'to' as infinitival, but in 'be used to' the 'to' is a preposition, so the verb must be 'riding'; 'used to ride' without 'is' would mean a past habit that has stopped.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Is used to ride” baca “to”-nya sebagai infinitive, padahal di “be used to” itu preposisi, jadi kata kerjanya harus “riding”; “used to ride” tanpa “is” malah berarti kebiasaan lampau yang udah berhenti.
distractors.misconceptionId: “to” di “be used to” dibaca sebagai penanda infinitive.

distractors.misconception: slots a finite past form after the preposition 'to' in 'be used to'
distractors.whyFails: 'Used to rode' puts the finite past 'rode' after a preposition; prepositions only accept the -ing form, and the sentence describes Laras's situation now anyway.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Used to rode” naruh bentuk lampau berubah sesudah preposisi; preposisi cuma nerima bentuk -ing, dan kalimatnya juga lagi ngomongin keadaan Laras sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk lampau ditaruh sesudah preposisi “to” karena kebawa rasa lampau “used to”.

distractors.misconception: inserts infinitive 'be' after 'used to' although this 'to' is a preposition needing -ing
distractors.whyFails: 'Is used to be riding' reads the pattern as 'to + infinitive' and inserts 'be', but the preposition 'to' takes 'riding' directly, with no 'be' in between.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Is used to be riding” baca polanya sebagai “to + infinitive” terus nyelipin “be”, padahal preposisi “to” langsung nerima “riding” tanpa “be” di tengah.
distractors.misconceptionId: “be” infinitive diselipin sesudah “used to”, padahal “to”-nya preposisi.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Is used to' here means Laras is now familiar with the traffic, and in this pattern 'to' is a preposition, so the verb after it takes -ing: 'used to riding'.
explanation.rule: 'Be/get used to + -ing' means someone is, or becomes, familiar with something now; 'used to + base' is a different pattern for past habits that have stopped.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Ride' treats the 'to' as an infinitive marker on the model of past-habit 'used to ride'; 'rode' puts a finite past form after a preposition, which no preposition allows; 'be riding' also misreads 'to' as infinitival and inserts an unneeded 'be'.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check what stands before 'used to': a form of 'be' or 'get' means familiarity, so the next verb needs -ing; no 'be' means the past-habit pattern with a base verb.
explanation.memoryCue: 'Be' in front flips the 'to' into a preposition: am used to doing, got used to doing.
explanation.ruleId: “Be/get used to + -ing” artinya sekarang udah atau jadi terbiasa sama sesuatu; “used to + kata dasar” itu pola lain buat kebiasaan lampau yang udah berhenti.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Is used to” di sini artinya Laras sekarang udah terbiasa sama macetnya, dan di pola ini “to” itu preposisi, jadi kata kerja sesudahnya pakai -ing: “used to riding”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Ride” baca “to”-nya sebagai penanda infinitive niru pola kebiasaan lampau “used to ride”; “rode” naruh bentuk lampau berubah sesudah preposisi, dan itu nggak pernah boleh; “be riding” juga salah baca “to”-nya terus nyelipin “be” yang nggak perlu.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek apa yang berdiri di depan “used to”: kalau ada bentuk “be” atau “get”, artinya keterbiasaan, jadi kata kerja berikutnya pakai -ing; kalau nggak ada “be”, itu pola kebiasaan lampau dengan kata dasar.
explanation.memoryCueId: Ada “be” di depan, “to”-nya berubah jadi preposisi: “am used to doing”, “got used to doing”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Bedain “be/get used to + -ing” buat keterbiasaan sekarang dari “used to + kata dasar” buat kebiasaan lampau yang udah berhenti.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu baca “to” di “be used to” sebagai penanda infinitive, jadi sesudahnya kamu taruh kata dasar atau bentuk lampau kayak di pola “used to ride”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali sinyal keadaan sekarang “After two years ... is finally used to” → perlakukan “to” ini sebagai preposisi dan pilih bentuk -ing

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Choose the bare infinitive after 'would rather' instead of the to-infinitive that follows 'prefer'
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner generalizes the to-infinitive to every second verb, producing 'would rather to stay' on the model of 'prefer to stay'
templates.reasoningOperation: spot the frame ''d rather ... than + bare verb' -> choose the bare infinitive so both halves of the comparison match
templates.stem: It's been an exhausting week, so I'd rather ___ home tonight than join the office dinner.

distractors.misconception: generalizes the to-infinitive to 'would rather' on the model of 'prefer to'
distractors.whyFails: 'I'd rather to stay' is never grammatical: 'would rather' takes the bare infinitive, unlike 'prefer', which does take 'to + verb'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “I'd rather to stay” nggak pernah gramatikal: “would rather” nerimanya kata dasar polos, beda dari “prefer” yang memang pakai “to + kata kerja”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “would rather” ikut-ikutan pola “prefer to”, jadi ketambahan “to”.

distractors.misconception: imports the gerund complement of 'prefer' into the 'would rather' pattern
distractors.whyFails: 'I'd rather staying' has no valid source: 'would rather' accepts only the bare infinitive, while '-ing' belongs to patterns like 'prefer staying'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “I'd rather staying” nggak punya pola asal yang sah: “would rather” cuma nerima kata dasar polos, sedangkan -ing jatahnya pola kayak “prefer staying”.
distractors.misconceptionId: pelengkap -ing punya “prefer” dibawa ke pola “would rather”.

distractors.misconception: backshifts to a past form after 'would rather' although no second subject intervenes
distractors.whyFails: A past form after 'would rather' is only correct when a different subject follows, as in 'I'd rather you stayed'; with the same subject the verb stays bare.
distractors.whyFailsId: Bentuk lampau sesudah “would rather” cuma benar kalau ada subjek lain yang nyela, kayak “I'd rather you stayed”; kalau subjeknya sama, kata kerjanya tetap kata dasar.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerjanya digeser ke bentuk lampau padahal nggak ada subjek kedua.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Would rather' takes the bare infinitive, and the 'than' half of the comparison already shows it ('than join'), so the blank must be the matching bare form 'stay'.
explanation.rule: 'Would rather + bare infinitive (+ than + bare infinitive)' states a preference between actions; 'prefer' is the pattern that takes 'to + verb' or '-ing'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'To stay' copies the 'prefer to stay' pattern onto 'would rather', which never takes 'to'; 'staying' likewise imports the 'prefer staying' gerund; 'stayed' is only possible when a different subject follows, as in 'I'd rather you stayed'.
explanation.howToAvoid: Hear ''d rather'? Strip the verb bare — and glance at the 'than' half, which displays the bare form the blank must match.
explanation.memoryCue: 'Rather' hates 'to': I'd rather stay, I'd rather walk.
explanation.ruleId: “Would rather + kata dasar polos (+ than + kata dasar polos)” nyatain pilihan antar tindakan; “prefer” itu pola yang pakai “to + kata kerja” atau -ing.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Would rather” nerimanya kata dasar polos, dan belahan “than”-nya udah nunjukin itu (“than join”), jadi isiannya harus bentuk polos yang serupa: “stay”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “To stay” niru pola “prefer to stay” ke “would rather” yang nggak pernah pakai “to”; “staying” juga ngimpor gerund punya “prefer staying”; “stayed” cuma mungkin kalau ada subjek lain yang nyela, kayak “I'd rather you stayed”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Dengar “'d rather”? Bikin kata kerjanya polos — dan lirik belahan “than”-nya, di situ kelihatan bentuk polos yang harus dicocokin.
explanation.memoryCueId: “Rather” anti sama “to”: yang benar “would rather stay”, bukan “would rather to stay”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Milih kata dasar polos sesudah “would rather”, bukan “to + kata kerja” yang jodohnya “prefer”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nyamaratain semua kata kerja kedua harus pakai “to”, jadi keluar “would rather to stay” niru pola “prefer to stay”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali bingkai “'d rather ... than + kata dasar” → pilih kata dasar polos biar dua belahan perbandingannya seimbang

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Report an unmet schedule or expectation with the full pattern 'be supposed to'
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner drops the auxiliary 'be' before 'supposed to', mirroring Indonesian sentences that need no linking verb
templates.reasoningOperation: spot the schedule-versus-reality contrast 'in ten minutes / hasn't even arrived' -> assemble the full passive-shaped pattern 'is supposed to'
templates.stem: The ferry ___ leave in ten minutes, but the crew hasn't even arrived yet.

distractors.misconception: drops the obligatory 'be' before 'supposed to'
distractors.whyFails: 'The ferry supposed to leave' has no finite verb: 'supposed' is a participle and cannot carry the clause alone, so a form of 'be' is obligatory.
distractors.whyFailsId: “The ferry supposed to leave” nggak punya kata kerja berubah: “supposed” itu participle yang nggak bisa mikul klausanya sendirian, jadi bentuk “be”-nya wajib ada.
distractors.misconceptionId: “be” di depan “supposed to” dihilangin, kebawa kalimat Indonesia yang nggak butuh kata penghubung.

distractors.misconception: treats 'suppose' as an ordinary present-tense verb instead of the passive pattern 'be supposed to'
distractors.whyFails: 'The ferry supposes to leave' makes the ferry actively suppose something; the schedule-expectation meaning only exists in the passive-shaped 'is supposed to'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “The ferry supposes to leave” bikin kapalnya yang aktif menduga-duga; makna jadwal atau ekspektasi cuma ada di pola berbentuk pasif “is supposed to”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “suppose” dipakai kayak kata kerja kini biasa, padahal maknanya cuma ada di pola pasif “be supposed to”.

distractors.misconception: forces a progressive onto the fixed passive participle 'supposed'
distractors.whyFails: 'Is supposing to' turns the frozen participle into a progressive; the pattern is fixed as 'be + supposed + to' and never appears with '-ing'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Is supposing to” ngubah participle beku jadi bentuk sedang-berlangsung; polanya mati di “be + supposed + to” dan nggak pernah muncul pakai -ing.
distractors.misconceptionId: participle beku “supposed” dipaksa jadi bentuk -ing.

explanation.whyCorrect: The timetable says one thing and reality another, and that unmet expectation is exactly what 'be supposed to' marks: 'The ferry is supposed to leave in ten minutes.'
explanation.rule: 'Be supposed to + base verb' reports what a rule, schedule, or arrangement expects — which may not actually happen; the auxiliary 'be' is obligatory because 'supposed' is a participle.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Supposed to' drops the obligatory 'is', leaving the participle with no verb to carry the sentence; 'supposes to' treats 'suppose' as an ordinary present verb although the pattern is passive in form; 'is supposing to' forces a progressive onto a fixed participle.
explanation.howToAvoid: Never let 'supposed to' stand alone as the verb of the sentence — always weld a form of 'be' in front of it.
explanation.memoryCue: No 'be', no 'supposed to': is/was supposed to, always.
explanation.ruleId: “Be supposed to + kata dasar” ngelaporin apa yang diharapkan aturan, jadwal, atau kesepakatan — dan itu bisa aja nggak kejadian; kata bantu “be”-nya wajib karena “supposed” itu participle.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Jadwal ngomong satu hal, kenyataan ngomong hal lain, dan ekspektasi yang meleset kayak gitu persis kerjaannya “be supposed to”: “The ferry is supposed to leave in ten minutes”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Supposed to” ngilangin “is” yang wajib, jadi participle-nya nggak punya kata kerja buat mikul kalimat; “supposes to” memperlakukan “suppose” kayak kata kerja kini biasa padahal polanya berbentuk pasif; “is supposing to” maksa participle beku jadi bentuk -ing.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Jangan pernah biarin “supposed to” berdiri sendiri jadi kata kerja kalimat — selalu las bentuk “be” di depannya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Nggak ada “be”, nggak ada “supposed to”: selalu “is/was supposed to”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Ngelaporin jadwal atau ekspektasi yang meleset pakai pola lengkap “be supposed to”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngilangin “be” di depan “supposed to”, kebawa kalimat Indonesia yang nggak butuh kata penghubung.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali kontras jadwal vs kenyataan “in ten minutes / hasn't even arrived” → rakit pola lengkap berbentuk pasif “is supposed to”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use the unreal past simple after 'it's high time' to press for an overdue action
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner matches the tense to the feel of 'sudah waktunya' and puts a present or future form after 'it's high time'
templates.reasoningOperation: spot the overdue-action cue 'complaining for months' after 'it's high time' -> shift the verb into the unreal past simple
templates.stem: People have been complaining for months, so it's high time the council ___ the potholes.

distractors.misconception: keeps a present-tense verb after 'it's high time', calquing 'sudah waktunya' plus a present verb
distractors.whyFails: 'It's high time the council repairs' uses the real present, but this idiom requires the unreal past simple even though the meaning is about now.
distractors.whyFailsId: “It's high time the council repairs” pakai bentuk kini nyata, padahal idiom ini minta past simple tak nyata walaupun maknanya soal sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: sesudah “it's high time” kata kerjanya dibiarin bentuk kini, kebawa pola “sudah waktunya” plus kata kerja biasa.

distractors.misconception: marks the clause after 'it's high time' with future 'will' because the action is still to come
distractors.whyFails: 'It's high time the council will repair' adds a future marker the idiom never allows; the overdue-now meaning is carried by the past form 'repaired'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “It's high time the council will repair” nambahin penanda masa depan yang nggak pernah diizinin idiom ini; makna telat-sekarang justru dibawa bentuk lampau “repaired”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “will” ditambahin sesudah “it's high time” karena aksinya memang belum terjadi.

distractors.misconception: uses the present progressive after 'it's high time' as if the action were already under way
distractors.whyFails: 'Is repairing' would claim the repair is already happening, which the months of complaints deny; the frame also requires a past, not present, form.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Is repairing” bakal ngeklaim perbaikannya udah jalan, padahal keluhan berbulan-bulan justru bilang belum; bingkainya juga minta bentuk lampau, bukan kini.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk sedang-berlangsung dipakai sesudah “it's high time”, seolah aksinya udah jalan.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'It's high time' presses for something overdue, and the clause after it takes the unreal past simple even though the meaning is now: 'it's high time the council repaired.'
explanation.rule: 'It's (high/about) time + subject + past simple' says an action is overdue now or urgently expected; the past form signals unreality, not past time.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Repairs' matches the Indonesian feel of 'sudah waktunya' plus a present verb, but this idiom rejects the real present; 'will repair' adds a future marker the frame never allows; 'is repairing' would claim the work is already under way, which the complaint denies.
explanation.howToAvoid: After 'it's high time', push the verb one step back into the past even though you mean today.
explanation.memoryCue: 'High time' = past form, present pressure.
explanation.ruleId: “It's (high/about) time + subjek + past simple” bilang sebuah aksi udah telat sekarang atau mendesak banget; bentuk lampaunya nandain ketaknyataan, bukan waktu lampau.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “It's high time” ngedesak sesuatu yang udah telat, dan klausa sesudahnya pakai past simple tak nyata walaupun maknanya sekarang: “it's high time the council repaired”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Repairs” cocok sama rasa “sudah waktunya” plus kata kerja biasa, tapi idiom ini nolak bentuk kini nyata; “will repair” nambahin penanda masa depan yang nggak pernah diizinin bingkai ini; “is repairing” bakal ngeklaim kerjaannya udah jalan, padahal keluhannya bilang belum.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Sesudah “it's high time”, dorong kata kerjanya mundur satu langkah ke bentuk lampau walaupun maksudmu hari ini.
explanation.memoryCueId: “High time” = bentuk lampau, desakan sekarang.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai past simple tak nyata sesudah “it's high time” buat desakan yang udah telat.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nyocokin tense ke rasa “sudah waktunya”, jadi sesudah “it's high time” malah naruh bentuk kini atau “will”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali sinyal telat “complaining for months” sesudah “it's high time” → geser kata kerjanya ke past simple tak nyata

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Mark an openly counterfactual comparison after 'as if' with the unreal past 'were'
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner keeps a real, present-tense comparison after 'as if' even when the sentence openly denies that the comparison is true
templates.reasoningOperation: spot the denial cue 'a very different story' after 'as if' -> choose the unreal past 'were'
templates.stem: Rian spends money as if he ___ a millionaire, but his bank balance tells a very different story.

distractors.misconception: keeps the real-possibility present after 'as if' although the sentence denies the comparison
distractors.whyFails: 'As if he is a millionaire' would leave the comparison possibly true, but the clause about his bank balance rules that out, so the unreal past 'were' is required.
distractors.whyFailsId: “As if he is a millionaire” bakal ninggalin perbandingannya mungkin benar, padahal klausa soal saldo banknya nutup kemungkinan itu, jadi wajib past tak nyata “were”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk kini nyata dipertahanin sesudah “as if”, padahal kalimatnya sendiri nyangkal perbandingannya.

distractors.misconception: reads 'as if' as reporting genuine experience with the present perfect
distractors.whyFails: 'As if he has been a millionaire' asserts real experience up to now, which contradicts the sentence's point that he is not one at all.
distractors.whyFailsId: “As if he has been a millionaire” ngeklaim pengalaman nyata sampai sekarang, dan itu nabrak inti kalimatnya bahwa dia sama sekali bukan jutawan.
distractors.misconceptionId: “as if” dibaca kayak laporan pengalaman nyata, jadi dipasangin present perfect.

distractors.misconception: puts conditional 'would' inside the 'as if' clause as if it were a result clause
distractors.whyFails: 'Would' marks the result clause of a conditional; after 'as if', the unreality is signalled by the past form 'were', not by 'would be'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Would” itu penanda klausa hasil kalimat pengandaian; sesudah “as if”, ketaknyataan ditandai bentuk lampau “were”, bukan “would be”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “would” diselipin ke dalam klausa “as if”, ketukar sama klausa hasil pengandaian.

explanation.whyCorrect: The sentence openly denies the comparison — his bank balance shows he is not a millionaire — so 'as if' takes the unreal past: 'as if he were a millionaire.'
explanation.rule: 'As if / as though + past simple' marks a comparison the speaker presents as unreal; a present form after 'as if' is reserved for comparisons that may genuinely be true.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Is' presents the millionaire idea as possibly true, clashing with the stated denial; 'has been' asserts genuine experience up to now, which the sentence rules out; 'would be' drags a conditional-result form into the 'as if' clause, where it has no place.
explanation.howToAvoid: When the sentence itself tells you the comparison is false, shift the verb after 'as if' into the past — 'were' for 'be'.
explanation.memoryCue: Unreal 'as if' loves 'were': he talks as if he were the boss.
explanation.ruleId: “As if / as though + past simple” nandain perbandingan yang disodorin sebagai tak nyata; bentuk kini sesudah “as if” jatahnya perbandingan yang mungkin beneran terjadi.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Kalimatnya terang-terangan nyangkal perbandingannya — saldo banknya nunjukin dia bukan jutawan — jadi “as if” pakai past tak nyata: “as if he were a millionaire”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Is” nyodorin ide jutawan itu sebagai mungkin benar, nabrak penyangkalan yang udah ditulis; “has been” ngeklaim pengalaman nyata sampai sekarang, yang justru ditutup kalimatnya; “would be” narik bentuk klausa hasil pengandaian ke dalam klausa “as if” yang bukan tempatnya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau kalimatnya sendiri ngasih tahu perbandingannya bohong, geser kata kerja sesudah “as if” ke bentuk lampau — “were” buat “be”.
explanation.memoryCueId: “As if” yang tak nyata jodohnya “were”: “he talks as if he were the boss”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Nandain perbandingan yang jelas-jelas nggak nyata sesudah “as if” pakai past tak nyata “were”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nahan bentuk kini yang nyata sesudah “as if” padahal kalimatnya sendiri bilang perbandingannya nggak benar.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali sinyal penyangkalan “a very different story” sesudah “as if” → pilih past tak nyata “were”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Express that a completed action was unnecessary in hindsight with 'needn't have + past participle'
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner treats 'didn't need to' and 'needn't have' as interchangeable, losing the signal that the action was actually carried out for nothing
templates.reasoningOperation: spot that the action is done ('printed') but pointless ('reads everything on screen') -> choose 'needn't have' before the past participle
templates.stem: You ___ printed the whole report — the committee reads everything on screen these days.

distractors.misconception: uses 'didn't need to' where the sentence shows the unnecessary action was actually done
distractors.whyFails: 'Didn't need to' must be followed by the base form 'print', so it cannot stand before 'printed'; it also leaves open whether any printing happened, while this sentence shows it did.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Didn't need to” wajib diikuti kata dasar “print”, jadi nggak bisa berdiri di depan “printed”; bentuk itu juga ngegantungin apakah nyetaknya kejadian, padahal kalimat ini nunjukin udah kejadian.
distractors.misconceptionId: “didn't need to” dipakai padahal kalimatnya nunjukin tindakannya terlanjur dilakukan.

distractors.misconception: swaps absent past necessity for a negative deduction with 'mustn't have'
distractors.whyFails: 'Mustn't have printed' would be a deduction that the printing never happened, contradicting the printed report in front of everyone; it does not mean 'it wasn't necessary'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Mustn't have printed” itu simpulan bahwa nyetaknya nggak pernah kejadian, nabrak laporan tercetak yang ada di depan mata; artinya bukan “nggak perlu”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “mustn't have” dikira artinya “nggak perlu”, padahal itu simpulan bahwa sesuatu tidak terjadi.

distractors.misconception: uses present 'needn't' with a past participle, leaving the finished act unmarked
distractors.whyFails: 'You needn't printed' has no 'have' to license the participle; plain 'needn't' pairs with a base form and points to present necessity, not a finished act.
distractors.whyFailsId: “You needn't printed” nggak punya “have” buat ngizinin participle-nya; “needn't” polos jodohnya kata dasar dan nunjuk keperluan sekarang, bukan tindakan yang udah selesai.
distractors.misconceptionId: “needn't” polos dipasangin past participle, padahal tanpa “have” dia nunjuk keperluan sekarang.

explanation.whyCorrect: The report was printed, and only afterwards does it turn out to have been unnecessary; 'needn't have + past participle' is precisely the form that says a completed action was pointless.
explanation.rule: 'Needn't have + past participle' means someone did something that turns out to have been unnecessary; 'didn't need to + base' merely says there was no necessity, without confirming the action happened.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Didn't need to' requires the base form 'print', so it cannot precede 'printed', and it would leave the printing unconfirmed; 'mustn't have' is a deduction that something did not happen, contradicting the printed report; 'needn't' without 'have' pairs with a base form and points to present necessity.
explanation.howToAvoid: Action already done and wasted? Reach for 'needn't have' plus the participle; if you only mean there was no obligation, use 'didn't need to' with the base form.
explanation.memoryCue: 'Needn't have done' = did it for nothing.
explanation.ruleId: “Needn't have + past participle” artinya seseorang terlanjur ngelakuin sesuatu yang ternyata nggak perlu; “didn't need to + kata dasar” cuma bilang nggak ada keharusan, tanpa mastiin tindakannya kejadian.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Laporannya udah dicetak, dan baru belakangan ketahuan itu nggak perlu; “needn't have + past participle” persis bentuk buat bilang tindakan yang udah selesai itu sia-sia.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Didn't need to” minta kata dasar “print”, jadi nggak bisa berdiri di depan “printed”, dan dia ngegantungin apakah nyetaknya kejadian; “mustn't have” itu simpulan bahwa sesuatu nggak terjadi, nabrak laporan yang udah tercetak; “needn't” tanpa “have” jodohnya kata dasar dan nunjuk keperluan sekarang.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tindakannya udah terlanjur dan sia-sia? Ambil “needn't have” plus participle; kalau maksudmu cuma nggak ada kewajiban, pakai “didn't need to” dengan kata dasar.
explanation.memoryCueId: “Needn't have done” = udah dikerjain, ternyata percuma.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Bilang kalau tindakan yang terlanjur dilakukan ternyata nggak perlu pakai “needn't have + past participle”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nganggep “didn't need to” dan “needn't have” bisa saling tukar, jadi sinyal bahwa tindakannya terlanjur dilakukan sia-sia ikut hilang.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali bahwa tindakannya udah terjadi (“printed”) tapi sia-sia (“reads everything on screen”) → pilih “needn't have” di depan past participle

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Build the paired correlative 'no sooner ... than' with subject-auxiliary inversion and the past perfect
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner fronts 'no sooner' for emphasis but keeps ordinary subject-verb order, as Indonesian never inverts after a fronted adverbial
templates.reasoningOperation: spot fronted 'No sooner ... than' -> invert 'had' before the subject and keep the past perfect participle
templates.stem: No sooner ___ the presentation than the projector broke down.

distractors.misconception: fronts 'no sooner' but keeps ordinary subject-auxiliary order
distractors.whyFails: With 'No sooner' fronted, inversion is obligatory: 'No sooner we had begun' keeps statement order and is ungrammatical; only 'No sooner had we begun' works.
distractors.whyFailsId: Kalau “No sooner” dimajuin, inversinya wajib: “No sooner we had begun” nahan urutan kalimat berita dan jadi nggak gramatikal; yang jalan cuma “No sooner had we begun”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “no sooner” udah dimajuin, tapi urutan subjek dan kata bantunya masih urutan kalimat biasa.

distractors.misconception: inverts correctly but leaves a bare verb after 'had'
distractors.whyFails: 'Had we begin' pairs 'had' with a bare form; the past perfect needs the participle 'begun'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Had we begin” masangin “had” sama bentuk dasar; past perfect butuhnya participle “begun”.
distractors.misconceptionId: inversinya udah benar, tapi kata kerja sesudah “had” dibiarin bentuk dasar.

distractors.misconception: uses plain past-simple statement order, ignoring both the inversion and the past perfect
distractors.whyFails: 'No sooner we began' neither inverts nor uses the past perfect; the fronted 'no sooner ... than' frame demands 'had' before the subject plus a participle.
distractors.whyFailsId: “No sooner we began” nggak ngebalik urutan dan nggak pakai past perfect; bingkai “no sooner ... than” di depan nuntut “had” sebelum subjek plus participle.
distractors.misconceptionId: dipakai urutan kalimat biasa dengan past simple, padahal “no sooner” di depan minta inversi plus past perfect.

explanation.whyCorrect: Fronting 'No sooner' forces the auxiliary before the subject, and the first of the two past events takes the past perfect: 'No sooner had we begun ... than the projector broke down.'
explanation.rule: 'No sooner + had + subject + past participle + than + past simple' reports two events in immediate sequence; the fronted negative opener makes subject-auxiliary inversion obligatory, and 'no sooner' pairs with 'than', never 'when'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'We had begun' keeps statement word order although the fronted 'no sooner' demands inversion; 'had we begin' inverts but leaves the verb bare where 'had' needs 'begun'; 'we began' ignores both the inversion and the past perfect the pattern requires.
explanation.howToAvoid: See 'No sooner' at the front with 'than' later? Flip 'had' before the subject and finish with the participle.
explanation.memoryCue: No sooner HAD I done ... THAN it happened.
explanation.ruleId: “No sooner + had + subjek + past participle + than + past simple” ngelaporin dua kejadian yang beruntun rapat; pembuka negatif di depan bikin inversi subjek-kata bantu wajib, dan “no sooner” jodohnya “than”, nggak pernah “when”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Majuin “No sooner” maksa kata bantunya pindah ke depan subjek, dan kejadian pertama dari dua peristiwa lampaunya pakai past perfect: “No sooner had we begun ... than the projector broke down”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “We had begun” nahan urutan kalimat berita padahal “no sooner” di depan nuntut inversi; “had we begin” udah ngebalik tapi kata kerjanya dibiarin dasar padahal “had” butuh “begun”; “we began” ngelewatin dua-duanya, inversi dan past perfect.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Lihat “No sooner” di depan dengan “than” menyusul? Balik “had” ke depan subjek dan tutup pakai participle.
explanation.memoryCueId: “No sooner HAD I done ... THAN it happened.”

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Ngerakit korelasi berpasangan “no sooner ... than” dengan inversi subjek-kata bantu plus past perfect.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu majuin “no sooner” buat penekanan tapi urutan subjek-kata kerjanya dibiarin biasa, karena bahasa Indonesia memang nggak pernah ngebalik urutan sesudah keterangan di depan.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali “No sooner ... than” di depan → balik “had” ke depan subjek dan pertahankan participle past perfect

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Open a concessive clause with 'however + adverb' rather than 'whatever' or a bare 'no matter'
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner treats 'however', 'whatever', and 'no matter' as interchangeable concessive openers regardless of the word class that follows them
templates.reasoningOperation: spot the adverb 'carefully' right after the blank in a concessive clause -> choose 'However', the only opener that attaches directly to an adverb
templates.stem: ___ carefully you word the email, someone in the office will still find a reason to complain.

distractors.misconception: equates 'whatever' with 'however' and attaches it to an adverb it cannot modify
distractors.whyFails: 'Whatever' pairs with nouns, as in 'whatever wording you choose'; it cannot modify the adverb 'carefully', which only 'however' can front.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Whatever” jodohnya kata benda, kayak “whatever wording you choose”; dia nggak bisa nempel ke adverbia “carefully”, yang cuma bisa dibuka “however”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “whatever” dikira sama dengan “however”, jadi ditempelin ke adverbia yang nggak bisa dia dampingi.

distractors.misconception: opens the concession with 'although' but keeps the fronted-adverb pattern that only '-ever' openers allow
distractors.whyFails: 'Although' must introduce a clause in normal order, as in 'Although you word it carefully'; 'Although carefully you word' is not a grammatical sequence.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Although” harus buka klausa urutan biasa, kayak “Although you word it carefully”; “Although carefully you word” bukan rangkaian yang gramatikal.
distractors.misconceptionId: “although” dipakai buat buka pola adverbia-di-depan, padahal dia cuma bisa buka klausa urutan biasa.

distractors.misconception: drops the obligatory 'how' after 'no matter' before an adverb
distractors.whyFails: 'No matter' cannot attach directly to 'carefully'; it needs a wh-word first: 'No matter how carefully you word the email'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “No matter” nggak bisa langsung nempel ke “carefully”; dia butuh kata tanya dulu: “No matter how carefully you word the email”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “no matter” ditempel langsung ke adverbia, padahal wajib ada “how” dulu.

explanation.whyCorrect: Only 'however' can stand directly before an adjective or adverb to open a concessive clause: 'However carefully you word the email' means 'no matter how carefully'.
explanation.rule: 'However + adjective/adverb + subject + verb' concedes that a quality, to any degree, will not change the result; 'whatever' pairs with nouns, and 'no matter' needs a wh-word such as 'how' before the adjective or adverb.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Whatever' modifies nouns, so it cannot attach to 'carefully'; 'Although' introduces a normally ordered clause and cannot be followed by a fronted adverb; 'No matter' is incomplete without 'how' before 'carefully'.
explanation.howToAvoid: If the very next word is an adjective or adverb, the opener must be 'however'; give 'whatever' a noun and give 'no matter' its 'how'.
explanation.memoryCue: 'However hard, however carefully' — 'however' owns the adverb.
explanation.ruleId: “However + adjektiva/adverbia + subjek + kata kerja” ngakuin bahwa sekuat apa pun kualitasnya, hasilnya nggak berubah; “whatever” jodohnya kata benda, dan “no matter” butuh kata tanya kayak “how” sebelum adjektiva atau adverbianya.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Cuma “however” yang bisa berdiri langsung di depan adjektiva atau adverbia buat buka klausa konsesif: “However carefully you word the email” artinya “sehati-hati apa pun”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Whatever” dampingannya kata benda, jadi nggak bisa nempel ke “carefully”; “Although” bukanya klausa urutan biasa dan nggak bisa langsung diikuti adverbia yang dimajuin; “No matter” belum lengkap tanpa “how” di depan “carefully”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau kata persis berikutnya adjektiva atau adverbia, pembukanya harus “however”; kasih “whatever” kata benda dan kasih “no matter” si “how”-nya.
explanation.memoryCueId: “However hard, however carefully” — adverbia itu punyanya “however”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Buka klausa konsesif dengan “however + adverbia”, bukan “whatever” atau “no matter” yang belum lengkap.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nganggep “however”, “whatever”, dan “no matter” bisa saling ganti tanpa lihat kelas kata yang nempel sesudahnya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali adverbia “carefully” persis sesudah isian di klausa konsesif → pilih “However”, satu-satunya pembuka yang bisa nempel langsung ke adverbia

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Replace a repeated verb phrase with the stranded auxiliary that matches the antecedent clause
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner completes an elliptical clause with an all-purpose 'do' or 'be' instead of echoing the auxiliary that built the first clause
templates.reasoningOperation: spot the present-perfect antecedent 'hasn't submitted ... yet' -> echo the same auxiliary, 'have', in the elliptical clause
templates.stem: Dewi hasn't submitted her thesis draft yet, but most of her classmates already ___.

distractors.misconception: echoes a perfect-built clause with 'be' instead of its own auxiliary 'have'
distractors.whyFails: 'Most of her classmates already are' would stand for a form of 'be', but the antecedent 'hasn't submitted yet' is built on 'have', so the echo must be 'have'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Most of her classmates already are” bakal mewakili bentuk “be”, padahal klausa induk “hasn't submitted yet” dibangun pakai “have”, jadi gemanya harus “have”.
distractors.misconceptionId: klausa yang dibangun “have” malah dijawab pakai “be”, kebawa pola satu kata penghubung serba-guna.

distractors.misconception: falls back on default 'do' although the antecedent clause is present perfect
distractors.whyFails: 'Already do' would stand for a present-simple habit; the sentence tracks a one-off completed submission marked by 'yet', so the perfect auxiliary 'have' is required.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Already do” bakal mewakili kebiasaan present simple; kalimatnya lagi ngikutin satu pengumpulan yang udah rampung dan ditandai “yet”, jadi kata bantu perfect “have” yang wajib.
distractors.misconceptionId: “do” dipakai sebagai kata bantu serba-guna, padahal klausa induknya dibangun pakai present perfect “have”.

distractors.misconception: shifts the stranded auxiliary into the past perfect although the sentence is anchored in the present
distractors.whyFails: 'Already had' forms a past perfect pointing to a moment before some past reference time, but this sentence is anchored in the present by 'hasn't ... yet'; what works is present-perfect 'have' or, in informal AmE, past-simple 'did'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Already had” membentuk past perfect yang nunjuk ke titik sebelum suatu acuan lampau, padahal kalimat ini berpijak di masa kini lewat “hasn't ... yet”; yang berterima “have” (present perfect) atau, dalam AmE informal, “did” + past simple.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu gantungnya digeser ke past perfect, padahal kalimatnya masih berpijak di masa kini dengan “yet”.

explanation.whyCorrect: The first clause is built on the present perfect 'hasn't submitted ... yet', so the elliptical clause echoes the same auxiliary: 'most of her classmates already have.'
explanation.rule: In verb-phrase ellipsis, a stranded auxiliary stands for the whole repeated verb phrase and must copy the tense and aspect of the antecedent clause: have/has for the present perfect, do/does for the present simple, and so on.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Are' answers with 'be', which plays no part in the perfect of 'hasn't submitted'; 'do' would stand for a present-simple habit, but the submission is a one-off act tracked with 'yet'; 'had' shifts to the past perfect although the sentence is anchored in the present.
explanation.howToAvoid: Before dropping the repeated verb phrase, look back at the auxiliary that built it and repeat exactly that one.
explanation.memoryCue: Echo the engine: hasn't she? — but the others have.
explanation.ruleId: Di elipsis frasa kerja, kata bantu yang digantung mewakili seluruh frasa kerja yang keulang dan wajib niru tense plus aspek klausa induknya: “have/has” buat present perfect, “do/does” buat present simple, dan seterusnya.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Klausa pertamanya dibangun pakai present perfect “hasn't submitted ... yet”, jadi klausa elipsisnya ngegemain kata bantu yang sama: “most of her classmates already have”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Are” jawabnya pakai “be” yang nggak ikut ngebangun perfect di “hasn't submitted”; “do” bakal mewakili kebiasaan present simple, padahal pengumpulannya aksi sekali jadi yang diikuti “yet”; “had” geser ke past perfect padahal kalimatnya berpijak di masa kini.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Sebelum ngebuang frasa kerja yang keulang, tengok dulu kata bantu yang ngebangunnya dan ulang persis yang itu.
explanation.memoryCueId: Ulangi kata bantu yang sama: dia “hasn't”, yang lain udah “have”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Ganti frasa kerja yang keulang pakai kata bantu gantung yang cocok sama klausa induknya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nutup klausa elipsis pakai “do” atau “be” serba-guna, bukan ngulang kata bantu yang dipakai klausa pertama.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali induk present perfect “hasn't submitted ... yet” → gemain kata bantu yang sama, “have”, di klausa elipsisnya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'but for' plus a noun phrase to compress an unreal negative condition into a formal conditional sentence
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner reaches for clause machinery like 'unless' or a truncated 'if not' because Indonesian 'kalau bukan karena' feels like it needs a conjunction, not a preposition
templates.reasoningOperation: spot a bare noun phrase before the comma plus 'would not have survived' in the result clause -> select 'But for', the only option that attaches an unreal condition directly to a noun phrase
templates.stem: ___ the surgeon's quick thinking, the patient would not have survived the night.

distractors.misconception: treats the conjunction 'unless' as if it could govern a bare noun phrase
distractors.whyFails: 'Unless' introduces a finite clause with its own verb; 'Unless the surgeon's quick thinking' has no verb, so no condition is ever formed.
distractors.whyFailsId: “unless” butuh klausa lengkap dengan kata kerjanya sendiri; “Unless the surgeon's quick thinking” nggak punya kata kerja, jadi syaratnya nggak kebentuk.
distractors.misconceptionId: “unless” dianggap bisa langsung nempel ke frasa benda tanpa kata kerja.

distractors.misconception: truncates the fixed frame 'if it had not been for' down to a bare 'if not'
distractors.whyFails: English allows 'if it had not been for' or 'had it not been for' before a noun phrase, but a bare 'if not' cannot govern one.
distractors.whyFailsId: yang sah itu “if it had not been for” atau “had it not been for” sebelum frasa benda; “if not” polos nggak bisa megang frasa benda.
distractors.misconceptionId: frasa baku “if it had not been for” dipotong jadi “if not” doang.

distractors.misconception: uses the exclusion preposition 'except' to build an unreal condition
distractors.whyFails: 'Except' removes an item from a set ('everyone except Rudi'); it cannot mean 'if X had not existed', so no conditional reading survives.
distractors.whyFailsId: “except” ngeluarin satu hal dari kelompok (“everyone except Rudi”); dia nggak bisa berarti “kalau X nggak ada”, jadi makna pengandaiannya hilang.
distractors.misconceptionId: “except” dipakai buat bikin pengandaian, padahal fungsinya cuma ngecualiin.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'But for the surgeon's quick thinking' packs the unreal condition 'if it had not been for her quick thinking' into one prepositional phrase, matching 'would not have survived'.
explanation.rule: 'But for + noun phrase' expresses an unreal negative condition in formal English and pairs with 'would' or 'would have' in the main clause.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Unless' and a bare 'if not' both need a finite clause rather than a noun phrase, and 'except' only excludes items from a set instead of setting up a condition.
explanation.howToAvoid: When only a noun phrase follows the gap and the main clause carries 'would (not) have', test whether the gap means 'if it had not been for' — that slot belongs to 'but for'.
explanation.memoryCue: 'But for you' = 'if it had not been for you' — one small phrase, one whole unreal condition.
explanation.ruleId: “But for” + frasa benda nyatain pengandaian negatif yang nggak kejadian; pasangannya “would/would have” di klausa utama.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “But for the surgeon's quick thinking” = “kalau bukan karena kesigapan si dokter bedah” — satu frasa, satu pengandaian utuh, cocok sama “would not have survived”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Unless” dan “if not” polos sama-sama butuh klausa lengkap, bukan frasa benda; “except” cuma ngeluarin item dari daftar, bukan bikin pengandaian.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau setelah titik kosong cuma ada frasa benda dan klausa utamanya pakai “would (not) have”, cek: maksudnya “kalau bukan karena”? Itu jatahnya “but for”.
explanation.memoryCueId: “But for you” = “kalau bukan karena kamu” — frasa kecil, pengandaian utuh.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “but for” + frasa benda buat madatin pengandaian “kalau bukan karena” di kalimat formal.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nyari konjungsi kayak “unless” atau motong “if not” karena “kalau bukan karena” kerasa butuh anak kalimat, padahal Inggris formal cukup satu preposisi.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat frasa benda polos sebelum koma + “would not have survived” di klausa hasil → pilih “But for”, satu-satunya opsi yang bisa bawa pengandaian lewat frasa benda

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use the semi-modal 'daren't' with a bare infinitive to say someone lacks the courage to do something
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner translates Indonesian 'tidak berani' word by word or treats modal 'dare' like an ordinary verb that needs 'to', so the negative ends up without a working operator
templates.reasoningOperation: read the cover-story consequence in the second clause -> the gap must mean 'lacks the courage to' -> select 'daren't', the semi-modal that carries its own negation and takes a bare infinitive
templates.stem: She ___ tell her manager the real reason for the delay, so she blames the traffic instead.

distractors.misconception: keeps modal 'daren't' but still adds 'to' before the verb
distractors.whyFails: As a modal, 'daren't' behaves like 'can't' or 'mustn't' and takes a bare infinitive; 'to' is only possible in the lexical system 'doesn't dare (to) tell'.
distractors.whyFailsId: sebagai modal, “daren't” kelakuannya kayak “can't” atau “mustn't”: wajib ketemu kata kerja dasar; “to” cuma boleh di sistem biasa “doesn't dare (to) tell”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “daren't” masih dikasih “to”, padahal modal minta kata kerja dasar.

distractors.misconception: negates 'dare' with bare 'not' and no operator, copying Indonesian 'tidak berani'
distractors.whyFails: English negation needs a finite operator: modal 'daren't' or do-support in 'doesn't dare'. 'She not dare tell' has neither, so the clause has no working verb form.
distractors.whyFailsId: negasi Inggris butuh operator finit: “daren't” atau “doesn't dare”; “she not dare tell” nggak punya dua-duanya, klausanya nggak jalan.
distractors.misconceptionId: “tidak berani” diterjemahin jadi “not dare” tanpa kata bantu apa pun.

distractors.misconception: treats 'dare' as an adjective and negates it with 'be'
distractors.whyFails: 'Dare' is a verb, not an adjective, so 'be' cannot negate it; the grammatical negatives are 'daren't tell' or 'doesn't dare (to) tell'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “dare” itu kata kerja, bukan kata sifat; “be” nggak bisa jadi negatornya — yang bener “daren't tell” atau “doesn't dare (to) tell”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “dare” dianggap kata sifat, jadi dinegasi pakai “be” kayak “is not brave”.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'She daren't tell' means she lacks the courage to tell: 'daren't' carries the negation itself and meets the bare infinitive 'tell' directly.
explanation.rule: Modal 'daren't' works like 'can't': negation is built in and it is followed by a bare infinitive without 'to'; the valid lexical alternative is 'doesn't dare (to) tell'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Daren't to' smuggles 'to' after a modal; 'not dare' has no finite operator at all; 'isn't dare' treats the verb 'dare' as an adjective negated with 'be'.
explanation.howToAvoid: When negating 'dare', commit to one system — modal 'daren't + bare verb' or lexical 'doesn't dare (to)' — and never mix or drop both operators.
explanation.memoryCue: 'Daren't' belongs to the 'can't' family: no 'to', no 'do', negation built in.
explanation.ruleId: Modal “daren't” kelakuannya kayak “can't”: negasinya udah nempel, diikuti kata kerja dasar tanpa “to”; alternatif sahnya “doesn't dare (to) tell”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “She daren't tell” = dia nggak berani cerita; “daren't” bawa negasi sendiri dan langsung ketemu “tell” bentuk dasar.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “daren't to” nyelipin “to” yang haram buat modal; “not dare” nggak punya operator finit sama sekali; “isn't dare” ngira “dare” itu kata sifat yang bisa dinegasi pakai “be”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Pas mau negasi “dare”, pilih satu sistem: modal (“daren't” + kata dasar) atau biasa (“doesn't dare (to)”) — jangan dicampur, jangan dilepas dua-duanya.
explanation.memoryCueId: “daren't” satu keluarga sama “can't”: tanpa “to”, tanpa “do”, negasinya udah nempel.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai semi-modal “daren't” + kata kerja dasar buat bilang nggak berani ngelakuin sesuatu.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nerjemahin “tidak berani” kata per kata atau ngasih “to” ke modal “dare”, jadi negasinya nggak punya operator yang bener.
templates.reasoningOperationId: baca akibatnya di klausa kedua (dia terus nyalahin macet) → titik kosong artinya “nggak berani” → pilih “daren't”: negasi udah nempel, kata kerjanya bentuk dasar tanpa “to”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use a possessive determiner before a gerund to name the doer of the action in formal complements
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner strings a pronoun plus verb after 'objected to' the way Indonesian strings 'keberatan dia merilis', so the gerund loses its -ing form or its doer takes the wrong case
templates.reasoningOperation: register the preposition 'to' after 'objected' -> the gap must be a noun-like -ing clause with its own doer -> select the possessive + gerund 'his releasing'
