templates.stem: The committee objected to ___ the findings before the external audit was complete.

distractors.misconception: inserts an infinitive after the preposition 'to' of 'object to'
distractors.whyFails: The 'to' in 'object to' is a preposition, not an infinitive marker; only an -ing form can follow it, so 'to release' has no slot there.
distractors.whyFailsId: “to” di “object to” itu preposisi, bukan penanda infinitif; setelahnya cuma bentuk -ing yang boleh — “to release” nggak punya slot di situ.
distractors.misconceptionId: setelah “objected to”, malah dipasang infinitif “to release”.

distractors.misconception: places subject-case 'he' before a gerund
distractors.whyFails: The subject form 'he' is only licensed in a finite clause of its own; the doer of a gerund takes possessive 'his' in formal style or object 'him', never 'he'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “he” cuma sah jadi subjek klausa finit; pelaku gerund pakai posesif “his” (formal) atau objek “him”, nggak pernah “he”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kasus subjek “he” ditaruh di depan gerund.

distractors.misconception: leaves a bare verb after a preposition instead of a gerund
distractors.whyFails: A preposition can only govern noun-type material, so the verb must appear as the gerund 'releasing'; the bare form 'release' cannot stand there.
distractors.whyFailsId: preposisi cuma bisa megang unsur sebangsa benda; “release” harus jadi gerund “releasing” dulu, bentuk dasar nggak bisa berdiri di situ.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerjanya dibiarin bentuk dasar tanpa -ing, kebawa kebiasaan bahasa Indonesia yang nggak ngerubah kata kerja.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Objected to his releasing the findings' makes the release itself the object of 'to': 'his' names the doer and 'releasing' is the noun-like form of the verb.
explanation.rule: After a preposition ('object to', 'insist on'), the doer of a gerund is written as a possessive in formal register: 'his releasing', 'their being late'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Him to release' plants an infinitive after a preposition; 'he releasing' uses a subject case that only finite clauses license; 'him release' leaves a bare verb no preposition can govern.
explanation.howToAvoid: After 'object to / insist on / approve of', run two checks: has the verb become -ing, and is the doer possessive (or at least object case)? Subject 'he' is never an option.
explanation.memoryCue: 'They objected to my being late' — possessive + -ing keeps it formal.
explanation.ruleId: Setelah preposisi (“object to”, “insist on”), pelaku gerund ditulis posesif di register formal: “his releasing”, “their being late”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “objected to his releasing the findings” = keberatan atas tindakan dia ngerilis temuan; “his” nandain pelakunya, “releasing” bentuk benda dari kata kerjanya.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “him to release” nyelipin infinitif setelah preposisi; “he releasing” pakai kasus subjek yang cuma sah di klausa finit; “him release” ninggalin kata kerja telanjang yang nggak bisa dipegang preposisi.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Habis “object to / insist on / approve of”, cek dua hal: kata kerjanya udah jadi -ing? pelakunya udah posesif (atau minimal bentuk objek)? “he” nggak pernah boleh.
explanation.memoryCueId: “They objected to my being late” — posesif + -ing, formalnya begitu.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai kata ganti posesif di depan gerund buat nyebut pelakunya di kalimat formal.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngerangkai “keberatan dia merilis” kata per kata, jadi gerund-nya kehilangan bentuk -ing atau pelakunya salah kasus.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat preposisi “to” setelah “objected” → yang boleh ngikut cuma klausa -ing yang kayak benda, lengkap sama pelakunya → pilih posesif + gerund “his releasing”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use the marginal preposition 'barring' with a noun phrase to mean 'if X does not happen'
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner swaps the categories 'meskipun ada' (despite) and 'kecuali kalau ada' (barring), because both feel like formal exception words although their meanings run in opposite directions
templates.reasoningOperation: check the follow-up clause: objections would push the deal to March -> the gap must mean 'if no objections arise' -> select 'Barring', not a concession or an exclusion word
templates.stem: ___ any further objections from the regulator, the deal will be completed on Friday; if objections do come in, the deal will slip to March.

distractors.misconception: picks concessive 'despite' although the follow-up says objections would delay the deal
distractors.whyFails: 'Despite' would promise completion even if objections arrive, which the second half of the sentence flatly contradicts ('the deal will slip to March').
distractors.whyFailsId: “despite” janji deal-nya tetap selesai walaupun ada keberatan; itu bertabrakan langsung sama “if objections do come in, the deal will slip to March”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “despite” dipilih padahal kalimat lanjutannya bilang keberatan bakal nunda deal.

distractors.misconception: chooses clause-taking 'unless' although only a noun phrase follows
distractors.whyFails: 'Unless' is a conjunction and must introduce a finite clause ('unless the regulator objects'); it cannot govern the bare noun phrase 'any further objections'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “unless” itu konjungsi yang wajib bawa klausa finit (“unless the regulator objects”); dia nggak bisa megang frasa benda “any further objections”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “unless” dipasang di depan frasa benda doang.

distractors.misconception: reads 'except' as if it meant 'provided none arise'
distractors.whyFails: 'Except' excludes members from a stated set ('every objection except this one'); it never means 'if none arise', so the conditional reading collapses.
distractors.whyFailsId: “except” ngeluarin anggota dari kelompok yang udah disebut; dia nggak pernah berarti “asal nggak muncul”, jadi makna syaratnya nggak kebentuk.
distractors.misconceptionId: “except” dibaca seolah artinya “asal nggak ada”.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Barring any further objections' means 'if no further objections arise', which lines up with the follow-up: objections would push the deal to March.
explanation.rule: 'Barring + noun phrase' means 'if X does not happen'; it differs from 'despite' (it happens anyway even with X) and from 'unless' (which requires a clause).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Despite' promises completion whatever happens, clashing with the second clause; 'unless' needs a finite clause, not a noun phrase; 'except' only excludes items from a set.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask which reading the sentence needs: 'goes ahead even if X exists' or 'goes ahead provided X does not appear'? The second slot belongs to 'barring'.
explanation.memoryCue: 'Barring surprises' = provided no surprises show up — they are barred at the door.
explanation.ruleId: “Barring + frasa benda” = “kalau X nggak muncul”; beda sama “despite” (tetap jalan walau X ada) dan “unless” (wajib bawa klausa).
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Barring any further objections” = kalau nggak ada keberatan lagi — nyambung sama lanjutan kalimatnya: kalau ada keberatan, deal-nya mundur ke Maret.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Despite” janji tetap selesai walau ada keberatan — tabrakan sama klausa kedua; “unless” butuh klausa finit, bukan frasa benda; “except” cuma ngecualiin item dari daftar.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dulu: kalimatnya bilang “tetap jalan walaupun ada” atau “jalan asal nggak ada”? Yang kedua jatahnya “barring”.
explanation.memoryCueId: “Barring surprises” = asal nggak ada kejutan — kejutannya dipagerin di luar pintu.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai preposisi formal “barring” + frasa benda buat bilang “kalau nggak ada X”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nuker kategori: “meskipun ada” (despite) sama “kecuali kalau ada” (barring) kerasa mirip-mirip formal, padahal artinya kebalik.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek klausa lanjutannya: kalau ada keberatan, deal-nya mundur ke Maret → titik kosong harus berarti “kalau nggak ada keberatan” → pilih “Barring”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'all the + comparative' with a because-reason to intensify a quality in the light of that reason
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner reads 'all the ___' as a superlative frame or fills it with an everyday intensifier, although this fixed frame only accepts a comparative form
templates.reasoningOperation: spot the frame 'all the ___' followed by a because-reason -> the frame only licenses a comparative -> select 'more'
templates.stem: Her win at the national final is all the ___ impressive because she trained for two years without a coach.

distractors.misconception: reads the 'all the' frame as a superlative and picks 'most'
distractors.whyFails: The superlative 'the most impressive' is a different pattern; inside the fixed frame 'all the ___' only a comparative fits, so the sequence 'all the most' never occurs.
distractors.whyFailsId: superlatif “the most impressive” itu pola lain; di bingkai “all the ___” yang sah cuma komparatif, jadi urutan “all the most” nggak pernah kebentuk.
distractors.misconceptionId: bingkainya dibaca superlatif, jadi milih “most”.

distractors.misconception: drops quantifier 'much' into 'all the' as if it were an intensifier
distractors.whyFails: 'Much' can strengthen a comparative ('much more impressive'), but the string 'all the much impressive' does not exist in English grammar.
distractors.whyFailsId: “much” bisa nemenin komparatif (“much more impressive”), tapi urutan “all the much impressive” nggak ada di tata bahasa Inggris.
distractors.misconceptionId: “much” ditaruh seolah “all the much” itu pengintensif.

distractors.misconception: forces everyday 'very' into the 'all the + comparative' frame
distractors.whyFails: 'Very' attaches directly to an adjective ('very impressive') and never follows 'all the'; the frame demands a comparative form.
distractors.whyFailsId: “very” nempel langsung ke kata sifat (“very impressive”) dan nggak pernah ngikutin “all the”; bingkainya minta bentuk komparatif.
distractors.misconceptionId: “very” sehari-hari dipaksa masuk bingkai formal ini.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'All the more impressive because she trained without a coach' means the reason makes the achievement even more impressive; 'more' supplies the comparative the frame demands.
explanation.rule: 'All the + comparative (+ because/for + reason)' intensifies a quality in the light of a reason; only comparative forms ('more', 'less', 'better') can fill the slot.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Most' builds the non-existent sequence 'all the most'; 'much' and 'very' are not comparatives, so neither can complete the 'all the ___' frame.
explanation.howToAvoid: When you meet 'all the ___' plus a reason, resist the superlative reading — fill the slot with a comparative: 'all the more', 'all the better'.
explanation.memoryCue: 'All the more X because Y' = Y makes it even more X.
explanation.ruleId: “All the + komparatif (+ because/for + alasan)” = makin terasa justru karena alasannya; yang boleh masuk cuma bentuk komparatif (“more”, “less”, “better”).
explanation.whyCorrectId: “all the more impressive because she trained without a coach” = makin mengesankan justru karena dia latihan tanpa pelatih; “more” ngasih bentuk komparatif yang diminta bingkainya.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “most” bikin urutan “all the most” yang nggak ada; “much” dan “very” bukan komparatif, jadi nggak bisa ngelengkapin bingkai “all the ___”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Ketemu “all the ___” plus alasan? Itu bukan superlatif — isi pakai komparatif: “all the more / all the better”.
explanation.memoryCueId: “All the more X because Y” — gara-gara Y, X-nya makin nambah.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “all the + komparatif” + alasan buat bilang kualitasnya makin terasa justru karena alasan itu.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu baca “all the ___” kayak bingkai superlatif atau ngisi pengintensif biasa, padahal bingkai baku ini khusus minta bentuk komparatif.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat bingkai “all the ___” yang diikuti alasan “because...” → bingkai ini cuma nerima komparatif → pilih “more”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Negate a participle clause by placing 'not' directly before the -ing form
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner carries the Indonesian 'tidak/bukan' pattern into English, so the negator surfaces as 'no', loses the -ing, or drags in a finite 'didn't' that cannot head a subjectless adjunct
templates.reasoningOperation: see a subjectless adjunct before the comma that must mean 'because she did not want' -> place 'not' immediately before the participle -> select 'Not wanting'
templates.stem: ___ to cause a scene in front of the clients, Maya quietly slipped out of the meeting room.

distractors.misconception: leaves the participle as a bare verb after 'not'
distractors.whyFails: The adjunct needs the participle 'wanting'; bare 'want' carries no -ing, so 'Not want to cause' never forms a participle clause.
distractors.whyFailsId: adjunct ini butuh partisip “wanting”; “want” polos nggak punya -ing, jadi “Not want to cause” nggak pernah jadi klausa partisip.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerjanya dibiarin bentuk dasar, kebawa kebiasaan bahasa Indonesia yang nggak ngerubah kata kerja.

distractors.misconception: translates Indonesian 'tidak' as 'no' to negate a participle
distractors.whyFails: 'No' negates nouns ('no time', 'no money'); a participle clause is negated with 'not', so 'No wanting' is ungrammatical.
distractors.whyFailsId: “no” cuma negasiin kata benda (“no time”, “no money”); klausa partisip dinegasi pakai “not”, jadi “No wanting” salah bentuk.
distractors.misconceptionId: “tidak/bukan” diterjemahin jadi “no” buat negasi kata kerja.

distractors.misconception: lets a finite 'didn't want' head a subjectless adjunct
distractors.whyFails: 'Didn't want' is a finite verb that needs its own subject and cannot hang in front of the main clause; the adjunct slot only accepts a participle like 'Not wanting'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “didn't want” itu kata kerja finit yang butuh subjeknya sendiri, nggak bisa nggantung di depan klausa utama; slot adjunct ini cuma nerima partisip kayak “Not wanting”.
distractors.misconceptionId: klausa finit “didn't want” dipaksa jadi adjunct tanpa subjek.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Not wanting to cause a scene' means 'because she did not want to cause a scene'; 'not' in front of 'wanting' negates the whole participle clause.
explanation.rule: Non-finite clauses are negated by 'not' placed directly before the -ing or -ed form: 'Not wanting...', 'Not having received...'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Not want' loses the -ing; 'No wanting' uses 'no', which only negates nouns; 'Didn't want' is a finite verb that cannot head a subjectless adjunct.
explanation.howToAvoid: To negate an -ing clause, apply one formula only: 'not' + -ing form. Never swap in 'no' and never call in 'didn't'.
explanation.memoryCue: 'Not wanting to intrude, she left' — 'not' comes first, then the -ing.
explanation.ruleId: Klausa non-finit dinegasi dengan “not” tepat sebelum bentuk -ing/-ed: “Not wanting...”, “Not having received...”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Not wanting to cause a scene” = karena dia nggak pengin bikin ribut; “not” di depan “wanting” negasiin seluruh klausa partisipnya.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Not want” kehilangan -ing; “No wanting” pakai “no” yang cuma buat kata benda; “Didn't want” kata kerja finit yang butuh subjek sendiri, nggak bisa nggantung di depan koma.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Mau negasi klausa -ing? Rumusnya satu: “not” + bentuk -ing. Jangan ganti jadi “no”, jangan panggil “didn't”.
explanation.memoryCueId: “Not wanting to intrude, she left” — “not” selalu duluan, baru bentuk -ing.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Negasiin klausa partisip dengan naruh “not” persis di depan bentuk -ing.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu bawa pola “tidak/bukan” ke Inggris — negatornya berubah jadi “no”, kehilangan -ing, atau malah manggil “didn't” yang nggak boleh mimpin adjunct tanpa subjek.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat adjunct tanpa subjek sebelum koma yang maksudnya “karena nggak mau bikin ribut” → taruh “not” persis sebelum partisip → pilih “Not wanting”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'albeit' before an adjective or short phrase to add a compressed concession without a finite clause
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner treats contrast words as interchangeable, although 'despite' demands a noun phrase, 'whereas' demands a full finite clause, and only 'albeit' is licensed before a lone adjective here
templates.reasoningOperation: see a lone adjective after the comma that concedes a drawback -> the connector must license a verbless concession -> select 'albeit'
templates.stem: The trial results look promising, ___ preliminary, so the lab plans to repeat the study with a larger sample.

distractors.misconception: attaches the preposition 'despite' directly to an adjective
distractors.whyFails: 'Despite' is a preposition and must govern a noun phrase or -ing form ('despite their preliminary nature'); it cannot sit directly before the bare adjective 'preliminary'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “despite” itu preposisi yang wajib megang frasa benda atau bentuk -ing (“despite their preliminary nature”); nempel langsung ke kata sifat polos “preliminary” nggak gramatikal.
distractors.misconceptionId: preposisi “despite” ditempel langsung ke kata sifat.

distractors.misconception: puts clause conjunction 'whereas' before a lone adjective
distractors.whyFails: 'Whereas' contrasts two full finite clauses ('whereas the second trial was larger'); it has no reduced use before a bare adjective.
distractors.whyFailsId: “whereas” ngontrasin dua klausa finit lengkap (“whereas the second trial was larger”); dia nggak punya versi ringkas di depan kata sifat tunggal.
distractors.misconceptionId: konjungsi antar-klausa “whereas” dipasang di depan kata sifat tunggal.

distractors.misconception: confuses focus particle 'even' with concessive 'even if' or 'even though'
distractors.whyFails: Bare 'even' only adds an extreme item on the same scale ('cheap, even free'); it cannot concede a drawback, so 'promising, even preliminary' fails to express the intended contrast — that reading needs 'even if' plus a clause, or 'albeit'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “even” polos cuma nambahin item paling ekstrem di skala yang sama (“cheap, even free”); dia nggak bisa ngakuin kekurangan, jadi kontras “masih tahap awal”-nya nggak tersampaikan — butuh “even if” + klausa, atau “albeit”.
distractors.misconceptionId: partikel penegas “even” (bahkan) ketuker sama konsesi “even if/though”.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Promising, albeit preliminary' concedes the drawback in two words: 'albeit' is designed exactly for a concession this short, with no verb needed.
explanation.rule: 'Albeit + adjective/adverb/prepositional phrase' inserts a concession without a finite clause: 'encouraging, albeit preliminary'; 'albeit' never introduces a clause with its own verb.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Despite' is a preposition that must govern a noun phrase; 'whereas' requires two finite clauses; bare 'even' is a focus particle that adds an extreme item and cannot concede a drawback.
explanation.howToAvoid: If the concession is just one adjective, reach for 'albeit' (or 'though'); never 'despite', which asks for a noun, not an adjective.
explanation.memoryCue: 'Albeit' = 'although it be' — a concession squeezed into one word, no verb required.
explanation.ruleId: “Albeit + kata sifat/adverbia/frasa preposisi” nyisipin konsesi tanpa klausa finit: “encouraging, albeit preliminary”; “albeit” nggak pernah bawa klausa berkata-kerja.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “promising, albeit preliminary” = menjanjikan, walau masih tahap awal — “albeit” memang dirancang buat konsesi sependek ini, tanpa kata kerja.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “despite” preposisi yang wajib megang frasa benda; “whereas” wajib bawa dua klausa finit; “even” polos cuma partikel penegas “bahkan”, nggak bisa ngakuin kekurangan.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Konsesinya cuma satu kata sifat? Pakai “albeit” (atau “though”); jangan “despite” — dia minta kata benda, bukan kata sifat.
explanation.memoryCueId: “Albeit” = “although it be” — konsesi dipadetin jadi satu kata, tanpa kata kerja.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “albeit” di depan kata sifat atau frasa pendek buat nyisipin konsesi ringkas tanpa klausa finit.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu perlakukan semua kata kontras kayak bisa saling tukar, padahal “despite” minta frasa benda, “whereas” minta klausa penuh, dan cuma “albeit” yang sah di depan kata sifat tunggal di sini.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat kata sifat tunggal setelah koma yang ngakuin kekurangan → konektornya harus bisa bawa konsesi tanpa kata kerja → pilih “albeit”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Correct hypercorrected 'whom' back to 'who' when the relative pronoun is the subject of an embedded verb
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner hears 'whom' as the safer, more formal choice after a verb like 'believed', so the subject of the embedded 'was' gets hypercorrected into object case
templates.reasoningOperation: bracket the comment clause 'everyone believed' -> what remains is '... was the strongest candidate', which still needs a subject -> the pronoun must be subject-case 'who', not 'whom'
templates.stem: Find and correct the error: “They hired the architect whom everyone believed was the strongest candidate.”
options: They hired the architect whom everyone believed he was the strongest candidate.
They hired the architect which everyone believed was the strongest candidate.
They hired the architect who everyone believed was the strongest candidate.
They hired the architect whose everyone believed was the strongest candidate.

distractors.option: They hired the architect whom everyone believed he was the strongest candidate.
distractors.misconception: keeps 'whom' and patches the clause with a resumptive 'he', mirroring Indonesian 'yang dia'
distractors.whyFails: English relative clauses do not allow a resumptive pronoun; 'whom ... he was' gives the verb 'was' two competing subjects and leaves 'whom' with no role at all.
distractors.whyFailsId: klausa relatif Inggris nggak boleh ada pronomina ulang; “whom ... he was” bikin “was” punya dua calon subjek dan “whom” nggak kebagian peran apa-apa.
distractors.misconceptionId: “whom” dipertahanin terus ditambal “he”, persis pola “yang dia” di bahasa Indonesia.

distractors.option: They hired the architect which everyone believed was the strongest candidate.
distractors.misconception: swaps in 'which' although the antecedent is a person
distractors.whyFails: 'Which' only takes non-human antecedents; 'the architect which' is ungrammatical regardless of the case problem in the original.
distractors.whyFailsId: “which” cuma buat rujukan non-manusia; “the architect which” salah dari akarnya, terlepas dari urusan kasus di kalimat aslinya.
distractors.misconceptionId: “which” dipakai padahal yang dirujuk orang.

distractors.option: They hired the architect whose everyone believed was the strongest candidate.
distractors.misconception: reads formal-sounding 'whose' as another safe upgrade of 'who'
distractors.whyFails: 'Whose' is possessive and must be followed by a noun ('whose design'); standing alone before 'everyone believed' it has nothing to possess.
distractors.whyFailsId: “whose” itu posesif yang wajib diikutin kata benda (“whose design”); berdiri sendiri sebelum “everyone believed” dia nggak punya apa-apa buat dimiliki.
distractors.misconceptionId: “whose” dikira upgrade formal lain dari “who”.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Who ... was the strongest candidate' is correct because 'who' is the subject of 'was'; 'everyone believed' is only an inserted comment that can be bracketed out.
explanation.rule: When the embedded verb still needs a subject after you bracket a comment like 'everyone believed', the relative pronoun is 'who'; 'whom' is reserved for object positions.
explanation.whyOthersFail: The 'whom ... he was' version adds a resumptive pronoun like Indonesian 'yang dia'; 'which' rejects human antecedents; 'whose' is possessive and demands a following noun.
explanation.howToAvoid: Cover 'everyone believed' or 'we think' with a finger: if the verb after it is still hunting for a subject, write 'who'.
explanation.memoryCue: Bracket the comment: 'who [everyone believed] was...' — 'who' stays the subject.
explanation.ruleId: Kalau kata kerja sisipan (“was”) masih butuh subjek setelah kamu nutup komentar kayak “everyone believed”, pronomina relatifnya “who”; “whom” cuma buat posisi objek.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “who ... was the strongest candidate” bener karena “who” jadi subjek “was”; “everyone believed” cuma komentar sisipan yang bisa dikurung.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: versi “whom ... he was” nambah pronomina ulang ala “yang dia”; “which” nolak rujukan orang; “whose” posesif yang wajib diikuti kata benda.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tutupin “everyone believed / we think” pakai jari: kalau kata kerja setelahnya masih nyari subjek, tulis “who”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Kurung komentarnya: “who [everyone believed] was...” — “who” tetap jadi subjek.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Balikin “whom” hasil hiperkoreksi jadi “who” waktu pronomina relatifnya jadi subjek kata kerja sisipan.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngerasa “whom” lebih aman dan formal setelah “believed”, padahal yang dibutuhin subjek buat “was” — kasus objek malah bikin salah.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kurung dulu komentar “everyone believed” → sisanya “... was the strongest candidate” masih butuh subjek → pronominanya harus “who”, bukan “whom”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Keep the base form of the present simple verb after a plural subject.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner adds -s to every present simple verb, even after a plural subject like 'we'.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the subject -> check whether it is singular or plural -> keep the base form after a plural subject
templates.stem: We ___ to school by bus.

distractors.misconception: adds -s to the verb although the subject is plural
distractors.whyFails: 'Goes' is only for he, she, or it; 'we' takes the base form 'go'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “goes” cuma buat he, she, it. “We” pakai “go”.
distractors.misconceptionId: nambahin -s ke kata kerja, padahal subjeknya jamak.

distractors.misconception: progressive confusion
distractors.whyFails: 'Going' needs 'are' before it and describes an action right now, not a daily routine.
distractors.whyFailsId: “going” butuh “are” di depannya dan artinya lagi jalan sekarang, bukan rutinitas.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dipakai buat kebiasaan.

distractors.misconception: past-tense confusion
distractors.whyFails: 'Went' is the past form; the sentence describes a present routine.
distractors.whyFailsId: “went” bentuk lampau, padahal kalimatnya soal kebiasaan sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk lampau dipakai buat kebiasaan sekarang.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'We' is plural, so the present simple verb stays in the base form: we go.
explanation.rule: Present simple: add -s only after he, she, or it. I, you, we, and they keep the base form.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Goes' belongs to a singular subject; 'going' is missing 'are'; 'went' is the past.
explanation.howToAvoid: Look at the subject first. If it is we, you, they, or I, do not add -s.
explanation.memoryCue: We go, she goes.
explanation.ruleId: Present simple: -s cuma buat he, she, it. I, you, we, they tetap bentuk dasar.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “We” itu jamak, jadi kata kerjanya tetap bentuk dasar: we go.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Goes” buat subjek tunggal. “Going” kurang “are”. “Went” bentuk lampau.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Lihat subjeknya dulu. Kalau we, you, they, atau I, jangan tambah -s.
explanation.memoryCueId: Ingat aturannya: “we go”, tapi “she goes”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kata kerja present simple tetap bentuk dasar sesudah subjek jamak.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nambahin -s ke semua kata kerja present simple, padahal sesudah “we” nggak perlu.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cari subjeknya → cek tunggal atau jamak → jamak tetap bentuk dasar

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Form a negative ability statement with can't plus a base verb.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner builds the negative of 'can' with 'don't' or adds 'to' after the modal.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the meaning as not able -> select can't -> keep the verb in base form
templates.stem: I ___ ride a bike, but I want to learn.

distractors.misconception: do auxiliary
distractors.whyFails: 'Can' makes its own negative with 'not'; it never takes 'don't'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “can” punya negatif sendiri pakai “not”, nggak pernah pakai “don't”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu do.

distractors.misconception: adds 'to' after the modal can
distractors.whyFails: After 'can' or 'can't' the verb is bare: can't ride, not can't to ride.
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “can't” kata kerjanya polos: can't ride, bukan can't to ride.
distractors.misconceptionId: nambahin “to” sesudah can, padahal can langsung ketemu kata kerja dasar.

distractors.misconception: uses the past form for a present ability
distractors.whyFails: 'Couldn't' is the past form; 'I want to learn' shows the sentence is about now.
distractors.whyFailsId: “couldn't” bentuk lampau, padahal “I want to learn” nunjukin ini soal sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai bentuk lampau, padahal yang dibicarain kemampuan sekarang.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Can't' expresses a present inability and is followed directly by the base verb 'ride'.
explanation.rule: Negative ability: can't (cannot) + base verb. No 'don't', no 'to'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Don't can' mixes two negatives that never combine; 'can't to' adds an extra 'to'; 'couldn't' points to the past.
explanation.howToAvoid: Treat can like a switch: can / can't, then the verb with nothing in between.
explanation.memoryCue: Can't + verb: can't ride, can't swim.
explanation.ruleId: Nggak bisa: can't (cannot) + kata kerja dasar. Tanpa don't, tanpa to.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Can't” artinya nggak bisa sekarang, langsung diikuti kata kerja dasar “ride”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Don't can” nyampur dua negatif. “Can't to” kelebihan “to”. “Couldn't” nunjuk masa lampau.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Anggap can kayak tombol: can atau can't, lalu langsung kata kerjanya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Can't + kata kerja: can't ride, can't swim.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Bikin kalimat nggak bisa pakai can't plus kata kerja dasar.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu bikin negatif can pakai “don't” atau nambahin “to” sesudahnya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali maknanya nggak mampu → pakai can't → kata kerjanya tetap dasar

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Add -ed to a regular verb for a finished action with a past time word.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner keeps the base verb after 'last night' or doubles the past marking with 'did'.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the past time word -> check that the verb is regular -> add -ed once
templates.stem: Last night I ___ a film with my family.

distractors.misconception: missing-past-marking
distractors.whyFails: 'Last night' is finished, so the verb needs the past ending -ed.
distractors.whyFailsId: “last night” udah lewat, jadi kata kerjanya butuh akhiran -ed.
distractors.misconceptionId: tanda lampaunya hilang.

distractors.misconception: doubles the past marking with 'did' plus -ed
distractors.whyFails: 'Did' already carries the past, so the verb after it stays bare; a statement does not need 'did' at all.
distractors.whyFailsId: “did” udah bawa makna lampau, jadi kata kerjanya harus polos. Kalimat berita malah nggak butuh “did”.
distractors.misconceptionId: nandain lampau dua kali: “did” plus -ed.

distractors.misconception: progressive-form substitution
distractors.whyFails: 'Watching' needs 'was' before it and does not simply state a finished event.
distractors.whyFailsId: “watching” butuh “was” di depannya dan nggak nyatain kejadian yang udah selesai.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dipakai buat kejadian selesai.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Last night' places the action in the finished past, so the regular verb takes -ed: watched.
explanation.rule: Past simple of regular verbs: verb + -ed, used once, with no 'did' in a statement.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Watch' has no past marking; 'did watched' marks the past twice; 'watching' is not a finished-action form.
explanation.howToAvoid: See a past time word? Add -ed to the verb and stop there.
explanation.memoryCue: Last night → -ed.
explanation.ruleId: Past simple kata kerja teratur: kata kerja + -ed, cukup sekali, tanpa did di kalimat berita.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Last night” udah lewat, jadi kata kerjanya pakai -ed: watched.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Watch” nggak ada tanda lampaunya. “Did watched” nandain lampau dua kali. “Watching” bukan bentuk kejadian selesai.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Lihat kata waktu lampau? Tambah -ed ke kata kerjanya, lalu berhenti di situ.
explanation.memoryCueId: Ada “last night”? Kata kerjanya pakai -ed.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Tambahin -ed ke kata kerja teratur buat kejadian selesai yang ada kata waktu lampaunya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu biarin kata kerjanya polos sesudah “last night”, atau nandain lampau dua kali pakai “did”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cari kata waktu lampaunya → kata kerja teratur → tambah -ed sekali

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Pair 'are' with the -ing verb for a plural subject acting right now.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner chooses 'is' for a plural subject or drops the be-auxiliary before the -ing verb.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify 'Look!' as a now cue -> check the subject is plural -> apply are + verb-ing
templates.stem: Look! The children ___ in the garden.

distractors.misconception: be verb
distractors.whyFails: 'Children' is plural, so the auxiliary must be 'are', not 'is'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “children” itu jamak, jadi kata bantunya “are”, bukan “is”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja be.

distractors.misconception: missing-be-auxiliary
distractors.whyFails: The -ing verb cannot stand alone; it needs 'are' to make a full sentence.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata kerja -ing nggak bisa berdiri sendiri, butuh “are” supaya jadi kalimat utuh.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu be-nya hilang.

distractors.misconception: present-simple-habit
distractors.whyFails: 'Play' describes a habit; 'Look!' shows the action is happening right now.
distractors.whyFailsId: “play” nyatain kebiasaan, padahal “Look!” nunjukin kejadiannya lagi jalan sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk kebiasaan dipakai buat kejadian yang lagi jalan.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Look!' points to an action in progress now, and 'the children' is plural, so the form is 'are playing'.
explanation.rule: Present continuous: am/is/are + verb-ing. Plural subjects take 'are'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Is playing' has the wrong auxiliary for a plural subject; 'playing' has no auxiliary; 'play' is a habit form.
explanation.howToAvoid: Two checks: is it happening now (use -ing) and is the subject plural (use are)?
explanation.memoryCue: Look! → are + -ing.
explanation.ruleId: Present continuous: am/is/are + kata kerja -ing. Subjek jamak pakai “are”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Look!” nunjuk kejadian yang lagi jalan, dan “the children” itu jamak, jadi bentuknya “are playing”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Is playing” salah kata bantu buat subjek jamak. “Playing” nggak punya kata bantu. “Play” bentuk kebiasaan.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Dua cek: lagi jalan sekarang (pakai -ing) dan subjeknya jamak (pakai are)?
explanation.memoryCueId: Ada “Look!”? Pakai are + -ing.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pasangin “are” sama kata kerja -ing buat subjek jamak yang lagi beraksi sekarang.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pilih “is” buat subjek jamak, atau ngilangin kata bantu be di depan kata kerja -ing.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat “Look!” → kejadian lagi jalan → subjek jamak pakai are + -ing

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Form a negative command with don't plus the base verb.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner negates a command with 'not' alone or adds -s to the verb.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify a warning to the listener -> select the negative command -> apply don't + base verb
templates.stem: The floor is wet. ___ here, please!

distractors.misconception: using the -ing form on its own, which describes an activity instead of telling someone to act
distractors.whyFails: A command cannot be negated with bare 'not'; English needs 'don't' before the verb.
distractors.whyFailsId: larangan nggak bisa cuma pakai “not”. Bahasa Inggris butuh “don't” di depan kata kerjanya.
distractors.misconceptionId: larangannya cuma pakai not tanpa do.

distractors.misconception: adding -s as if the command needed subject-verb agreement with a singular subject
distractors.whyFails: 'Doesn't' is for he, she, or it in statements; a command to the listener uses 'don't'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “doesn't” buat he, she, it di kalimat berita. Larangan ke lawan bicara pakai “don't”.
distractors.misconceptionId: perintah dikasih -s seolah butuh subjek tunggal.

distractors.misconception: uses the third-person -s form after 'you' in a command
distractors.whyFails: After 'don't' the verb stays bare: don't run, never don't runs.
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “don't” kata kerjanya tetap polos: don't run, bukan don't runs.
distractors.misconceptionId: nambahin -s ke perintah, padahal perintah nggak punya subjek yang butuh -s.

explanation.whyCorrect: The speaker tells the listener not to do something, so the negative command is 'Don't run'.
explanation.rule: Negative imperative: Don't + base verb. No subject, no -s.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Not run' lacks 'do'; 'doesn't run' treats the listener as he/she; 'don't runs' adds an -s the base form never takes.
explanation.howToAvoid: Telling someone not to do something? Start with 'Don't' and keep the verb bare.
explanation.memoryCue: Don't + verb: Don't run, Don't touch.
explanation.ruleId: Larangan: Don't + kata kerja dasar. Tanpa subjek, tanpa -s.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Pembicara ngelarang lawan bicaranya, jadi larangannya “Don't run”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Not run” kurang “do”. “Doesn't run” nganggap lawan bicara kayak he/she. “Don't runs” nambah -s yang nggak pernah ada di bentuk dasar.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Mau ngelarang orang? Mulai dari “Don't”, lalu kata kerjanya tetap polos.
explanation.memoryCueId: Don't + kata kerja: Don't run, Don't touch.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Bikin larangan pakai don't plus kata kerja dasar.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu bikin larangan pakai “not” aja, atau nambahin -s ke kata kerjanya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali ini peringatan buat lawan bicara → larangan → don't + kata kerja dasar

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Place a frequency adverb after the verb be.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner puts the frequency adverb before 'is/are', copying its position with ordinary verbs.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the main verb -> check whether it is be -> place the adverb after be
templates.stem: Rudi ___ for class.

distractors.misconception: puts the frequency adverb before the verb be
distractors.whyFails: With 'be', the adverb comes after the verb: is never, not never is.
distractors.whyFailsId: sama be, kata keterangannya sesudah kata kerja: is never, bukan never is.
distractors.misconceptionId: naruh kata keterangan frekuensi di depan is/are, padahal harusnya sesudahnya.

distractors.misconception: puts the frequency adverb after the object
distractors.whyFails: Frequency adverbs sit in the middle of the sentence, not at the end after the adjective.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata keterangan frekuensi duduk di tengah kalimat, bukan di ujung sesudah kata sifat.
distractors.misconceptionId: naruh kata keterangan frekuensi di belakang objek, padahal tempatnya di depan kata kerja.

distractors.misconception: leaving the bare verb with no third-person marking after a singular subject
distractors.whyFails: 'Rudi' needs the finite form 'is'; bare 'be' cannot carry the sentence.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Rudi” butuh bentuk “is”. “Be” polos nggak bisa jadi kata kerja utama kalimat.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja dibiarin polos padahal subjeknya tunggal.

explanation.whyCorrect: The verb is 'be', so the frequency adverb follows it: Rudi is never late.
explanation.rule: Frequency adverbs go before an ordinary verb but after the verb be (am/is/are).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Never is' reverses the order; 'is late never' pushes the adverb to the end; 'never be' has no finite verb.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: is the verb 'be'? If yes, adverb after it. If not, adverb before it.
explanation.memoryCue: Be first, then never: is never late.
explanation.ruleId: Kata keterangan frekuensi di depan kata kerja biasa, tapi sesudah be (am/is/are).
explanation.whyCorrectId: Kata kerjanya be, jadi kata keterangan frekuensinya nyusul: Rudi is never late.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Never is” urutannya kebalik. “Is late never” ngedorong kata keterangannya ke ujung. “Never be” nggak punya kata kerja utuh.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya: kata kerjanya be? Kalau ya, kata keterangan sesudahnya. Kalau bukan, di depannya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Be dulu, baru never: is never late.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Taruh kata keterangan frekuensi sesudah kata kerja be.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu naruh kata keterangan frekuensi di depan “is/are”, niru posisinya di kata kerja biasa.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cari kata kerja utamanya → ternyata be → taruh kata keterangannya sesudah be

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use apostrophe-s on a singular noun to show who owns something.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner writes the owner's name with no marker or with a plain -s and no apostrophe.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the owner -> check that the owner is singular -> add 's before the thing owned
templates.stem: This is my ___ car. He bought it last year.

distractors.misconception: drops the marker of ownership entirely, lining up two nouns as Indonesian does
distractors.whyFails: 'My father car' puts two nouns side by side with no sign of ownership.
distractors.whyFailsId: “my father car” cuma nyandingin dua kata benda tanpa tanda kepemilikan.
distractors.misconceptionId: tanda kepemilikannya dibuang, dua kata benda dijejerin kayak di bahasa Indonesia.

distractors.misconception: writes a plain -s ending that superficially resembles the possessive but loses the apostrophe
distractors.whyFails: 'Fathers' means more than one father; ownership needs the apostrophe: father's.
distractors.whyFailsId: “fathers” artinya lebih dari satu ayah. Kepemilikan butuh tanda petik: father's.
distractors.misconceptionId: cuma nulis -s tanpa tanda petik.

distractors.misconception: inserting a duplicate owner pronoun after the name, marking possession twice
distractors.whyFails: English does not add 'his' after the owner's name; the 's already shows possession.
distractors.whyFailsId: bahasa Inggris nggak nambahin “his” sesudah nama pemilik. Tanda 's udah nunjukin kepemilikan.
distractors.misconceptionId: nambahin kata ganti pemilik sesudah nama, jadi kepemilikannya dobel.

explanation.whyCorrect: The car belongs to one person, my father, so the owner takes 's: my father's car.
explanation.rule: Singular owner + 's + thing owned: father's car, Sinta's bag.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Father' has no marker; 'fathers' is a plural, not a possessive; 'father his' doubles the owner.
explanation.howToAvoid: Who owns it? Put 's right after that person, then the thing.
explanation.memoryCue: Owner + 's + thing.
explanation.ruleId: Pemilik tunggal + 's + barangnya: father's car, Sinta's bag.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Mobilnya punya satu orang, ayahku, jadi pemiliknya dapet 's: my father's car.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Father” nggak ada tandanya. “Fathers” itu jamak, bukan kepemilikan. “Father his” pemiliknya dobel.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Siapa pemiliknya? Taruh 's langsung sesudah orang itu, baru barangnya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Pemilik + 's + barang.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai tanda 's di kata benda tunggal buat nunjukin siapa pemiliknya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nulis nama pemiliknya tanpa tanda apa pun, atau cuma -s tanpa tanda petik.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cari pemiliknya → kata benda tunggal → tambah 's di depan barang yang dimiliki

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Ask a polite offer question with 'Would you like' plus a noun.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner offers with flat 'Do you want' or breaks the fixed 'would like' shape.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify a polite offer to a guest -> select would like -> apply question order Would you like
templates.stem: A guest arrives at your house. You ask: “___ some tea?”

distractors.misconception: stating a general preference in casual flat form instead of the polite request formula
distractors.whyFails: 'Do you like tea?' asks about general taste, not whether the guest wants some now.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Do you like tea?” nanya suka teh atau nggak secara umum, bukan nawarin teh sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: nanya selera umum, bukan nawarin dengan sopan.

distractors.misconception: gluing an -ing onto the verb after 'would', a blend of two separate patterns
distractors.whyFails: After 'would' the verb stays bare: would like, never would liking.
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “would” kata kerjanya tetap polos: would like, bukan would liking.
distractors.misconceptionId: nempelin -ing sesudah would, nyampur dua pola.

distractors.misconception: uses 'want' where the polite would-like formula is expected
distractors.whyFails: A question needs 'would' before 'you'; statement order does not ask anything.
distractors.whyFailsId: pertanyaan butuh “would” di depan “you”. Urutan kalimat berita nggak nanya apa-apa.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai “want” yang terlalu langsung, padahal konteksnya minta dengan sopan.

explanation.whyCorrect: Offering something politely uses the fixed question 'Would you like...?'
explanation.rule: Polite offer: Would + you + like + noun? The verb 'like' stays in its base form.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Do you like' asks about taste in general; 'would you liking' adds an -ing; 'you would like' is not a question.
explanation.howToAvoid: Offering food or drink? Start with 'Would you like'.
explanation.memoryCue: Would you like...? = a polite offer.
explanation.ruleId: Tawaran sopan: Would + you + like + kata benda? Kata “like” tetap bentuk dasar.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Nawarin sesuatu dengan sopan pakai pertanyaan tetap “Would you like...?”
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Do you like” nanya selera secara umum. “Would you liking” nambah -ing. “You would like” bukan pertanyaan.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Nawarin makanan atau minuman? Mulai dari “Would you like”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Would you like...? = tawaran sopan.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Nawarin sesuatu dengan sopan pakai “Would you like” plus kata benda.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nawarin pakai “Do you want” yang datar, atau ngerusak bentuk tetap “would like”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali ini tawaran sopan ke tamu → pakai would + like → urutan tanya: Would you like

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Follow 'enjoy' with the -ing form of the next verb.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner puts a to-infinitive or a bare verb after 'enjoy'.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the preference verb enjoy -> select the -ing form for the next verb
templates.stem: I really enjoy ___ to music while I study.

distractors.misconception: following the feeling verb with a bare infinitive, chaining verbs directly as Indonesian does
distractors.whyFails: Two verbs cannot sit side by side; after 'enjoy' the second verb needs -ing.
distractors.whyFailsId: dua kata kerja nggak bisa nempel begitu aja. Sesudah “enjoy” kata kerja keduanya butuh -ing.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja perasaan langsung disambung kata kerja polos kayak di bahasa Indonesia.

distractors.misconception: uses a to-infinitive after 'enjoy'
distractors.whyFails: 'Enjoy' never takes 'to'; it is always followed by -ing.
distractors.whyFailsId: “enjoy” nggak pernah pakai “to”. Selalu diikuti -ing.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai “to” sesudah enjoy, padahal enjoy selalu diikuti bentuk -ing.

distractors.misconception: base-form overuse
distractors.whyFails: 'Listens' is a present simple form for he/she; it cannot follow another verb.
distractors.whyFailsId: “listens” bentuk present simple buat he/she, nggak bisa ngikut di belakang kata kerja lain.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk kata kerja berkonjugasi dipakai sesudah kata kerja lain.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Enjoy' is a preference verb, and the verb after it takes -ing: enjoy listening.
explanation.rule: Like, love, hate, and enjoy are followed by verb + -ing.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Listen' is bare; 'to listen' uses the wrong pattern for enjoy; 'listens' is a finite verb, not a verb form that can follow enjoy.
explanation.howToAvoid: After a feeling verb, picture the -ing ending before you write the next verb.
explanation.memoryCue: Enjoy + -ing: enjoy listening, enjoy cooking.
explanation.ruleId: Like, love, hate, dan enjoy diikuti kata kerja + -ing.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Enjoy” kata kerja kesukaan, jadi kata kerja sesudahnya pakai -ing: enjoy listening.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Listen” polos. “To listen” pola yang salah buat enjoy. “Listens” kata kerja berkonjugasi yang nggak bisa nempel di belakang enjoy.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Sesudah kata kerja perasaan, bayangin akhiran -ing sebelum nulis kata kerja berikutnya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Enjoy selalu ketemu -ing: enjoy listening, enjoy cooking.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Sesudah “enjoy”, kata kerja berikutnya pakai bentuk -ing.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu naruh “to” atau kata kerja polos sesudah “enjoy”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat kata kerja perasaan enjoy → kata kerja berikutnya pakai -ing

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'have never + past participle' for an experience that has not happened in someone's life.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses the past simple for a life experience that has no specific time.
templates.reasoningOperation: check that no time is given -> identify a life experience -> apply have/has + never + past participle
templates.stem: My grandmother ___ a plane. She always travels by train.

distractors.misconception: uses the past simple for a life experience without a time
distractors.whyFails: There is no finished time like 'last year'; the sentence covers her whole life up to now, so present perfect is needed.
distractors.whyFailsId: nggak ada waktu selesai kayak “last year”. Kalimatnya nyakup seumur hidup sampai sekarang, jadi butuh present perfect.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai past simple buat pengalaman hidup yang nggak disebut waktunya.

distractors.misconception: leaving the bare verb although 'have' needs the past participle after it
distractors.whyFails: After 'has', the verb must be the past participle 'flown', not the bare 'fly'.
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “has” kata kerjanya harus past participle “flown”, bukan “fly” polos.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja dibiarin polos padahal sesudah have butuh past participle.

distractors.misconception: mixes 'have' with a finite past form of 'be' instead of the participle
distractors.whyFails: 'Has' pairs with a past participle, not an -ing form, and 'never' goes after 'has'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “has” berpasangan sama past participle, bukan -ing. “Never” juga tempatnya sesudah “has”.
distractors.misconceptionId: have dicampur sama bentuk -ing, bukan past participle.

explanation.whyCorrect: Her whole life up to now is the time frame, and 'she always travels by train' shows it is still true, so 'has never flown' fits.
explanation.rule: Life experience without a specific time: have/has + never/ever + past participle.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Never flew' closes the time off in the past; 'has never fly' lacks the participle; 'never has flying' uses -ing and the wrong word order.
explanation.howToAvoid: No date or finished time word? Use have/has + past participle.
explanation.memoryCue: Never in my life → has never flown.
explanation.ruleId: Pengalaman hidup tanpa waktu pasti: have/has + never/ever + past participle.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Rentang waktunya seumur hidup sampai sekarang, dan “she always travels by train” nunjukin itu masih berlaku, jadi “has never flown” yang pas.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Never flew” nutup waktunya di masa lampau. “Has never fly” kurang past participle. “Never has flying” pakai -ing dan urutannya salah.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Nggak ada tanggal atau kata waktu selesai? Pakai have/has + past participle.
explanation.memoryCueId: Belum pernah seumur hidup → has never flown.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “have never + past participle” buat pengalaman yang belum pernah terjadi seumur hidup.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai past simple buat pengalaman hidup yang nggak disebut waktunya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: nggak ada waktu yang disebut → pengalaman hidup → have/has + never + past participle

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Choose 'for' before a length of time in a present perfect sentence.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses 'since' before a period like 'ten years' or drops the present perfect link.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the length of time -> keep the present perfect -> select for, not since
templates.stem: Mr. Hadi has taught at our school ___ ten years, and he still loves it.

distractors.misconception: uses 'since' before a length of time
distractors.whyFails: 'Since' introduces a starting point like 2015, not a length like 'ten years'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “since” buat titik mulai kayak 2015, bukan lamanya kayak “ten years”.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai “since” di depan lamanya waktu, padahal since buat titik mulai.

distractors.misconception: sealing the period off as a completed event, though the family still lives there
distractors.whyFails: 'During' says when something happened inside a period; it does not measure how long a state has lasted.
distractors.whyFailsId: “during” bilang kapan sesuatu terjadi di dalam suatu masa, bukan ngukur berapa lama keadaan itu bertahan.
distractors.misconceptionId: rentangnya ditutup seolah udah selesai.

distractors.misconception: uses 'for' before a starting point
distractors.whyFails: 'From' needs an end point ('from 2015 to 2025'); on its own it cannot follow the present perfect here.
distractors.whyFailsId: “from” butuh titik akhir (“from 2015 to 2025”). Sendirian, dia nggak bisa ngikut present perfect di sini.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai “for” di depan titik mulai, padahal for buat lamanya waktu.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Ten years' is a length of time, so the present perfect takes 'for': has taught for ten years.
explanation.rule: Present perfect + for + length of time; present perfect + since + starting point.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Since' wants a starting point; 'during' names when, not how long; 'from' needs a 'to' to close the range.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: is it a number of years or a date? Number → for. Date → since.
explanation.memoryCue: For ten years, since 2015.
explanation.ruleId: Present perfect + for + lamanya waktu. Present perfect + since + titik mulai.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Ten years” itu lamanya waktu, jadi present perfect-nya pakai “for”: has taught for ten years.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Since” minta titik mulai. “During” nyebut kapan, bukan berapa lama. “From” butuh “to” buat nutup rentangnya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya: ini jumlah tahun atau tanggal? Jumlah → for. Tanggal → since.
explanation.memoryCueId: Lamanya waktu pakai “for”, titik mulai pakai “since”: “for ten years”, “since 2015”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pilih “for” di depan lamanya waktu di kalimat present perfect.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai “since” di depan rentang kayak “ten years”, atau ngilangin present perfect-nya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali lamanya waktu → present perfect tetap → pakai for, bukan since

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use the irregular comparative 'worse' for 'bad' in a comparison with 'than'.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner builds the comparative of 'bad' with -er or 'more', or reaches for the superlative.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify 'than' -> select a comparative -> recall that bad is irregular -> apply worse
templates.stem: The traffic today is ___ than yesterday. We will be late.

distractors.misconception: regular -er ending forced onto an irregular adjective
distractors.whyFails: 'Bad' is irregular; it never takes -er.
distractors.whyFailsId: “bad” itu tak beraturan, nggak pernah pakai -er.
distractors.misconceptionId: akhiran -er dipaksain ke kata sifat tak beraturan.

distractors.misconception: regular 'more + adjective' pattern applied to an irregular adjective
distractors.whyFails: 'More bad' follows the regular pattern, but 'bad' has its own form: worse.
distractors.whyFailsId: “more bad” ngikutin pola biasa, padahal “bad” punya bentuk sendiri: worse.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola “more + kata sifat” dipakai buat kata sifat tak beraturan.

distractors.misconception: superlative 'best' used where 'than' demands a comparative
distractors.whyFails: 'Worst' compares three or more things; 'than' signals a two-way comparison.
distractors.whyFailsId: “worst” buat bandingin tiga atau lebih. “Than” nandain perbandingan dua hal.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk paling dipakai padahal “than” minta bentuk banding.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Than' asks for a comparative, and the comparative of 'bad' is the irregular 'worse'.
explanation.rule: Irregular comparatives: good → better, bad → worse, far → further.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Badder' and 'more bad' apply regular patterns to an irregular word; 'worst' is the superlative.
explanation.howToAvoid: Memorize the short list of irregular pairs before you reach for -er or more.
explanation.memoryCue: Good, better — bad, worse.
explanation.ruleId: Bentuk banding tak beraturan: good → better, bad → worse, far → further.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Than” minta bentuk banding, dan bentuk banding “bad” itu “worse”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Badder” dan “more bad” nerapin pola biasa ke kata tak beraturan. “Worst” bentuk paling.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Hafalin daftar pendek pasangan tak beraturan sebelum kamu ambil -er atau more.
explanation.memoryCueId: Hafalin pasangannya: good jadi better, bad jadi worse.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai bentuk tak beraturan “worse” buat “bad” di perbandingan dengan “than”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu bikin perbandingan “bad” pakai -er atau “more”, atau malah ambil bentuk paling.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat “than” → butuh bentuk banding → bad itu tak beraturan → worse

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'more' before a long adjective in a comparison.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner adds -er to a long adjective or stacks 'more' and -er together.
templates.reasoningOperation: count the syllables -> identify a long adjective -> apply more + adjective without -er
templates.stem: This book is ___ (interesting) than the film.

distractors.misconception: adds -er to a long adjective
distractors.whyFails: 'Interesting' has three syllables, so it takes 'more', not -er.
distractors.whyFailsId: “interesting” tiga suku kata, jadi pakai “more”, bukan -er.
distractors.misconceptionId: nambahin -er ke kata sifat panjang, padahal yang panjang pakai more.

distractors.misconception: doubles the comparative marking by putting 'more' before an adjective already ending in '-er'
distractors.whyFails: 'More' and -er both mark the comparative; use only one.
distractors.whyFailsId: “more” dan -er sama-sama nandain banding. Pakai satu aja.
distractors.misconceptionId: tanda bandingnya dobel: more plus -er.

distractors.misconception: uses the superlative after 'the' for a two-item comparison
distractors.whyFails: 'Than' compares two things, so the comparative is needed, not the superlative.
distractors.whyFailsId: “than” bandingin dua hal, jadi butuh bentuk banding, bukan bentuk paling.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai bentuk paling, padahal cuma dua hal yang dibandingin.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Interesting' is a long adjective, so its comparative is 'more interesting'.
explanation.rule: Short adjectives take -er (cheaper); long adjectives take more (more interesting). Never both.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Interestinger' forces -er onto a long word; 'more interestinger' marks the comparative twice; 'the most interesting' is a superlative.
explanation.howToAvoid: Say the adjective aloud: three syllables or more → more.
explanation.memoryCue: Long word → more; short word → -er.
explanation.ruleId: Kata sifat pendek pakai -er (cheaper). Kata sifat panjang pakai more (more interesting). Jangan dua-duanya.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Interesting” kata sifat panjang, jadi bentuk bandingnya “more interesting”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Interestinger” maksain -er ke kata panjang. “More interestinger” nandain banding dua kali. “The most interesting” bentuk paling.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Ucapin kata sifatnya: tiga suku kata atau lebih → more.
explanation.memoryCueId: Kata panjang → more. Kata pendek → -er.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “more” di depan kata sifat panjang saat membandingkan.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nambahin -er ke kata sifat panjang, atau numpuk “more” sama -er sekaligus.
templates.reasoningOperationId: hitung suku katanya → kata sifat panjang → more + kata sifat, tanpa -er

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Keep an adjective, not an -ly adverb, after the verb be.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner adds -ly after 'is/are' because the word describes how something seems.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the verb -> check whether it is be -> select an adjective to describe the subject
templates.stem: Be careful, the soup is very ___.

distractors.misconception: uses the adverb where an adjective after 'be' is needed
distractors.whyFails: After 'is', the word describes the soup itself, so it must be an adjective, not an -ly adverb.
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “is”, katanya ngegambarin supnya sendiri, jadi harus kata sifat, bukan -ly.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai bentuk -ly sesudah is/are, padahal sesudah be yang dibutuhin kata sifat.

distractors.misconception: uses the bare adjective after an action verb where a manner adverb in '-ly' is required
distractors.whyFails: 'Heat' is a noun or verb; 'very' needs an adjective after it.
distractors.whyFailsId: “heat” itu kata benda atau kata kerja. “Very” butuh kata sifat sesudahnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata benda dipakai di tempat kata sifat.

distractors.misconception: switches to a comparative adjective although nothing is being compared and the slot needs an adverb
distractors.whyFails: Nothing is being compared, and 'very' does not go with a comparative.
distractors.whyFailsId: nggak ada yang dibandingin, dan “very” nggak cocok sama bentuk banding.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk banding dipakai padahal nggak ada yang dibandingin.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Is' links the soup to a description, so the adjective 'hot' is required.
explanation.rule: After be (am/is/are) use an adjective; after an action verb use an -ly adverb.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Hotly' is an adverb; 'heat' is not an adjective; 'hotter' compares, but nothing is compared here.
explanation.howToAvoid: See is/are before the gap? Choose the plain adjective.
explanation.memoryCue: Is hot, walks slowly.
explanation.ruleId: Sesudah be (am/is/are) pakai kata sifat. Sesudah kata kerja aksi pakai kata keterangan -ly.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Is” nyambungin sup sama gambarannya, jadi butuh kata sifat “hot”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Hotly” kata keterangan. “Heat” bukan kata sifat. “Hotter” bentuk banding, padahal nggak ada yang dibandingin.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Ada is/are di depan titik-titik? Pilih kata sifat polos.
explanation.memoryCueId: Sesudah is pakai kata sifat: is hot. Sesudah kata kerja aksi pakai -ly: walks slowly.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Sesudah kata kerja be, pakai kata sifat, bukan kata keterangan -ly.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nambahin -ly sesudah “is/are” karena kata itu ngegambarin sesuatu.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cari kata kerjanya → ternyata be → gambarkan subjeknya pakai kata sifat

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Ask about a countable plural noun with 'How many'.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner asks about countable things with 'how much' or drops the quantity word.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the noun -> check that it is plural and countable -> select How many
templates.stem: ___ brothers and sisters do you have?

distractors.misconception: asks about a countable plural noun with 'how much'
distractors.whyFails: 'Brothers and sisters' can be counted, so the question word is 'how many'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “brothers and sisters” bisa dihitung, jadi kata tanyanya “how many”.
distractors.misconceptionId: nanya benda yang bisa dihitung pakai “how much”, padahal harusnya “how many”.

distractors.misconception: asks quantity with bare 'how' and drops the quantity word entirely
distractors.whyFails: Bare 'how' asks about manner, not number.
distractors.whyFailsId: “how” sendirian nanya cara, bukan jumlah.
distractors.misconceptionId: nanya jumlah cuma pakai “how”, kata jumlahnya hilang.

distractors.misconception: adds a partitive 'of' straight after 'how much' before a bare noun
distractors.whyFails: 'Of' only fits before 'the/your/them': how many of your friends, not how many of brothers.
distractors.whyFailsId: “of” cuma pas di depan “the/your/them”: how many of your friends, bukan how many of brothers.
distractors.misconceptionId: nambahin “of” langsung di depan kata benda polos.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Brothers and sisters' is a plural countable noun, so the question starts with 'How many'.
explanation.rule: How many + plural countable noun; how much + uncountable noun.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'How much' is for uncountable nouns; 'how' alone asks about manner; 'how many of' needs 'the/your' after it.
explanation.howToAvoid: Can you put a number before the noun (two brothers)? Then ask 'How many'.
explanation.memoryCue: Count it → how many.
explanation.ruleId: How many + kata benda jamak yang bisa dihitung. How much + kata benda yang nggak bisa dihitung.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Brothers and sisters” bisa dihitung dan jamak, jadi pertanyaannya mulai dari “How many”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “How much” buat yang nggak bisa dihitung. “How” sendirian nanya cara. “How many of” butuh “the/your” sesudahnya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Bisa ditaruh angka di depannya (two brothers)? Tanyanya pakai “How many”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Bisa dihitung → how many.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Nanya jumlah benda yang bisa dihitung pakai “How many”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nanya benda yang bisa dihitung pakai “how much”, atau ngilangin kata jumlahnya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat kata bendanya → jamak dan bisa dihitung → How many

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Introduce a result with 'so' after the reason has been stated.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses 'because' in front of the result instead of the reason.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify which clause is the reason and which is the result -> apply so to the result clause
templates.stem: It was raining hard, ___ we stayed at home.

distractors.misconception: introduces the result clause with 'because'
distractors.whyFails: 'Because' introduces the reason, but 'we stayed at home' is the result of the rain.
distractors.whyFailsId: “because” buka alasan, padahal “we stayed at home” itu akibat dari hujannya.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai “because” di depan akibat, padahal because buat alasan.

distractors.misconception: puts 'because of' before a full clause although it only takes a noun phrase
distractors.whyFails: 'Because of' is followed by a noun ('because of the rain'), not a full clause.
distractors.whyFailsId: “because of” diikuti kata benda (“because of the rain”), bukan klausa utuh.
distractors.misconceptionId: “because of” ditaruh di depan klausa utuh, padahal cuma buat kata benda.

distractors.misconception: uses the purpose connector 'so that' where a plain reason connector is needed
distractors.whyFails: 'So that' shows a purpose or goal; staying home was a result, not a plan.
distractors.whyFailsId: “so that” nunjukin tujuan. Tinggal di rumah itu akibat, bukan rencana.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai penghubung tujuan “so that”, padahal butuh penghubung akibat.

explanation.whyCorrect: The rain is the reason and staying home is the result, so the result clause starts with 'so'.
explanation.rule: Reason + so + result. Because + reason.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Because' would mark staying home as the reason; 'because of' needs a noun; 'so that' expresses purpose.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: does this clause explain why (because) or what happened next (so)?
explanation.memoryCue: Rain → so → stayed home.
explanation.ruleId: Alasan + so + akibat. Because + alasan.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Hujan itu alasannya dan tinggal di rumah itu akibatnya, jadi klausa akibat mulai dari “so”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Because” bakal bikin tinggal di rumah jadi alasannya. “Because of” butuh kata benda. “So that” nyatain tujuan.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya: klausa ini jelasin kenapa (because) atau apa yang terjadi berikutnya (so)?
explanation.memoryCueId: Hujan → so → tinggal di rumah.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Buka akibat pakai “so” sesudah alasannya disebut.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai “because” di depan akibat, bukan di depan alasan.
templates.reasoningOperationId: mana alasan dan mana akibat → klausa akibat pakai so

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Keep the state verb 'know' in the present simple even when talking about now.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner puts 'know' into the continuous because the situation is happening at the moment.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify a state verb -> recall that states do not take -ing -> keep the present simple
templates.stem: Sorry, I ___ the answer right now.

distractors.misconception: Assumes present time always requires present continuous.
distractors.whyFails: 'Know' is a state verb, so it stays in the present simple even with 'right now'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “know” kata kerja keadaan, jadi tetap present simple walau ada “right now”.
distractors.misconceptionId: ngira waktu sekarang selalu butuh bentuk -ing.

distractors.misconception: reduces the sentence to a fragment: an -ing form with no finite verb to carry the tense
distractors.whyFails: A negative present simple needs 'don't'; bare 'not know' is not a full verb.
distractors.whyFailsId: negatif present simple butuh “don't”. “Not know” polos bukan kata kerja utuh.
distractors.misconceptionId: kalimatnya jadi potongan tanpa kata kerja utuh.

distractors.misconception: bare-verb-without-auxiliary
distractors.whyFails: After 'don't' the verb is bare: don't know, never don't knowing.
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “don't” kata kerjanya polos: don't know, bukan don't knowing.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja polos tanpa kata bantu.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Know' describes a state, not an action, so even 'right now' takes the present simple: don't know.
explanation.rule: State verbs (know, like, want, belong) normally stay in the present simple, not the continuous.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Am not knowing' forces a state into -ing; 'not know' has no auxiliary; 'don't knowing' adds -ing after don't.
explanation.howToAvoid: 'Right now' does not mean -ing automatically; check whether the verb is a state first.
explanation.memoryCue: Know, like, want — no -ing.
explanation.ruleId: Kata kerja keadaan (know, like, want, belong) biasanya tetap present simple, bukan bentuk -ing.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Know” ngegambarin keadaan, bukan aksi, jadi walau ada “right now” tetap present simple: don't know.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Am not knowing” maksain keadaan jadi -ing. “Not know” nggak punya kata bantu. “Don't knowing” nambah -ing sesudah don't.
explanation.howToAvoidId: “Right now” nggak otomatis berarti -ing. Cek dulu kata kerjanya keadaan atau bukan.
explanation.memoryCueId: Know, like, want — tanpa -ing.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kata kerja keadaan “know” tetap present simple walau ngomongin sekarang.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu bikin “know” jadi bentuk -ing karena kejadiannya lagi berlangsung.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali kata kerja keadaan → keadaan nggak pakai -ing → present simple

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'any' after a negative verb instead of a second negative word.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner adds 'no' after 'don't', producing a double negative.
templates.reasoningOperation: check that the verb is already negative -> recall the one-negative rule -> select any
templates.stem: We don't have ___ milk left, so I'll buy some.

distractors.misconception: uses 'no' before a verb already negated with 'not'
distractors.whyFails: 'Don't' is already negative; adding 'no' makes a double negative.
distractors.whyFailsId: “don't” udah negatif. Nambah “no” bikin negatif dobel.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai “no” sesudah kata kerja yang udah negatif, jadi negatifnya dobel.

distractors.misconception: combining a negated verb ('didn't') with a negative pronoun, creating a non-standard double negative
distractors.whyFails: 'Nothing' is a negative pronoun and cannot stand before the noun 'milk' after 'don't'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “nothing” itu kata ganti negatif, nggak bisa berdiri di depan kata benda “milk” sesudah “don't”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja negatif digabung sama kata ganti negatif.

distractors.misconception: incorrectly splitting the compound negative pronoun into two words
distractors.whyFails: 'None' replaces a noun ('we have none'); it cannot go directly before 'milk'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “none” ngegantiin kata benda (“we have none”), nggak bisa langsung di depan “milk”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti dipakai di depan kata benda.

explanation.whyCorrect: The verb 'don't have' already carries the negative, so the noun takes 'any': don't have any milk.
explanation.rule: One negative per clause: don't + any, or have + no. Never don't + no.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'No' and 'nothing' double the negative; 'none' cannot sit before a noun.
explanation.howToAvoid: Count the negatives. If the verb has 'not', the next word is 'any'.
explanation.memoryCue: Don't … any / have … no.
explanation.ruleId: Satu negatif per klausa: don't + any, atau have + no. Jangan don't + no.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Don't have” udah negatif, jadi kata bendanya pakai “any”: don't have any milk.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “No” dan “nothing” bikin negatif dobel. “None” nggak bisa duduk di depan kata benda.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Hitung negatifnya. Kalau kata kerjanya udah ada “not”, kata berikutnya “any”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Satu negatif aja: don't … any, atau have … no.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Sesudah kata kerja negatif, pakai “any”, bukan kata negatif kedua.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nambahin “no” sesudah “don't”, jadi negatifnya dobel.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kata kerjanya udah negatif → cuma boleh satu negatif → pakai any

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'the' before an ordinal like 'first' because it points to one specific item.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner treats 'first day' as a new, indefinite noun and uses 'a'.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the ordinal first -> recall that only one first exists -> select the
templates.stem: Today is ___ first day of the school year.

distractors.misconception: uses the indefinite article before 'first'
distractors.whyFails: There is only one first day, so it is specific and takes 'the'.
distractors.whyFailsId: hari pertama cuma ada satu, jadi udah pasti dan pakai “the”.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai “a” di depan first, padahal urutan kayak first selalu pakai the.

distractors.misconception: same indefinite-article error as 'a', plus a vowel-sound trigger confusion
distractors.whyFails: 'An' is indefinite and also wrong before the consonant sound in 'first'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “an” itu artikel nggak pasti, dan juga salah di depan bunyi konsonan di “first”.
distractors.misconceptionId: artikel nggak pasti dipakai dan bunyi awalnya juga bukan vokal.

distractors.misconception: assuming proper-noun-adjacent phrases never take an article
distractors.whyFails: A singular noun phrase like 'first day' cannot stand without an article.
distractors.whyFailsId: frasa kata benda tunggal kayak “first day” nggak bisa berdiri tanpa artikel.
distractors.misconceptionId: ngira frasa yang mirip nama nggak butuh artikel.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'First' picks out one unique day, so the noun phrase is definite: the first day.
explanation.rule: Use 'the' with ordinals (the first, the second) and superlatives (the best), because only one thing fits.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'A' and 'an' present the day as one of many; leaving out the article is not possible with a singular count noun.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ordinal or superlative in front of the noun? Reach for 'the'.
explanation.memoryCue: The first, the last, the best.
explanation.ruleId: Pakai “the” sama kata urutan (the first, the second) dan bentuk paling (the best), karena yang cocok cuma satu.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “First” nunjuk satu hari yang unik, jadi frasanya pasti: the first day.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “A” dan “an” nampilin harinya sebagai salah satu dari banyak. Tanpa artikel nggak mungkin buat kata benda tunggal yang bisa dihitung.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Ada kata urutan atau bentuk paling di depan kata benda? Ambil “the”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Urutan dan bentuk paling selalu pakai the: the first, the last, the best.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “the” di depan urutan kayak “first” karena nunjuk satu hal yang pasti.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nganggap “first day” kata benda baru yang belum jelas, jadi pakai “a”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat kata urutan “first” → yang pertama cuma satu → the

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'would + base verb' in the result clause of an unreal present condition.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner puts 'will' or the past simple in the result clause after an unreal if-clause.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify a past simple unreal if-clause -> apply would + base verb in the result clause
templates.stem: If I had more free time, I ___ a new language.

distractors.misconception: real/likely framing applied to an admittedly unlikely event
