explanation.whyCorrectId: Janjinya dilaporin di masa lampau, jadi “will” jadi “would”: said he would help.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Will” nggak mundur. “Wills” nambah -s yang nggak mungkin. “Would to” nyelipin “to” ekstra.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Ada modal di kalimat langsungnya? Tuker sama pasangan lampaunya dan kata kerjanya tetap polos.
explanation.memoryCueId: Will → would sesudah said.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Geser “will” jadi “would” waktu laporin janji belakangan.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu biarin “will” apa adanya atau nganggap modal kayak kata kerja biasa sesudah kata pelapor lampau.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali modal will → cek kata pelapornya lampau → geser will jadi would

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Report a yes/no question with 'if' and statement word order.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner keeps the question inversion or uses 'that' when reporting a yes/no question.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify a yes/no question -> select if or whether -> restore subject + verb order and backshift
templates.stem: "Are you hungry?" she asked. → She asked me ___ hungry.

distractors.misconception: keeps direct-question inversion and omits if/whether
distractors.whyFails: It keeps the question inversion and has no 'if' to introduce the reported question.
distractors.whyFailsId: masih urutan pertanyaan dan nggak ada “if” buat ngenalin pertanyaan yang dilaporin.
distractors.misconceptionId: pembalikan khas pertanyaan langsung dipertahanin dan pembukanya dihilangin.

distractors.misconception: uses 'that' for a yes/no reported question
distractors.whyFails: 'That' reports statements; a yes/no question needs 'if' or 'whether'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “that” buat laporin kalimat berita. Pertanyaan ya/tidak butuh “if” atau “whether”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “that” dipakai buat pertanyaan “yes” atau “no” yang dilaporin.

distractors.misconception: adds whether but retains auxiliary-subject inversion
distractors.whyFails: 'If' is right, but the subject must come before the verb: if I was.
distractors.whyFailsId: “if” udah bener, tapi subjeknya harus sebelum kata kerja: if I was.
distractors.misconceptionId: pembukanya udah bener tapi pembalikan kata bantunya dipertahanin.

explanation.whyCorrect: A yes/no question is reported with 'if' plus statement order, and 'are' shifts back to 'was'.
explanation.rule: Reported yes/no question: asked + if/whether + subject + verb (backshifted).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Was I' and 'if was I' keep the inversion, and 'that I was' uses the statement connector.
explanation.howToAvoid: Can the direct question be answered with yes or no? Then start the report with 'if'.
explanation.memoryCue: Are you…? → asked if I was…
explanation.ruleId: Pertanyaan ya/tidak yang dilaporin: asked + if/whether + subjek + kata kerja (dimundurin).
explanation.whyCorrectId: Pertanyaan ya/tidak dilaporin pakai “if” plus urutan kalimat berita, dan “are” mundur jadi “was”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Was I” dan “if was I” masih kebalik. “That I was” pakai penghubung kalimat berita.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Pertanyaan langsungnya bisa dijawab ya atau tidak? Mulai laporannya pakai “if”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Pertanyaan “Are you…?” dilaporin jadi “asked if I was…”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Laporin pertanyaan ya/tidak pakai “if” dan urutan kalimat berita.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu tetap pakai urutan pertanyaan atau pakai “that” waktu laporin pertanyaan ya/tidak.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali pertanyaan ya/tidak → pilih if atau whether → balikin urutan subjek + kata kerja dan mundurin waktunya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use zero article with 'hospital' when someone is there as a patient.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner adds 'the' or 'a' to an institution noun used for its purpose.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the institution noun -> check that the person is there as a patient -> select no article
templates.stem: Grandpa is in ___ after his operation, so we visit him every evening.

distractors.misconception: focuses on a particular building instead of institutional attendance
distractors.whyFails: 'The hospital' points to a building; being a patient there uses no article.
distractors.whyFailsId: “the hospital” nunjuk gedungnya. Dirawat sebagai pasien nggak pakai artikel.
distractors.misconceptionId: perhatian dialihin ke satu gedung tertentu, bukan ke kegiatan belajarnya.

distractors.misconception: introduces one unspecified building rather than the attendance idiom
distractors.whyFails: 'A hospital' introduces one random building, not Grandpa's stay as a patient.
distractors.whyFailsId: “a hospital” ngenalin satu gedung sembarang, bukan rawat inap Kakek.
distractors.misconceptionId: satu gedung yang nggak jelas dikenalin, bukan ungkapan kegiatan belajarnya.

distractors.misconception: turns one routine of attendance into a generic plural destination
distractors.whyFails: Plural 'hospitals' turns one stay into a general destination.
distractors.whyFailsId: “hospitals” yang jamak bikin satu rawat inap jadi tujuan umum.
distractors.misconceptionId: satu kebiasaan belajar diubah jadi tujuan jamak yang umum.

explanation.whyCorrect: Grandpa is there as a patient, so 'in hospital' takes no article.
explanation.rule: No article when the institution is used for its purpose: in hospital, at school, in prison. Add 'the' for the building itself.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'The' and 'a' treat the hospital as a building, and the plural makes no sense for one stay.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: patient, pupil, or prisoner? Then drop the article.
explanation.memoryCue: In hospital = as a patient.
explanation.ruleId: Tanpa artikel kalau lembaganya dipakai sesuai fungsi: in hospital, at school, in prison. Pakai “the” buat gedungnya.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Kakek di sana sebagai pasien, jadi “in hospital” tanpa artikel.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “The” dan “a” nganggap rumah sakitnya cuma gedung. Jamak nggak masuk akal buat satu kali rawat.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya: pasien, murid, atau tahanan? Kalau ya, buang artikelnya.
explanation.memoryCueId: In hospital = sebagai pasien.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Tanpa artikel di depan “hospital” kalau orangnya dirawat sebagai pasien.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nambahin “the” atau “a” ke kata lembaga yang dipakai sesuai fungsinya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali kata lembaganya → cek orangnya ada di sana sebagai pasien → pilih tanpa artikel

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Leave out the object relative pronoun, or use 'that', for a thing.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses 'who', 'whose', or 'what' for a non-human object in a relative clause.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the antecedent as a thing -> check that it is the object of the clause -> select that or nothing
templates.stem: The film ___ we watched last night was really boring.

distractors.misconception: Uses a personal relative pronoun for a non-human antecedent.
distractors.whyFails: 'Who' is for people; a film needs 'that' or 'which'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “who” buat orang. Film butuh “that” atau “which”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata penghubung buat orang dipakai pada kata benda yang bukan orang.

distractors.misconception: uses possessive 'whose' where the clause needs an object relative pronoun or nothing at all
distractors.whyFails: 'Whose' shows possession; nothing belongs to anyone here.
distractors.whyFailsId: “whose” nunjukin kepemilikan. Di sini nggak ada yang punya apa-apa.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kepemilikan “whose” dipasang padahal nggak ada makna punya-punyaan di kalimatnya.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'what' as a relative pronoun, a common cross-linguistic transfer error.
distractors.whyFails: 'What' is never a relative pronoun after a noun in English.
distractors.whyFailsId: “what” nggak pernah jadi kata ganti relatif sesudah kata benda di bahasa Inggris.
distractors.misconceptionId: “what” dipakai sebagai kata penghubung, kekeliruan yang lazim kebawa dari bahasa lain.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'The film' is a thing and the object of 'watched', so 'that' fits — and it could even be left out.
explanation.rule: Object relative pronoun for things: that / which, or nothing at all: the film (that) we watched.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Who' is for people, 'whose' marks possession, and 'what' cannot follow a noun.
explanation.howToAvoid: Try deleting the pronoun. If the sentence still works, 'that' or nothing is right.
explanation.memoryCue: The film (that) we watched.
explanation.ruleId: Kata ganti relatif objek buat benda: that / which, atau nggak ada sama sekali: the film (that) we watched.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “The film” itu benda dan objek dari “watched”, jadi “that” pas — bahkan bisa dibuang.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Who” buat orang. “Whose” nandain kepemilikan. “What” nggak bisa ngikut kata benda.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Coba hapus kata gantinya. Kalau kalimatnya masih jalan, “that” atau kosong yang bener.
explanation.memoryCueId: Kata gantinya bisa hilang: “the film (that) we watched”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Buang kata ganti relatif objek, atau pakai “that”, buat benda.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai “who”, “whose”, atau “what” buat objek bukan orang di klausa relatif.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali yang dirujuk itu benda → cek dia objek klausanya → pilih that atau kosong

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'a lot' before a comparative to strengthen it.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner puts 'very', 'so', or 'too' before a comparative adjective.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the comparative -> select an intensifier that works with comparatives -> avoid very/so/too
templates.stem: The test was ___ easier than I expected.

distractors.misconception: Transfers the common absolute-adjective intensifier 'very' onto a comparative form.
distractors.whyFails: 'Very' goes before a plain adjective (very easy), not before 'easier'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “very” di depan kata sifat biasa (very easy), bukan di depan “easier”.
distractors.misconceptionId: penguat kata sifat biasa kebawa ke bentuk perbandingan.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'so', which needs a following 'that'-clause or exclamatory context, as a plain intensifier before a comparative.
distractors.whyFails: 'So' needs a 'that' clause or an exclamation and does not modify 'easier'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “so” butuh klausa “that” atau kalimat seru, dan nggak nempel ke “easier”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “so” yang minta anak kalimat akibat dipakai sebagai penguat biasa.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'too' (meaning excessive) as if it were a neutral intensifier.
distractors.whyFails: 'Too' means 'more than is good' and cannot strengthen a comparative.
distractors.whyFailsId: “too” artinya “lebih dari yang baik” dan nggak bisa nguatin bentuk banding.
distractors.misconceptionId: “too” yang berarti berlebihan dipakai seolah penguat yang netral.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Easier' is a comparative, so it takes a comparative intensifier: a lot easier.
explanation.rule: Before a comparative use much, far, a lot, or a bit — never very.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Very', 'so', and 'too' belong with plain adjectives, not with -er forms.
explanation.howToAvoid: See -er or 'more'? Reach for much / far / a lot.
explanation.memoryCue: Very easy, but a lot easier.
explanation.ruleId: Di depan bentuk banding pakai much, far, a lot, atau a bit — jangan very.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Easier” bentuk banding, jadi penguatnya penguat bentuk banding: a lot easier.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Very”, “so”, dan “too” pasangannya kata sifat biasa, bukan bentuk -er.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Lihat -er atau “more”? Ambil much / far / a lot.
explanation.memoryCueId: Very easy, tapi a lot easier.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “a lot” di depan bentuk banding buat nguatinnya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu naruh “very”, “so”, atau “too” di depan kata sifat bentuk banding.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali bentuk bandingnya → pilih penguat yang cocok sama bentuk banding → hindari very/so/too

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Echo a surprising statement by repeating its words and swapping in a question word.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner rebuilds a full inverted question instead of echoing the statement.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify an echo for clarification -> keep the statement order -> substitute the question word for the missing part
templates.stem: A: "My brother is moving to Iceland." B: "He's moving ___?"

distractors.misconception: Forms a standard inverted question instead of echoing the statement's structure.
distractors.whyFails: It turns the echo into a standard inverted question and repeats the subject.
distractors.whyFailsId: ngubah gemanya jadi pertanyaan biasa yang kebalik dan ngulang subjeknya.
distractors.misconceptionId: pertanyaan terbalik yang baku disusun, bukan ngulang susunan pernyataannya.

distractors.misconception: Fully reformulates the question with standard word order rather than echoing.
distractors.whyFails: It rebuilds the whole question instead of echoing the surprising part.
distractors.whyFailsId: bikin ulang seluruh pertanyaan, bukan ngulang bagian yang bikin kaget.
distractors.misconceptionId: kalimatnya disusun ulang sepenuhnya, bukan diulang.

distractors.misconception: Uses a gerund fragment instead of the statement's original verb form.
distractors.whyFails: It repeats the verb fragment; the echo already has 'He's moving' before the gap.
distractors.whyFailsId: ngulang potongan kata kerjanya. Gemanya udah punya “He's moving” sebelum titik-titik.
distractors.misconceptionId: penggalan bentuk -ing dipakai menggantikan bentuk kata kerja aslinya.

explanation.whyCorrect: An echo question keeps the statement's order and replaces the surprising part with 'where': He's moving where?
explanation.rule: Echo question: repeat the statement, put the wh-word in the slot of the surprising information, add rising intonation.
explanation.whyOthersFail: The other options switch to inverted question order or duplicate words already in the echo.
explanation.howToAvoid: Copy the sentence, then drop the wh-word exactly where the surprising word was.
explanation.memoryCue: He's moving where?
explanation.ruleId: Pertanyaan gema: ulangi pernyataannya, taruh kata tanya di posisi info yang bikin kaget, nada naik.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Pertanyaan gema ngikutin urutan pernyataan dan ngeganti bagian yang bikin kaget sama “where”: He's moving where?
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Pilihan lain balik ke urutan pertanyaan biasa atau ngulang kata yang udah ada di gemanya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Salin kalimatnya, lalu taruh kata tanya persis di tempat kata yang bikin kaget.
explanation.memoryCueId: He's moving where?

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Ulangi pernyataan yang bikin kaget dengan nyelipin kata tanya di bagian yang dikagetin.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu bikin ulang pertanyaan lengkap yang kebalik, bukan ngulang pernyataannya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali ini pertanyaan gema buat memastikan → urutan pernyataannya tetap → ganti bagian yang bikin kaget sama kata tanya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use the present perfect with 'this month' because the period is still open.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses the past simple because the actions are finished, ignoring that the time period continues.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the unfinished period this month -> select the present perfect -> avoid closed-past forms
templates.stem: It's only the 10th, and I ___ two books this month already.

distractors.misconception: Uses past simple because a specific number of emails is mentioned.
distractors.whyFails: Past simple closes the period, but 'this month' is still going on.
distractors.whyFailsId: past simple nutup periodenya, padahal “this month” masih jalan.
distractors.misconceptionId: past simple dipakai padahal rentang waktunya belum tutup.

distractors.misconception: Uses past continuous to describe a series of completed actions.
distractors.whyFails: Past continuous shows an action in progress, not two completed books.
distractors.whyFailsId: past continuous nunjukin aksi yang lagi jalan, bukan dua buku yang udah selesai.
distractors.misconceptionId: past continuous dipakai buat nggambarin serangkaian tindakan yang udah tuntas.

distractors.misconception: Uses present simple, ignoring that the sentence reports completed past actions within the current period.
distractors.whyFails: Present continuous means right now; 'already' shows the books are finished.
distractors.whyFailsId: present continuous artinya sekarang ini. “Already” nunjukin bukunya udah selesai.
distractors.misconceptionId: present simple dipakai padahal kalimatnya nyebut tindakan lampau tertentu.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'This month' is not over, so completed actions inside it take the present perfect: have read.
explanation.rule: Present perfect with unfinished periods: today, this week, this month, this year.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Read' treats the month as finished, 'was reading' shows progress, and 'am reading' means at this moment.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: is the time period still open? If yes, use have/has + past participle.
explanation.memoryCue: This month (still open) → have read.
explanation.ruleId: Present perfect sama periode yang belum selesai: today, this week, this month, this year.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “This month” belum berakhir, jadi aksi yang selesai di dalamnya pakai present perfect: have read.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Read” nganggap bulannya udah selesai. “Was reading” nunjukin proses. “Am reading” artinya saat ini.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya: periode waktunya masih terbuka? Kalau ya, pakai have/has + past participle.
explanation.memoryCueId: This month (masih terbuka) → have read.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai present perfect sama “this month” karena periodenya masih jalan.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai past simple karena aksinya udah selesai, padahal periode waktunya masih lanjut.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali periode yang belum selesai this month → pilih present perfect → hindari bentuk lampau tertutup

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'be able to' after 'will' because two modals cannot stand together.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner stacks 'will can' or puts a finite modal where a non-finite form is needed.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the modal will -> recall that can cannot follow another modal -> select be able to
templates.stem: After the course, you ___ speak basic Korean.

distractors.misconception: places the finite modal 'can' after infinitive 'to'
distractors.whyFails: 'Can' is a finite modal and cannot follow 'will'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “can” itu modal berkonjugasi dan nggak bisa ngikut “will”.
distractors.misconceptionId: modal bertense ditaruh sesudah “to”.

distractors.misconception: uses a finite past/conditional modal in a non-finite slot
distractors.whyFails: 'Could' is also a finite modal; two modals never stack.
distractors.whyFailsId: “could” juga modal berkonjugasi. Dua modal nggak pernah ditumpuk.
distractors.misconceptionId: modal bertense lampau dipakai di posisi yang minta bentuk tanpa tense.

distractors.misconception: uses a gerund-participle where a bare infinitive is required
distractors.whyFails: After 'will' the verb is the bare form 'be', not 'being'.
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “will” kata kerjanya bentuk polos “be”, bukan “being”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dipakai di posisi yang minta bentuk dasar.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Will' already fills the modal slot, so ability is expressed with 'be able to': will be able to speak.
explanation.rule: Ability after another modal or 'to': use be able to (will be able to, hope to be able to).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Will can' and 'will could' stack two modals, and 'will being' uses the wrong verb form.
explanation.howToAvoid: Need 'can' after will, must, or to? Swap it for 'be able to'.
explanation.memoryCue: Will + be able to.
explanation.ruleId: Kemampuan sesudah modal lain atau “to”: pakai be able to (will be able to, hope to be able to).
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Will” udah ngisi slot modal, jadi kemampuannya pakai “be able to”: will be able to speak.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Will can” dan “will could” numpuk dua modal. “Will being” salah bentuk kata kerja.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Butuh “can” sesudah will, must, atau to? Tuker sama “be able to”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Will + be able to.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “be able to” sesudah “will” karena dua modal nggak bisa berdiri bersama.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu numpuk “will can” atau naruh modal di tempat yang butuh bentuk tak berkonjugasi.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali modal will → ingat can nggak bisa ngikut modal lain → pilih be able to

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Shift 'you' and 'your' to 'me' and 'my' when the listener reports what was said to them.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner keeps the original second-person pronouns or shifts only one of them.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify who is speaking now -> shift the subject pronoun -> shift the possessive to match
templates.stem: Nina told me: "You forgot your umbrella." → Nina told me that ___ had forgotten ___ umbrella.

distractors.misconception: Keeps the original speaker's first-person pronoun and possessive unchanged in the reported version.
distractors.whyFails: It keeps Nina's original 'you/your' although I am now reporting about myself.
distractors.whyFailsId: masih pakai “you/your” aslinya dari Nina, padahal sekarang aku yang laporin soal diriku.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti dan kata kepemilikan penutur aslinya dibiarin utuh.

distractors.misconception: Shifts the subject pronoun but forgets to shift the corresponding possessive.
distractors.whyFails: The subject shifts to 'I' but the possessive is left as 'your'.
distractors.whyFailsId: subjeknya geser jadi “I” tapi kata ganti miliknya masih “your”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti subjeknya udah digeser tapi kata kepemilikannya kelupaan.

distractors.misconception: Shifts the possessive but forgets to shift the subject pronoun.
distractors.whyFails: The possessive shifts to 'my' but the subject stays 'you'.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata ganti miliknya geser jadi “my” tapi subjeknya masih “you”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kepemilikannya udah digeser tapi kata ganti subjeknya kelupaan.

explanation.whyCorrect: Nina was talking to me, so 'you forgot your umbrella' becomes 'I had forgotten my umbrella'.
explanation.rule: Pronouns shift to the reporter's point of view — and subject and possessive must shift together.
explanation.whyOthersFail: One option shifts nothing, and the other two shift only half of the pair.
explanation.howToAvoid: Change the subject pronoun first, then check that the possessive matches it.
explanation.memoryCue: You/your (said to me) → I/my.
explanation.ruleId: Kata ganti geser ke sudut pandang pelapor — subjek dan kepemilikan harus geser bareng.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Nina ngomong ke aku, jadi “you forgot your umbrella” jadi “I had forgotten my umbrella”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Satu pilihan nggak geser apa-apa, dua lainnya cuma geser separuh pasangannya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Ganti kata ganti subjeknya dulu, lalu cek kata ganti miliknya udah cocok.
explanation.memoryCueId: Kata “you/your” yang dibilang ke aku berubah jadi “I/my”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Geser “you” dan “your” jadi “me” dan “my” waktu pendengar laporin apa yang dibilang ke dia.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu biarin kata ganti orang kedua aslinya, atau cuma geser salah satunya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali siapa yang ngomong sekarang → geser kata ganti subjeknya → geser kata gantinya milik supaya cocok

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'none of' before an object pronoun to say zero out of a group.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner drops 'of' before the pronoun or picks a quantifier with the wrong meaning.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the object pronoun them -> select a quantifier with of -> match the meaning zero
templates.stem: I called three friends, but ___ them answered.

distractors.misconception: drops 'of' before the object pronoun
distractors.whyFails: Before a pronoun like 'them', 'none' needs 'of'.
distractors.whyFailsId: di depan kata ganti kayak “them”, “none” butuh “of”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “of” dihilangin di depan kata ganti objek.

distractors.misconception: drops 'of' and ignores the explicitly two-person set
distractors.whyFails: 'No' goes directly before a noun (no friends), never before 'them'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “no” langsung di depan kata benda (no friends), nggak pernah di depan “them”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “of” dihilangin sekaligus ngabaikan bahwa kelompoknya jelas dua orang.

distractors.misconception: drops 'of' and reverses the affirmative meaning
distractors.whyFails: 'Any of them answered' is not negative; the sentence needs 'none of'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “any of them answered” nggak negatif. Kalimatnya butuh “none of”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “of” dihilangin sekaligus ngebalik makna kalimatnya jadi negatif.

explanation.whyCorrect: Nobody answered, and 'them' is a pronoun, so the form is 'none of them'.
explanation.rule: Quantifier + of + object pronoun: none of them, both of us, all of you, some of it.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'None' and 'no' are missing 'of', and 'any of' does not express zero.
explanation.howToAvoid: See them / us / you / it after the quantifier? Insert 'of'.
explanation.memoryCue: None of them, both of us.
explanation.ruleId: Penanda jumlah + of + kata ganti objek: none of them, both of us, all of you, some of it.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Nggak ada yang ngangkat, dan “them” itu kata ganti, jadi bentuknya “none of them”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “None” dan “no” kurang “of”. “Any of” nggak nyatain nol.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Ada them / us / you / it sesudah penanda jumlahnya? Selipin “of”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Di depan kata ganti selalu ada “of”: “none of them”, “both of us”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “none of” di depan kata ganti objek buat bilang nol dari sekelompok.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngilangin “of” di depan kata ganti, atau milih penanda jumlah yang maknanya salah.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali kata ganti objek them → pilih penanda jumlah plus of → cocokin maknanya nol

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'ones' to replace a plural noun after an adjective.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses singular 'one', 'them', or repeats the noun after an adjective.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the plural noun being replaced -> check that an adjective comes before the gap -> select ones
templates.stem: These shoes are too small. Do you have any bigger ___?

distractors.misconception: picks plural 'ones' to replace a single noun
distractors.whyFails: 'Shoes' is plural, so the substitute must be plural 'ones'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “shoes” jamak, jadi penggantinya harus “ones” yang jamak.
distractors.misconceptionId: “ones” jamak dipakai buat gantiin satu benda doang.

distractors.misconception: uses definite 'it' after 'a new' where the indefinite substitute 'one' is needed
distractors.whyFails: 'Them' cannot follow an adjective like 'bigger'; it stands alone.
distractors.whyFailsId: “them” nggak bisa ngikut kata sifat kayak “bigger”. Dia berdiri sendiri.
distractors.misconceptionId: “it” yang definit dipasang sesudah “a new”, padahal slotnya minta pengganti tak tentu “one”.

distractors.misconception: repeats the replaced noun and stacks the substitute 'one' after it
distractors.whyFails: It repeats the noun and adds the substitute on top of it.
distractors.whyFailsId: ngulang kata bendanya dan nambah pengganti di atasnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: nominanya diulang terus masih ditumpuk lagi sama pengganti “one”.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Ones' stands in for the plural 'shoes' after the adjective 'bigger': any bigger ones.
explanation.rule: Adjective + one (singular) / ones (plural) replaces a noun already mentioned.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'One' is singular, 'them' cannot take an adjective, and 'shoes ones' doubles the noun.
explanation.howToAvoid: Count the noun you are replacing: one thing → one, several → ones.
explanation.memoryCue: Bigger ones = bigger shoes.
explanation.ruleId: Kata sifat + one (tunggal) / ones (jamak) ngegantiin kata benda yang udah disebut.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Ones” ngegantiin “shoes” yang jamak sesudah kata sifat “bigger”: any bigger ones.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “One” tunggal. “Them” nggak bisa dikasih kata sifat. “Shoes ones” kata bendanya dobel.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Hitung kata benda yang diganti: satu → one, banyak → ones.
explanation.memoryCueId: Bigger ones = bigger shoes.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “ones” buat ngegantiin kata benda jamak sesudah kata sifat.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai “one” tunggal, “them”, atau ngulang kata bendanya sesudah kata sifat.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali kata benda jamak yang diganti → cek ada kata sifat sebelum titik-titik → pilih ones

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'forget to + verb' for a task that was not done.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses 'forget -ing' (a memory of a past event) when the meaning is a task left undone.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify a task that was not done -> select forget + to-infinitive -> avoid the memory pattern with -ing
templates.stem: Oh no, I forgot ___ the door when I left this morning!

distractors.misconception: applies the 'future duty' pattern ('remember to do') to a sentence that is actually recalling a completed past action
distractors.whyFails: 'Forget locking' would mean I have no memory of locking it; here the locking never happened.
distractors.whyFailsId: “forget locking” artinya aku nggak ingat pernah ngunci. Di sini nguncinya nggak pernah terjadi.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola kewajiban nanti dipakai buat kalimat yang lagi inget kejadian lampau.

distractors.misconception: uses the bare infinitive, which isn't a valid pattern after 'remember' in either meaning
distractors.whyFails: A bare verb cannot follow 'forget'.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata kerja polos nggak bisa ngikut “forget”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar dipakai padahal bukan pola yang sah sesudah “remember”.

distractors.misconception: applies a perfect to-infinitive after 'remember', which English does not use for recalling a past action
distractors.whyFails: The perfect infinitive is not used after 'forget' for a simple undone task.
distractors.whyFailsId: perfect infinitive nggak dipakai sesudah “forget” buat tugas biasa yang kelewat.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk to sempurna dipasang ke “remember”, padahal buat ingatan lampau pola itu nggak dipakai.

explanation.whyCorrect: The door was never locked, so 'forget to lock' (a task not done) is the meaning needed.
explanation.rule: Forget/remember + to-infinitive = a duty; forget/remember + -ing = a memory of something that happened.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Locking' points to a memory, 'lock' is bare, and 'to have locked' is the wrong pattern.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: did the action happen? If it did not, use 'forget to'.
explanation.memoryCue: Forgot to lock = didn't lock.
explanation.ruleId: Forget/remember + to-infinitive = kewajiban. Forget/remember + -ing = ingatan soal yang udah terjadi.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Pintunya nggak pernah dikunci, jadi “forget to lock” (tugas yang nggak dikerjain) maknanya yang dibutuhin.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Locking” nunjuk ingatan. “Lock” polos. “To have locked” pola yang salah.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya: aksinya terjadi? Kalau nggak, pakai “forget to”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Forgot to lock = nggak ngunci.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “forget to + kata kerja” buat tugas yang nggak dikerjain.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai “forget -ing” (ingatan soal kejadian lampau), padahal maknanya tugas yang kelewat.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali tugas yang nggak dikerjain → pilih forget + to-infinitive → hindari pola ingatan dengan -ing

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'more and more + adjective' for a change that keeps growing.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses a single comparative or a superlative for an ongoing, increasing change.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify a change that keeps increasing -> select the doubled comparative -> avoid superlatives
templates.stem: Phones are getting ___ every year.

distractors.misconception: treats a continuous, ongoing change as a single fixed-point comparison
distractors.whyFails: 'Than' needs a second item to compare with; nothing follows it here.
distractors.whyFailsId: “than” butuh hal kedua buat dibandingin. Di sini nggak ada yang ngikut.
distractors.misconceptionId: perubahan yang jalan terus diperlakuin sebagai perbandingan di satu titik aja.

distractors.misconception: confuses a progressive change over time with a superlative ranking among multiple items
distractors.whyFails: A superlative names the top item; it cannot show a change 'every year'.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk paling nyebut yang teratas. Nggak bisa nunjukin perubahan “every year”.
distractors.misconceptionId: perubahan yang jalan ketuker sama peringkat superlative di antara banyak hal.

distractors.misconception: uses a single comparative with 'more' for a short adjective, and frames it as a comparison to a norm rather than ongoing change
distractors.whyFails: 'Expensive' is a long adjective, so it takes 'more', not -er.
distractors.whyFailsId: “expensive” kata sifat panjang, jadi pakai “more”, bukan -er.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai satu bentuk “more” buat kata sifat pendek, dan dibingkai sebagai perbandingan sama kebiasaan.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Every year' shows a continuing increase, so the doubled comparative 'more and more expensive' fits.
explanation.rule: Progressive change: -er and -er (bigger and bigger) or more and more + long adjective.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Than' has no partner, the superlative is a fixed top point, and -er does not fit a long adjective.
explanation.howToAvoid: Is it still changing? Double the comparative.
explanation.memoryCue: More and more expensive every year.
explanation.ruleId: Perubahan bertahap: -er and -er (bigger and bigger) atau more and more + kata sifat panjang.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Every year” nunjukin kenaikan terus-menerus, jadi bentuk banding ganda “more and more expensive” pas.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Than” nggak punya pasangan. Bentuk paling itu titik puncak tetap. -er nggak cocok buat kata sifat panjang.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Masih berubah? Gandakan bentuk bandingnya.
explanation.memoryCueId: More and more expensive every year.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “more and more + kata sifat” buat perubahan yang terus meningkat.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai satu bentuk banding atau bentuk paling buat perubahan yang terus naik.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali perubahan yang terus meningkat → pilih bentuk banding ganda → hindari bentuk paling

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'It is said that' to report a general opinion without naming who says it.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses active 'they say' with a wrong form or drops the dummy subject 'it'.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify a general belief with no named source -> select it + is + past participle + that
templates.stem: ___ that this old house is haunted, but I don't believe it.

distractors.misconception: using active voice with a vague 'they' plus an incorrect continuous form for a general belief
distractors.whyFails: A vague 'they' in the continuous does not report a general belief.
distractors.whyFailsId: “they” yang samar dalam bentuk -ing nggak laporin keyakinan umum.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk aktif dengan “they” yang samar dipakai bareng bentuk continuous yang keliru.

distractors.misconception: treating 'it' as an active subject capable of believing
distractors.whyFails: 'It says' makes 'it' the speaker; the house does not say anything.
distractors.whyFailsId: “it says” bikin “it” jadi pembicara. Rumahnya nggak ngomong apa-apa.
distractors.misconceptionId: “it” diperlakuin sebagai subjek pelaku yang bisa meyakini sesuatu.

distractors.misconception: dropping the required dummy subject 'it' from the impersonal passive pattern
distractors.whyFails: The impersonal passive needs the dummy subject 'it' in front.
distractors.whyFailsId: pasif impersonal butuh subjek semu “it” di depan.
distractors.misconceptionId: subjek semu “it” yang diwajibin pola ini dihilangin.

explanation.whyCorrect: Nobody in particular is the source, so the impersonal passive 'It is said that…' is used.
explanation.rule: Impersonal reporting: It + is/was + said/believed/thought + that + clause.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'They are saying' is active and continuous, 'it says' turns 'it' into a speaker, and 'is said' lacks 'it'.
explanation.howToAvoid: Reporting a rumour or common belief? Start with 'It is said / believed that'.
explanation.memoryCue: It is said that…
explanation.ruleId: Pelaporan impersonal susunannya “It” + “is/was” + “said/believed/thought” + “that” + klausa.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Nggak ada sumber tertentu, jadi pasif impersonal “It is said that…” yang dipakai.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “They are saying” aktif dan -ing. “It says” bikin “it” jadi pembicara. “Is said” kurang “it”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Laporin rumor atau keyakinan umum? Mulai dari “It is said / believed that”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Rumor atau keyakinan umum dibuka pakai “It is said that…”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “It is said that” buat laporin pendapat umum tanpa nyebut siapa yang bilang.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai “they say” aktif dengan bentuk salah, atau ngilangin subjek semu “it”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali keyakinan umum tanpa sumber jelas → pilih it + is + past participle + that

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use the passive infinitive 'to be + past participle' after 'expected'.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses an active infinitive or a gerund after 'is expected'.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify that the subject receives the action -> select to be + past participle after expected
templates.stem: The results are expected ___ on Friday.

distractors.misconception: using active infinitive when the subject (the policy) cannot perform the announcing itself
distractors.whyFails: The results cannot publish anything; they are published, so the passive is needed.
distractors.whyFailsId: hasilnya nggak bisa nerbitin apa-apa. Hasilnya yang diterbitin, jadi butuh pasif.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk to aktif dipakai padahal subjeknya nggak mungkin ngumumin sendiri.

distractors.misconception: using a gerund where an infinitive pattern after 'expected' is required
distractors.whyFails: 'Expected' takes a to-infinitive, not a gerund.
distractors.whyFailsId: “expected” pakai to-infinitive, bukan -ing.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dipakai padahal sesudah “expected” yang diminta pola bentuk to.

distractors.misconception: adding continuous aspect to the passive infinitive unnecessarily
distractors.whyFails: The continuous form adds an ongoing meaning that does not fit a single release.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk -ing nambah makna berlangsung yang nggak cocok buat satu kali terbit.
distractors.misconceptionId: makna berkelanjutan ditambahin ke bentuk to pasif tanpa perlu.

explanation.whyCorrect: The results receive the action, so after 'expected' the passive infinitive 'to be published' is used.
explanation.rule: Be expected / supposed / likely + to be + past participle when the subject is acted on.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'To publish' is active, 'publishing' is the wrong pattern, and 'to be publishing' adds an unneeded continuous.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: does the subject do the action or receive it? Receive → to be + participle.
explanation.memoryCue: Expected to be published.
explanation.ruleId: Be expected / supposed / likely + to be + past participle kalau subjeknya yang dikenai aksi.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Hasilnya yang kena aksi, jadi sesudah “expected” pakai infinitive pasif “to be published”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “To publish” aktif. “Publishing” pola yang salah. “To be publishing” nambah -ing yang nggak perlu.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya: subjeknya ngelakuin aksi atau kena aksi? Kena → to be + participle.
explanation.memoryCueId: Expected to be published.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai infinitive pasif “to be + past participle” sesudah “expected”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai infinitive aktif atau -ing sesudah “is expected”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali subjeknya yang kena aksi → pilih to be + past participle sesudah expected

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'try to + verb' for making an effort at something hard.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses 'try -ing' (test a method) when the meaning is a difficult attempt.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify a hard effort rather than an experiment -> select try + to-infinitive
templates.stem: The box was heavy, but I tried ___ it alone. I couldn't.

distractors.misconception: using 'try to' (make a difficult effort) where 'try -ing' (experiment with a solution) is meant
distractors.whyFails: 'Try lifting' means testing lifting as one method; here the speaker struggled and failed at the effort.
distractors.whyFailsId: “try lifting” artinya nyoba ngangkat sebagai salah satu cara. Di sini pembicaranya berusaha keras dan gagal.
distractors.misconceptionId: “try to” yang berarti usaha keras dipakai padahal maksudnya nyoba satu cara.

distractors.misconception: using the bare infinitive after 'try', which isn't a valid pattern
distractors.whyFails: A bare verb cannot follow 'try'.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata kerja polos nggak bisa ngikut “try”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar dipakai sesudah “try” padahal itu bukan pola yang sah.

distractors.misconception: using a perfect gerund, implying the action is already completed
distractors.whyFails: A perfect gerund says the lifting is already done, which contradicts 'I couldn't'.
distractors.whyFailsId: perfect gerund bilang ngangkatnya udah selesai, bertentangan sama “I couldn't”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing perfect dipakai jadi tindakannya seolah udah kelar.

explanation.whyCorrect: Lifting the box was a hard effort that failed, so 'tried to lift' is the meaning needed.
explanation.rule: Try + to-infinitive = make an effort (hard); try + -ing = test a method to see if it works.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Lifting' is the experiment meaning, 'lift' is bare, and 'having lifted' says it already happened.
explanation.howToAvoid: Was it difficult and maybe impossible? Then 'try to'.
explanation.memoryCue: Tried to lift (effort) vs. try restarting (method).
explanation.ruleId: Try + to-infinitive = berusaha (sulit). Try + -ing = nyoba satu cara buat lihat hasilnya.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Ngangkat kotaknya usaha keras yang gagal, jadi “tried to lift” maknanya yang dibutuhin.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Lifting” makna percobaan cara. “Lift” polos. “Having lifted” bilang udah terjadi.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Sulit dan mungkin nggak bisa? Pakai “try to”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Tried to lift (usaha) vs. try restarting (cara).

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “try to + kata kerja” buat usaha keras ngelakuin sesuatu yang sulit.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai “try -ing” (nyoba satu cara), padahal maknanya usaha yang sulit.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali ini usaha keras, bukan percobaan cara → pilih try + to-infinitive

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'could have + past participle' for a past chance that was not taken.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses 'should have' (criticism) or a present modal for a missed past opportunity.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify a past chance that was not taken -> select could have + past participle -> avoid criticism forms
templates.stem: We ___ the early train, but we chose to sleep in. No regrets!

distractors.misconception: Confuses missed opportunity with retrospective advice/criticism.
distractors.whyFails: 'Should have' criticises a mistake, but the speaker says 'no regrets'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “should have” ngeritik kesalahan, padahal pembicaranya bilang “no regrets”.
distractors.misconceptionId: peluang yang terlewat ketuker sama nasihat atau teguran sesudah kejadian.

distractors.misconception: Confuses expressing a past possibility with reporting a completed achieved ability.
distractors.whyFails: 'Were able to' reports that we actually caught it — we did not.
distractors.whyFailsId: “were able to” laporin kita beneran ngejar keretanya — padahal nggak.
distractors.misconceptionId: nyatain kemungkinan lampau ketuker sama laporan kemampuan yang kelaksana.

distractors.misconception: Uses present modal for a past hypothetical situation.
distractors.whyFails: 'Can' is present; the missed train is in the past.
distractors.whyFailsId: “can” bentuk sekarang. Kereta yang kelewat itu di masa lampau.
distractors.misconceptionId: modal bentuk present dipakai buat keadaan lampau yang cuma dibayangin.

explanation.whyCorrect: Catching the train was possible but did not happen, and there is no criticism, so 'could have caught' fits.
explanation.rule: Could have + past participle = a past possibility that was not used; should have = criticism.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Should have' blames, 'were able to' says it happened, and 'can' is not past.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: possible but not done, and no blame? Then 'could have'.
explanation.memoryCue: Could have, but didn't.
explanation.ruleId: Could have + past participle = kemungkinan lampau yang nggak dipakai. Should have = kritik.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Ngejar keretanya mungkin tapi nggak terjadi, dan nggak ada kritik, jadi “could have caught” pas.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Should have” nyalahin. “Were able to” bilang itu terjadi. “Can” bukan lampau.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya: mungkin tapi nggak dilakuin, dan nggak ada yang disalahin? Pakai “could have”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Could have, tapi nggak.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “could have + past participle” buat kesempatan lampau yang nggak diambil.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai “should have” (kritik) atau modal sekarang buat kesempatan lampau yang kelewat.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali kesempatan lampau yang nggak diambil → pilih could have + past participle → hindari bentuk kritik

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'the' with a plural country name like 'the Philippines'.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner applies the no-article rule for country names to plural or descriptive names.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify a plural country name -> recall the exception -> select the
templates.stem: My aunt works as a nurse in ___ Philippines.

distractors.misconception: Treats the country name as an ordinary countable noun needing an indefinite article.
distractors.whyFails: A country name is not a countable noun that takes 'a'.
distractors.whyFailsId: nama negara bukan kata benda yang bisa dihitung pakai “a”.
distractors.misconceptionId: nama negara diperlakukan sebagai kata benda terhitung biasa yang butuh artikel tak tentu.

distractors.misconception: Applies the indefinite article rule based on the following vowel sound, ignoring that country names don't take indefinite articles at all.
distractors.whyFails: 'An' is chosen by the following vowel sound, but no indefinite article fits a country name.
distractors.whyFailsId: “an” dipilih dari bunyi vokal sesudahnya, tapi artikel tak tentu mana pun nggak cocok buat nama negara.
distractors.misconceptionId: aturan artikel tak tentu diterapkan berdasarkan bunyi vokal, tanpa melihat bahwa nama negara memang tidak memakainya.

distractors.misconception: Overgeneralizes the common 'no article before country names' rule to every country name.
distractors.whyFails: Most countries take no article, but plural names like the Philippines and the Netherlands need 'the'.
distractors.whyFailsId: kebanyakan negara tanpa artikel, tapi nama jamak kayak the Philippines dan the Netherlands butuh “the”.
distractors.misconceptionId: aturan umum tanpa artikel di depan nama negara diberlakukan untuk semua nama negara.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Philippines' is a plural country name, so it takes 'the': the Philippines.
explanation.rule: Zero article for most countries (Japan, Indonesia); 'the' for plural or descriptive names (the Philippines, the United States, the UK).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'A' and 'an' never go with country names, and zero article ignores the plural-name exception.
explanation.howToAvoid: Does the country name end in -s or contain a word like States/Kingdom/Republic? Use 'the'.
explanation.memoryCue: The Philippines, the Netherlands, the USA.
explanation.ruleId: Tanpa artikel buat kebanyakan negara (Japan, Indonesia). “The” buat nama jamak atau deskriptif (the Philippines, the United States, the UK).
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Philippines” nama negara jamak, jadi pakai “the”: the Philippines.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “A” dan “an” nggak pernah dipakai sama nama negara. Tanpa artikel ngabaikan pengecualian nama jamak.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Nama negaranya berakhiran -s atau ada kata kayak States/Kingdom/Republic? Pakai “the”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Nama negara jamak pakai “the”: “the Philippines”, “the Netherlands”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “the” sama nama negara jamak kayak “the Philippines”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nerapin aturan tanpa artikel buat nama negara ke nama yang jamak atau deskriptif.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali nama negara jamak → ingat pengecualiannya → pilih the

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'for' after the noun 'reason'.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner attaches 'of' or another preposition to 'reason' by analogy with similar nouns.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the noun reason -> recall its fixed preposition -> select for
templates.stem: Nobody knows the reason ___ his sudden decision to leave.

distractors.misconception: Assumes 'of' universally links a noun to what it relates to.
distractors.whyFails: 'Of' feels natural because it links many nouns, but 'reason' takes 'for'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “of” kerasa wajar karena nyambungin banyak kata benda, tapi “reason” pakai “for”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “of” dikira selalu bisa nyambungin kata benda sama hal yang berkaitan.

distractors.misconception: Transfers the preposition pattern from a related phrase like 'search for' onto 'solution'.
distractors.whyFails: 'To' belongs to 'solution to' or 'answer to', not to 'reason'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “to” punya “solution to” atau “answer to”, bukan “reason”.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola kata depan dari ungkapan berkaitan kayak “search for” dibawa ke “solution”.

distractors.misconception: Borrows a preposition associated with 'deal with' or 'cope with' a problem.
distractors.whyFails: 'About' introduces a topic; 'reason' needs the cause marker 'for'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “about” ngenalin topik. “Reason” butuh penanda sebab “for”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata depan yang lekat di “deal with” dipinjem buat “solution”.

explanation.whyCorrect: The noun 'reason' is always followed by 'for': the reason for his decision.
explanation.rule: Fixed noun + preposition pairs: reason for, solution to, answer to, effect on.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Of' is a default guess, 'to' belongs to other nouns, and 'about' introduces a topic rather than a cause.
explanation.howToAvoid: Store the noun and its preposition as one chunk: reason for.
explanation.memoryCue: Reason for, solution to.
explanation.ruleId: Pasangan tetap kata benda + kata depan: reason for, solution to, answer to, effect on.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Kata benda “reason” selalu diikuti “for”: the reason for his decision.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Of” tebakan bawaan. “To” punya kata benda lain. “About” ngenalin topik, bukan sebab.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Simpan kata benda sama kata depannya sebagai satu paket: reason for.
explanation.memoryCueId: Reason for, solution to.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “for” sesudah kata benda “reason”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nempelin “of” atau kata depan lain ke “reason” karena niru kata benda yang mirip.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali kata benda reason → ingat kata depan tetapnya → pilih for

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Pair a superlative with 'have ever + past participle'.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses the past simple or repeats 'have' without a participle after a superlative + ever.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify superlative + ever -> select the present perfect -> apply have + past participle
templates.stem: That was the funniest film I ___ ever ___.

distractors.misconception: Uses past simple twice instead of the fixed present perfect + ever pattern.
distractors.whyFails: After superlative + ever the fixed pattern is present perfect, not past forms.
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah bentuk paling + ever, pola tetapnya present perfect, bukan bentuk lampau.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk lampau dipakai dua-duanya, jadi klaim sepanjang hidupnya lepas dari sekarang.

distractors.misconception: Repeats the auxiliary 'have' without the required past participle 'had' for the main verb 'eat/have (a meal)'.
distractors.whyFails: 'Have' needs the past participle 'seen', not the base 'see'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “have” butuh past participle “seen”, bukan “see” polos.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu “have” diulang tanpa past participle yang dibutuhin kata kerja utamanya.

distractors.misconception: Mixes past simple auxiliary 'did' with present perfect 'have', producing an inconsistent structure.
distractors.whyFails: 'Did' is past simple; it does not combine with 'ever' after a superlative.
distractors.whyFailsId: “did” past simple. Nggak bisa digabung sama “ever” sesudah bentuk paling.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu past simple “did” dicampur sama present perfect jadi susunannya nggak selaras.

explanation.whyCorrect: Superlative + 'ever' takes the present perfect: the funniest film I have ever seen.
explanation.rule: The + superlative + (that) + subject + have/has ever + past participle.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Had; saw' and 'did; see' use past forms, and 'have; see' lacks the participle.
explanation.howToAvoid: Hear 'the -est … ever'? Finish with have/has + participle.
explanation.memoryCue: The best I have ever seen.
explanation.ruleId: The + bentuk paling + (that) + subjek + have/has ever + past participle.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Bentuk paling + “ever” pakai present perfect: the funniest film I have ever seen.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Had; saw” dan “did; see” pakai bentuk lampau. “Have; see” kurang participle.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Denger “the -est … ever”? Tutup pakai have/has + participle.
explanation.memoryCueId: Bentuk paling plus “ever” selalu ketemu present perfect: “the best I have ever seen”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pasangin bentuk paling sama “have ever + past participle”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai past simple atau ngulang “have” tanpa participle sesudah bentuk paling + ever.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali bentuk paling + ever → pilih present perfect → terapin have + past participle

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Keep all items in a list in the same to-infinitive form.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner mixes infinitives and gerunds in one list.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the list -> check that every item has the same form -> convert the odd item to match
templates.stem: Which sentence has correct parallel structure? "She wants to travel, learning languages, and to meet new people."
options: She wants to travel, learn languages, and meet new people.
She wants to travel, learning languages, and meeting new people.
She wants travelling, learn languages, and to meet new people.
She wants to travel, learning languages, and to meet new people.

distractors.option: She wants to travel, learning languages, and meeting new people.
distractors.misconception: Fixes only two of the three items, still leaving the list form inconsistent overall reasoning.
distractors.whyFails: It fixes only the last item; 'to travel' and 'learning' still clash.
distractors.whyFailsId: cuma ngebetulin butir terakhir. “To travel” dan “learning” masih bentrok.
distractors.misconceptionId: cuma dua dari tiga bagiannya yang dibetulin, jadi bentuknya tetap nggak selaras.

distractors.option: She wants travelling, learn languages, and to meet new people.
distractors.misconception: Converts the first item to infinitive while leaving the other two as gerunds.
distractors.whyFails: It changes the first item and leaves three different forms.
distractors.whyFailsId: ngubah butir pertama dan nyisain tiga bentuk yang beda.
distractors.misconceptionId: bagian pertamanya diubah jadi bentuk to sementara dua lainnya dibiarin bentuk -ing.

distractors.option: She wants to travel, learning languages, and to meet new people.
distractors.misconception: This is the original unedited sentence, left unchanged.
distractors.whyFails: This is the original sentence with the error untouched.
distractors.whyFailsId: ini kalimat aslinya, kesalahannya belum disentuh.
distractors.misconceptionId: kalimat aslinya dibiarin apa adanya tanpa perbaikan.

explanation.whyCorrect: All three items share one 'to': to travel, (to) learn, and (to) meet — the same form throughout.
explanation.rule: Parallel structure: items in a list must use the same grammatical form.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Two options still mix -ing with infinitives, and one is the unedited original.
explanation.howToAvoid: Read each list item after 'wants to': does it fit? If not, change its form.
explanation.memoryCue: To travel, learn, and meet — one shape.
explanation.ruleId: Struktur paralel: butir-butir dalam daftar harus pakai bentuk tata bahasa yang sama.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Ketiga butir berbagi satu “to”: to travel, (to) learn, dan (to) meet — bentuknya sama semua.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Dua pilihan masih nyampur -ing sama infinitive, satu lagi kalimat asli yang belum diubah.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Baca tiap butir sesudah “wants to”: cocok? Kalau nggak, ubah bentuknya.
explanation.memoryCueId: To travel, learn, and meet — satu bentuk.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Semua butir di daftar tetap dalam bentuk to-infinitive yang sama.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nyampur infinitive dan -ing dalam satu daftar.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali daftarnya → cek semua butir bentuknya sama → ubah butir yang beda supaya cocok

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use the past perfect after 'If only' for a regret about the past.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses the past simple or 'would have' after 'If only' about a past event.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify a regret about a finished past event -> select had + past participle after If only
templates.stem: If only I ___ harder for the exam last week!

distractors.misconception: staying with the past simple, which cannot mark the unreal past that regret needs
distractors.whyFails: Past simple after 'if only' is for a present wish; 'last week' makes this a past regret.
distractors.whyFailsId: past simple sesudah “if only” buat harapan sekarang. “Last week” bikin ini penyesalan lampau.
distractors.misconceptionId: past simple dipertahanin buat penyesalan lampau.

distractors.misconception: moving the 'would have' shape of the result clause into the wish clause itself
distractors.whyFails: 'Would have' is the result-clause shape; it does not follow 'if only'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “would have” bentuk klausa akibat. Nggak ngikut “if only”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk klausa hasil dipindah ke klausa harapan.

distractors.misconception: choosing the present perfect, which ties the missed reading to the present moment
distractors.whyFails: Present perfect ties the studying to now, but 'last week' is finished.
distractors.whyFailsId: present perfect ngiket belajarnya ke sekarang, padahal “last week” udah selesai.
distractors.misconceptionId: present perfect dipilih buat kejadian yang udah ketutup.

explanation.whyCorrect: The exam was last week, so the regret uses the past perfect: If only I had studied harder.
explanation.rule: If only / I wish + past perfect = regret about the past; + past simple = wish about the present.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Studied' is the present-wish form, 'would have' belongs in a result clause, and 'have studied' is not past enough.
explanation.howToAvoid: See a past time word with 'if only'? Go one step further back: had + participle.
explanation.memoryCue: If only I had… (too late now).
explanation.ruleId: If only / I wish + past perfect = penyesalan soal lampau. + past simple = harapan soal sekarang.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Ujiannya minggu lalu, jadi penyesalannya pakai past perfect: If only I had studied harder.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Studied” bentuk harapan sekarang. “Would have” punya klausa akibat. “Have studied” belum cukup lampau.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Ada kata waktu lampau sama “if only”? Mundur satu langkah lagi: had + participle.
explanation.memoryCueId: Udah terlambat buat disesali: “If only I had…”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai past perfect sesudah “If only” buat penyesalan soal masa lampau.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai past simple atau “would have” sesudah “If only” soal kejadian lampau.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali penyesalan soal kejadian lampau yang selesai → pilih had + past participle sesudah If only

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'wish + would' to complain about someone else's repeated behaviour.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses the past simple, present, or 'will' after 'wish' when complaining about another person's habit.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify a complaint about another person's habit -> select wish + would + base verb
templates.stem: My neighbour plays loud music every night. I wish he ___ it down.

distractors.misconception: treats a complaint about repeated behaviour as a wished-for state with wish + past simple
distractors.whyFails: 'Wish + past simple' describes a state; a complaint about repeated behaviour uses 'would'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “wish + past simple” ngegambarin keadaan. Keluhan soal kelakuan berulang pakai “would”.
distractors.misconceptionId: keluhan soal kebiasaan orang lain dibungkus “wish + past simple”.

distractors.misconception: keeping the present tense after 'wish', reading the situation as a real current fact
distractors.whyFails: The present tense cannot follow 'wish'.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk sekarang nggak bisa ngikut “wish”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk sekarang dipertahanin sesudah “wish”.

distractors.misconception: puts future 'will' after 'wish', calquing Indonesian 'akan'
distractors.whyFails: 'Will' never follows 'wish'; the form is 'would'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “will” nggak pernah ngikut “wish”. Bentuknya “would”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “will” dipasang sesudah “wish” karena kebawa makna “akan”.

explanation.whyCorrect: The speaker is annoyed by the neighbour's habit and wants it to change, so 'wish he would turn' is used.
explanation.rule: Wish + would + base verb = annoyance about someone else's behaviour that they could change.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Turned' is for states, 'turns' is present, and 'will' is not allowed after 'wish'.
explanation.howToAvoid: Complaining about what another person keeps doing? 'I wish they would…'
explanation.memoryCue: I wish he would stop!
explanation.ruleId: Wish + would + kata kerja dasar = kesal sama kelakuan orang lain yang bisa dia ubah.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Pembicara kesal sama kebiasaan tetangganya dan mau itu berubah, jadi pakai “wish he would turn”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Turned” buat keadaan. “Turns” bentuk sekarang. “Will” nggak boleh sesudah “wish”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Ngeluh soal yang terus dilakuin orang lain? “I wish they would…”
explanation.memoryCueId: Kesal sama kelakuan orang lain: “I wish he would stop!”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “wish + would” buat ngeluh soal kelakuan orang lain yang berulang.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai past simple, bentuk sekarang, atau “will” sesudah “wish” waktu ngeluh soal kebiasaan orang lain.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali keluhan soal kebiasaan orang lain → pilih wish + would + kata kerja dasar

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'get used to + -ing' for becoming comfortable with something new.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner reads the 'to' in 'get used to' as an infinitive marker and adds a bare verb.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify get used to as a preposition pattern -> select the -ing form after to
templates.stem: It took me a month to get used to ___ up at five for work.

distractors.misconception: reads the 'to' in 'be used to' as an infinitive marker, copying the past-habit pattern
distractors.whyFails: The 'to' in 'get used to' is a preposition, so the verb after it takes -ing.
distractors.whyFailsId: “to” di “get used to” itu kata depan, jadi kata kerja sesudahnya pakai -ing.
distractors.misconceptionId: “to” di “be used to” dibaca sebagai penanda infinitive.

distractors.misconception: slots a finite past form after the preposition 'to' in 'be used to'
distractors.whyFails: A past form cannot follow the preposition 'to'.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk lampau nggak bisa ngikut kata depan “to”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk lampau ditaruh sesudah preposisi “to” karena kebawa rasa lampau “used to”.

distractors.misconception: inserts infinitive 'be' after 'used to' although this 'to' is a preposition needing -ing
distractors.whyFails: 'Be' treats the 'to' as an infinitive marker; the pattern needs -ing directly.
distractors.whyFailsId: “be” nganggap “to” penanda infinitive. Polanya butuh -ing langsung.
distractors.misconceptionId: “be” infinitive diselipin sesudah “used to”, padahal “to”-nya preposisi.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Get used to' is followed by a gerund: get used to getting up at five.
explanation.rule: Be/get used to + -ing = be/become comfortable with; used to + base verb = past habit.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Get', 'got', and 'be getting' all treat 'to' as part of an infinitive instead of a preposition.
explanation.howToAvoid: Is there a 'be' or 'get' before 'used to'? Then the next verb ends in -ing.
explanation.memoryCue: Get used to getting up early.
explanation.ruleId: Be/get used to + -ing = terbiasa / jadi terbiasa. Used to + kata kerja dasar = kebiasaan lampau.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Get used to” diikuti -ing: get used to getting up at five.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Get”, “got”, dan “be getting” semuanya nganggap “to” bagian infinitive, bukan kata depan.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Ada “be” atau “get” sebelum “used to”? Kata kerja berikutnya berakhiran -ing.
explanation.memoryCueId: Get used to getting up early.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “get used to + -ing” buat jadi terbiasa sama hal baru.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu baca “to” di “get used to” sebagai penanda infinitive dan nambah kata kerja polos.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali get used to sebagai pola kata depan → pilih bentuk -ing sesudah to

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use a bare verb after 'would rather'.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner adds 'to' or -ing after 'would rather' by analogy with 'prefer'.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify would rather -> recall that it takes a bare verb -> select the base form
templates.stem: I'd rather ___ tea than coffee in the evening.

distractors.misconception: generalizes the to-infinitive to 'would rather' on the model of 'prefer to'
distractors.whyFails: 'Prefer to drink' takes 'to', but 'would rather' takes the bare verb.
distractors.whyFailsId: “prefer to drink” pakai “to”, tapi “would rather” pakai kata kerja polos.
distractors.misconceptionId: “would rather” ikut-ikutan pola “prefer to”, jadi ketambahan “to”.

distractors.misconception: imports the gerund complement of 'prefer' into the 'would rather' pattern
distractors.whyFails: -ing belongs to 'prefer drinking', not to 'would rather'.
distractors.whyFailsId: -ing punya “prefer drinking”, bukan “would rather”.
distractors.misconceptionId: pelengkap -ing punya “prefer” dibawa ke pola “would rather”.

distractors.misconception: backshifts to a past form after 'would rather' although no second subject intervenes
distractors.whyFails: A past form is not used after 'would rather' when the speaker talks about their own preference now.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk lampau nggak dipakai sesudah “would rather” kalau pembicara ngomongin kesukaannya sendiri sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerjanya digeser ke bentuk lampau padahal nggak ada subjek kedua.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Would rather' is followed directly by the base verb: I'd rather drink tea.
explanation.rule: Would rather + base verb (+ than + base verb); prefer + to-infinitive or -ing.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'To drink' and 'drinking' copy the 'prefer' patterns, and 'drank' is a past form.
explanation.howToAvoid: After 'rather', write the verb with nothing in front of it.
explanation.memoryCue: I'd rather drink tea than coffee.
explanation.ruleId: Would rather + kata kerja dasar (+ than + kata kerja dasar). Prefer + to-infinitive atau -ing.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Would rather” langsung diikuti kata kerja dasar: I'd rather drink tea.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “To drink” dan “drinking” niru pola “prefer”. “Drank” bentuk lampau.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Sesudah “rather”, tulis kata kerjanya tanpa apa pun di depannya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Sesudah “would rather” kata kerjanya polos: “I'd rather drink tea than coffee”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai kata kerja polos sesudah “would rather”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nambah “to” atau -ing sesudah “would rather” karena niru “prefer”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali would rather → ingat dia pakai kata kerja polos → pilih bentuk dasar

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'was supposed to' for a past arrangement that did not happen.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner drops 'be' before 'supposed to' or treats 'suppose' as an ordinary verb.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify an expectation that was not met -> select be + supposed to -> match the past form was
templates.stem: Dani ___ meet us at six, but he never showed up.

distractors.misconception: drops the obligatory 'be' before 'supposed to'
distractors.whyFails: 'Supposed to' always needs a form of 'be' in front: was supposed to.
distractors.whyFailsId: “supposed to” selalu butuh bentuk “be” di depannya: was supposed to.
distractors.misconceptionId: “be” di depan “supposed to” dihilangin, kebawa kalimat Indonesia yang nggak butuh kata penghubung.

distractors.misconception: treats 'suppose' as an ordinary present-tense verb instead of the passive pattern 'be supposed to'
distractors.whyFails: 'Suppose' as an ordinary verb means 'think'; the expectation pattern needs 'be supposed to'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “suppose” sebagai kata kerja biasa artinya “mengira”. Pola harapan butuh “be supposed to”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “suppose” dipakai kayak kata kerja kini biasa, padahal maknanya cuma ada di pola pasif “be supposed to”.

distractors.misconception: forces a progressive onto the fixed passive participle 'supposed'
distractors.whyFails: 'Supposed' here is a fixed participle and never takes -ing.
distractors.whyFailsId: “supposed” di sini participle tetap dan nggak pernah pakai -ing.
distractors.misconceptionId: participle beku “supposed” dipaksa jadi bentuk -ing.

explanation.whyCorrect: Meeting at six was the arrangement, and it failed, so 'was supposed to meet' expresses the unmet expectation.
explanation.rule: Be supposed to + verb = what is expected or arranged; the 'be' changes for tense (is/was).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Supposed to' has no 'be', 'supposes to' is the wrong verb, and 'supposing' cannot replace the participle.
explanation.howToAvoid: Always say be + supposed to as one unit: is supposed to, was supposed to.
explanation.memoryCue: Was supposed to = should have, but didn't.
explanation.ruleId: Be supposed to + kata kerja = yang diharapkan atau dijanjikan. “Be”-nya berubah ngikut waktu (is/was).
explanation.whyCorrectId: Ketemu jam enam itu janjinya, dan gagal, jadi “was supposed to meet” nyatain harapan yang nggak terpenuhi.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Supposed to” nggak ada “be”. “Supposes to” salah kata kerja. “Supposing” nggak bisa ngegantiin participle-nya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Selalu ucapin be + supposed to sebagai satu paket: is supposed to, was supposed to.
explanation.memoryCueId: Was supposed to = harusnya, tapi nggak.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “was supposed to” buat janji lampau yang nggak terjadi.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngilangin “be” sebelum “supposed to” atau nganggap “suppose” kata kerja biasa.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali harapan yang nggak terpenuhi → pilih be + supposed to → cocokin bentuk lampau was

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use the past simple after 'It's time' when talking about now.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses a present or future verb after 'it's time' + subject.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify it's time + subject -> recall the unreal past -> select the past simple
templates.stem: It's late. It's time we ___ home.

distractors.misconception: keeps a present-tense verb after 'it's high time', calquing 'sudah waktunya' plus a present verb
distractors.whyFails: After 'it's time + subject', the verb takes the unreal past, not the present.
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “it's time + subjek”, kata kerjanya pakai lampau tak nyata, bukan bentuk sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: sesudah “it's high time” kata kerjanya dibiarin bentuk kini, kebawa pola “sudah waktunya” plus kata kerja biasa.

distractors.misconception: marks the clause after 'it's high time' with future 'will' because the action is still to come
distractors.whyFails: 'Will' does not follow 'it's time we'; the fixed form is past simple.
distractors.whyFailsId: “will” nggak ngikut “it's time we”. Bentuk tetapnya past simple.
distractors.misconceptionId: “will” ditambahin sesudah “it's high time” karena aksinya memang belum terjadi.

distractors.misconception: uses the present progressive after 'it's high time' as if the action were already under way
distractors.whyFails: The continuous describes what is happening; 'it's time' says what should happen.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk -ing ngegambarin yang lagi terjadi. “It's time” bilang yang seharusnya terjadi.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk sedang-berlangsung dipakai sesudah “it's high time”, seolah aksinya udah jalan.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'It's time we' is followed by the unreal past even though the meaning is now: it's time we went home.
explanation.rule: It's (high) time + subject + past simple = something should happen now or should have happened already.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Go', 'will go', and 'are going' all ignore the unreal-past rule after 'it's time we'.
explanation.howToAvoid: See 'it's time' with a subject after it? Put the verb in the past simple.
explanation.memoryCue: It's time we went.
explanation.ruleId: It's (high) time + subjek + past simple = sesuatu harusnya terjadi sekarang atau udah seharusnya terjadi.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “It's time we” diikuti lampau tak nyata walau maknanya sekarang: it's time we went home.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Go”, “will go”, dan “are going” semuanya ngabaikan aturan lampau tak nyata sesudah “it's time we”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Lihat “it's time” dengan subjek sesudahnya? Taruh kata kerjanya di past simple.
explanation.memoryCueId: It's time we went.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai past simple sesudah “It's time” walau ngomongin sekarang.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai kata kerja sekarang atau masa depan sesudah “it's time” + subjek.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali it's time + subjek → ingat lampau tak nyata → pilih past simple

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use the past simple after 'as if' for something that is clearly not true.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner keeps the present or adds 'would' after 'as if' when the comparison is unreal.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify an unreal comparison after as if -> select the past simple -> avoid present and would
templates.stem: He talks about the city as if he ___ there, but he has never left our village.

distractors.misconception: keeps the real-possibility present after 'as if' although the sentence denies the comparison
distractors.whyFails: The present suggests it might be true, but 'he has never left our village' shows it is not.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk sekarang ngesankan itu mungkin benar, padahal “he has never left our village” nunjukin nggak.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk kini nyata dipertahanin sesudah “as if”, padahal kalimatnya sendiri nyangkal perbandingannya.

distractors.misconception: reads 'as if' as reporting genuine experience with the present perfect
distractors.whyFails: Present perfect reports real experience; he has no such experience.
distractors.whyFailsId: present perfect laporin pengalaman nyata. Dia nggak punya pengalaman itu.
distractors.misconceptionId: “as if” dibaca kayak laporan pengalaman nyata, jadi dipasangin present perfect.

distractors.misconception: puts conditional 'would' inside the 'as if' clause as if it were a result clause
distractors.whyFails: 'Would' belongs in a result clause, not inside an 'as if' clause.
distractors.whyFailsId: “would” tempatnya di klausa akibat, bukan di dalam klausa “as if”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “would” diselipin ke dalam klausa “as if”, ketukar sama klausa hasil pengandaian.

explanation.whyCorrect: He has never lived there, so the unreal comparison uses the past simple: as if he lived there.
explanation.rule: As if / as though + past simple = unreal now; + present = possibly true.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Lives' and 'has lived' treat it as real, and 'would live' misplaces a conditional result form.
explanation.howToAvoid: Is the comparison clearly false? Move the verb one step back.
explanation.memoryCue: As if he lived there (he doesn't).
explanation.ruleId: As if / as though + past simple = nggak nyata sekarang. + bentuk sekarang = mungkin benar.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Dia nggak pernah tinggal di sana, jadi perbandingan nggak nyatanya pakai past simple: as if he lived there.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Lives” dan “has lived” nganggap itu nyata. “Would live” salah naruh bentuk akibat pengandaian.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Perbandingannya jelas salah? Geser kata kerjanya satu langkah ke belakang.
explanation.memoryCueId: As if he lived there (padahal nggak).
